quelle: Memoriale Beati Petri Fabri, primi sacerdotis Societatis Iesu, ed. Marcel Bouix SJ (Paris: Gauthier-Villars, 1873). First public edition; in the United States public domain. Reconstructed from the OCR of the Internet Archive scan memorialebeatipe0000sign.
provenienz: Favre's autograph is lost. Bouix printed the Latin text transmitted within the Society of Jesus through autographic printings (an internal printing is recorded for 1853), emending corrupt passages, omitting a few words he judged beyond repair, and rendering into Latin a handful of Spanish words embedded in the text. The critical edition of the original — largely Spanish — appeared only in the Monumenta Historica Societatis Iesu (Fabri Monumenta, Madrid 1914), whose canonical paragraph numbering (MF 1-443) this edition therefore cannot reproduce: the paragraph numbers here are this site's own, assigned to the 1873 text.
uebersetzung: The English is an unofficial machine-generated working translation made for this site directly from the 1873 Latin, consulting no copyrighted translation. Cite the Latin.

sections.arg: In hoc proæmio breviter indicat Auctor quasdam gratias quibus a Deo donatus est ab ortu usque ad trigesimum sextum ætatis suæ annum.

units.la: Benedic, anima mea, Domino, et noli oblivisci omnes retributiones ejus: qui redimit de interitu vitam tuam, et coronat te in misericordia et miserationibus; qui replet in bonis desiderium tuum, postquam propitiatus est, et quotidie propitiatur omnibus iniquitatibus tuis, et sanat infirmitates tuas, dans spem bonam, quod renovabitur ut aquilae juventus tua. Confitere semper, anima mea, et noli unquam oblivisci multa beneficia quae Dominus Noster Jesus Christus fecit tibi, et sin- gulis facit momentis, intercessione benedictae Matris il suae Domine meae, omniumque sanctorum et sanctarum coeli, et omnium etiam qui pro te orant in Ecclesia catholica. Adora, anima mea, Patrem caelestem, honorando ipsum semper, ei ex omnibus viribus tuis serviendo, totaque sapientia tua et voluntate; qui suo benedicto amore tam misericorditer te adjuvat et corroborat. Adora redemptorem tuum Dominum Nostrum J esum Christum, qui tanquam vera via, veritas et vita, sua sola gratia te docet et illuminat. Adora personam tui glorificatoris, Spiritus Sancti Paracleti, qui sua benigna communicatione, disponit corpus, animam, et spiritum tuum, ut sit mundus, rectus, et bonus in omnibus.
units.en: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: who redeems your life from destruction, and crowns you in mercy and compassion; who fills your desire with good things after he has been appeased, and daily is appeased over all your iniquities, and heals your infirmities, giving good hope that your youth shall be renewed like the eagle's. Confess always, my soul, and never forget the many benefits which Our Lord Jesus Christ has done for you, and does at every moment, by the intercession of his blessed Mother my Lady, and of all the saints, men and women, of heaven, and of all besides who pray for you in the catholic Church. Adore, my soul, the heavenly Father, honouring him always, serving him with all your strength and with all your wisdom and will; who by his blessed love so mercifully helps and strengthens you. Adore your redeemer, Our Lord Jesus Christ, who as the true way, the truth and the life, by his grace alone teaches and enlightens you. Adore the person of your glorifier, the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, who by his kindly communication disposes your body, soul and spirit to be clean, upright and good in all things.

units.la: Anno 1542, in octava Corporis Christi Domini Nostri, habui quoddam notabile desiderium faciendi deinceps quod eo -usque ex sola negligentia et pigritia omiseram, notandi scilicet, in gratiam memoriae, aliqua lumina spiritualia, ex iis quae Dominus dederit, sive ea sint ad melius orandum aut contemplandum, sive ad intelligendum. Prius autem quam de futuris loquar, visum est notare aliqua de praeterita mea vita usque ad hanc horam, sicut occurrit nunc, et me recordor sensisse in tlem- poribus illis, cum quadam notabili gratiarum actione, aut contritione, aut compassione, aut alio spirituali sensu Spiritus Sancti, aut admonitione proprii Angeli boni.
units.en: In the year 1542, on the octave of the Body of Christ Our Lord, I had a notable desire to do thenceforth what up to then I had omitted out of sheer negligence and sloth: namely, to note down, as an aid to memory, some of the spiritual lights which the Lord should give, whether for praying or contemplating better, or for understanding. But before speaking of things to come, it seemed good to note some things of my past life up to this hour, as they occur to me now and as I remember having felt them in those times, with some notable act of thanksgiving, or contrition, or compassion, or other spiritual feeling of the Holy Spirit, or admonition of my own good Angel.

units.la: Primum igitur beneficium quod notavi, cum gratiarum actione, fuit quod Dominus Noster, anno 1506, in diebus Paschalibus, me in mundum eduxerit, largitusque fuerit baptismatis gratiam, utque essem à bonis, catholicis, piisque parentibus educatus. Qui cum essent agricolae, sufficientes erant in bonis temporalibus ad me juvandum in debitis mediis ad salutem animae meae, conformiter ad id propter quod sum creatus. Sic autem me educarunt in timore Domini, ut statim a parvulo incaeperim mihi esse conscius; et, quod majoris divinae gratiae praevenientis signum est, etiam circa septimum annum sensi aliquoties speciales affectus devotionis; sic ut, ab eo tempore, Dominus tan-. quam sponsus animae meae, voluerit quidem illam possidere. Utinam sapuissem! utinam scivissem introducere ipsum, et sequi, et nunquam ab eo separari!
units.en: The first benefit, then, which I noted with thanksgiving was that Our Lord, in the year 1506, in the days of Easter, brought me into the world and bestowed the grace of baptism, and that I was brought up by good, catholic and devout parents. Though they were farmers, they had sufficient temporal means to help me in the ways needful for the salvation of my soul, in conformity with the end for which I was created. And they brought me up in the fear of the Lord in such a way that from a small child I began to have a conscience; and — what is a sign of greater prevenient divine grace — even about my seventh year I sometimes felt special affections of devotion; so that from that time the Lord, as the bridegroom of my soul, willed indeed to possess it. Would that I had had the sense! Would that I had known how to let him in, and to follow him, and never to be separated from him!

units.la: Circa annum decimum, sensi desiderium quod- dam studendi: cum enim essem pastor et mundo EES ES destinatus a parentibus, non poteram quiescere, et flebam desiderio scholae; ita ut coacti fuerint parentes, contra suam intentionem, me mittere ad studium vel scholas; videntesque apertum fructum notabilemque progressum ïn studiis, tum in intelligendo, tum etiam in memorando, non potuerunt impedire quominus pergerem in studio; permittente etiam Domino ut ad nihil essem minus idoneus aut pollens quam ad secularia negotia. Studui autem praeceptore Petro Veliardo, qui non solum catholica sed etiam sancta doctrina vitaeque ferventissıimae sanctitate sic claruit, ut omnes poëtas et auctores, quos interpretabatur, faceret evangelicos: omnia enim applicabat ad aedificationem juventutis in timore Domini justo et casto. Locus autem ubi sepultus jacet, vocatur Korse tribus distans leucis a pago ubi natus sum, cui nomen Villareto, in magno Bornando, in Episcopatu dioecesis Genevensis, quae tota tunc erat satis catholica.
units.en: About my tenth year I felt a certain desire to study: for since I was a shepherd, destined by my parents for the world, I could not rest, and wept with longing for school; so that my parents were compelled, against their own intention, to send me to study, that is to the schools. And seeing the evident fruit and notable progress in my studies, both in understanding and in memory, they could not prevent my going on with study — the Lord also permitting that I should be fit for and capable of nothing less than secular business. I studied under the master Pierre Veillard, who was distinguished not only for catholic but for holy teaching, and for the sanctity of a most fervent life, in such measure that he made all the poets and authors he expounded evangelical: for he applied everything to the building up of youth in the just and chaste fear of the Lord. The place where he lies buried is called La Roche, three leagues distant from the village where I was born, which is named Villaret, in the Grand Bornand, in the diocese of Geneva, which at that time was still catholic enough throughout.

units.la: Doctrina et exemplo vite hujus praeceptoris, proficiebamus omnės ejus discipuli in timore Domini; et ita, cum essem circiter annorum duodecim, habui quosdam spiritusimpulsus ad offe- rendum me servitio Dei; venique quadam die valde laetus in quemdam agrum, erat enim vacationis tempus, exercebamque aliquando pastoris officium cum, inquam, tunc haberem magnum desiderium puritatis, promisi Deo castitatem in aeternum. O misericordia Dei, quae ambulabas mecum, et me ex tunc volebas apprehendere, quare te non bene cognovi? O Spiritus Sancte, cur ex eo tempore non scivi segregare me ab omnibus, ut quaererem te et ingrederer tuam scholam, quandoquidem invitabas et praeveniebas in talibus benedictionibus? Tu nihilominus me apprehendisti; tu me indelebili timoris tui charactere signasti; quem si permisisses tolli, sicut caetera bona gratuita, quidni factus essem sicut Sodoma et Gomorra!
units.en: By the teaching and example of this master's life all of us, his pupils, made progress in the fear of the Lord; and so, when I was about twelve years old, I had certain impulses of the spirit to offer myself to the service of God; and one day, in great gladness, I went out into a field — for it was holiday time, and I still sometimes did a shepherd's work — and there, having then a great desire of purity, I promised to God chastity for ever. O mercy of God, that walked with me and even then wished to take hold of me — why did I not know you well? O Holy Spirit, why from that time did I not know how to withdraw myself from everything, to seek you and to enter your school, since you were inviting me and going before me with such blessings? You nevertheless took hold of me; you marked me with the indelible character of your fear; and had you allowed that to be taken away, like the other free gifts, why should I not have become as Sodom and Gomorrah?

units.la: Novem annos fui in schola, et aetate crescens et scientia, licet non usquein finem illius temporis in sapientia bonitatis et castitatis oculorum meorum. Est itaque quod in hoc multum recognoscam, in gratiarum actione magna, et in dolore etcontritione cordis, propter peccata quae quotidie, ad eorum aliqua nascendo et in iis crescendo, committebam contra Dominum meum; multoque plura commisissem nisi divina Bonitas permisisset in anima mea, cum timore ejus, in ordinatum quoddam desiderium sciendi et discendi litteras. Hoc igitur impulsu, me eduxit Dominus de patria, ubi non poteram integre, nec et in posterum debite ei servire. Benedictus sis mihi, Domine, in aeternum de tanto mihi tunc praestito beneficio, dum me voluisti extrahere a carne mea tam corrupta, spiritui contraria, et ad ascendendum in cognitionem et sensum tuae Majestatis tantoraumque paroxysmorum tam infirma.
units.en: Nine years I spent at school, growing in age and in knowledge, though not to the end of that time in the wisdom of goodness and in chastity of my eyes. Here, then, is much for me to acknowledge, with great thanksgiving and with grief and contrition of heart, on account of the sins which I daily committed against my Lord, being born to some of them and growing in them; and I should have committed many more had not the divine Goodness allowed there to remain in my soul, together with his fear, an ordered desire of knowing and of learning letters. By this impulse the Lord led me out of my native country, where I could not serve him wholly, nor in future as I ought. Blessed be you to me, O Lord, for ever, for so great a benefit then bestowed, when you willed to draw me out from my flesh, so corrupt, so contrary to the spirit, and so weak for ascending to the knowledge and feeling of your Majesty and of such great struggles.

units.la: Anno 1525, aetatis autem meae decimo nono, exiens e patria veni Parisios. Recordare, o anima mea, spirituàlium calcarium, quibus jam Dominus tuam conscientiam in sui timore stimulabat, serupulis videlicet quibusdam et conscienti remorsibus, qwbus incipiebat te daemon vexare; ut sic quaereres Creatorem tuum, si sapuisses; et sine quibus nec te forte potuisset Ignatius penetrare, nec tu ab eo auxilium quaesisses, ut postea evenit.
units.en: In the year 1525, the nineteenth of my age, leaving my country I came to Paris. Remember, O my soul, the spiritual spurs with which the Lord was already pricking your conscience in his fear — certain scruples, that is, and remorses of conscience with which the demon was beginning to vex you; so that you might thereby seek your Creator, had you had the sense; and without which perhaps Ignatius could not have penetrated you, nor would you have sought help from him, as afterwards came to pass.

units.la: Anno 1529, aetalis autem meae vigesimo tertio, Decima die Januarii, creatus sum Baccalaureus in artibus; et post Pascha, Licentiatus sub magistro Joanne Penna, maximo in medicina. Det mihi Bonitas divina gratiam et memoriam, ad recognos- cenda varia ejus beneficia corporalia et spiritualia, quae mihi, his tribus annis cum dimidio, per varia media contulit: dando mihi scilicet talem praeceptorem, talemque societatem qualem inveni in suo cubiculo, dico autem maxime de magistro Francisco Xaverio, qui est de Societate Jesu.
units.en: In the year 1529, the twenty-third of my age, on the tenth day of January, I was made Bachelor of Arts; and after Easter, Licentiate, under master Juan de la Peña, a man most eminent in his science. May the divine Goodness give me grace and memory to acknowledge his various benefits, bodily and spiritual, which in those three years and a half he conferred on me by various means: giving me, namely, such a teacher, and such companionship as I found in his room — I speak above all of master Francis Xavier, who is of the Society of Jesus.

units.la: Hoc.anno venit Ignatius, ut esset in eodem collegio sanclae Barbarae et in eodem cubiculo, volens nobiscum ingredi cursum artium in sanctó'Remigio sequenti. Erat autem supradictus magister Xaverius id oneris suscepturus. Benedicta sit in aeternum Divina Providentia, quae sic ordinavit in meum bonum et salutem! Cum enim ab illo fuisset sic ordinatum, ut ego docerem praedictum sanctum virum, consecutus sum ejus exteriorem conversationem, deinde vero interiorem. Qui cum simul viveremus in eodem cubiculo, et eadem mensa, eadem bursa esset, ipse mihi fuit 1n spiritualibus praeceptor, dans modum ascendendi in cognitionem divinae voluntatis et propriae. Tandem facti sumus unum in desideriis et voluntate, junctoque proposito eligendi hanc vitam quam nunc habemus, quicumque sumus aut unquam fuerint de hac Societate, qua non sum dignus. Det mihi divina Clementia gratiam ad bene memoranda et ponde- randa beneficia, quae hoc tempore per hunc virum mihi Dominus Noster contulit; praecipue vero quod mihi dederit primum intelligere conscientiam meam, tentationes et scrupulos quibus tanto tempore detentus fueram, non sciens, nec intelligens aut inveniens viam qua possem quiescere. Erant autem scrupuli ex timore quod a multo tempore non fuissem bene confessus de peccatis; quibus adeo vexabar, ut libenter in remedium elegissem in desertum ire, herbis ibi semper et radicibus me nutriendo; tentationes autem, de faedis malisque imaginationibus carnalibus, suggerente spiritu fornicationis, quem tunc non cognoscebam per spiritum. Sed mihi Ignatius consuluit ut confiterer primum generaliter doctori Castro, et deinde singulis hebdomadis, sumendo etiam Eucharistiam, dans ad id examen quotidianum conscientiae; necdum enim volebat me in aliis exercitiis ponere, etiamsi haberem ad ea permagnum a Domino desiderium.
units.en: In this year came Ignatius, to be in the same college of Sainte-Barbe and in the same room, intending to enter with us the course of arts at the following feast of Saint Remy. And the aforesaid master Xavier was to undertake that charge. Blessed for ever be the Divine Providence, which ordered this for my good and my salvation! For when it had been so arranged that I should teach that holy man, I gained first his outward conversation, and then his inward. And as we lived together in the same room and at the same table and from the same purse, he became my teacher in spiritual things, giving me a way of ascending to the knowledge of the divine will and of my own. In the end we became one in desires and in will, joined in the purpose of choosing this life which we now have — all of us who are, or shall ever be, of this Society, of which I am not worthy. May the divine Clemency give me grace to remember well and weigh well the benefits which Our Lord conferred on me at that time through this man; above all that he gave me to understand my conscience, and the temptations and scruples by which I had been held so long, neither knowing nor understanding nor finding the way by which I might have peace. For the scruples came from a fear that for a long time I had not confessed my sins well; and I was so vexed by them that I would gladly, as a remedy, have chosen to go into a desert, to feed there for ever on herbs and roots; and the temptations were of foul and evil carnal imaginations, at the prompting of the spirit of fornication, which at that time I did not know in the spirit. But Ignatius counselled me first to make a general confession to Doctor Castro, and then to confess every week, receiving also the Eucharist, and gave me for this a daily examination of conscience; for he was not yet willing to set me in the other exercises, although I had from the Lord a very great desire for them.

units.la: Sic nobis transierünt quatuor circiter anni, in tali conversatione et animo, conversando etiam cum aliis; proficiebamque ego in Spiritu quotidie, et gratia aliorum et gratia mei ipsius; probabarque in multis flammis, in aquis tentationum, multis quidem annis, et fere usquequo Parisiis discessi; in vana gloria, in qua Dominus mihi dedit magnam cognitionem mei ipsius meorumque defectuum; permittens me in eis nimium profundarıi et angustiari, in remedium vanae gloriae; et ita, sola sua gratia, mihi dedit in hac materia multam pacem. In gula etiam multos passus sum labores, nec unquam scivi pacem consequi usque ad tempus Exercitiorum, in quibus fui sex dies sine ullo cibo aut potu, praeter eum qui solet qari in communione, scilicet parum vini, cum semel communicarem. Habui etiam plures alias tentationes turbationum, super alienorum defectuum contemplatione, suspicionibus, judiciis, in quo etiam non mihi defuit gratia consolatoris et doctoris, qui me ad primos gradus promovit: charitas enim proximi ad id ipsum disponebat. Scrupulos etiam de qualibet: re, super imperfectionibus innumeris tunc incognitis, habui eo tempore, usque ad egressum Parisiis.
units.en: So there passed for us about four years, in such conversation and spirit, conversing also with others; and I made progress in the Spirit daily, both by the grace of others and by my own; and I was tried in many flames, in the waters of temptations, for many years indeed, and almost until I left Paris: in vainglory, in which the Lord gave me great knowledge of myself and of my defects, allowing me to sink and be straitened in them exceedingly, as a remedy against vainglory; and so, by his grace alone, he gave me much peace in this matter. In gluttony also I suffered many labours, nor did I ever know how to obtain peace until the time of the Exercises, in which I passed six days without any food or drink except that which is customarily given in communion, that is a little wine, when I once communicated. I had also several other temptations of disquiet, over the contemplation of other men's defects, suspicions, judgments; in which also the grace of the consoler and teacher who advanced me to the first steps did not fail me: for the charity of my neighbour disposed me to the same. Scruples also about anything and everything, over innumerable imperfections then unknown, I had at that time, up to my departure from Paris.

units.la: Variis itaque modis me docuit Dominus, remedium adhibens contra multas tristitias inde pro- venientes, ut non possim digne satis recordari; possim vero dicere nunquam me fuisse in angustia, anxietate, scrupulo, dubitatione, timore, aliove malo spiritu quem notabiliter sentirem, quin simul, ac paucis post diebus, invenirem verum remedium in Domino Nostro, dante eo gratiam petendi, pulsandi, quaerendi, et in quo includuntur innumerae gratiae, cognitionem affectuum variorumque spirituum, quos in dies magis magisque cognoscebam. Reliquerat enim mihi Dominus calcaria quaedam quae non me sinebant unquam esse tepidum. Circa igitur judicium et discretionem malorum spirituum aut sensum ciřca res meas aut divinas aut proximi, nunquam, ut dixi, me permisit Dominus decipi, quantum ezistimo; sed in omnibus, et sanctorum Angelorum et Spiritus Sancti illustrationibus, opportuno tempore me liberabat.
units.en: In various ways, then, the Lord taught me, applying a remedy against the many sadnesses arising thence, so that I cannot worthily remember it all; but I can say that I was never in anguish, anxiety, scruple, doubt, fear, or any other evil spirit that I notably felt, without at the same time, or within a few days, finding a true remedy in Our Lord, he giving the grace of asking, knocking, seeking — in which are included innumerable graces, the knowledge of my affections and of the various spirits, which day by day I came to know more and more. For the Lord had left me certain spurs which never allowed me to be lukewarm. As to the judgment and discernment of evil spirits, therefore, and my sense of my own affairs or of divine things or of my neighbour's, the Lord never, as I said, allowed me to be deceived, so far as I judge; but in all things, by the illuminations both of the holy Angels and of the Holy Spirit, he freed me at the fitting time.

units.la: Contigit autem in fine horum quatuor annorum circiter, quod cum me invenissem jam fortem in solo Domino, super propositis in quibus perseveraveram plusquam duos annos, sequendi scilicet Ignitium in vitae paupertate, nec aliud exspectassem quam studiorum meorum, ejusque et magistri Francisci, caelerorumque ejusdem animi et-propositi, finem; hoc inquam tempore, sum profectus visitaturus parentes; fuique cum patre, qui mortua jam matre adhuc vivebat, septem meènses.
units.en: It happened at the end of these four years or so, when I found myself already strong in the Lord alone in the purposes in which I had persevered more than two years — namely of following Ignatius in poverty of life — and awaited nothing but the end of my studies and of his and master Francis's and of the others of the same mind and purpose, that at this time I set out to visit my parents; and I stayed seven months with my father, who was still living, my mother being already dead.

units.la: Anno 1534, aetatis meae vigesimo octavo, rediens Parisios consummandus in studio theologico, accepi Exercitia, initiatusque sum sacris ordinibus, etsi nondum delata esset littera tituli; fecique primum sacrum die sanctae Mariae Magdalenae, advocatae meae omniumque peccatorum'et peccatricum. In hoc capitulo includuntur innumera beneficia, quae Dominus contulit animae meae, vocando ad tantum gradum, dandoque gratias ut essent omnia propter ipsum Filium, non autem aliqua intentione mundana acquirendi honores aut bona temporalia; cum tamen antea, id est, antequam firmarem animum in instituto vitae quod mihi per Ignatium Dominus dedit, essem semper talibus ventis confusus et agitatus: nunc quidem eligendo esse medicum, nunc jurisperitum, nunc regentem, nunc doctorem in theologia, nune clericum sine gradu, aliquando etiam monachum; quibus etiam ventis ego movebar prius, secundum elementum quod erat magis aut minus praedominans, id est, secundum quod reg- nabat haec aut illa affectio. A quibus affectibus me, sicut dictum est, liberans Dominus, sic me sui spiritus consolationibus roboravit, ut omnino deliberarem esse sacerdos, totus suo servitio dedicatus, in hac tam ardua perfectaque vocatione ut non sim futurus unquam dignus in ea Ipsi servire, nec esse in simili electione, tam digna quae a me recognoscatur semper, quomodocumque et quibuscumque potero animae meae et corporis operibus.
units.en: In the year 1534, the twenty-eighth of my age, returning to Paris to be completed in the study of theology, I received the Exercises, and was initiated into holy orders, though the letter of title had not yet been delivered; and I said my first Mass on the day of Saint Mary Magdalene, my advocate and the advocate of all sinners, men and women. In this chapter are included innumerable benefits which the Lord conferred on my soul, calling me to so great a rank, and giving graces that all might be for the sake of the Son himself, and not with any worldly intention of acquiring honours or temporal goods; whereas before — that is, before I settled my mind in the institute of life which the Lord gave me through Ignatius — I was ever confused and tossed by such winds: now choosing to be a physician, now a lawyer, now a regent, now a doctor in theology, now a cleric without a degree, sometimes even a monk; and by these winds I was moved, according to the element which was more or less predominant, that is, according as this or that affection reigned. From these affections, as has been said, the Lord freed me, and so strengthened me with the consolations of his spirit that I resolved altogether to be a priest, wholly dedicated to his service, in this so arduous and perfect a vocation that I shall never be worthy to serve Him in it — nor to stand in such an election, so worthy to be acknowledged by me always, in whatever way and by whatever works of my soul and body I shall be able.

units.la: Hoc eodem anno, die Sanctae Mariae in Augusto, omnes qui tunc eramus in eadem deliberatione, et Exercitati praeter magistram Franciscum, qui cum esset in eadem determinatione, nondum acceperat Exercitia, eodem die, iuquam, ivimus omnes ad Sanctam Mariam Montis Martyrum, et votum fecimus serviendi Deo, proficiscendique die assignato Hierosolymam, et relinquendi parentes et reliqua praeter viaticum; et decrevimus, post reditum inde, ponere nos sub obedicntia Pontificis Romani. Eramus autem, qui hac prima die convenimus, Ignatius, magister Franciscus, ego Faber, magister Bobadilla, magister Laynes, magister Salmeron, magister Simon; Jaius enim ñondum in eodem proposito venerat Lutetiam: magister Joannes vero et Pascasius nondum erant capti. Eodemque die in duobus sequentibus annis, ibamus omnes ad eumdem locum, ad confirmandum eam determinationem; ad quam inveniebamus toties multum augmenti spiritualis. Erant jam nobiscum in his annis magister Jaius, magister Joannes Codurius et magister Pascasias, omnes hi, inquam, erant in ultimo nobiscum. "r Anno 1536, die 145 Novembris, profecti sumus Eutetia omnes novem supradicti, praeter magistrum Ignatium qui fuerat profectus anno cum dimidio ante, iveratque Venetias, ibique nos expectabat; quo et venimus post Nativitatem. In quo itinere tanta nobis Dominus beneficia contulit, ut non possint scribi nunquam. Ibamus pedites; praeterivimus Lotharingiam, et Germaniam ubi erant jam multae civitates Lutheranae sive Zuimglianae, ex quibus Basilea, Constantia, etc. Erat autem tempus hiemale, frigidum valde; quo etiam tempore bellum erat inter Galliam et Hispaniam: ex quibus tamen periculis eripuit nos et praeservavit Dominus. Cum venissemus igitur Venetias sospites, laeti in Spiritu, ingressi sumus xenodochia et hospitalia: quatuor scilicet in hospitale sanctorum Joannis et Pauli, quinque vero in hospitale incurabilium, exspectantes tempus Quadragesimale; ituri tunc Romam postulatum copiam a Pontifice Paulo IH eundi Hierosolymam.
units.en: In this same year, on the day of Saint Mary in August, all of us who were then in the same deliberation, and had made the Exercises — except master Francis, who, though of the same determination, had not yet received the Exercises — on that day, I say, we all went to Saint Mary of the Mount of Martyrs, and made a vow to serve God, and to set out on an appointed day for Jerusalem, leaving parents and everything else except our journey-money; and we decreed that after our return thence we would place ourselves under the obedience of the Roman Pontiff. Those of us who came together on that first day were Ignatius, master Francis, I Faber, master Bobadilla, master Laynez, master Salmerón, master Simón; for Jay had not yet come to Paris in the same purpose, and master Jean and Paschase were not yet won. And on the same day in the two following years we all went to the same place to confirm that determination; and each time we found in it great spiritual increase. In those years there were now with us master Jay, master Jean Codure and master Paschase — all these, I say, were with us at the last. In the year 1536, on the 15th day of November, we set out from Paris, all nine above named, except master Ignatius, who had set out a year and a half before and had gone to Venice, and there awaited us; and we came to him after the Nativity. On this journey the Lord conferred such benefits on us as can never be written. We went on foot; we passed through Lorraine, and through Germany, where there were already many Lutheran or Zwinglian cities, among them Basel, Constance, and others. It was winter time, and very cold; and at that time also there was war between France and Spain: yet from these dangers the Lord snatched and preserved us. When therefore we had come safe to Venice, glad in the Spirit, we entered the hospices and hospitals: four, namely, into the hospital of Saints John and Paul, five into the hospital of the incurables, awaiting the season of Lent; intending then to go to Rome to ask leave of Pope Paul III to go to Jerusalem.

units.la: Anno 1837, post Pascha, habita copia a Pontifice, fuimus profecturi Hierosolymam; et cum non possemus id tum facere, dispersi sumus in diversa loca, volentes tribus mensibus solitarii vivere, omnibus aliis curis expediti; simul etiam ut melius praeparari possent qui nondum erant sacerdotes, disponentes scilicet se ad tantum mystérium. Fuimus autem, Ignatius, ego et magister Laynes, Vicentiae; magister Franciscus et magister. Salmeron duodecim abhinc milliaribus; magister Joannes et Baccalaureus Trevisi; magister Jaius et magister Sımon Bassani; Bobadilla et Pascasius Veronae. Post id vero temporis vocati sumus Romam, ivimusque eo tres qui eramus Vicentiae; erat autem mensis Octobris.
units.en: In the year 1537, after Easter, having obtained leave from the Pontiff, we were to set out for Jerusalem; and since we could not then do so, we dispersed to various places, wishing to live three months in solitude, freed from all other cares; and also that those who were not yet priests might be the better prepared, disposing themselves for so great a mystery. Ignatius, I, and master Laynez were at Vicenza; master Francis and master Salmerón twelve miles away; master Jean and the Bachelor at Treviso; master Jay and master Simón at Bassano; Bobadilla and Paschase at Verona. After that time we were called to Rome, and the three of us who were at Vicenza went there; it was the month of October.

units.la: Anno 1838, cum venissent omnes Nostri Romam, videremusque: tunc non patere viam proficiscendi hoc anno Hierosolymam, accepimus facultatem qua possemus tanquam Apostolici praedicatores ubique praedicare et audire confessiones. Fecit autem nobis diploma cardinalis Neapolitanus qui tunc erat legatus Romae; fecit antem ipsum mense Maii. Velit Dominus ut sciam recognoscere partem meam in tantis beneficiis, in communi nobis ab ipso collatis, toto eo anno, in quo habuimus tantas contradictiones in nostris bonis propositis, transivimusque per tot ignes perturbationum, rnaxime in inquisitione quam procuravimus fieri de nobis; factumque tandem est judicium; non obstantibus quibuslibet magnis favoribus in contrarium. Fuit etiam memorabile beneficium, et quasi totius Societatis fundamentum, quod eodem anno, post habitam sententiam nosirae purgationis, cum nos ipsos praesentaverimus in holocaustum summo pontifici Paulo IlI, ut videret in quo nos possemus servire Christo in aedificationem omnium qui sunt sub potestate sedis apostolicae, in paupertate perpetua, et parati etiam ire ex obedientia sua usque ad extremos Indos; voluit, inquam, Dominus ut nos acceptaret, et de nostris propositis gauderet. Qua-. propter semper ero obligatus, ut quilibet sociorum aliorum, reddere gratias ipsi Domino messis, id est, universae Ecclesiae catholicae, Jesu Ghristo Domino Nostro, qui dignatus est declarare suum beneplacitum per vocem sui vicarii in terra, quae est manifestissima vocatio; et voluit nobis indicare, sibi placere ut serviremus el, seque velle uti nobis amieternun.
units.en: In the year 1538, when all of ours had come to Rome and we saw that the way of going to Jerusalem was not open that year, we received a faculty by which we might, as Apostolic preachers, preach everywhere and hear confessions. The Cardinal of Naples, who was then legate at Rome, made out the diploma for us; he made it in the month of May. May the Lord grant that I know how to acknowledge my share in such great benefits, conferred on us in common by him throughout that year, in which we met such great contradictions in our good purposes and passed through so many fires of disturbance, above all in the inquisition which we ourselves procured to be made concerning us; and judgment was at last given, notwithstanding all the great inducements offered to the contrary. It was also a memorable benefit, and as it were the foundation of the whole Society, that in the same year, after the sentence of our vindication had been obtained, when we presented ourselves as a holocaust to the supreme pontiff Paul III, that he might see in what we could serve Christ for the edification of all who are under the power of the apostolic see, in perpetual poverty, and ready also to go at his obedience even to the farthest Indies — the Lord, I say, willed that he should accept us and rejoice in our purposes. Wherefore I shall always be bound, as shall every one of the other companions, to render thanks to the Lord of the harvest himself, that is, for the whole catholic Church, to Jesus Christ Our Lord, who deigned to declare his good pleasure through the voice of his vicar on earth — which is a most manifest vocation — and willed to signify to us that it pleased him that we should serve him, and that he willed to make use of us for ever.

units.la: Anno 1539, mense Maii, magister Laynes et ego, jussu Pontificis, Roma profecti samus Parmam, cum illustrissimo cardinali S. Angeli; faimusque ibi usque ad mensem Septembris annı 1540. Recordare, anima mea, beneficiorum illic acceptorum a Deo, tantum fruclum operante per nos et dominum Hieronymum Domenechum: dico autem per confessiones, et praedicationes, et Exercitia; necnon etiam eorum quae facta sunt Scisae. Recordare etiam infirmitatis quae.duravit fere tres menses, incipientis a 25 Aprilis annı 1540; in qua re nec oblivisci poteris multum spiritualem fructum quem voluisses facere, secundum cognitionem datam tibi a Domino ut te confortaret in spiritu. Recordare quam multum semper debiturus sis domino Laurentio et domino Maximo, in quorum aedibus fuisti; specialiter. vero ortae inde occasionis. Recordare, ad nunquam perdendam devotionem, festivitatis sanctorum Petri et Pauli, et praecipue sancti Joannis Baptistae, et Visitationis Dominae nostrae, quibus tantum debes; quod tibi nunquam memoria excidet debitum tuum.
units.en: In the year 1539, in the month of May, master Laynez and I, at the command of the Pontiff, set out from Rome for Parma with the most illustrious Cardinal of Sant'Angelo; and we were there until the month of September of the year 1540. Remember, my soul, the benefits there received from God, who worked so much fruit through us and through don Jerónimo Doménech: I mean by confessions, and sermons, and the Exercises; and remember also the things done at Sissa. Remember too the illness which lasted almost three months, beginning from the 25th of April of the year 1540; in which matter you cannot forget the great spiritual fruit you would have wished to accomplish, according to the knowledge given you by the Lord to strengthen you in spirit. Remember how much you must always owe to don Lorenzo and to don Massimo, in whose houses you stayed; and especially the occasion that arose thence. Remember, so as never to lose the devotion, the feast of Saints Peter and Paul, and above all of Saint John the Baptist, and of the Visitation of Our Lady, to which you owe so much that your debt will never fall from your memory.

units.la: Hoc eodem anno profectus sum jussu Pontificis, iturus in Hispanias cum dominoOrtizio, qui vocatus ab Imperatore, me secum duxit in hanc Germaniam, ad colloquia Wormatiae. Accessimus autem 24 Octobris.
units.en: In this same year I set out at the command of the Pontiff, to go to Spain with Doctor Ortiz, who, being called by the Emperor, took me with him into this Germany, to the colloquies at Worms. We arrived on the 24th of October.

units.la: At recordare, anima mea, datae tibi eodem die a Domino Nostro devotionis cujusdam memorabilis usque ad mortem: erat autem de vita Christi Domini mei; incipiendo scilicet eo die per horas canonicas memorari specialiter singulorum dierum Christi ab incarnatione usque ad ascensionem; similiter Dominae Nostrae ab ejus conceptione usque ad mortem; recordare etiam magnae spei conceptae quod id esses perfecturus ante mortem.
units.en: But remember, my soul, the memorable devotion given you by Our Lord on that same day, to last until death: it concerned the life of Christ my Lord; beginning, that is, on that day to commemorate specially, through the canonical hours, the several days of Christ from the incarnation to the ascension, and likewise of Our Lady from her conception to her death; remember also the great hope conceived that you would complete this before death.

units.la: Recordare etiam memorabilium consolationum quas tibi Dominus in orationibus tuis dedit Wormatiae, cognitionis tantae ad inveniendos modos orandi, gratias agendi, a Domino petendi diversas gratias, et tibi, et vivis, et mortuis; orationum etiam quae suggerebantur tibi a Spiritu Sancto pro Germania. Hoc anno instituta est et confirmata bulla nostra Societas Jesu Christi Domini Nostri.
units.en: Remember also the memorable consolations which the Lord gave you in your prayers at Worms: so great a knowledge for finding ways of praying, of giving thanks, of asking from the Lord divers graces for yourself, for the living and for the dead; and the prayers also which were suggested to you by the Holy Spirit for Germany. In this year our Society of Jesus Christ Our Lord was instituted and confirmed by bull.

units.la: Anno 15841, in Januario, profecti sumus Ratisbonam, ubi facta diaeta imperialis. In itinere habuisti magnas consolationes in variis orationibus et contemplationibus, offerebanturque multi novique modi et materiae orandi in itinere. Verbi gratia, accedendo ad locum aliquem, videndo vel audiendo de ipso, accepisti modum orandi, petendique a Domino gratiam ut Archangelus talis regionis habens dominatum nobis foret propitius, cum omnibus Angelis custodibus talium habitationum, utque verus custos et pastor Jesus Christus, qui erat in Ecclesia ejusdem loci, nos juvaret, provideretque omnibus necessitatibus personarum illius loci; verbi gratia, peccatorum existentium in articulo mortis, animarum defunctorum, desolatorum, et quovis alio modo tribulatorum. Cum etiam transirem montes, agros, aut vineas, offerebantur mihi modi orandi pro multiplicatione talium bonorum, agendique gratias vice possessoris, aut postulandi veniam pro illis qui nesciunt in spiritu recognoscere ea bona, neque illud a quo procedunt. Invocabam similiter sanctos quibus curae sunt talia loca, orans ut facerent qüod nesciunt facere. tales habitatores, postulantes gratiam, sanctitatem, pro ipsis gratias agentes, et necessaria ipsis petentes. ı Hoc eodem anno, Ratisbonae recepi alias innumerabiles gratias. Primum quidem quod mihi Dominus dedit operari in suo servitio magnam messem, maxime in confessionibus nobilium curiae Imperatoris, principisque mei ducis Sabaudiae, qui me in suum confessarium elegit; in quibus confessionibus factus est multus fructus, et jactum est semen in alia majora quae inde sunt orta; in Exercitiis etiam magnatum Hispanorum, Italorum et Germanorum, ex quibus fere totum bonum secutum est quod est postea factum in Germania. Suscepi etiam de manu Spiritus Sancti alia notabilia beneficia, ad proprium meum spirituale augmentum, circa novos modos orandi aut contemplandi in posterum, aut in confirmationem (cum clariore cognitione et sensu) consuetorum, ut verbi gratia in Litaniis, mysteriis Christi, et doctrina christiana; petendo diversas gratias, conformiter scilicet ad horum quodlibet, aut veniam; aut gratias agendo Deo illis tribus viis; idem etiam faciendo discurrendo per tres poten- tias, quinque sensus, perque praecipuas corporis partes, et per bona etiam temporalia recepta; et sicut id possum facere pro me, sic etiam pro aliqua persona viva aut mortua, applicando deinde missam ut omnia praedicta melius effectum sortiantur.
units.en: In the year 1541, in January, we set out for Regensburg, where the imperial diet was held. On the journey you had great consolations in various prayers and contemplations, and many new ways and matters of prayer offered themselves on the road. For example, on approaching some place, seeing it or hearing of it, you received a way of praying and asking grace from the Lord, that the Archangel holding dominion over that region might be favourable to us, with all the guardian Angels of the dwellings there; and that the true guardian and shepherd Jesus Christ, who was in the church of that place, might help us and provide for all the needs of the persons of that place — for example, of sinners in the article of death, of the souls of the departed, of the desolate, and of those troubled in any other way. When also I crossed mountains, fields or vineyards, there offered themselves to me ways of praying for the multiplication of such goods, of giving thanks in the owner's stead, or of asking pardon for those who know not how to acknowledge those goods in the spirit, nor him from whom they proceed. I invoked likewise the saints who have such places in their care, praying them to do what the inhabitants of such places know not how to do — asking for them grace and holiness, giving thanks on their behalf, and begging for them the things they need. In this same year, at Regensburg, I received other innumerable graces. First, that the Lord gave me to work a great harvest in his service, above all in the confessions of the nobles of the Emperor's court, and of my prince the Duke of Savoy, who chose me for his confessor; in which confessions much fruit was wrought, and seed was sown for other greater things which have sprung from them; and in the Exercises of great men, Spanish, Italian and German, from which has followed almost all the good that has since been done in Germany. I received also from the hand of the Holy Spirit other notable benefits, for my own spiritual increase, concerning new ways of praying or contemplating thereafter, or in confirmation — with clearer knowledge and feeling — of accustomed ones; as for example in the Litanies, the mysteries of Christ, and christian doctrine; asking divers graces, in conformity with each of these, or pardon; or giving thanks to God by those three ways; doing the same also in running through the three powers, the five senses, and the principal parts of the body, and through the temporal goods received; and as I can do this for myself, so also for some person living or dead, applying then the Mass that all the aforesaid may take better effect.

units.la: Inveneram etiam librum quemdam RatisbonaeBeatae Gertrudis Virginis, in quo scribuntur aliae spirituales devotiones quas ipsa, dum viveret, crescere in dies senserat; unde accepi varios modos orandi, multumque ad id juvamen.
units.en: I had also found at Regensburg a book of the Blessed Virgin Gertrude, in which are written other spiritual devotions which she, while she lived, had felt growing from day to day; from it I received various ways of praying, and much help towards them.

units.la: Hoc eodem anno, mihi Dominus contulit beneficium, ut facerem scilicet in Octava Visitationis Dominae Nostrae solemnia vota meae professionis, mitteremque eam ad magistrum Ignatium, qui erat electus praepositus. Feci autem hanc professionem Ratisbonae, in altari majori Ecclesiae Dominae Nostre quae dicitur Capellae Veteris, cum multa consolatione spirituali et confortatione animae meae, cum abnegatione bonorum jam abnegatorum voluptatumque carnis jam relictarum, cum humilitate inabnegatione et subjectione omnimoda propriae voluntatis ad omnia. Recepi, inquam, novam fortitudinem, et novam cognitio- nem incrementaque magna bonae voluntatis. Sunt ou noo L A ———— u autem vota de castitate, pauperlate, obedientia Praeposito Societatis. Aliud etiam votum obedientiae quo promittimus obedientiam Summo Pontifici circa missiones. Feci autem promissionem hanc coram SS. Sacramento dum communicaturus essem; cujus forma est sequens: Ego, Petrus Faber, promitto et voveo Domino Nostro, Nostre Dominae, et omnibus sañctis coelestibus, servare perpetuam Castitatem, cum eorum auxilio, et perpetuam Paupertatem, et perpetuam Obedientiam Praeposito Societatis Jesu Christi; item servare perpetuam Obedientiam Summo Pontifici in missionibus; et totum hoc promitto facere conformiter ad constitutiones et regulam dictae Societatis. Hanc professionem sic feci; et quia verum est, denuo facio Domino Nostro et Dominae Nostrae, et tibi magistro Ignatio de Loyola, sicut locum tenenti Jesu Christi, in dicta Societate praeposito; subsignavique mea manu, nono Julii 1541. — Petrus Faber.
units.en: In this same year the Lord conferred on me the benefit of making, on the octave of the Visitation of Our Lady, the solemn vows of my profession, and of sending it to master Ignatius, who had been elected superior. I made this profession at Regensburg, at the high altar of the church of Our Lady which is called the Old Chapel, with much spiritual consolation and strengthening of my soul; with renunciation of goods already renounced and of pleasures of the flesh already left; with humility, in the denial and entire subjection of my own will in all things. I received, I say, new strength, new knowledge, and great increase of good will. The vows are of chastity, of poverty, and of obedience to the Superior of the Society; and another vow of obedience, by which we promise obedience to the Supreme Pontiff as regards missions. I made this promise before the Most Holy Sacrament, as I was about to communicate; and its form is as follows: I, Peter Faber, promise and vow to Our Lord, to Our Lady, and to all the saints of heaven, to keep, with their help, perpetual Chastity, perpetual Poverty, and perpetual Obedience to the Superior of the Society of Jesus Christ; likewise to keep perpetual Obedience to the Supreme Pontiff as regards missions; and all this I promise to do in conformity with the constitutions and rule of the said Society. This profession I so made; and because it is true, I make it anew to Our Lord and Our Lady, and to you, master Ignatius de Loyola, as holding the place of Jesus Christ, superior in the said Society; and I have signed with my own hand, the ninth of July 1541. — Peter Faber.

units.la: Eodem anno, 27 Julii, profecti sumus Ratisbona D. Ortizius et ego, cum tota ejus familia, transivimusque per patriam meam et Galliam, ubi fuimusdetenti et incarcerati septem dies. Quare noli unquam oblivisci magna beneficia Domini Nostri, qui nos liberavit gratia sua a detinentibus nos, deditque gratiam conversandi cum illis et fructificandi cum illorum animabus, ita ut etiam dux mihi confiteretur; factumque est ut bona opera nostra a Domino data erga totum mundum, non fuerint captivata, offuscata aut perturbata circa ipsos. Nihilominus habui aliquas tentationes diffidentiae et timoris, non exituros nos inde tam cito, nec sine magnis expensis domini Ortizii; in quibus etiam recepi contrariam a Deo medicinalem consolationem, in omni bona spe omnium fere quae contigerunt in nostra liberatione.
units.en: In the same year, on the 27th of July, Doctor Ortiz and I set out from Regensburg with his whole household, and passed through my native country and through France, where we were detained and imprisoned seven days. Wherefore never forget the great benefits of Our Lord, who by his grace freed us from those who held us, and gave grace to converse with them and to bear fruit with their souls, so that even the captain made his confession to me; and it came to pass that our good works, given by the Lord towards the whole world, were not taken captive, darkened or disturbed as regards them. Nevertheless I had some temptations of distrust and fear that we should not get out so soon, nor without great expense to Doctor Ortiz; in which also I received from God the contrary, healing consolation, in good hope of almost everything that came to pass in our deliverance.

units.la: Die sanctae Elizabeth reginae Hungariae, habui magnam devotionem, oblatis mihi septem personis cum desiderio habendi eas in memoria mea, ad orandum pro ipsis, non respiciendo ad eorum defectus: erat autem summus Pontifex, Imperator, rex Angliae, Lutherus, Turca, Bucerus, Philippus Melanchthon. Occasio autem fuit quia.senseram in anima judicari praediċtos a multis; unde oriebatur mihi quaedam sancta compassio, proveniens ex bono spiritu. Rodem die promiši Christo, fecique votum non accipiendi unquam aliquid pro confes- sionibus, missis, aut praedicationibus; non vivendi ex reditu, nisi offerretur aliquo modo cui non possem resistere cum bona conscientia; et hujus voti multum oportet recordari, tanquam insignis beneficii Christi Domini Nostri, qui me adjuvat hoc modo ad melius servandum paupertatis * votum. } Die Praesentationis, cum auxilio Spirits totius sanctimoniae et perfection?s castitatis, et ad melius servandum votum castitatis, mihi dedit Deus quemdam sensum cujusdam spiritualis reverentiae erga illam purissimam infantem Dominam Nostram; pro cujus reverentiae testimonio et memoria, proposui abstinere in aeternum cavereque ne unquam ingeram faciem meam cuivis parvulo aut parvulae, qualibet etiam licita intentione; tantum abest ut id mihi debeat contingere cum personis grandioribus.
units.en: On the day of Saint Elizabeth queen of Hungary I had a great devotion, seven persons being set before me with the desire of keeping them in my memory, to pray for them without regard to their defects: they were the supreme Pontiff, the Emperor, the king of England, Luther, the Turk, Bucer, and Philip Melanchthon. The occasion was that I had felt in my soul that these men were judged by many; whence arose in me a certain holy compassion, proceeding from a good spirit. On the same day I promised Christ, and made a vow, never to accept anything for confessions, Masses or sermons, and not to live on fixed revenue, unless it were offered in some way which I could not with good conscience resist; and this vow must be much remembered, as a signal benefit of Christ Our Lord, who helps me in this way to keep better the vow of poverty. On the day of the Presentation, with the help of the Spirit of all holiness and perfection of chastity, and for the better keeping of the vow of chastity, God gave me a certain feeling of spiritual reverence towards that most pure child Our Lady; in testimony and memory of which reverence I resolved to abstain for ever, and to take care never to thrust my face upon any little boy or girl, with whatever even lawful intention — so far ought that to be from happening to me with grown persons.

units.la: Hoc eodem anno, ingrediens Hispaniam, habui notabiles devotiones et spirituales sensus super invocatione principalium Archangelorum, Angelorum custodum, Sanctoramque Hispaniae. Specialiter habui magnum affectum ad sanctum Narcis- sum qui est Gerundae, ad: sanctam Eulaliam quae ee m aa est Barcinone, ad Nostram Dominam Montis Serrati, ad Nostram Dominam del Pilar, ad sanctum Jacobum, sanctum Isidorum, sanctum Ildefonsum, ad sanctos martyres Justum et Pastorem, ad Dominam Nostram de Guadalupe, ad sanctam Encratidem Caesaraugustae, eos rogando omnes ut vellent acceptare meum iter in Hispaniam, et me" juvare suis orationibus ad faciendum aliquem bonum fructum; sicuti ctum est, magis eorum intercessionibus quam mea diligentia. Illud etiam proposui facere in quolibet regno et principatu, commendare me scilicet principalibus Angelis, Archangelis, Angelis custodibus, Sanctisque quos scirem principaliter honorari in tali provincia aut dominatione; unde etiam mihi confirmata est devotio quorumdam sanctorum qui celebrantur in Italia, quos expressius habeo in meo breviario Romano; aliorumque quos in Germania vidi celebrari; specialiter trium Regum et undecim millium Virginum, particulariter autem sanctae Ursulae et sanctae Pinnosae, cujus caput cum eadem sagitta qua transfixum fuit meis propriis oculis vidi in quodam monasterio Sancti Benedicti; sancti etiam Helveti in Moremberg et sancti Maximini Treviris.
units.en: In this same year, entering Spain, I had notable devotions and spiritual feelings in invoking the principal Archangels, the guardian Angels, and the Saints of Spain. In particular I had great affection towards Saint Narcissus, who is at Girona; towards Saint Eulalia, who is at Barcelona; towards Our Lady of Montserrat, Our Lady del Pilar, Saint James, Saint Isidore, Saint Ildephonsus, the holy martyrs Justus and Pastor, Our Lady of Guadalupe, and Saint Engratia at Zaragoza; praying them all to be pleased to accept my journey into Spain and to help me by their prayers to bear some good fruit — as was done, more by their intercessions than by my diligence. I resolved also to do the like in every kingdom and principality: to commend myself, that is, to the principal Angels, Archangels, guardian Angels, and to the Saints whom I should know to be chiefly honoured in that province or dominion; whence also was confirmed in me the devotion of certain saints who are celebrated in Italy, whom I have more expressly in my Roman breviary; and of others whom I saw celebrated in Germany, especially of the three Kings and of the eleven thousand Virgins, and particularly of Saint Ursula and of Saint Pinnosa, whose head, with the same arrow by which it was pierced, I saw with my own eyes in a certain monastery of Saint Benedict; and of Saint Helvetius at Moremberg, and of Saint Maximin at Trier.

units.la: In Gallia etiam accepi devotionem ad sanctam Genovefam, sanctumque Marcellum episcopum Parisiensem, quorum corpora sunt civitati in magnum patrocinium; ad sanctum etiam Dionysium Areopagitam, cujus corpus est in Ecclesia sancti Dionysii in Gallia. Item Narbonae ad sanctum Paulum Sergium, Massiliae ad sanctam Mariam Magdalenam, Marthamque ejus sororem et ad, sanctum Lazarum. In Sabaudia etiam habui devotionem, quam non oportet omittere, ad sanctum Brunonem, fundatorem Carthusiae, ad sanctum Amedeum qui est Nantuae, prope quam fuimus incarcerati; ad fratrem Joannem de Parcio, et ad fratrem Joannem Bourĝğeois, et ad meum preceptorem magistrum Petrum Veliardum, quos etsi non canonizatos ego sanctos existimo; ad sanctum etiam Claudium qui ést canonizatus. Alios plures sanctos notabam hoc tempore, accipiens eos in advocatos, proponebamque nunquam eorum oblivisci, sed invocare eos pro me, pro vivis et mortuis, et praecipue pro illis qui vel vivunt vel mortui sunt in locis in quibus tales sancti mortui, nati vel conversati sunt, sive in Europa, Africa, Asia, aut in quibus- vis insulis. In talibus sensi magnam devotionem multumque spiritum ad eas devotiones prosequendas et me in ipsis dilatandum, invocando etiam quandoque Apostolos aliosque sanctos qui fructum fecerant in diversis mundi partibus, ut spiritualem curam susciperent Societatis nostrae, omniumque sodalium existentium in talibus terris aut provinciis, ad quas ipsi applicarunt aliquando intentionem suae charitatis. His soleo uti, quoties orare volo specialiter pro aliquo loco aut regno, invocando scilicet eos sanctos et angelos qui habent et habuerunt specialem curam talium animarum vivorum aut mortuorum.
units.en: In France also I received a devotion towards Saint Geneviève and Saint Marcel, bishop of Paris, whose bodies are a great patronage to the city; towards Saint Denys the Areopagite also, whose body is in the church of Saint-Denis in France. Likewise at Narbonne towards Saint Paul Sergius; at Marseille towards Saint Mary Magdalene, Martha her sister, and Saint Lazarus. In Savoy also I had a devotion, which must not be passed over, towards Saint Bruno, founder of the Carthusians; towards Saint Amadeus, who is at Nantua, near which we were imprisoned; towards brother Jean de Parcio, and brother Jean Bourgeois, and my teacher master Pierre Veillard, whom, though not canonized, I hold to be saints; and towards Saint Claude, who is canonized. Many other saints I noted at this time, taking them for advocates, and resolved never to forget them, but to invoke them for myself, for the living and the dead, and chiefly for those who live or have died in the places where such saints died, were born, or dwelt, whether in Europe, Africa, Asia, or in any islands. In such things I felt great devotion and much spirit for pursuing these devotions and enlarging myself in them, invoking also at times the Apostles and other saints who bore fruit in divers parts of the world, that they might take spiritual care of our Society and of all its members who are in such lands or provinces, to which they themselves once applied the intention of their charity. These I am wont to use whenever I wish to pray specially for some place or kingdom, invoking, that is, those saints and angels who have and have had special care of such souls, living or dead.

units.la: Circa tempus hoc incepi quamdam devotionem datam mihi a Domino, ad melius recitandum horas canonicas, dicendi scilicet inter Psalmos, ad renovationem spiritus, brevem hanc orationem quam susceperam ex Evangelio: Pater caelestis, da mihi spiritum bonum! in quo sensi varias utilitates. Aliam devotionem accepi praeponendam singulis septem horis canonicis, applicando unam quamque alicui intentioni, et specialiter rebus attentione dignis. Est autem id dicere decies: Jesus, Maria! in principio cujuslibet horae; ut sic habeam occasionem reducendi ın mentem de- cem haec: 1° honorem Domini Nostri; 2° gloriam Sanctorum ejus; 3° bonorum memoriam, ut crescant in qualibet intentione bona quam contingat habere in illa hora; 4° eorum qui in ea hora fuerint in peccato mortali, ut scilicet illis prosit tale officium, ne perseverent in peccato, sed convertantur; 5° rerum catholicarum, ut in dies crescant; 6° pacis universalis intersprincipes Christianos et Catholicos; 7° eorum qui in tali hora fuerint in aliqua tribulatione corporali; 8° positorum in tribulatione et afflictione spirituali; 9° existentium in articulo mortis; 10° existentium in purgatorio, ut in illa hora et ea quae correspondet officio quod tunc recito, habeant aliquod levamen a paeoenis suis et laboribus.
units.en: About this time I began a certain devotion given me by the Lord for the better recitation of the canonical hours: namely, to say between the Psalms, for the renewal of the spirit, this short prayer which I had taken from the Gospel: Heavenly Father, give me a good spirit! — in which I felt various profits. Another devotion I received, to be set before each of the seven canonical hours, applying each hour to some intention, and specially to things worthy of attention. It is to say ten times, Jesus, Mary! at the beginning of each hour, so as to have occasion of bringing to mind these ten things: first, the honour of Our Lord; second, the glory of his Saints; third, the memory of good people, that they may grow in every good intention they may happen to have in that hour; fourth, of those who in that hour are in mortal sin, that such an office may profit them, so that they may not persevere in sin but be converted; fifth, of the interests of the catholic faith, that they may grow from day to day; sixth, of universal peace among Christian and Catholic princes; seventh, of those who in that hour are in some bodily tribulation; eighth, of those placed in spiritual tribulation and affliction; ninth, of those in the article of death; tenth, of those in purgatory, that in that hour, and in the hour corresponding to the office I then recite, they may have some relief from their pains and labours.

units.la: Nota hic, anima mea, ut te Dominus a tot tantisque perturbationibus spiritus liberaverit, et ab angustiis et tentationibus quas sustinebas super defectibus tuis, super agitationibus spiritus fornicationis, superque negligentiis faciendi fructum. Recordare quam claras acceperis cogitationes, occasione talium tentationum, et quod nullam fere - habueris notabilem tentationem, in qua non fueris consolata, non solum cum clara cognitione, sed etiam cum spiritu, contrario tristitiis, timoribus, pusillanimitatibus aut affectionibus inordinatarum prosperitatum: dante Domino tantam charitatem tamque puros sensus in remedia spiritus fornicationis, et media ad puritatem munditiamque cordis et carnis; remedia etiam et media contra mundum et spiritum ipsius contraque malignos spiritus.
units.en: Note here, my soul, how the Lord has freed you from so many and so great disturbances of spirit, and from the anguishes and temptations you used to suffer over your defects, over the agitations of the spirit of fornication, and over your negligences in bearing fruit. Remember what clear thoughts you received on the occasion of such temptations, and that you had almost no notable temptation in which you were not consoled — not only with clear knowledge, but also with a spirit contrary to sadnesses, fears, faint-heartednesses, or affections of inordinate prosperity: the Lord giving so great charity and such pure feelings for the remedies against the spirit of fornication, and means towards purity and cleanness of heart and flesh; remedies also and means against the world and its spirit, and against the malignant spirits.

units.la: Recepisti, etiam a Domino magnum desiderium cum spe, ut esses habitaculum Spiritus Sancti, et ne Spiritus maligni habitarent in spiritibus vitalibus aut animalibus corporis tui. Cujus gratia, solebam facere varios discursus per potentias, sensus, principaliaque membra totius corporis, exorans Dominum ut omnino dignaretur me mundare. Super virtutem etiam sobrietatis, castitatis et diligentiae, et ex altera parte, humilitatis, patientiae et charitatis, habui multa dona in cognitione et sensu; dante Domino multas orationes circa ipsas, cum multis affectibus fidei et spei. Sit ipse benedictus in saecula saeculorum! Amen.
units.en: You received also from the Lord a great desire, with hope, to be a dwelling-place of the Holy Spirit, and that malignant spirits might not dwell in the vital or animal spirits of your body. For which grace I used to make various rounds through the powers, the senses, and the principal members of the whole body, beseeching the Lord that he would deign to cleanse me altogether. Concerning the virtue also of sobriety, of chastity and of diligence, and on the other side of humility, patience and charity, I had many gifts in knowledge and feeling; the Lord giving many prayers about them, with many affections of faith and hope. Blessed be he for ever and ever! Amen.

units.la: Super doctrina catholica conformiter ad Ecclesiam romanam, habui innumeras. visitationes: super illius constitutionibus et ceremoniis; super piis peregrinationibus; votis, jejuniis, cultu Sanctorum et Sanctarum, Angelorumque et Dominae Nostrae, atque animarum purgatoril, etc.; sentiendo in omnibus multum spiritum, multamque devotionem in talium approbatione.
units.en: Concerning catholic doctrine in conformity with the Roman Church I had innumerable visitations: concerning her constitutions and ceremonies; concerning pious pilgrimages, vows, fasts, the veneration of the Saints, men and women, of the Angels and of Our Lady, and of the souls in purgatory, and the rest; feeling in all these much spirit and much devotion in the approval of such things.

units.la: Anno 1542, mense Januarii!, profectus sum ab Hispania, reversusque sum in Germaniam jussu Pontificis; in quo itinere Dominus mthi innumera contulit beneficia, maxime adimplendo praecipuum desiderium temporale quod sentiebam, scilicet dari mihi aliquam societatem ad ejus servitium (fuerunt autem magistri Joannes Arragonius et Alvarus Alphonsus); liberando etiam nos in tam longo periculosoque itinere ab omnibus malis temporalibus, contra omnem spem humanam; ut in Catalonia a latronibus et carceribus; in Gallia a militibus; ingredientes Helvetiam in finibus Sabaudiae, ab haereticis; in Allemania ab infestationibus et contagionibus; denique, quod omnibus majus est, a tentationibus divisivis, id est, spiritus divisionis.
units.en: In the year 1542, in the month of January, I set out from Spain and returned to Germany at the command of the Pontiff; on which journey the Lord conferred on me innumerable benefits, above all by fulfilling the chief temporal desire I felt — namely, that some companionship should be given me for his service (they were masters Juan de Aragón and Álvaro Alfonso); and by freeing us, on so long and dangerous a journey, from all temporal evils, against all human hope: as in Catalonia from robbers and prisons; in France from soldiers; entering Switzerland, on the borders of Savoy, from heretics; in Germany from infestations and contagions; and finally — what is greater than all — from divisive temptations, that is, from the spirit of division.

units.la: Multos sensus amoris et spei super haereticis et toto mundo mihi Dominus dedit in hoc itinere, dederatque antea; specialiter autem devotionem quamdam, usque ad mortem continuandam, cum fide, spe et charitate, circa bonum harum septem civitatum, scilicet Wittembergae in Saxonia, praecipuae civitatis Sarmatiae, cujus nomen ignoro, Gebennae in Sabaudiae ducatu, Constantinopolis in Graecia, Antiochiae, Hierosolymae, Alexandriae in Africa. Hoc proposui semper habere in memoria, cum spe quod ego vel aliquis de Societate Jesu Christi tandem esset facturus sacrum in dictis omnibus civitatibus.
units.en: Many feelings of love and hope concerning the heretics and the whole world the Lord gave me on this journey, and had given before; in particular a certain devotion, to be continued until death, with faith, hope and charity, for the good of these seven cities: Wittenberg in Saxony; the chief city of Sarmatia, whose name I do not know; Geneva in the duchy of Savoy; Constantinople in Greece; Antioch; Jerusalem; and Alexandria in Africa. This I resolved to keep always in memory, with the hope that I, or someone of the Society of Jesus Christ, would at last say Mass in all the said cities.

sections.arg: In hoc Memoriali fuse enarrat Auctor sensa et lumina quibus a Deo donatus est a mense Junio anni 1542 usque ad mensem Julium anni 1543.

units.la: In octava corporis Christi, cum desiderarem conversationem habere cum Decano Spirae ad utilitatem ejus in Exercitiis spiritualibus, nec possem opere consequi quod volebam, nisi sola oratione; habui quamdam devotionem quam non hactenus senseram, orandi scilicet primo Patrem ipsius coeaelestem quasi qui ambiat; secundo ejus Matrem et Dominam, Matrem Dei; tertio ejus magistrum tanquam paedagogum Angelum custodem; quarto Sanctos et Sanctas ad ipsum specia- liter affectos ad modum fratrum et sororum. Haec mihi videbatur bona ambitio ad captandam cujuslibet amicitiam; offerebaturque mihi recitandum pro prima dicta persona, Pater noster > pro secunda, Ave Maria; pro tertia, Deus qui miro ordine Angelorum, etc.; pro quarto autem, Omnes Sancti tui, quaesumus, Domine, etc: Offerebaturque tanquam necessarium valde ad habendam cujuslibet benevolentiam, ultra ea quae per opera fieri possunt, devotionem habere ad omnes Angelos custodes, qui nobis possunt praeparare personas multis modis, et violentiam inimicorum tentationesque reprimere.
units.en: On the octave of the Body of Christ, when I desired to have conversation with the Dean of Speyer for his profit in the spiritual Exercises, and could not obtain by action what I wished, but only by prayer, I had a certain devotion which I had not felt until then: namely, to pray first to his heavenly Father, as one might court a man's father; secondly to his Mother and Lady, the Mother of God; thirdly to his teacher, the guardian Angel, as to his tutor; fourthly to the Saints, men and women, specially attached to him, after the manner of brothers and sisters. This seemed to me a good ambition for winning anyone's friendship; and it was suggested to me to recite for the first person named the Our Father; for the second, the Hail Mary; for the third, the collect 'O God, who in wonderful order the Angels...'; and for the fourth, 'All thy Saints, we beseech thee, O Lord...'. And it was suggested as something very necessary, for gaining anyone's good will beyond what can be done by works, to have devotion to all the guardian Angels, who can prepare persons for us in many ways, and restrain the violence and the temptations of our enemies.

units.la: Nota hic, anima mea, et recordare quod Dominus tibi, praeterito tempore, dederit multam cognitionem super tentationibus et molestiis daemoniorum; unde aliquando fecisti orationes et discursus circa Sanctos, aut circa mysteria Christi, vel doctrinam christianam, aut circa membra corporis tui, etc., etc.; petens gratiam contra inimicum, et specialiter contra spiritum for- nicationis, ut virtus' ejus amplius non esset in lumbis tuis, sed ejiceretur ex omni loco ubi esset spiritus. vitalis vel animalis tui Corpo- ris; item ab intellectu, memoria et voluntate; Enty item a locis ubi esses. Idque orabas cum multa devotione spiritus, multaque spe quod sic futurum esset ante tuam mortem; et suggerebat Spiritus Sanctus ut orares multum suam divinam bonitatem et puritatem, ut habitaret in corpore tuo sicut in templo suo, et in spiritu etiam tuo; atque ut Angeli possent invenire habitationem corporalem in spiritibus corporis tui, expellendo inimicos. Pro hac autem munditie inveniebas magnam spem, statuens apud te, sicut a multo ante tempore feceras, servare multam temperantiam in cibo et potu, in omnibusque actibus exterioribus cum modestia; videns esse valde necessarium, ne mali spiritus tantam habeant potestatem ad habitandum vel ad movendum carnem tuam sive spiritum, quod non inveniant cor nec cibo gravatüm nec potu. Benedic igitur, anima mea, Domino, pro tanto desiderio tibi dato, cum tali voluntate corporalis sanctimoniae spiritualisque munditiae; et quod tanto tempore dederit tibi sentire stimulos necessarios ad virtutem castitatis corporis et spiritus, cum spe illam obtinendi. Ad proprium etiam Angelum cum'essem specialiter devotus, sensi multa auxilia, orans ut me defen- deret a meo malo spiritu, specialiterque a spiritu fornicationis.
units.en: Note here, my soul, and remember that the Lord in time past gave you much knowledge concerning the temptations and vexations of the demons; whence you sometimes made prayers and rounds among the Saints, or the mysteries of Christ, or christian doctrine, or the members of your own body, and so forth; asking grace against the enemy, and specially against the spirit of fornication, that his power might no longer be in your loins, but that he might be cast out from every place where there is a vital or animal spirit of your body; likewise from the intellect, the memory and the will; likewise from the places where you might be. And you prayed this with much devotion of spirit, and much hope that so it would be before your death; and the Holy Spirit prompted you to pray much to his divine goodness and purity, that he might dwell in your body as in his temple, and in your spirit also; and that the Angels might find a bodily habitation in the spirits of your body, driving out the enemies. And for this cleanness you found great hope, resolving with yourself, as you had done long before, to keep much temperance in food and drink, and modesty in all outward acts; seeing it to be very necessary, lest the evil spirits have such power to dwell in or to move your flesh or spirit, that they should find the heart weighed down neither by food nor by drink. Bless the Lord, therefore, my soul, for so great a desire given you, with such a will to bodily holiness and spiritual cleanness; and that for so long a time he has given you to feel the spurs needful for the virtue of chastity of body and spirit, with hope of obtaining it. Being specially devoted also to my own Angel, I felt many helps, praying him to defend me from my own evil spirit, and specially from the spirit of fornication.

units.la: Die sancti Joannis Baptistae, habui sensique in meo spiritu notabilem sensum magnitudinis sancti Joannis; sensique magnum dolorem spiritualem quod in hac Allemania non tanti fieret, neque tantum curaretur ejus solemnitas, quantum in aliis regionibus; ideoque desideravi cum multo affectu posse movere eos qui auctoritatem habent praelaturamque spiritualem, ut fieret festum hoc solemnius. Die sanctorum Joannis et Pauli, habui cognitionem quamdam et adjutorium ad melius dicendum officium. Erat autem, verbi gratia, quod notandi essent quatuor limites et termini, extra quos non esset exeundum tempore officii: 4° locus ubi recitaretur; 2° personae aut sancti occurrentes in tali oratione; 3° verba, et 4 opera intervenientia in tali officio. Est id utile incipientibus ad melius resistendum memoriae, intellectui, sensibus aut' desideriis, per alia loca, personas, colloquia aut opera occurrentia dispersis; et similiter de tempore. Aliud etiam adjutorium notavi, quod antea expertus fueram saepius ad idem utile esse: in eo est autem quod antequam dicatur officium, jam a longe percipiatur quaelibet pars principalis talis officii, aut horae, cum magno desiderio sistendi in ipsis; sicut si quis sibi ipsi diceret: Tu debes recitare: 1° illum psalmum; &% illum; 3 illum, etc.; et cum tali consideratione ingredi, officiumque incipere. Item, finito officio, procurare etiam ut non exeat inde spiritus saltem desiderium, scilicet perseverandi quantum poteris in reflexione, ita ut non exeat foras totus homo. Prodest etiam occupatum in aliis, ante sive post officium, procurare saepius ' ex iis negotiis quantumcumque poteris distrahi, cogitando et desiderando illa quae faciunt pertinentque ad officium dictum vel dicendum. Qui enim non desiderat orare, nisi quando adest tempus ad id destinatum, certum est eum tune non posse talem habere devotionem, nisi miraculose fundatam. Quapropter necesse est determinata esse assignataque tempora ad orandum, saepiusque in memoriam reduci, cum desiderio, perseverantia et timore, ne forte contingat deficere; et post officium, cum dolore perseveranti, si forte defeceris, quod non bene dixeris; ita ut talis tristitia et dolor sine interruptione duret usque ad venturum exercitium. Sitque dolor non solum propter distractiones tibi displicentes, sed qui procedat ex amore et affectu verborum Dei et materiarum orationis. Multi enim dolent quod non habeant devotionem in oratione, non tam ex amore ipsius orationis, id est Dei et Sanctorum, et verborum ipsius orationis, quam ex odio et timore distractivarum cogitationum, aut desideriorum aliarum rerum temporalium etiam necessariarum, aut rerum malarum; aut etiam bonarum, sed non spectantium ad propositum: haec tamen via bona est ad amorem; quo adepto, quilibet desiderat attentionem ad res ipsas; et non solum attentionem mentis, sed etiam intentionem affectus, propter ipsum Deum et verba ipsius, et opera quae sunt in tali officio, licet etiam non sentiret ullam distractionem ad res alienas. Hoc eodem tempore, infra octavas sancti Joannis Baptistae, notavi quoddam valde necessarium ad ordinandum proprias res, desideria et curas, et breviter rationem omnem vitae propriae, et ad obtinendam quietudinem in spirifualibus et corpo- ralibus occupationibus. Fuitque ad propositum illius auctoritatis Jesu Christi: Nolite curare de crastino; quod scilicet in desideriis et curis spiritualibus convenit, quoad fieri possit, non curare de crastino; sed quod sic debeat homo disponere horas suas tempusque illius diei, ut non se permittat divagari, cogitare, aut curare, cum gaudio vel tristitia, de eo quod postea succedere debet; divisa enim cura in tam multorûm tamque longinquorum cogitationibus, non potest praesens bene fieri, nec ad id tam perfecte attendi, quantum posset non disperso spiritu.
units.en: On the day of Saint John the Baptist I had and felt in my spirit a notable sense of the greatness of Saint John; and I felt great spiritual grief that in this Germany he is not made so much of, nor his solemnity so much cared for, as in other regions; and so I desired with much affection to be able to move those who have authority and spiritual prelacy, that this feast might be kept more solemnly. On the day of Saints John and Paul I had a certain understanding and help towards saying the office better. It was, for instance, that four limits and bounds should be noted, outside which one should not go during the office: first, the place where it is recited; second, the persons or saints occurring in that prayer; third, the words; and fourth, the works involved in that office. This is useful for beginners, the better to resist memory, understanding, senses or desires when they scatter to other places, persons, conversations or works; and likewise as to time. Another help I noted, which I had often found useful before for the same end: it is that before the office is said, each principal part of the office or hour should be perceived from afar, with a great desire of dwelling in them; as if one should say to himself: You are to recite, first, this psalm; second, that one; third, that one; and so enter with this consideration, and begin the office. Likewise, when the office is finished, to take care that the spirit — at least the desire — does not depart from it: persevering, that is, as much as you can in reflection, so that the whole man does not go out of doors. It profits also one who is occupied in other things, before or after the office, to contrive often to be drawn away from those affairs as much as possible, thinking on and desiring the things which make for and belong to the office said or to be said. For he who does not desire to pray except when the time appointed for it is at hand, certainly cannot then have such devotion, unless it be miraculously given.
