Wherefore it is necessary that fixed times be determined and assigned for prayer, and be often called to mind, with desire, perseverance and fear, lest perhaps you fail; and after the office, with persevering sorrow, if you have perhaps failed and not said it well; so that such sadness and sorrow may last without interruption until the exercise to come. And let the sorrow be not only for the distractions that displease you, but such as proceeds from love and affection for the words of God and the matters of prayer. For many grieve that they have no devotion in prayer, not so much from love of prayer itself — that is, of God and the Saints and the very words of the prayer — as from hatred and fear of distracting thoughts, or of desires of other temporal things, even necessary ones, or of evil things, or even of good things which do not belong to the purpose. Yet this way is a good one towards love; and when love is gained, everyone desires attention to the things themselves — and not only attention of mind but intention of affection, for the sake of God himself and his words and the works which are in that office, even if he should feel no distraction at all towards other things. At this same time, within the octave of Saint John the Baptist, I noted something very necessary for ordering one's own affairs, desires and cares — in short, the whole plan of one's own life — and for obtaining quiet in spiritual and bodily occupations. It bore on that saying of Jesus Christ: Take no thought for the morrow; namely, that in spiritual desires and cares it is fitting, so far as may be, to take no thought for the morrow; but that a man should so dispose his hours and the time of that day as not to allow himself to wander, to think, or to care, with joy or sadness, about what is to follow afterwards; for when care is divided among the thoughts of so many and such distant things, the present cannot be done well, nor attended to as perfectly as it could be by a spirit not dispersed.

units.la: Quaedam se mihi obtulit petitio pariter, a sanctissima Trinitate postulanda: ut scilicet mihi gratiam daret, quando contigerit me habere bonum aliquod desiderium, opus, aut contemplationem, etc.; quod omnes'potentiae meae sic concurrerent, ut in talibus etiam non impedirer; contra vero quando contingeret earum aliquam dominari, quod nunquam aliae concurrerent, sed potius impedirent.
units.en: A certain petition likewise offered itself to me, to be asked of the most holy Trinity: that he would give me grace, whenever I should happen to have some good desire, work, or contemplation, that all my powers might so concur that even in such things I should not be hindered; and on the contrary, whenever one of them should happen to dominate wrongly, that the others might never concur with it, but rather hinder it.

units.la: Die Visitationis beatae Mariae, circa propositum humilitatis quam debemus majoribus nostris, et habere convenit ad omnes creaturas, amore Domini Nostri, habui sensum quemdam bonum super humilitate Dominae Nostrae, quae ivit ad serviendum cognatae suae sanctae Elisabeth, ei se humiliando, cum esset mater Praecursoris Domini Nostri Jesu Christi.
units.en: On the day of the Visitation of blessed Mary, concerning the purpose of humility which we owe to those set over us, and which it is fitting to have towards all creatures for the love of Our Lord, I had a certain good feeling about the humility of Our Lady, who went to serve her kinswoman Saint Elizabeth, humbling herself before her, though she was the mother of the Precursor of Our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Hic habui magnum desiderium in spiritu meo, ut omnes existentes aliquo modo in obedientia -exercerentur usque ad obtinendam perfectam humilitatem, patientiam et charitatem; ad supportandum et honorandum majores suos, bonos et malos; respicientes et affectantes solum bonum' et non quod malum est: quantoque superior minus bonus esse videretur in suo gradu, tanto magis inferior perficeretur in suo, qui est esse servum obedientem, diligentem et fidelem, timore et amore Domini Nostri. Merentur enim, qui sic fuerunt grati Deo servi, habere tandem bonos dominos, et non e conira; scilicet postquam ipsi etiam desierunt esse subditi: tunc neque talis dominus malus meretur quod Dominus Noster det ipsi alios meliores servos ac subditos; neque subditi jam alienati merentur meliores dominos.
units.en: Here I had a great desire in my spirit that all who stand in any way under obedience might be exercised until they gained perfect humility, patience and charity, so as to bear with and honour those over them, good and bad alike, looking to and desiring only what is good, and not what is evil; and that the less good a superior might seem in his rank, the more the inferior might be perfected in his — which is to be an obedient, loving and faithful servant, in the fear and love of Our Lord. For those who have been servants pleasing to God in this way deserve at last to have good masters, and not the reverse; that is, when they too have ceased to be true subjects, then neither does such a bad master deserve that Our Lord should give him other, better servants and subjects, nor do subjects already estranged deserve better masters.

units.la: Die quodam intra octavas Visitationis Virginis Mariae, ego sensi quaedam intima desideria, in quibus petebam a Deo Patre ut esset mihi, licet indigno, pater speciali modo, ita ut me efficeret filium suum obedientem et agnoscentem. A Filio Domino Nostro petebam ut dignaretur mihi esse in dominum, et efficere gratia sua ut ego deinceps sim ipsi in servum, cum omni timore. A Spiritu Sancto ego petebam ut ipse esset mihi in magistrum, docens me esse discipulum ejus. Pro his autem impetrandis, cum magna devotione implorabam auxilium et intercessionem electae filiae Dei Patris, ancillae Jesu Christi ac Matris, et ee CN NE ee Ed paS i i + ki. w e.. discipulae Spiritus Sancti, quae fuit Virgo Maria, cui facile est apud Deum omnia supra dicta obtinere.
units.en: On a certain day within the octave of the Visitation of the Virgin Mary I felt certain intimate desires, in which I asked of God the Father that he would be a father to me, unworthy though I am, in a special way, so as to make me his obedient and grateful son. Of the Son, Our Lord, I asked that he would deign to be my master, and by his grace bring it about that I should henceforth be his servant, with all fear. Of the Holy Spirit I asked that he would be my teacher, teaching me to be his disciple. And to obtain these things I implored with great devotion the help and intercession of the chosen daughter of God the Father, the handmaid and Mother of Jesus Christ, and the disciple of the Holy Spirit — the Virgin Mary, for whom it is easy to obtain from God all that has been said.

units.la: Desiderabam etiam ut ipsa me doceret verum modum esse filium, servum et discipulum, ad ipsius exemplum, et qualiter ipsa sit; et quomodo Jesus Christus fuerit suus filius, servus et discipulus, sic etiam esse; et quomodo fuerit humilis, talisque qualem convenit esse in quolibet trium modorum dictorum.
units.en: I desired also that she would teach me the true way of being a son, a servant and a disciple after her own example, and as she herself is; and how Jesus Christ was her son, her servant and her disciple, that I might be so too; and how he was humble, and of what sort it is fitting to be in each of the three ways named.

units.la: Item extendendo ulterius mateřiam hanc, cognovi esse necessarium quod praedicaretur. Quando enim subditi fuissent inducti ad gradum verae obedientiae, humilitatis, subjectionis et reverentiae erga suos majores, Dominus Noster illis se applicaret, eisque daret superiores juxta cor suum. E contra vero dici potest de non disposito ad recognoscendum bonum, quod mereatur eo privari; et qui nondum est factus servus, non meretur sibi dari dominum cujus bonitate possit aut sciat ipse frui. Unde et sperandum est quod quando subditi, aut saltem electi, assecuti fuerint talem humilitatem, patientiam et charitatem, quae sufficiant ad honòrandum, serviendum, et tolerandum quem- y a a a =. aie iw 4 E % ka cumque majorem suum quântumlibet malüm, non amittendo bonam voluntatem, sed crescendo potius in ipsa, cum proposito observandi sic usque ad mortem; tunc, inquam, sperari potest quod movebitur Dominus dare alios majores; non autem e contra, scilicet si videamus malos in dies pejorari circa obedientiam. Honora, reverere et observa majoré$ tuos, maxime autem superiores; nee solum majores tuos, sed eos omnes qui vel potestate, vel auctoritate, vel doctrina aut virtute, aut aetate, teipso sunt majores. Multi reperiuntur adhuc qui parentes et superiores suos amoris affectu prosequuntur; itemque qui obediunt eis, atque succurrunt in necessitatibus; sed qui insuper honorent ex intimis ac vere revereantur, pauci. Tu ama omnes proximos tuos, et omnibus quantum datur benefac; specialiter autem erga majores habeas affectus reverentiae, honoris, verecundiae, et reliquos affectus qui inferiores recte ordinant erga superiores; et erga aequales, affectus fraternae dilectionis, illis semper deferens; erga minores autem esto beneolus, ac benignus, et facilis, tanquam conditionis illorum amicus, et minorum, ultimorumque con- kroo w ho T a sectator. Sic fiet ut omnes ad descensum pertrahas, ipse ad novissimum virorum descendens, qui fuit Christus crucifixus. Opta reprehendi a quacumque persona, sive sit supra te, sive sub te, sive a dextris, vel a sinistris tuis: item in quocumque tempore, sive sis laetus, sive tristis, sive calidus, aut frigidus; in qualibet tua imperfectione, aut defectu, vero vel apparente; nec imponas modum reprehensori tuo, sed opta ut ipse eum modum servet qui te maxime possit affligere.
units.en: Again, carrying this matter further, I knew that it was necessary that it should be preached. For when subjects had been brought to the degree of true obedience, humility, subjection and reverence towards those over them, Our Lord would apply himself to them and give them superiors after his own heart. And the contrary can be said of one not disposed to acknowledge the good: that he deserves to be deprived of it; and he who has not yet become a servant does not deserve to be given a master whose goodness he could or would know how to enjoy. Hence too it is to be hoped that when subjects, or at least the chosen among them, have attained such humility, patience and charity as suffice for honouring, serving and tolerating any superior of theirs, however bad, without losing good will but rather growing in it, with the purpose of continuing so until death — then, I say, it may be hoped that the Lord will be moved to give other superiors; but not the other way round, if we see bad men growing daily worse as regards obedience. Honour, revere and respect those greater than you, and above all your superiors; and not only those set over you, but all who in power, or authority, or learning, or virtue, or age are greater than yourself. Many are still found who follow their parents and superiors with an affection of love, and likewise who obey them and help them in their needs; but few who besides honour them from their inmost heart and truly revere them. Love all your neighbours, and do good to all so far as is given you; but towards those above you have affections of reverence, honour and modesty, and the other affections which rightly order inferiors towards superiors; towards equals, affections of brotherly love, always deferring to them; and towards those beneath you be kindly, benign and easy of access, as a friend of their condition and a follower of the lesser and the last. So it will come about that you draw all men towards the descent, yourself descending to the lowest place of men — which was Christ crucified. Desire to be reproved by any person whatsoever, whether above you or below you, at your right hand or at your left; likewise at any time, whether you are glad or sad, warm or cold; in any imperfection or defect of yours, real or apparent; and do not prescribe a manner to your reprover, but desire that he keep the manner which can afflict you most.

units.la: Quidam significavit mihi se desiderare hoc bonum ex me, ut tam clare ipsum reprehenderem quam ipse me reprehendit. Cui ego servavi hoc responsum: cum reprehensiones inter nos non sint de rebus directe Deo displicentibus, sed solum de modis loquendi, vel conversandi, aut de alis modis se habendi in ordine ad homines, difficile est mihi, inquam, peregrino in omnibus, corripere aut emendare in talibus eos qui mentem meam et sensum non faciunt sibi regulam. Ego dicam facile: hoc mihi non sapit;' vel displicet, aut non proþatur: sed respondebitur meum judicium ac voluntatem meam non esse bonan regulam; potius volent sequi sensa patriae suae; et magis displi- cere timebunt multis, sicut sibi videtur, quam uni mihi. Sic fiet ut impediar ne possim vel audeam tales reprehendere. Aliud est de inferioribus meis, qui meam voluntatem et meum judicium - pro regula habent, in his quae sunt bona, vel indifferentia; quique parati sunt subesse superiori suo quamlibet imperfecto; volentes abnegare semẹtipsos in omnibus. Hoc ego non ita feci sefħel, cum essem Parisiis, et mihi aliqua imperaret Pater Ignatius, cui solebam respondere, communem usum non ferre quaedam quae sibi opportuna videbantur. Hoc ego proponebam apud me ad respondendum praedicto fratri, licet non fecerim, intelligens tentationem et infirmitatem spiritus subesse in talibus verbis. Quisquis vere obedienter sub aliena potestate militare optat, is se totum et omnes actus suos, ac omnem suum modum, sub beneplacito et sub judicio sui superioris rejiciat; metiatur se juxta formam ejusdem, cui se judicandum et erudiendum tradidit; et parum sit e1 caeteris omnibus hominibus placere, aut aliquid videri, nisi et suo judicio et arbitrio placuerit in Christo Jesu Domino Nostro.
units.en: A certain man signified to me that he desired this good from me, that I should reprove him as plainly as he reproved me. For him I kept this answer: since the reproofs between us are not about things directly displeasing to God, but only about ways of speaking or conversing, or other ways of behaving in relation to men, it is difficult for me — a stranger in all things — to correct or amend in such matters those who do not make my mind and my sense a rule for themselves. I may easily say: this does not taste right to me, or it displeases me, or I do not approve it; but the answer will be that my judgment and my will are not a good rule; they will rather wish to follow the notions of their own country, and will fear to displease the many, as it seems to them, more than to displease me alone. Thus it comes about that I am hindered from being able, or daring, to reprove such men. It is another matter with those under me, who hold my will and my judgment for a rule in things good or indifferent, and who are ready to be subject to their superior however imperfect, wishing to deny themselves in all things. This I once failed to do, when I was at Paris and Father Ignatius commanded me certain things; I used to answer him that common usage did not bear certain things which seemed to him opportune. This I purposed within myself to say in answer to the aforesaid brother, though I did not do it, understanding that a temptation and weakness of spirit lay beneath such words. Whoever truly desires to serve under another's power in obedience, let him cast himself wholly, with all his acts and his whole manner, under the good pleasure and judgment of his superior; let him measure himself by the standard of the one to whom he has given himself to be judged and instructed; and let it be a small thing to him to please all other men, or to seem anything, unless he has pleased his superior's judgment and discretion in Christ Jesus Our Lord.

units.la: Hic datum est nosse quid sim ego et fuerim hactenus, debilis in ferendis reprehensionibus. Superiorum enim reprehensiones me nimium saepe in superbiam recalcitrandi erexerunt, ut minus humilem, minusque subjectum. Inferiorum vero, aut aequalium correctiones me nimium dejecerunt. Det Deus gratiam servandi in omnibus modum et gradum meum, sic scilicet ut ne me male prosternat minor, nec male erigat superior. Det Deus ut magis sim attentus ad emendationem, quam ad modum verbaque ejus qui me reprehendit. Qui non habet in se aut non invenit unde seipsum consoletur, facile succumbit sub onus reprehensionis; qui autem in se ipso habet, vel putat se habere unde seipsum consoletur, cito seipsum consolatur super reprehensionibus. Hinc fit ut debeas caute reprehendere eos qui sibi ipsis displicent; nimium enim dejiciuntur nisi bene admoneantur; sibi autem placentes facilius ferunt reprehensiones. Aliter ergo.te habeas erga melancholicum aut flegmaticum, et aliter erga colericum aut sanguineum; sed da operam tu, ut nec sis colericus, nec'sanguineus quantum ad consensum, nec flegmaticus aut melancholicus, juxta illud: Vir Sapiens dominabitur astris: hoc fit per gratiam Domini Nostri Jesu Christi, qui naturas nostras in seipso, et per seipsum, et ex seipso perficit.
units.en: Here it was given me to know what I am, and have been hitherto: weak in bearing reproofs. For the reproofs of superiors have too often stirred me up to the pride of kicking back, making me less humble and less subject; while the corrections of inferiors or equals have cast me down too much. May God give grace to keep in all things my measure and my degree, so that neither may a lesser man wrongly prostrate me, nor a superior wrongly puff me up. May God grant that I be more attentive to amendment than to the manner and words of him who reproves me. He who has not in himself, or does not find, whence to console himself, easily sinks under the burden of reproof; but he who has in himself, or thinks he has, whence to console himself, quickly consoles himself over reproofs. Hence you should be cautious in reproving those who are displeased with themselves; for they are cast down too much unless they are admonished well; while those pleased with themselves bear reproofs more easily. Bear yourself, then, in one way towards the melancholic or phlegmatic, and in another towards the choleric or sanguine; but for your own part take care to be neither choleric nor sanguine so far as consent goes, nor phlegmatic nor melancholic — according to the saying: The wise man shall rule the stars. This is done by the grace of Our Lord Jesus Christ, who perfects our natures in himself, and through himself, and from himself.

units.la: Alio quoque die infra idem tempus Visitationis, dum inciperem consuetum discursum mysteriorum vitae Christi super Annuntiatione, in qua ego considerabam Beatara Virginem offerre seipsam totam in ancillam Redemptoris,,yenerunt magna et optima desideria, ut quidquid ego essem facturus, prius per gratiam cujusdam annunciationis recte intenderem; itemque omnes mulieres, antequam conciperent, haberent jam intentionem suamin omnia bona opera quae Dominus requisiturus est in filiis vel filiabus; et ita de patribus corporalibus et spiritualibus ipsorum, qui habent filios spirituales, vel discipulos qui ipsis obediunt: optabam etiam ut quaecumque nunc video mihi prodesse, ex bonis operibus, vel laboribus, vel studiis praeteritis, essent quasi: illa ego omnia ab initio vitae meae ordinassem in utilitatem istorum Germanorum.
units.en: On another day within the same season of the Visitation, when I began the accustomed round of the mysteries of the life of Christ with the Annunciation, in which I considered the Blessed Virgin offering her whole self as the handmaid of the Redeemer, there came great and excellent desires: that whatever I was to do, I might first rightly intend it through the grace of a kind of annunciation; and likewise that all women, before they conceived, might already have directed their intention to all the good works which the Lord will require of their sons or daughters; and so of their fathers, bodily and spiritual, who have spiritual sons, or disciples who obey them. I desired also that whatever I now see profiting me, from good works or labours or studies of the past, might be as though I had ordered them all, from the beginning of my life, to the profit of these Germans.

units.la: Super considerationem Visitationis, considerando gratiam Virginis quae ita placebat Altissimo ut etiam potuerit impetrare sanctificationem Joannis Baptisíae, optabam ut ipsa Virgo dignaretur visi- tare animam meam et corpus, et quidquid in eis esset, et impetrare ut sanctificaretur, fieretque Deo gratum, et si quid impurum esset mundaretur. Super loco qui est de pastoribus qui venerunt ad Jesum natum, ego petebam hanc gratiam, ut Dominus dignaretur corrigere me totum, et elevare ad altiora, sicut correxit pastores, qui 1nfima desiderabant, et juxta infima intelligebant: cum Magis autem cupiebam deprimi, et humiliari corde et desideriis, sicut mente elevari cum pastoribus.
units.en: In considering the Visitation — pondering the grace of the Virgin, who so pleased the Most High that she could even obtain the sanctification of John the Baptist — I desired that the Virgin herself would deign to visit my soul and body and whatever is in them, and obtain that they be sanctified and made pleasing to God, and that if anything were impure it might be cleansed. On the passage about the shepherds who came to the new-born Jesus, I asked this grace: that the Lord would deign to correct me wholly and raise me to higher things, as he corrected the shepherds, who desired lowly things and understood according to lowly things; but with the Magi I desired to be brought low and humbled in heart and desires, as with the shepherds to be raised in mind.

units.la: Eodem die, in missa, dum considerarem Deum esse miseratorem et misericordem, et quod respicit laborem et dolorem, item quod omnia essent illi praesentia, rogabam ab ipso ut dignaretur misereri huic nationi Germanicae et compati ei, quasi jam ipsa pateretur illa omnia quae ei eveWent mala, si non revertatur ad fidem catholicam et ad devotionem Romanae religionis.
units.en: On the same day, at Mass, while I considered that God is pitying and merciful, and that he looks upon toil and grief, and that all things are present to him, I begged of him that he would deign to have mercy on this German nation and to have compassion on it, as though it were already suffering all those evils which will befall it if it does not return to the catholic faith and to the devotion of the Roman religion.

units.la: -In octava Visitationis, considerabam eum esse diem in quo, anno revoluto, ego feceram meam professionem. Habui magnam devotionem circa vota mea, petendo gratiam a Deo Patre pro per- severantia et continuo augmento castitatis, qua debeat reaedificari caro mea et roborari contra suas fragilitates, quae maxime cognoscuntur ex ipsis concupiscentiis carnalibus. Filio committebam curam obedientiae meae, qui et ipse factus est obediens usque ad mortem; Spiritui Sancto commendabam paupertatem, orans ut me semper vellet conservare in affectu paupertatis ita ut nunquam relinquerem ejus affectum. Rogabam etiam ut omnes meae tres polentiae semper crescerent in cogitatione, memoria et affectionibus, conformiter ad dicta supra vota; et quod ad haec Pater mihi influeret potentiam in qualibet earum, habendo specialem curam meae memoriae: Filius vero influeret similiter sapientiam et lucem, curamque susciperet intellectus; Spiritus Sanctus inspiraret dona quaelibet, et curam haberet voluntatis. Sanctissimam etiam Trinitatem, quae est una essentia, orabam ut residerét in meo corde in sua bonitate, diffundendo personalia attributa per tres potentias. Dominam autem meam orabam ut esset ad omnia advocata, cum sit ipsa tam verum exemplar virginitatis, obedientiae et paupertatis; habens carnem purissi- mam, animamque mundissimam, et sanctissimum spiritum; cum sit quaelibet earum gratiarum effecta in ea cum tanta potentia virtutis divinae, tantaque sapientia et bonitate, ut sufficeret quae- libet harum alias duas conservare in sua puritate, periso id est tam perfecte munda caro, quae sufficeret ad hoc quod nulla immunditia posset aut sciret accedere sive pertingere ad animam nec ad spiritum; et similiter tam plenus donis spiritus, quod sufficeret animam sic abstrahere, ut nec ipsam nec carnem posset ingredi aliquid non purissimum; sic et anima tantam habebat perfectionem que sufficeret ad 1ilłustrandum spiritum et carnem.
units.en: On the octave of the Visitation I considered that it was the day on which, a year before, I had made my profession. I had great devotion concerning my vows, asking grace of God the Father for perseverance and continual increase of chastity, by which my flesh must be built up anew and strengthened against its frailties, which are known above all from the carnal concupiscences themselves. To the Son I committed the care of my obedience — he who himself became obedient unto death; to the Holy Spirit I commended poverty, praying that he would keep me always in the affection of poverty, so that I might never abandon it. I prayed also that all my three powers might ever grow in thought, memory and affections, in conformity with the vows named; and that to this end the Father would pour power into each of them, taking special care of my memory; the Son would likewise pour in wisdom and light, and take charge of the intellect; the Holy Spirit would inspire his several gifts, and have care of the will. I prayed also the most holy Trinity, which is one essence, to reside in my heart in its goodness, diffusing the personal attributes through the three powers. And I prayed my Lady to be advocate for all this, since she is so true a pattern of virginity, obedience and poverty; having most pure flesh, a most clean soul, and a most holy spirit; each of these graces having been wrought in her with such power of divine virtue, such wisdom and goodness, that any one of them would suffice to keep the other two in their purity: flesh, that is, so perfectly clean that it would suffice to prevent any uncleanness from being able to approach or reach the soul or the spirit; and likewise a spirit so full of gifts that it would suffice so to draw the soul upward that nothing not most pure could enter it or the flesh; and so too the soul had such perfection as would suffice to give light to spirit and flesh.

units.la: Die Divisionis Apostolorum, habui quaedam magna desideria quod tale festum esset in magna veneratione multumque universale. Habui etiam in orationibus magnas consolationes et desideria, quod Apostoli sequerentur Jesum Christum in domum meam, utpote qui melius scirent ipsum honorare, ei ministrare, ejusque intelligere voluntatem, colloquia et verba: excusando me ignorantem in similibus officiis. Oblate sunt etiam mihi multaecoòmmendationes ad fratres meds dispersos.
units.en: On the day of the Dispersion of the Apostles I had certain great desires that such a feast should be held in great veneration and be widely universal. I had also in my prayers great consolations and desires that the Apostles might follow Jesus Christ into my house, as those who would know better how to honour him, to minister to him, and to understand his will, his conversations and his words — excusing myself as ignorant in such offices. There were also offered to me many commendations for my brethren dispersed abroad.

units.la: Die sanctiAlexii, habui quamdam considerationem, cum essem in discursu mysteriorum Christi considerationeque trium Regum, magnumque desiderium quod peregrinatio Domini Joannis esset in rećognitionem peregrinationis trium Regum venientium adorare Christum; quodque esset conveniens quod ipsi visitarentur aen suis reliquiis, quippe qui tantum honoraverunt Dominum Nostrum; unde etiam se mihi offereDant recordationes quaedam super peregrinationem sancti Alexii, sancti Jacobi, sancti Rochi, Domini Nostri Jesu Christi, Beate Mariae Dominae Nostrae, sanctorum Apostolorum; et ex omnibus spes mihi dabatur has peregrinationes valde acceptas fore Domino Nostro et omnibus sanctis, praesertim his temporibus et in his regionibus, ubi jam tam paucae peregrinationes exibentur, propter haereses quae pretium et existimationem auferunt hujusmodi operibus quae tanti sunt momenti.
units.en: On the day of Saint Alexis, while I was in the round of the mysteries of Christ and the consideration of the three Kings, I had a great desire that the pilgrimage of Don Juan might be in acknowledgment of the pilgrimage of the three Kings who came to adore Christ; and that it would be fitting that they should be visited in their relics, seeing that they so greatly honoured Our Lord. Whence there came to me also certain recollections concerning the pilgrimage of Saint Alexis, of Saint James, of Saint Roch, of Our Lord Jesus Christ, of Blessed Mary Our Lady, and of the holy Apostles; and from all of them hope was given me that these pilgrimages would be very acceptable to Our Lord and to all the saints, especially in these times and in these regions, where so few pilgrimages are now made, because of the heresies which strip works of this kind — works of such great moment — of their worth and esteem.

units.la: Quadam die, dum mihi veniret in mentem Annunciatio Beatae Mariae Virginis, et desiderarem habere -aliquas annunciationes meorum sociorum, non tamen nisi qualiter placeret Domino, añimadverti me interim aliquibus gravari tristitiis Y T y aG y e n] R AED R DRIV et amaritudinibus, tribus de causis vel de aliquibus earum: prima, ad cognoscendum et ad non timendum me non esse gratum Deo et Sanctis ejus, propter imperfectiones et defectus proprios; secunda, me existimando longe esse à Domino; tertia, propter timorem, quem generabat mihi, esse infructuosum, parvos fructus considerando quos homo faciat. Hinc veniebat mihi ingens desiderium ut ipsa Virgo Maria me Deo gratum redderet, primo nempè ut illa quae est gratią plena; secundo, eo quod illi semper Ghistus praesens adfuerit, me Christo ipsi vicinum et proximum redderet; tertio, eo quod. ipsa est benedicta inter omnes mulieres, inter homines maledictus esse non merear; quarto, eo quod fructus ejus est benedictus, concedat mihi gratiam ad faciendum aliquem fructum in servitio Christi Domini Nostri.
units.en: One day, when the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary came into my mind and I desired to have some good tidings of my companions — yet only as it should please the Lord — I noticed that I was meanwhile weighed down by certain sadnesses and bitternesses, from three causes, or from some of them: the first, in knowing, and in fearing, that I am not pleasing to God and his Saints, because of my own imperfections and defects; the second, in reckoning myself to be far from the Lord; the third, because of the fear which the thought of being unfruitful bred in me, considering the small fruits a man produces. Hence there came to me a vast desire that the Virgin Mary herself would render me pleasing to God: first, as she who is full of grace; secondly, that as Christ was always present with her, she would render me near and close to Christ himself; thirdly, that as she is blessed among all women, I might not deserve to be accursed among men; fourthly, that as her fruit is blessed, she would grant me grace to bear some fruit in the service of Christ Our Lord.

units.la: Quadam die, scilicet dum Dominus -Joannes volebat peregrinari Coloniam, habui ingentia quaedam desideria ut ejus peregrinatio esset Deo accepta admodum, et Dominae Nostré Matri ejus, ac omnibus Angelis et omnibus Sanctis, sed praecipue tribus Regibus, et sanctae Ursulae consortibusque ejus; et haec omnia ad commo- -dum ipsius Domini Joannis, ad pacificationem tumultuum bellicorum, ad serenitatem temporis, ad compensationem boni ab Hispania recepti, et propter Deo acceptas peregrinationes quas Germani olim in ipsa fecerunt, visitando sanctum Jacobum, sanctam Mariam Montis. Sertati et Nostram Dominam de Guadalupa; item ad itineris securitatem a latronibus et exteris periculis; item ad Dominum placandum et Sanctos ejus, propter offensiones factas ab aliquibus annis, propter navigationum, peregrinationum, et aliorum piorum sanctorumque operum ad paenitentiam et ad honorem Dei et Sanctorum ejus, et quorumcumque caeterorum bonorum operum, contemptum.
units.en: One day — namely when Don Juan wished to go on pilgrimage to Cologne — I had certain vast desires that his pilgrimage might be fully acceptable to God, and to Our Lady his Mother, and to all the Angels and all the Saints, but chiefly to the three Kings and to Saint Ursula and her companions; and all this for the benefit of Don Juan himself, for the pacifying of the tumults of war, for fair weather, in repayment of the good received from Spain, and on account of the pilgrimages acceptable to God which the Germans of old made in Spain, visiting Saint James, Saint Mary of Montserrat and Our Lady of Guadalupe; likewise for the safety of the journey from robbers and outward dangers; likewise to appease the Lord and his Saints for the offences committed for some years past by the contempt of processions, pilgrimages, and other pious and holy works of penance done to the honour of God and his Saints, and of all other good works.

units.la: Similiter aderat et offerebatur mihi spiritus ad magpificandum quodvis opus pium propter solum Deum atque Dominum Nostrum et ejus Sanctorum gloriam factum. Veniebat etiam mihi non minus doloris stimulus, quod viderem Sanctorum opera non contemplari, et etiam vitae Domini Nostri Jesu Christi gesta non ruminari nec ponderari. Specialiter quod martyrum dolores et tormenta non propius mirarentur dolebam, cum ipsi tam Deo cari et accepti fuerint. Hinc quatuor notavi, in quibus opus magis faciendum esse facile cognosci potest. Primum. est aspicere quid agatur; verbi gratia, si cedit ad honorem Dei, ad gloriam Sanctorum, vel ad paenitentiam in propriam utilitatem animae, vel ad proximi utilitatem, etc.; secundum, propter quem tale fit opus, scopum intentionis operantis intuendo; tertium, quo spiritu agitur, id est utrum ex timore Dei servili vel filiali, aut ex amore Dei vel proximi, aut ex aliquo pio et recto affectu movente volun- tatem, vel etiam ex bono dictamine rationis cui obedit voluntas; quartum, acceptationem divinae Majestatis tam liberalis, tam bonae, tam misericordis, quae laborem et dolorem considerat, quae etiam adeo honorificatura est eos qui ministra- verunt Jesu Christo Filio suo Domino Nostro, quae. etiam vult ut ipse Christus sit ille magnus Angelus habens thuribulum aureum, quo ipse possit facere valere omnia bona nostra.
units.en: Likewise there was present and offered to me a spirit for magnifying any pious work whatever, done solely for God and Our Lord and the glory of his Saints. And there came to me no less a sting of grief at seeing that the works of the Saints are not contemplated, and that the deeds of the life of Our Lord Jesus Christ are not chewed over and weighed. Especially I grieved that the pains and torments of the martyrs are not more closely wondered at, seeing that they were so dear and acceptable to God. Hence I noted four things by which it can easily be known where a work is to be esteemed more. The first is to look at what is done: for instance, whether it tends to the honour of God, to the glory of the Saints, or to penance for the profit of one's own soul, or to the profit of one's neighbour, and so on. The second, for whose sake the work is done, looking to the aim of the doer's intention. The third, with what spirit it is done: that is, whether from servile or filial fear of God, or from love of God or of one's neighbour, or from some devout and right affection moving the will, or again from a good dictate of reason which the will obeys. The fourth, the acceptance of the divine Majesty, so liberal, so good, so merciful, who considers toil and grief; who moreover will so greatly honour those who have ministered to Jesus Christ his Son Our Lord; and who wills that Christ himself be that great Angel with the golden censer, by whom he can give worth to all our good works.

units.la: Die sanctae Praxedis, Christi vitae mysteria scrutando, mihi postulationes gratiarum occurrerunt, et a Deo ipso petenda per merita Annunciationis, TAATA Incarnationis, Visitationis; et ut modum et ritum quo scirem ipsum laudare et honorare et in ipso et de ipso cogitare, ipsum cognoscere, memorari, amare et desiderare, ipsi servire, ipsum velle, videre, audire, odorari, gustare, palpare, concederet; et haec omnia, Christi intercessionibus, normae ořdinationum et methodorum sanctae ejus Ecclesiae conformia, in doctrina vera et catholica, in sanctis sacramentis, sanctorum precibus et invocationibus, et in piorum operum animarum in purgatorio detentarum memoria.
units.en: On the day of Saint Praxedes, searching the mysteries of the life of Christ, petitions for graces occurred to me, to be asked of God himself through the merits of the Annunciation, the Incarnation, the Visitation; and that he would grant me the manner and rite by which I might know how to praise and honour him, to think in him and of him, to know him, remember him, love him and desire him, to serve him, to will him, to see, hear, smell, taste and touch him; and all this, by the intercessions of Christ, in conformity with the norm of the ordinances and methods of his holy Church, in true and catholic doctrine, in the holy sacraments, in the prayers and invocations of the saints, and in the remembrance, by pious works, of the souls detained in purgatory.

units.la: In missa aliud mihi accidit desiderium,videlicet ut in omnibus quantumcumque bonis operibus quae facturus eram, haec mediante bono et sancto spiritu facerem. Hinc cogitabam non gratum Deo esse aliqua sanctae Ecclesiae reformare ad hereticorum voluntatem: nam quamvis ipsi multa, quemadmodum et daemones, vera fateantur, verumtamen veritatis spiritu haud dicunt, qui spiritus veritatis Sanctus Spiritus est.
units.en: At Mass another desire came to me: namely, that in all the works I was to do, however good, I might do them by means of a good and holy spirit. Hence I thought that it is not pleasing to God to reform anything in holy Church according to the will of the heretics: for although they, like the demons, confess many things that are true, yet they do not say them by the spirit of truth — and the spirit of truth is the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Tandem, post missam, cum sentirem non in me esse quem antea sentiebam gustum spiritualium, quem obnixe desiderarem, aliud mihi non respuen- dum desiderium occurrit: quod Dominus Jesus Christus faceret me medullitus et occulte visitare meos defectus (secreto eos reparando), intellectus, memoriae, voluntatis et sensus: item virtutes omnes secretas et dona, super quibus nunquam meditatus fueram, quamvis iis; plus quam his quorum in me esse defectum sentio, egerem.
units.en: At length, after Mass, feeling that the relish of spiritual things which I used to feel was not in me, though I earnestly desired it, another desire, not to be rejected, occurred to me: that the Lord Jesus Christ would inwardly and secretly visit my defects (repairing them in secret) — of intellect, memory, will and sense; likewise all the secret virtues and gifts on which I had never meditated, although I needed them more than those whose defect I feel in myself.

units.la: Aliud habueram quidem antea desiderium, scilicet ut Dominus dignaretur mihi in omnibus, juxta ejus beneplacitum, dirigere quae in me, aliquo bono sanctoque spiritu dictante, sensi, aut in alis: multa enim soleo loqui, scribere et facere, non servando spiritum illum quo prius illa caeperam. Nam, verbi gratia, quaedam quandoque spiritu sedato et jucundo, et cum exteriori gratia profero, quae antea quidem compuncto cum spiritu senseram, cumque quibusdam gemitibus spiritualibus: unde fit ut ex eo minus prosit audienti, quia non datur in tam bono spiritu, quam bonus erat ille in quo tale quid acceperam. Quaerebam igitur ut Dominus dignaretur dare mihi gratiam, ita ut idem esset spiritus in partu et in augmento operis, in locutione vel scriptura, qui fuerat in conceptione. Hoc erit quando idem spiritus erit in affectu, in cogitatione, in locutione et in opere. Hinc specialis mihi aliquis intellectus occurrit et cognitio illius loci: Ductus est Jesus a Spiritu in desertum; et alterius: Venit in spiritu in templum; ubi specialis quidam spiritus sensus percipitur, movens personam ad operandum vel ad loqtendum, et non relinquens eam in suo humano et proprio sensu.
units.en: I had indeed had another desire before: that the Lord would deign to direct in all things, according to his good pleasure, what I have felt in myself at the dictate of some good and holy spirit, or in others. For I am wont to say, write and do many things without keeping the spirit in which I had first conceived them. For example, I sometimes utter with a calm and cheerful spirit, and with outward grace, things which I had first felt with a contrite spirit and with certain spiritual groanings; whence it comes that they profit the hearer less, because they are not given in so good a spirit as was that in which I had received them. I sought therefore that the Lord would deign to give me grace, that the same spirit might be in the bringing forth and growth of a work, in speech or in writing, as was in its conception. This will be when the same spirit is in the affection, in the thought, in the speech and in the work. Hence a special understanding and knowledge came to me of that passage: Jesus was led by the Spirit into the desert; and of that other: He came in the spirit into the temple; where a certain special feeling of the spirit is perceived, moving the person to act or to speak, and not leaving him to his own human sense.

units.la: In sancti Jacobi festivitate in missae introitu et principio, me alligatum percipiendo meis defectibus et imperfectionibus, et recitando versum: Quare tristis incedo dum afjiligit me inimicus? talis mihi intellectus interrogative, occurrit, loquens mihi in meo spiritu: Quid propter tui afflictiones et suggestiones inimici tristis es, quum ipse non conetur te tristem reddere nisi quia voluntati ejus non acquiescis? Merito quidem tristareris, si Dominus Jesus Christus te ipsum affligeret.
units.en: On the feast of Saint James, at the introit and beginning of Mass, perceiving myself bound by my defects and imperfections, and reciting the verse: Why do I go sorrowful while the enemy afflicts me? — such an understanding came to me by way of question, speaking to me in my spirit: Why are you sad on account of your afflictions and the suggestions of the enemy, seeing that he strives to make you sad only because you do not acquiesce in his will? You would have reason indeed to be sad if the Lord Jesus Christ himself were afflicting you.

units.la: Eo ipso die, venit mihi in mentem quod et alias saepe senseram quidem, oportere ad melio- rem inveniendam spiritus praeparationem, homi- nem primam suam intentionem ad ea quae Dei sunt erectam habere; et quia homo in ipsis proficit, oculum quidem non habendo suum principaliter (quemadmodum et huc usque saepe feci) ad perturbationem tentationis et tristitiae remedium. Qui enim Dominum Nostrum quaerit et-quae ejus sunt, solum et praecipue ut tentationes et tristitiam repellat, immediate -pro seipsa devotionem non quaereret. Igitur in semetipso ineptus esset et devotionem parvi faciens, nisi affligeretur; et hoc est amorem per timorem imperfectionis et miseriae quaerere, ad sensum bonum et spiritualem, id est, ad mali evitationem. Ob id, juste quidem et misericorditer, ad tempus, ejusmodi in suos Deus immittit perturbationes; et -quia eras absque ejus bonorum affectu, et ne tepidus et otiosus fias, tales stimulos immittit et afflictiones et calcaria, ad ingrediendum in via Domini, absque quiete, quousque in Deo ipso Domino Nostro Jesu Christo requiescas. Etiam nequidem otiari deberes si inimici nullas sentires perturbationes, sive tentationes, sive malitiae sensus, vanitates aut imper- fectiones, quemadmodum tepidis et otiosis, et omnibus his qui ne cadant attendunt, mos est, in via Domini progressum negligentibus; quibus ipro spirituali sufficientia securitas non cadendi, quamvis multus pateat ad progressum accessus, sufficeret. Noli igitur esse contentus in hce quod non descendas, aut non diminuaris, aut non retrocedas; sed pone in corde tuo ascensiones, augmenta, et progressus in interiora; non propter timorem descendendi, retrocedendi aut cadendi, sed propter amorem sanctitatis; et non solum propterea quod tales cogitationes te possunt defen- dere a malis cogitationibus. Desideres et sitias sentire res spirituales, non quasi sint remedia contra malos aut vanos affectus, sed propter id quod in se habent. Sic fiet tandem ut pervenias ad amorem Dei propter ipsum solum Deum. Proinde dimitte omne quod vanum et otiosum est, nedum peccata, tanquam impedimenta quae prohibent aditum ad Deum et conspectum Dei, et quietem in ipso atque conversationem.
units.en: On that same day it came into my mind — as I had indeed often felt at other times — that in order to find a better preparation of spirit a man must have his first intention raised to the things of God, and make progress in them for their own sake, not having his eye chiefly (as I have often done even till now) on the remedy for the disturbance of temptation and sadness. For he who seeks Our Lord and the things that are his solely and chiefly to drive off temptations and sadness, would not be seeking devotion immediately for its own sake. He would therefore be inept in himself, and one who made little of devotion except when afflicted; and this is to seek love through fear of imperfection and misery — for a good and spiritual purpose, indeed, namely the avoidance of evil. For this reason God justly and mercifully sends, for a time, disturbances of this kind upon his own; and because you were without affection for his good things, and lest you become lukewarm and idle, he sends such stings and afflictions and spurs, to drive you into the way of the Lord, without rest, until you rest in God himself, Our Lord Jesus Christ. Nor indeed ought you to be idle even if you felt no disturbances of the enemy, no temptations, no sense of malice, vanities or imperfections — as is the way of the lukewarm and idle, and of all those who attend only to not falling, neglecting progress in the way of the Lord; for whom, in place of spiritual sufficiency, the security of not falling would be enough, although abundant access to progress lies open. Be not content, then, with not going down, or not being diminished, or not going back; but set in your heart ascents, increases, and progress into the interior; not for fear of descending, going back or falling, but for love of holiness; and not only because such thoughts can defend you from evil thoughts. Desire and thirst to feel spiritual things, not as remedies against evil or vain affections, but for what they have in themselves. So it will come about at last that you attain to the love of God for the sake of God himself alone. Accordingly put away all that is vain and idle, not to say sins, as hindrances which bar the approach to God and the sight of God, and rest and conversation in him.

units.la: In die sanctaee Marthae virginis, hospitae Jesu Christi, dum orarem pro anima Galliae, de cujus morte acceperam nuntium, simul ac de morte Dominae Antoniae quae fuerat serviens ipsi Mar- chionissae de Postura, ego inveni magnam devotionem et discursus spirituales circa ipsas; et legendo orationes quasdam quae dici solent in Ecclesia pro defunctis, ubi est etiam commendatio corporum sepultorum, legendo, inquam, tales orationes, sensi magnum spiritum ad tales corporum pias commendationes. Veniebant quoque mihi in mentem, cum sancto affectu fidei magnae, aliae et bonae considerationes, quas op tabam fieri plus quam unquam factae fuerunt, super sepulturas catholicorum fidelium; etiam dato quod ertum esset animas ipsas esse in caelis. Sentiebam enim Deo placere orationes pro ipsa resurrectione talium corporum. Item sumi posse, ex occasione dictae sepulturae, considerationem illius summae Sapientiae, qua futura est ipsa miranda resurrectio; et quod talis pulvis qui nune cernitur, futurus sit tam speciosum corpus in gloriam uniuscujusque nostrum. Agi possunt gratiae Deo, visis talibus corporum reliquiis, quod tam multa bona operatus est Deus per illa instrumenta, quae tanquam nihil sunt nunc in sepulchris. His et similibus considera- E ae i E i PFET, i tionibus, nòn solum invitantur Christiani, in memoriam spirituum ipsorum defunctorum, ad agendum gratias, si jam sunt in caelis, et ad deprecandam veniam, si sunt in purgatorio; sed etam ut in ipsis crescat fides ejus articuli et dilatetur, qui est de carnis resurrectione.
units.en: On the day of Saint Martha the virgin, hostess of Jesus Christ, while I prayed for the soul of Gallia, of whose death I had received word, and likewise for the death of Doña Antonia, who had been in the service of the Marchioness herself, I found great devotion and spiritual reflections concerning them; and reading certain prayers which are wont to be said in the Church for the departed, where there is also a commendation of the buried bodies — reading, I say, such prayers, I felt a great spirit for these pious commendations of bodies. There came also into my mind, with a holy affection of great faith, other good considerations, which I wished might be made more than they have ever been, over the burial-places of catholic faithful, even granted it were certain that their souls are in heaven. For I felt that prayers for the resurrection of such bodies are pleasing to God. Likewise, that from the occasion of such burial one may draw the consideration of that supreme Wisdom by which the wonderful resurrection itself is to come; and that such dust as is now seen will one day be so beautiful a body, to the glory of each one of us. Thanks may be given to God, at the sight of such remains of bodies, that God worked so many good things through those instruments which now are as nothing in their graves. By these and like considerations Christians are invited, in memory of the spirits of the departed themselves, not only to give thanks if they are already in heaven, and to beg pardon for them if they are in purgatory, but also that faith in that article which concerns the resurrection of the flesh may grow in them and be enlarged.

units.la: In die dedicationis beate Mariae de Portinncula, quae solemñitas est Dominae Nostre de Angelis, ego habui multa sensa spiritualia, sensique multam devotionem juxta hoc, ut dedicaretur jam anima mea et corpus meum in templum vivum Domino, ad recipienda et retinenda spiritualia Dei dona.
units.en: On the day of the dedication of blessed Mary of the Portiuncula, which is the solemnity of Our Lady of the Angels, I had many spiritual feelings, and felt much devotion to this end: that my soul and my body might now be dedicated as a living temple to the Lord, for receiving and retaining the spiritual gifts of God.

units.la: Adfuit etiam desiderium vehemens ut omnia, quae hactenus a Deo in factis, verbis, vel sanctis inspirationibus emanarunt et ordinata sunt, cum consideratione magna et attentione a me et ab omnibus notarentur. Item, ut quaecumque habcmus in Ecclesia, a nostris sanctis et piis prae- decessoribus ordinata, haee etiam considerentur cum gratiarum actionibus, cum timore ne ipsa tanquam ab indignis nobis auferantur.
units.en: There was present also a vehement desire that everything which has hitherto flowed forth and been ordained by God, in deeds, in words, or in holy inspirations, might be noted with great consideration and attention by me and by all. Likewise, that whatever we have in the Church, ordained by our holy and devout predecessors, might also be considered with thanksgiving, and with fear lest these things be taken away from us as unworthy of them.

units.la: Egi etiam gratias Deo in missa, sicut ante proposueram, pro omnibus correctionibus publicis, quae hactenus populis aut provinciis, vel civitatibus aut personis, a Deo factae sunt, vel praevidentur futurae ad emendationem vitae; et dolebam quod talia non notarentur, ut, verbi grátia, pestis, terre motus, bella, inundationes aquarum, siccitates, et ala hujusmodi mala temporalia; ex quibus erat agnoscendus Altissimus, et timendus Judex qui his modis. nobis proponit memoriam nostrorum novissimorum; volens ut redeamus ad viam paenitentiae; ut percipiamus dona bonitatis et misericordiae suae. Et qui nobis secundum adventum suum proponit, dum videt primi et humilis adventus sui memoriam a nobis jam recessisse; ipse etiam tunc nobis vult incutere diem judicii et adventum regni majestatis suae, quum videt evangelium regni despici a nobis et non suscipi.
units.en: I also gave thanks to God at Mass, as I had before resolved, for all the public corrections which have hitherto been made by God upon peoples or provinces, cities or persons, or are foreseen to come, for the amendment of life; and I grieved that such things are not noted — as, for example, plague, earthquakes, wars, floods, droughts, and other temporal evils of this kind; by which the Most High should be acknowledged, and feared as the Judge who in these ways sets before us the memory of our last things, wishing us to return to the way of penance and to perceive the gifts of his goodness and mercy. And he who sets before us his second coming, when he sees that the memory of his first and humble coming has already departed from us — he then wills to impress upon us the day of judgment and the coming of the kingdom of his majesty, when he sees the gospel of the kingdom despised by us and not received.

units.la: Hoc die volui notare et rèducere ad memoriam meàm quomodo singulis noctibus debeam me praesignare cum magna intentione, juxta in- H a U a telligentiam quam Dominus jampridem dedit mihi, pro ea re facienda. Item, ut dicam illos versiculos: Dignare me laudare te, Virgo sacrata; da mihi virtutem contra hostes tuos, qui sunt hostes fidei et humilitatis, castitatis et puritatis, mansuetudinis atque charitatis. Item: Procul recedant somnia; Noctem quietam et finem perfectum; et: Hostem repellas longius pacemque dones protinus. Debebam etiam non omittere unum Pater noster, unum Ave Maria, et unum Credo, sequendo et quaerendo eum spiritum qui tam saepe ad eam rem datus est. Hoc faciam post litaniam solitam et post examinationem conscientiae, et post ordinationem earum rerum quae mihi sunt instituende pro die sequenti. Mane quoque, postquam,.fuero lotus et compositus ad operandum, non debeo omittere praesignationem, partim eosdem versus, partim alios, pro exigentia temporis recitando, et etiam Pater noster, Ave Maria et Credo. Eodem die, circa verbum illud: Omne quod,calcaverit pes tuus, tuum erit, dum considerarem sanctos patres fuisse peregrinos -prius in terra quae postea ıpsıs fuit propria, ego concipiebam in spiritu bono spem magnam, quod regnum spirituale et hereditas Domini ventura sunt, in quibus peregrini nos sumus per desideria et cogitationes.
units.en: On this day I wished to note and recall to my memory how each night I should sign myself with great intention, according to the understanding which the Lord long ago gave me for doing this. Likewise, that I should say those versicles: Vouchsafe that I may praise thee, holy Virgin; give me strength against thine enemies — who are the enemies of faith and humility, of chastity and purity, of meekness and charity. Likewise: Far off let dreams depart; Grant a quiet night and a perfect end; and: Drive far away our enemy and straightway give us peace. I was also not to omit one Our Father, one Hail Mary, and one Creed, following and seeking that spirit which has so often been given for this. This I shall do after the accustomed litany, and after the examination of conscience, and after ordering the things I must set myself for the following day. In the morning too, after I have washed and made myself ready for work, I must not omit the signing, reciting partly the same verses, partly others as the time requires, and also the Our Father, Hail Mary and Creed. On the same day, concerning that word: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon shall be yours, while I considered that the holy fathers were first pilgrims in the land which afterwards became their own, I conceived in a good spirit a great hope that the spiritual kingdom and inheritance of the Lord are to come, in which we are now pilgrims by desires and thoughts.

units.la: In die. inventionis sancti Stephani protomartyris, dum cċonsiderarem illa corpora simul inventa, ego caepi per devotum desiderium rogare Christum Dominum ut tandem velit mihi concedere ut hisce videam oculis corpora *gloriosa quorum reliquias aliquas hucusque vidi, et generaliter omnium beatorum.
units.en: On the day of the finding of Saint Stephen the protomartyr, while I considered those bodies found together, I began with devout desire to beg Christ the Lord that he would at last grant me to see with these eyes the glorified bodies of those whose relics I have hitherto seen, and generally of all the blessed.

units.la: Semel dicendo officium meum, quum sentirem distractiones quasdam quas desiderarem auferri mihi, ego responsum in me habui idem quod habueram alias frequenter, id est quod nitendum fuisset extra tempus orationis ita cognoscere distractionum causas, cum desiderio quiescendi in suo tempore, ut merearis tempore orationis gaudere in lectione verborum Dei.
units.en: Once, saying my office, when I felt certain distractions which I desired to have taken from me, I had in myself the same answer I had often had at other times: that one ought to strive, outside the time of prayer, so to know the causes of one's distractions — with the desire of being at rest in their proper season — that you may deserve, in the time of prayer, to rejoice in the reading of the words of God.

units.la: Eodem modo in missa, dum desiderarem odorari corpus Christi cum devotione, cognovi quod deficiam in eo quod, extra illud tempus, non soleam me exercere in talibus desideriis. Propterea etiam fit tunc ut aliam gratiam non merear; sed nec illam tunc quam vellem et desi- derarem, cognoscere ac sentire id quod ago. Hoc itaque perinde est ac si quis ante prandium non curaverit conservare et quaerere appetitum comedendi, et tamen, dum est in mensa, incipit dolere quod non habeat appetitum; vel sicut contingeret si quis esset accepturus aliquos pretiosos liquores, qui aliqua certa hora debent dari apud aliquam personam, afferentibus vasa munda et offerentibus; et haec persona non recordetur lavare suum vas, quousque videat tempus illud dandi; quod si tune inciperet illud lavare, et interim praeteriret qpportunitas recipiendi talem liquòrem, ita esset necessarium expectare usque ad aliam horam, et interim non jam reddere mundum vas suum, sed conservare illud ita et praeparare illud melius, ad accipiendum talem liquorem in tempore opportuno.
units.en: In the same way at Mass, when I desired to savour the body of Christ with devotion, I recognized my failure in this, that outside that time I am not wont to exercise myself in such desires. For this reason too it comes about that I do not then deserve further grace — nor even that which I would then wish and desire, namely to know and feel what I am doing. It is just as if someone before dinner took no care to preserve and seek an appetite for eating, and yet, when he is at table, begins to grieve that he has no appetite; or as it would fall out if someone were to receive certain precious liquors, which at a fixed hour are to be given out at a certain person's house to those who bring clean vessels; and this person does not remember to wash his vessel until he sees the hour of giving at hand; and if he then began to wash it, and meanwhile the opportunity of receiving the liquor passed by, he would have to wait until another hour — and meanwhile not merely make his vessel clean again, but keep it so, and prepare it better, to receive the liquor at the fitting time.

units.la: Dum seme] multum dolerem quia non poteram adorare Jesum Christum quemadmodum tres Reges Magi, nec flere ut Magdalena, nec mereri: audire multa verba consolatoria, quae Christus in hoc mundo dixit, responsum fuit mihi redditum, dicens quod non feceram nec praeparaveram ani- mam meam quemadmodum tres Reges Magi, qui profecti fuerant ex tanta proprietate, relinquentes propriam patriam et omnia bona usque ad oblationem. Et ita veniebat, super alia omnia, notitia dispositionis in qua ibant personae illae quibus Jesus Christus similes gratias concedebat; et videbam clarissime qualiter multum gauderem si audirem illa verba: Remittuntur tibi peccata; imo illa: Hodie mecum eris in paradisô; non considerans quam longe sım ab ea dispositione in qua tales personae inveniebantur; et qualiter nunquam vere desideraverim inveniri in eo statu in quo tunc bonus latro erat in cruce; nec in aliquo simili actu illius quem fecit Magdalena plorans in convivio; nunquamque senserim talem laborem, propter caecitatem meam spiritualem, qualem senserat caecus corporaliter suam forsitan; etsi fides non deficiat mihi impetrandi gratiam spiritualis visionis. Et sic de aliis infirmitatibus spiritualibus, comparando illas corporalibus, quas Christus Dominus, qui labores ac dolores patientium et compatientium et fidem illorum considerat, sanabat et quotidie sanare solet, cernens cum illius suae pietatis oculis et charitatis visceribus omnium necessitates.
units.en: Once, when I grieved much because I could not adore Jesus Christ as the three Magi Kings did, nor weep like Magdalen, nor deserve to hear the many words of consolation which Christ spoke in this world, an answer was given me, saying that I had not done, nor prepared my soul, as the three Magi Kings, who had set out from such great possessions, leaving their own country and all their goods, even to the offering of gifts. And so there came, above all else, a knowledge of the disposition in which those persons went to whom Jesus Christ granted such graces; and I saw most clearly how greatly I should rejoice to hear those words: Your sins are forgiven you; nay, those others: Today you shall be with me in paradise — without considering how far I am from the disposition in which such persons were found, and how I have never truly desired to be found in the state in which the good thief then was on the cross, nor in any act like that which Magdalen did, weeping at the banquet; and how I have never felt, for my spiritual blindness, such distress as the bodily blind man perhaps felt for his — though faith does not fail me of obtaining the grace of spiritual sight. And so of the other spiritual infirmities, comparing them with the bodily ones which Christ the Lord healed, and daily is wont to heal — he who considers the toils and griefs of the suffering and the compassionate, and their faith, beholding with the eyes of his tenderness and the bowels of his charity the needs of all.

units.la: In festo beatae Mariae ad Nives, novi qualiter Dominus Noster, per aliquot praeteritos dies, sustinuerat me in quodam continuo fastidio, quia non inveniebam devotionem in orationibus et meditationibus; excitans in me, super omnia alia desideria temporalia, desiderium eum inveniendi. Magna enim merces videbatur mihi esse, non intrare in me solita fastidia vel desideria, quae mihi praedictum desiderium auferrent inveniendi devotionem animae meae in Deo meo et Domino Jesu Christo. In hoc enim videbam quod Jesus Christus incipiebat mihi gratiam concedere ordinandi animam meam, ut prima desideria cordis mei sint in eo quod est principale et primum; hoc est, quod semel sedeant in primo loco perfectae curae inveniendi Deum Dominum Nostrum in propria anima, mediantibus principalibus exercitiis ab hominibus habitis, quae sunt via immediata ad quaerendum et inveniendum Dominum meum Jesum Christum, id est oratio, et contemplatio, et super omnia missa.
units.en: On the feast of blessed Mary of the Snows I learned how Our Lord, through some days past, had sustained me in a certain continual weariness, because I found no devotion in prayers and meditations; stirring up in me, above all other temporal desires, the desire of finding him. For it seemed to me a great reward that the accustomed wearinesses or desires did not enter me, such as would take from me that desire of finding devotion for my soul in my God and Lord Jesus Christ. For in this I saw that Jesus Christ was beginning to grant me the grace of ordering my soul, so that the first desires of my heart might be set on what is principal and first; that is, that the perfect care of finding God Our Lord in one's own soul might once for all sit in the first place, by means of the principal exercises men have — which are the immediate way of seeking and finding my Lord Jesus Christ, namely prayer, and contemplation, and above all the Mass.

units.la: In die Transfigurationis, inveniens me maestum admodum quod noninvenerim devotionem, consolatus sum' me, cognoscens qualiter ejusmodi a a a i tristitia durabat jam multos per dies, et quod aliud nullum desiderium nec tristitia me potuerat a mei cordis intimis alienare et extrahere; quemadmodum fere semper contigerat, quando inveniens me paenis affectum, vel aliquo desiderio moderato inveniendi Deum, statim relinqguebam in me penetrare alud desiderium vel tristitiam, verbi gratia, super aedificationem proximi; vel habendi aliquod bonum nuntium, vel signa quibus Dei cultus circa proximos nostros crescerėt; vel contristabam me de aliquibus tentationibus peccatorum et imperfectionum mearum; et ita contingebat quod tales tristiti auferebant mihi meliorem třñistitiam, quae recta propter Deum erat. Ideo clare mihi visum est in hoc die, quod tanto majus beneficium mihi concedebat, quanto minus me deserebat tristitia, et desiderium hoc inveniendi eum me relinquebat; et quanto magis dilataretur et cresceret in latum, longum et profundum, nec relinquens eam tristitiam perdere per medium alterius inferioris. Notabam etiam hic gratiam quamdam animae meae, nec parvi faciebàm; hoc est qualiter nun- quam me invenissem tam exaltati cordis ad alia desideria et paenas quae mihi venire solebant, super prosperum adversumvye temporalem ani- marum profectum, tanquam qui a me fieri deberet; et quando inveniebam abundantiam aliquam in tali materia, ita me ipsum consolabar, quemadmodum in adversitate tristabar. Nunc videbatur mihi quod nulla prosperitas in nulla materia posset me consolari, nisi Dominus Noster mihi dederit aliquam abundantiam devotionis in Deum et Sanctos ejus directam; nec me aliquis maeror posset penetrare, qui constet ex paucitate eorum quae mihi ad agendum offeruntur.
units.en: On the day of the Transfiguration, finding myself very sorrowful that I had found no devotion, I consoled myself with recognizing how this sadness had now lasted many days, and that no other desire or sadness had been able to estrange me and draw me out from the depths of my heart; whereas almost always it had happened before that, when I found myself touched by pain, or by some moderate desire of finding God, I straightway allowed another desire or sadness to penetrate me — for example, over the edification of my neighbour, or the wish to have some good news, or signs by which the worship of God might grow among our neighbours; or I saddened myself over certain temptations of my sins and imperfections; and so it came about that such sadnesses took from me the better sadness, which was right and for God's sake. Therefore it appeared clear to me on this day that he was granting me a benefit the greater, the less that sadness left me and the desire of finding him remained; and the more it might be enlarged and grow in breadth, length and depth, not letting that sadness be lost through the intrusion of another and lower one. I noted here also a certain grace of my soul, and did not make little of it: namely, that I had never found myself so lifted of heart above the other desires and pains which used to come to me over the prosperous or adverse temporal progress of souls, as though it had to be wrought by me; and when I found some abundance in such matters, I used to console myself with it, just as in adversity I sorrowed. Now it seemed to me that no prosperity in any matter could console me, unless Our Lord should give me some abundance of devotion directed towards God and his Saints; nor could any grief penetrate me arising from the fewness of the things offered me to do.

units.la: Benedictus Dominus qui tot vias habet ad nos parumper, qui saltare non valemus, ad perfec- tionem et sui notitiam ducendos, quam tot genera timoris, maeroris et odii praecedere debent, super his omnibus infinitis creaturis, in quibus non est pax, quanquam sint media ad ascendendum ad amorem Dei, ut in eo omnino ingressi gaudeamus. Cum ex seipso egreditur homo, ad ipsum ingreditur et pascua invenit intus et foris; ita ut etiam reverti possit, inventa hac via alia quae ab amore incipit, in regionėm suam, a qua per viam timoris et multorum periculorum venerat biis aai et pervenerat ad acquirendum Dei amorem summum; ante quem amorem non poterat nisi ascendere et sursum aspicere. Ubi autem intraverit in amorem cordialem Dei, tunc poterit in eodem semper crescére, penetrando quotidie plura in ipso Deo; et poterit etiam magis tuto descendere ad proximos videndos.
units.en: Blessed be the Lord, who has so many ways of leading us — who cannot leap — step by step to perfection and to the knowledge of himself; before which so many kinds of fear, grief and hatred must go, concerning all these infinite creatures in which there is no peace, although they are means for ascending to the love of God, that entering wholly into him we may rejoice. When a man goes out of himself, he enters into Him, and finds pastures within and without; so that he can even return — having found this other way, which begins from love — into his own country, from which by the way of fear and many dangers he had come, and had attained to the supreme love of God; before which love he could only climb and look upward. But when he has entered into the heartfelt love of God, then he will be able ever to grow in it, penetrating daily further into God himself; and he will also be able more safely to descend, to look upon his neighbours.

units.la: Deus mihi et omnibus fratribus, sed ete cunctis viventibus viris et mulieribus, talem charitatem donet. Fateor enim me ab ipsa longe adhuc abesse; ab ipsa, inquam, id est a tanta: non enim mihi conscius sum me extra omnem charitatem esse, sicut nec extra Christi Domini gratiam. Sed est alia ratio Christi in quantum ipse est via, alia in quantum ipse est veritas, et alia in quantum ipse est vita. Et alia est ea quae dicitur via purgativa, alia quae dicitur illuminativa, ala quae dicitur perfectiva; sicut alii sunt incipientes, alii proficientes, et alii perfecti: quanquam in charitate omnes esse possint. Sed aliud quoque est, ut ita dicam, esse in charitate, aliud vivere in charitate, et aliud manere in charitate. Incipientes habent charitatem, in quantum noscunt et odio habent peccata; pro- ficientes quoque ipsam habent, sub nomine cognitionis, et desiderii rerum divinarum, id est christianarum virtutum, in quibus in dies ascendere et crescere cupiunt; perfecti autem Illam habent et experiuntur in proprio nomine; in quantum vero ipsi jam amore moventur ad inquisitionem cognitionis Dei et ejus voluntatis, ad ipsam omnibus quibus possunt modis faciendam. In primis igitur charitas efficit ut ipsi peccatis adversentur. propriis, et ut ipsa expellantur; in secundis, ut ipsas virtutes quae desiderantur acquirere nitantur; in ultimis vero facit ut cognitione immediata ipsius Dei et amore crescere affectent, et quidquid fecerint vel dixerint, vel cogitaverint, ex amore tanquam ex proprio quodam principio procedat. Quemadmodum etiam ipsi incipientes ad omnia opera sua bona principium primum habent odium peccati; et proficientes desiderium virtutum quibus ornari possint. Primi expoliare seipsos et veterem hominem satagunt incipientes; ' proficientes vestire se volunt, per quotidianum cultum; perfecti vero quaerunt apparere in veste nuptiali. Notandum tamen interea est quod in quolibet istorum trium generum hominum sunt tres ordines, ita ut etiam possimus dicere quosdam perfectos esse incipientes, quosdam proficientes, et quosdam perfectos; et ita in aliis duobus generibus suo modo dicatur; quia in quolibet genere sunt principium, medium et finis.
units.en: May God grant such charity to me and to all my brethren, and indeed to all living men and women. For I confess that I am still far from it — from it, I mean, in such measure; for I am not conscious of being outside all charity, as neither outside the grace of Christ the Lord. But there is one aspect of Christ inasmuch as he is the way, another inasmuch as he is the truth, and another inasmuch as he is the life. And there is one way which is called purgative, another which is called illuminative, another which is called perfective; as some are beginners, some progressing, and some perfect — though all can be in charity. But it is one thing, so to speak, to be in charity, another to live in charity, and another to abide in charity. Beginners have charity in so far as they know and hate their sins; the progressing have it too, under the name of knowledge and desire of divine things, that is, of christian virtues, in which they long to climb and grow daily; but the perfect have it and experience it under its own name, inasmuch as they are now moved by love itself to seek the knowledge of God and of his will, and to do it by every means they can. In the first, then, charity brings it about that they set themselves against their own sins, and that these are driven out; in the second, that they strive to acquire the virtues they desire; in the last, it makes them long to grow in the immediate knowledge and love of God himself, and whatever they do or say or think proceeds from love as from its own proper principle. Just so the beginners have, as the first principle of all their good works, the hatred of sin; and the progressing, the desire of the virtues with which they may be adorned. The first, the beginners, busy themselves with stripping themselves of the old man; the progressing wish to clothe themselves, by daily cultivation; but the perfect seek to appear in the wedding garment. It should be noted meanwhile that in each of these three kinds of men there are three ranks, so that we may even say that some are perfect beginners, some progressing, and some perfect; and so in the other two kinds in their own manner; for in every kind there are a beginning, a middle, and an end.

units.la: In die quo celebrabam festum sancti Patris Dominici, communicando in missa, ego habui magnum desiderium sub his verbis: Utinam omnia interiora mea, maxime cor, ita cede- rent Christo intranti, quod aperirentur, lccum ipsi in centro cordis relinquendo; vitia autem omnia sic fugarentur a facie ipsius, sicut cera a facie ignis fluit. Ante missam quoque, faciendo solitum discursum mysteriorum Christi, datus est mihi magnus sensus in eo ut peterem, per intercessionem sancti Dominici, gratias super mysteria, conformiter ad ea quae circa quodlibet mysterium sensit, dum viveret, et intellexit ipse Dominicus, contemplando super illa mysteria. Rogabam igitur ipsum ut intercederet ad Christum annuntiatum, ad Christum visitatorem, etc.
units.en: On the day when I celebrated the feast of the holy Father Dominic, communicating at Mass, I had a great desire under these words: Would that all my inward parts, above all my heart, might so yield to Christ entering that they would open, leaving him a place in the centre of the heart; and that all vices might so flee from his face as wax flows before the face of fire. Before Mass also, making the accustomed round of the mysteries of Christ, a great feeling was given me in asking, through the intercession of Saint Dominic, graces upon the mysteries, in conformity with what Dominic himself, while he lived, felt and understood about each mystery, contemplating those mysteries. I prayed him therefore to intercede with Christ announced, with Christ the visitor, and so on.

units.la: Eodem die, dum irem per vicos et non habe- I w RATETA FETE PEONES A N E rem laetıtiam super his quae occurrebant ad a visum, quin potius distractiones et tentationes vanitatum aut malarum cogitationum, unde se- quebatur tristitia, in me ego habui hoc respon- sum: Non modo non.debes tristis fieri, ex eo quod non invenis pacem in rebus istis, sed de hoc, in gratia gaudere debes. Tristari potius oportet quod non invenias pacem, et commoda, et consolationem, in vacationibus et exercitiis, et in conversatione illa quae in celis est. Multi sane reperiuntur qui non essent admodum anxii de conversatione quae in caelis est, si pacem invenirent faciliorem in ea quae in mundo cernitur. Ergo mentis oculi et aures, et intentiones omnium sensuum, sint ad res coeaelestes, ubi visus nihil videre potest quod non aedificet el consoletur, nec aures audire. Hic autem statim videres, siquidem libere velles aspicere omnia quae occurrunt, videres, inquam, actus et gestus hominum: et statim audires verba vana, aut scandalosa: hic non vides nisi jocosa, jucunda, ludicra, turpia, nihil serium, nihil grave, ad laudem Dei faciens; joci autem et risus et lusus ipsi in rebus pessimis sunt. Si quis igitur variis ten- tationibus ab istis prohibetur, et ad medi- tanda et desideranda caeoelestia quodammodo adigatur, is gloriam Deo det, qui non vult ipsum permittere cogitare perniciosa, nec vana, nec esse otiosum, nec vacantem.
units.en: On the same day, while I went through the streets and had no gladness in the things that met my sight, but rather distractions and temptations of vanities or evil thoughts, whence followed sadness, I had in myself this answer: Not only ought you not to be sad because you find no peace in these things, but you ought in grace to rejoice at it. You should rather be sad that you do not find peace, and comfort, and consolation in the free times and exercises, and in that conversation which is in heaven. Many indeed are found who would not be very anxious about the conversation which is in heaven, if they found an easier peace in that which is seen in the world. Therefore let the eyes and ears of the mind, and the intentions of all the senses, be towards heavenly things, where sight can see nothing that does not edify and console, nor the ears hear such. But here you would at once see — if indeed you chose to look freely at everything that meets you — you would see, I say, the acts and gestures of men, and at once hear vain or scandalous words: here you see nothing but jesting, amusing, playful, base things — nothing serious, nothing grave, making for the praise of God; and the jests and laughter and games themselves are about the worst of things. If anyone, then, is kept from these by various temptations, and in a manner driven to meditate on and desire heavenly things, let him give glory to God, who will not allow him to think pernicious or vain thoughts, nor to be idle or unoccupied.
