units.la: In festo sanctorum Cyriaci, Largi et Smaragdi, ego habui desiderium magnum uť Dominus Noster vellet mihi concedere, propter merita vitae, passionis et gloriae suae, quod missa valeret efficaciter pro animabus mortuorum in purgatorio commorantibus, perinde ac si ego offerrem eam cum omnibus desideriis, orationibus, suspiriis, angustiis et gratiarum actionibus, quae habet unaquaeque animarum in purgatorio pro seipsa, non valens proficere in illis ad sui ipsius remedium. Hoc, inquam, quod dico, erat desiderium quoddam quod mihi erat, ut Dominus Noster daret mihi sentire, pro unaquaque animarum harum, juxta meum posse, tantum ac ipsae sentiunt in cogitatione propriorum peccatorum, et beneficiorum a Deo acceptorum. Et non valens ego nec merens ejusmodi gratiam, optabam ut sacrificium et intercessio omnium beatorum, praecipue eorum quorum festum eo die celebrabatur, supplerent.
units.en: On the feast of Saints Cyriacus, Largus and Smaragdus I had a great desire that Our Lord would grant me, for the merits of his life, passion and glory, that the Mass might avail efficaciously for the souls of the dead dwelling in purgatory, just as if I offered it with all the desires, prayers, sighs, anguishes and thanksgivings which each of the souls in purgatory has for itself, being unable to profit by them for its own remedy. This, I say, was a certain desire I had: that Our Lord would give me to feel, for each of these souls, according to my capacity, as much as they themselves feel in the thought of their own sins and of the benefits received from God. And being unable and undeserving of such a grace, I wished that the sacrifice and the intercession of all the blessed, especially of those whose feast was celebrated that day, might supply it.

units.la: Eodem die, venit mihi in mentem res quaedam quam saepe alias senseram, hoc est qualiter sit efficax, et ad rem admodum pertinens, pro animabus quae in purgatorio sunt, quod quando Christum oramus pro eis, repraesentetur ipsi et offeratur charitas illa et compassio ex qua verbum illud procedebat: Hodie mecum eris in paradiso. Anima fidelis quae in purgatorio est, recte esse potest in comparatione, ad minimum quoad plures earum, constituta in majore necessitate quam latro, cui praedicta verba dicta sunt a Domino qui erat in cruce: et qualiter (sint ad rem pertinentia) septem illa verba quae Christus pendens dixit; quandoquidem incessanter ipsae animae proferunt similia illorum verba, hoc est rogando pro inimicis in hoc mundo relictis; rogando pro amicis et debitoribus ut provideatur eis, et in omnibus eorum necessitas suppleatur, dolendo etiam super eorum incredibilia mala et tormenta; habendo etiam continuo viscera charitatis aperta, ad faciendum pro eis quod vis bonum, si possent, et sitim spi- ritualem continuam super bonum successum omnium animarum, quae in hac vita sunt, praecipue suorum sociorum. Vellent similiter semper posse dicere: Consummatum est, et similiter liberari e manibus et potestate illorum tormentorum infernalium, et ingredi ad potestatem omnipotentis Dei Palris aeterni et gloriosi.
units.en: On the same day there came into my mind something I had often felt at other times: how efficacious it is, and very much to the point, for the souls that are in purgatory, that when we pray Christ for them there be represented and offered to him that charity and compassion from which proceeded the word: Today you shall be with me in paradise. The faithful soul in purgatory may rightly be reckoned — at least as regards many of them — to stand in greater need than the thief to whom those words were spoken by the Lord as he hung on the cross; and how much to the point are those seven words which Christ spoke as he hung there — seeing that those souls unceasingly utter the like of them: praying for the enemies they left in this world; praying for their friends and debtors, that provision be made for them and all their need supplied; grieving too over their own unbelievable pains and torments; keeping also the bowels of charity continually open, to do them any good they could, if they were able; and a continual spiritual thirst for the good success of all souls that are in this life, chiefly of their own companions. They would likewise wish to be able to say at last: It is finished — and likewise to be freed from the hands and power of those infernal torments, and to enter into the power of the almighty God, the eternal and glorious Father.

units.la: In vigilia sancti Laurentii, quae état dies sancti Romani Martyris, ante missam, mihi venit desiderium petendi gratiam contra omnes distractiones; eo modo ut quaererem a Domino gratiam, ut possem esse dominus et moderator mearum propriarum cogitationum et desideriorum; quia tune satis eram distractus. Inveni itaque satis magnam gratiam, faciendo discursum solitum, maxime vero dum peterem hujusmodi gratiam per eas passiones quas Christus Dominus habuit, dum anima ipsius tristis erat in agone, et dum erat in cruce dicens: Deus meus, Deus meus! ut quid dereliquisti me? Ad majorem quoque gratiam, mihi occurrit idem per sacratissimam gratiam Christi quae fuit in unione illa hypostatica. In missa, quum vel- lem communicare, cum magna devotione roga- bam Dominum ut me peccatorem dignaretur vocare et recipere ad se, et mihi dimittere peccata mea et mecum manducare.
units.en: On the vigil of Saint Laurence, which was the day of Saint Romanus the martyr, before Mass there came to me the desire of asking grace against all distractions; in this way, that I sought from the Lord the grace to be lord and master of my own thoughts and desires, for at that time I was much distracted. I found, then, a good measure of grace, making the accustomed round, and above all when I asked this grace through those sufferings which Christ the Lord bore when his soul was sorrowful in the agony, and when he was on the cross, saying: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? For yet greater grace, the same came to me through the most sacred grace of Christ which was in the hypostatic union. At Mass, when I was about to communicate, I begged the Lord with great devotion that he would deign to call me, a sinner, and receive me to himself, and forgive me my sins, and eat with me.

units.la: Quum finissem missam et ea quae leguntur, veniendo per vicum ad domum, sensi satis magnam gratiam, in eo quod recordabar satis particulariter et reflectebar super dicta missa percurrendo singulas partes ejus. Dabatur quoque animus ad ita excolendam memoriam super exercitiis factis in rebus spiritualibus; et rogabam Dominum ut, sicut tam saepe accidit me distrahi ex memoria et reflexione super aliis exercitiis, et negotiis, et actionibus, sive colloquiis ac cogitationibus rerum aliquarum non immediate ad Deum tendentium, ita etiam in orationibus et contemplationibus fieret spiritualibus; ut scilicet reflecti possem ab illa vehementi quadam inhaesione. Hoc autem spero futurum, quum non tam inordinati affectus erunt et actus, quam adhuc inordinati sunt. Inordinatio, quantum ad hoc, est inhaerere miņus et affici ad illa, quia non sunt ex toto corde, tota anima, tota mente, et omnibus viribus, ubique et. semper. Dum enim hic affectus, qui jam est vera charitas, totum cor et spiritum nostrum possederit ubique et semper, tunc caetera omnia ordinem tranquillitatis, id est, pacem assequentur, et sequentur usque eo ubi non turbantur intellectus, memoria et voluntas, et reliqua omnia. Sed hoc erit in patria Beatorum, ad quam quotidie ascendimus. i Eadem vigilia sancti Laurentii, post fficium completorii, accessit Dominus Joannes a sua peregrinatione rediens, scilicet Golonia. Ex cujus reditu Dominus Noster talem consolationem mihi dedit, qualem nunquam sensi; maxime quod Dominus Noster conservavit me, quod Dominus Noster liberavit me, ne commoverer spiritu, propter gaudium adventus ejus, et propter desiderium alloquendi et audiendi aliquid, nimirum nuntium spirituale, quemadmodum antea solebam, ita ut mihi auferret devotionem orationis vel contemplationis. =- Hic immediate sensi animam ulterius progredi ad Dominum Deum Nostrum, cum quibusdam profundis actionibus gratiarum, quiescendo quietissime in ipsis; nec commovebar animo ad com- municandum aliquid cum peregrino praedicto.
units.en: When I had finished Mass and the prayers that are read, coming home through the street I felt a good measure of grace, in that I remembered quite particularly and reflected upon the Mass I had said, running through its several parts. A mind was also given me so to cultivate the memory over the exercises performed in spiritual things; and I prayed the Lord that, as it so often happens that I am drawn away by the memory of, and reflection upon, other exercises and affairs and actions, or conversations and thoughts of things not tending immediately to God, so it might also come to pass in spiritual prayers and contemplations: that is, that I might be able to reflect back out of that vehement clinging. And this I hope will come to be, when my affections and acts are not so inordinate as they still are. Inordinateness, in this regard, is to cling less to those things, and be less affected towards them, because they are not from the whole heart, the whole soul, the whole mind, and all one's strength, everywhere and always. For when this affection, which is now true charity, has possessed our whole heart and spirit everywhere and always, then all the rest will attain the order of tranquillity, that is, peace; and will follow even to the point where intellect, memory and will, and all the rest, are not disturbed. But this will be in the fatherland of the Blessed, to which we daily ascend. On the same vigil of Saint Laurence, after the office of compline, Don Juan arrived, returning from his pilgrimage, that is from Cologne. At his return Our Lord gave me such consolation as I never felt; above all that Our Lord kept me, that Our Lord freed me from being stirred in spirit by the joy of his coming and by the desire of speaking with him and hearing something — namely his spiritual news — as I used to be before, in such a way as to rob me of the devotion of prayer or contemplation. Here I immediately felt my soul advance further towards the Lord Our God, with certain deep acts of thanksgiving, resting most quietly in them; nor was I moved in mind to communicate anything with the said pilgrim.

units.la: Itaque visum est mihi quod Dominus Noster per seipsum, cum sanctis suis, faciebat mihi celebrare festum super adventum istum, multo majori et meliori modo, sine aliqua comparatione, quam potuisset accidere, recipiendo consolationem meam humaniter, per viam praesentiae et colloquia totius prosperitatis spiritualis ex itinere.
units.en: And so it seemed to me that Our Lord by himself, with his saints, was making me celebrate a feast over that arrival, in a far greater and better way, beyond all comparison, than could have come about by taking my consolation in a human way, through his presence and through conversation about all the spiritual prosperity of the journey.

units.la: Discursus datus mihi fuit a Domino, ad gratiarum actionem per viam litaniarum, rogando Patrem ut benediceret Filio et Spiritui Sancto, et Filum ut benediceret Patri et Spiritui Sancto, et Spiritum Sanctum ut benediceret Patri et Filio. Eodem modo rogabam virginem Mariam ut daret gratias, sanctissimae et individuae Trinitati, propter omnes favores et dona nobis ex sui intercessione communicata, et quod sancta Trinitas benediceret Virgini; et eodem modo procedebam in aliis.
units.en: A round of prayer was given me by the Lord for thanksgiving by way of the litanies: begging the Father to bless the Son and the Holy Spirit, and the Son to bless the Father and the Holy Spirit, and the Holy Spirit to bless the Father and the Son. In the same way I begged the Virgin Mary to give thanks to the most holy and undivided Trinity for all the favours and gifts communicated to us by her intercession, and that the holy Trinity would bless the Virgin; and in the same way I proceeded with the others.

units.la: Rogabam eodem modo pro omnibus qui aliquid boni contulerant ipsi Domino Joanni per quodvis medium; idem faciebam pro illis qui fuerant in causa ut aliquid recepisset; et specialiter etiam agebam gratias sanctis tribus Regi- bus Magis et sanctae Ursulae.
units.en: I prayed in the same way for all who had conferred any good on Don Juan by any means; and I did the same for those who had been the cause of his receiving anything; and in particular I gave thanks to the holy three Magi Kings and to Saint Ursula.

units.la: In festivitate divi Laurentii, mane admodum, eodem modo discurri, per omnia mysteria, super gratiarum actionibus in omni loco secundum rem et materiam hujusmodi; et ingens quoddam sensi et inexplicabile desiderium, quod missa suppleret et valeret applicatim et efficaciter, loco omnium laborum quos oporteret nos, accipere in quaerendis omnibus calendariis omnium episcopatuum particulariter, ad honorandum nominatim omnes sanctos quorum collectae in eis inveniuntur; qui sancti sunt quaedam opera jam praecipua, facta divinis operantibus manibus. Sensi etiam majorem quam dici potest fidem, super multum adjutorium quod Dominus Noster nunquam deficiet mihi dare ac universae Societati per medium sanctorum suorum.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Laurence, very early, I made the same round through all the mysteries, with thanksgivings at every point according to the matter in hand; and I felt a certain vast and inexpressible desire that the Mass might supply for, and avail in place of, all the labours we should have to undertake in searching out all the calendars of all the dioceses one by one, in order to honour by name all the saints whose collects are found in them — which saints are, as it were, chief works already wrought by the divine hands at work. I felt also a greater faith than can be told concerning the great help which Our Lord will never fail to give me, and the whole Society, by means of his saints.

units.la: In illo versu etiam sensi multum spiritum, in eo scilicet quod dicitur: Adjuva me et salvus ero et meditabor in omnibus justificationibus tuis. Super Pater Noster, in missa, dum dicerem: Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie, venit mihi intrinsecus quoddam desiderium, quod scilicet Pater noster coelestis daret mihi ut sentirem, qualiter ipse det mihi panem animae et corporis; et ego dicebam: Domine, fac me sentire Eu tu das panem istum, qui mihi est Filius tuus.
units.en: In that verse too I felt much spirit, namely where it is said: Help me, and I shall be saved, and I will meditate on all thy justifications. At the Our Father in the Mass, when I said: Give us this day our daily bread, there came to me inwardly a certain desire: that our heavenly Father would grant me to feel how he gives me the bread of soul and body; and I said: Lord, make me feel that thou givest that bread, which for me is thy Son.

units.la: Eodem die, habui bonum quoddam desiderium, ut scilicet possem recordari semper ut quotidie commendarem me Domino Deo Nostro, et omni modo ei supplicationes facerem, accipiens ad hujus rei favorem in Christo Domino et Redemptore nostro, favorem Spiritus Sancti, Virginis Mariae, boni mei Angeli et sancti eodem die concurrentis.
units.en: On the same day I had a certain good desire: namely, that I might always remember to commend myself daily to the Lord Our God, and to make supplications to him in every way, taking in favour of this, in Christ our Lord and Redeemer, the favour of the Holy Spirit, of the Virgin Mary, of my good Angel, and of the saint falling on that day.

units.la: In festivate sancti Tiburtii et sanctae Susannae, antequam irem ad missam, oblatae mihi fuerunt personae quae magis faverant Domino Joanni in ejus peregrinatione, ubi habui magnam devotionem rogando Dominum Nostrum ut unicuique earum personarum faveret secundum opera earum, utendo et sua liberalitate et misericordia. Providebam etiam opera et verba, et benevolentiam interiorem; hoc est, qualiter aliqui, dum ei eleemosýmam facerent, operati erant aliquid boni; alii, quando ipsum ducebant per iter ne erraret; alii loquendo ei cum suavitate, alii con-. gratulantes ei; et ita offerebantur mihi bona desideria pro dictis personis.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Tiburtius and Saint Susanna, before I went to Mass, there were set before me the persons who had most favoured Don Juan in his pilgrimage; and I had great devotion, begging Our Lord to favour each of those persons according to their works, using both his liberality and his mercy. I also called to mind their works and words and inward good will: that is, how some, in giving him alms, had wrought something good; others, when they guided him on the way lest he go astray; others by speaking to him with gentleness, others by rejoicing with him; and so good desires were offered me for the said persons.

units.la: Nec omittebam orare pro ipsis in quibus Dominus Joannes nihil invenerat nisi rigorem et fastidium; et videbatur mihi quod piissimus Jesus velit similes personas aliquando demonstrari et cognosci, maxime ab illis qai aliquid charitatis habent, ut postea pro ipsis orent, dando eis exemplum humilitatis et patientiae ad eorum aedificationem, quemadmodum ipsiostendunt eis probationem justitiae quam unusquisque sanctorum meretur. Ideo voluit Dominus Noster Jesus Christus quod major crudelitas quam quae unquam visa fuit, sibi ipsi fieret, quia ipse talis erat ut posset juvare et aedificare melius tales personas et efficacius orare pro ipsis, considerando qualiter indigeant exemplo majoris humilitatis, aut patientiae et charitatis, quam usquam inveniremus: ideo esset melius semper ut pessimi quique essent apud optimos; ut unusquisque cum aliorum adjutorio posset melius proficere, dum observaret semper bonus regulam suam; quae est ut, quanto majorem rigorem justitiae contra se senserit, tanto ipse sit liberalior bonitate et misericordia.
units.en: Nor did I omit to pray for those in whom Don Juan had found nothing but harshness and disdain; and it seemed to me that the most loving Jesus wills that such persons should sometimes be pointed out and known, above all by those who have some charity, so that they may afterwards pray for them, giving them an example of humility and patience for their edification, even as those others show them the proof of the justice which each of the saints deserves. Therefore Our Lord Jesus Christ willed that a greater cruelty than was ever seen should be done to himself, because he was such that he could better help and edify such persons, and pray for them more efficaciously, considering how they need an example of greater humility, or patience and charity, than we should anywhere find: therefore it were always better that the worst men should be with the best, that each with the others' help might make better progress — the good man always keeping his rule, which is that the greater the rigour of justice he feels against himself, the more liberal let him be in goodness and mercy.

units.la: Et orans in quodam sacello sancti Joannis, in quo ego iterum oraveram, orando Dominum pro domo illa, venit mihi vehemens quoddam desiderium, ut quidquid desiderabam ad utilitatem illius domus et personarum in ea habitantium, propter misericordiam Dei Domini Nostri, accederet omnibus domibus et personis totius civitatis; et quod Dominus Noster ex sua pietate sic hoc confirmaret, ac si ego habitarem in singulis illis domibus.
units.en: And praying in a certain chapel of Saint John, in which I had prayed before, praying the Lord for that house, there came to me a vehement desire that whatever I desired for the profit of that house and of the persons dwelling in it might, by the mercy of God Our Lord, come to all the houses and persons of the whole city; and that Our Lord of his tenderness would confirm this, as though I dwelt in every one of those houses.

units.la: Eodem modo habui aliquas gratiarum actiones cognoscens beneficia Domini Nostri, agens ei gratias pro omnibus operibus, verbis et spiritibus nominatis in creatione: item pro omnibus operibus, verbis et spiritibus qui expressi sunt in nostra Redemptione; et finaliter pro omnibus verbis, operibus et spiritibus particulariter omnium illorum qui jam mihi noti sunt, ad utilitatem et consolationem mei.
units.en: In the same way I had certain thanksgivings, acknowledging the benefits of Our Lord: giving him thanks for all the works, words and spirits named in creation; likewise for all the works, words and spirits expressed in our Redemption; and finally for all the words, works and spirits, in particular, of all those who are now known to me, for my profit and consolation.

units.la: Eodem die, nescio qualiter, -coepi habere magnam devotionem, dum aliquid boni a Deo peterem pro me, et pro vivis et pro mortuis, ut Dominus Noster Deus omnipotens vellet id quod petebam conformare ad tantum affectum, perinde ac si ipse Redemptor Noster Jesus Christus id peteret, vel virgo Maria, vel hic, vel ille sanctus, vel animae quae cruciantur in Purgatorio. Et ad hoc veniebat devotio dicendi missam, quae tanti valoris est in seipsa, propter hostiam et sacrificium quae in ea offeruntur, ut nihil possimus petere quod justum sit, quin possimus impetrare par medium ipsius saçrificii in cruce facti.
units.en: On the same day — I know not how — I began to have great devotion, when I asked some good thing of God for myself, and for the living and the dead, that the Lord Our God almighty would conform what I asked to an affection as great as if our Redeemer Jesus Christ himself were asking it, or the Virgin Mary, or this or that saint, or the souls that are tormented in purgatory. And to this came the devotion of saying Mass, which is of such worth in itself, on account of the host and sacrifice offered in it, that we can ask nothing that is just without being able to obtain it by means of that sacrifice made on the cross.

units.la: Dominica in octava sancti Laurentii, habui quosdam notabiles sensus spirituales, dum dicerem matutinum dominicale; et ita oravı Dominum cum magno fervore, et sanctissimam Trinitatem, per gratiam Resurrectionis Domini, eo quod tunc fieret festum sanctissimae Trinitatis, ut vellet mihi dare specialem gratiam ad omnia officia Dominicalia; et quod in die Dominico mitteret mihi aliquod adjutorium, pro omnibus aliis festis ferialibus et sanctorum totius hebdomadae. Eodem modo feci hoc in missa, in principio, et fine et medio. Eodem die, habui similiter memoriam aliquorum punctorum quae alias senseram, et quorum jam oblitus eram, quae nunc notanda sunt: verbi gratia, ut ego orarem etdesiderarem, cum multa spe, ut Do- minus Noster, per suam bonitatem et patientiam, velit supplere omnibus meis defectibus; ita ut confusiones, quas saepe propter multas negligentias merui, non veniant mihi nisi quantum fuerint ad gloriam Dei et ad salvationem proximi; et quod spiritus maligni non habeant potestatem, quam ego mereor, super homines qui sentiunt meos defectus, vel vident ipsos, ut eos videlicet notent, et notabiliter contra gloriam Dei Domini mei et in damnum proximi sentiant ipsos. Nota hic, o anima mea, qualiter manifeste usa es talibus defectibus tantis in locis, coram tot hominibus, bonis et malis; qui defectus non fuerunt notati, nec aspecti fuerunt in: rigore justitiae. Ideo magis debes Domino Deo tuo, qui per se, et per medium orationum Sanctorum ejus et ministerium Angelorum ejus, non permittit, ut tuae res sinistro oculo aspiciantur, nec judicentur in rigore justitiae; maxime cum clarissime cognoscat quanta hucusque fecisti et locutus fuisti et dixisti, quae possènt et quidem deberent accipi in malam partem.
units.en: On the Sunday within the octave of Saint Laurence I had certain notable spiritual feelings while saying the Sunday matins; and so I prayed the Lord with great fervour, and the most holy Trinity — through the grace of the Lord's Resurrection, because the feast of the most holy Trinity was then kept — that he would give me special grace for all the Sunday offices; and that on the Lord's day he would send me some help for all the other ferial offices and feasts of saints of the whole week. In the same way I did this at Mass, at the beginning, the end and the middle. On the same day I likewise remembered certain points which I had felt at other times and had now forgotten, which are now to be noted: for example, that I should pray and desire, with much hope, that Our Lord, by his goodness and patience, would supply all my defects; so that the confusions which I have often deserved through many negligences may come upon me only in so far as they make for the glory of God and the salvation of my neighbour; and that the malignant spirits may not have the power, which I deserve, over the men who perceive my defects or see them — the power, that is, of making them note them, and take them notably against the glory of God my Lord and to the harm of their neighbour. Note here, O my soul, how openly you have shown such great defects in so many places, before so many men, good and bad; and those defects were not noted, nor looked upon in the rigour of justice. Therefore you owe the more to the Lord your God, who by himself, and by means of the prayers of his Saints and the ministry of his Angels, does not allow your affairs to be looked at with an evil eye, nor judged in the rigour of justice; especially since he knows most clearly how much you have hitherto done and spoken and said which could, and indeed ought to, be taken in bad part.

units.la: Eodem die, venit mihi in mentem quoddam speciale desiderium, quod Dominus Noster face- ret me sentire illud Glória in excelsis Deo Dominicale, et Kyrie eleison, dando mihi spiritum convenientem diei dominicali, id est, ipsius Domini.
units.en: On the same day there came into my mind a certain special desire: that Our Lord would make me feel the Sunday Gloria in excelsis Deo and the Kyrie eleison, giving me a spirit befitting the Lord's day — that is, of the Lord himself.

units.la: In vigilia Mariae, mense Augusti, cum dicerem officium sancti Hippolyti et sociorum ejus, perveniens ad illud: Sancta Concordia, cujus corpus fuit projectum in cloacas, et haustum ab illo sancto (Nicomede) cloacano; ad magnam consolationem sancti Justini sacerdotis; ego habui magnum spiritum compunctionis, considerans quod ille in suo officio faciebat rem sanctam et tam gratam Domino Deo Nostro. Unde venit mihi alter sensus in magnam utilitatem meam; et ita oravi, cum magna angustia, Matrem Domini mei, qui fructus ejus tam perfectus est, mihi impetraret gratiam ut possem et scirem servire cum perfecta voluntate Filio suo, in hoc meo officio sacerdotali, eo quod ille in suo officio tam humili et vili invenerit occasionem faciendi rem tanti momenti, in servitio Dei Nostri. Eodem modo rogabam pro omnibus officialibus cujuscumque conditionis, ut Domi- nus Noster det illis gratiam inveniendi occasio- E a E O nem, ut inter alia opera quae faciunt, possent aliquid facere in laudem Majestatis suae, vel immediato profectu animarum suàrum, vel in clara utilitate, vel in vera consolatione, vel in remedio necessitatis proximi sui, vivi aut mortu. Eodem modo in psalmo, Benedicite et Laudate, in laudibus, ego sensi magnam compunctionem, dante Domino mihi ut intelligerem et sentirem qualiter omnes creaturae serviunt ei cum effectu utilitatis, consolationis et remedii et necessitatis; sol illuminando, aqua refrigerando, ignis calefaciendo; et ego miserabilis nihil profectus faciebam, nec in ejus gloriam (nempe cum sim indevotus), nec in ejus cultum; item qualiter virgo Maria videbat fructus tam nobiles, tam notabiles in Annunciatione, in Visitatione, in Nativitate, videndo pastores elevatos ad tantam cognitionem, intelligens mysterium circumcisionis, videns reges adeo humiliatos; et ita rogabam ipsam ut tandem impetraret mihi gratiam concipiendi aliquem fructum, ut servus Filii sul, cum effectu alicujus rei. Et cum essem in tali desiderio, visum est mihi ac si intus me esset spes alicujus, qui vellet inservire magno alicui domino, tot annos serviens cum servis suis, et offerens seipsum in conspectu eorum, sperans ut, tandem appareat et videatur domino suo dignus qui admittatur pro praecipuo suo servo, declarando voluntatem suam ad id. Cum hoc, reprimebatur illud desiderium, humiliando me voluntati Christi Domini mei, qui solus scit ordinem mearum necessilatum et ea quae conveniunt nostrae saluti.
units.en: On the vigil of Mary, in the month of August, while saying the office of Saint Hippolytus and his companions, coming to the passage about Saint Concordia, whose body was thrown into the sewers and drawn out by that holy man of the sewers, Nicomedes, to the great consolation of the holy priest Justin, I had a great spirit of compunction, considering that he in his office was doing a thing holy and most pleasing to the Lord Our God. Whence another feeling came to me, to my great profit; and so I prayed, with great anguish, the Mother of my Lord, whose fruit is so perfect, to obtain for me the grace that I might be able, and know how, to serve her Son with a perfect will in this my priestly office — seeing that that man, in an office so humble and mean, found occasion to do a thing of such moment in the service of Our God. In the same way I prayed for all who hold offices of whatever condition, that Our Lord may give them grace to find occasion, among the other works they do, to do something to the praise of his Majesty, or to the immediate progress of their souls, or in manifest usefulness, or in true consolation, or in remedy of the need of their neighbour, living or dead. In the same way, at the psalm Benedicite and Laudate, at lauds, I felt great compunction, the Lord granting me to understand and feel how all creatures serve him with real effect of usefulness, consolation, remedy and need — the sun by giving light, water by cooling, fire by warming; and I, wretched man, was yielding no profit, neither to his glory (being indeed without devotion) nor to his worship. Likewise how the Virgin Mary saw fruits so noble and so notable at the Annunciation, at the Visitation, at the Nativity — seeing the shepherds raised to such knowledge, understanding the mystery of the circumcision, seeing kings so humbled; and so I prayed her that she would at last obtain for me the grace of conceiving some fruit, as a servant of her Son, with the effect of some real thing. And while I was in this desire, it seemed to me as though within me there were the hope of one who wished to serve some great lord, serving so many years among his servants, and offering himself in their sight, hoping that at last he may appear, and be seen by his lord, worthy to be admitted as his chief servant, the lord declaring his will to that end. With this, that desire was restrained, as I humbled myself to the will of Christ my Lord, who alone knows the order of my needs and what is fitting for our salvation.

units.la: In primis Vesperis Assumptionis, ego inveni tantam devotionem, dum essem in templo virginis Mariae de Spira, eo quod omnes caeremoniae, luminaria, organa, cantus, honor reliquiarum et ornamentorum, mihi dabant tantam devotionem quantam ego nescirem explicare. Cum illo spiritu, ego benedicebam illi qui candelas ibi posuerat, et collocaverat, et accenderat, et ordinaverat; et illi qui redditus ad hoc faciendum reliquerat, et eodem modo, organis et organistae, et fandatoribus; eodem modo, omnibus ornamentis quae ibi videbam ad cultum Domini esse collocata; item cantoribus et cantionibus puerorum qui canebant; et eodem modo reliquiariis, et illis qui reliquias quaesierant, vel E AO S O E o inveniendo eas honore decoraverant." ln summa dico quod ille spiritus erat cum quo ego existimabam magis minimum praedictorum et similium opus, cum fide catholica et simplici, quam mille gradus illius fidei otiose quam ita magnifaciunt qui sentiunt haeretice. Similiter sentiebam magnam bonitatem et misericordiam in Deo Domino Nostro, pro omnibus et singulis personarum illarum quae aliquid florum ponunt pro ipso cultu externo Dei et Sanctorum ejus, modo sit opus manuum suarum laborando, modo ponendo aliquid ex suis divitiis, modo suis verbis ordinando, vel aliquo alio modo.
units.en: At first Vespers of the Assumption I found such devotion, being in the church of the Virgin Mary at Speyer, because all the ceremonies, the lights, the organ, the chants, the honour of the relics and ornaments, gave me such devotion as I could not explain. With that spirit I blessed him who had placed the candles there, and set them up, and lit them, and ordered them; and him who had left revenues for the doing of it; and in the same way the organ and the organist, and the founders; in the same way all the ornaments which I saw placed there for the worship of the Lord; likewise the singers, and the singing of the boys who sang; and in the same way the reliquaries, and those who had sought out the relics, or, having found them, had adorned them with honour. In sum I say that that spirit was one with which I esteemed the least work of the aforesaid and the like, done with catholic and simple faith, more than a thousand degrees of that idle faith which they make so much of who think as heretics do. Likewise I felt great goodness and mercy in God Our Lord towards each and every one of those persons who contribute some flower to the outward worship of God and his Saints — whether it be the work of their hands in labour, or the giving of something from their riches, or the ordering of things by their words, or in any other way.

units.la: In festo virginis Mariae, tempore matutinorum, dum recitarem praedictum officium, idemque audiens dici in templo sub sacro à me facto, semper fui omnino in meipso, hoc est, sine ulla agitatione spiritus boni vel mali; ideo sentiebam propriam fragilitatėm et pondus meum in recitando, ut essem attentus. Nihilominus mihi postea visum est, licet perseverarm in eodem modo, quod proprium meum esse non tam humile et abjectum, tam incontinenter et sine ordine ac: alias inveniretur, quando hoc modo me deserebat Dominus Noster; hoc modo privatus eram alieno spiritu, et perseverans in meipso cum sufficientia ipsius tamen gratiae. Placeat Domino Nostro dare mihi gratiam ut ego possim quotidie crescere, ut fiam capacius vas, continentius et mundius; ut sit in seipso paratum ad non admittendos malos spiritus et ad recipiendos bonos. Sic recordatus sum et notavi qualiter, quasi per annum, semper in praecipvis festivitatibus me sine aliqua devotione comprehenderem; sine devotione, inquam, quae procederet ex motione interna spiritus, quae solet nos ex propria essentia in aliam multo meliorem mutare, operando in nobis cum sua praesentia; ut videretur mihi magnum esse donum Dei, quod homo saepe inveniatur veluti vivens in seipso, cum gratia essentiali, ut melius cognoscat et sciat distinguere proprium spiritum, quem habet ex suo essentiali esse, et esse quod habet in spiritu annexo, modo bonus sit, vel malus; et magni momenti res est, ad cognoscendum et discernendum inter bonum Spiritum et malum, scire, intelligere, et sentire in se alta et humilia in singula essentia; et etiam ad augmentum vel diminutionem, quae potest succedere in unoquoque vitae genere, quae in nobis potest accidere. Quarum prima est, in qua quodammodo possem dicere, ad bonam intelligentiam, non excludendo gratiam Dei: Vivo ego jam; in secunda: Non ego, vivit vero in me Christus; in tertia autem: Vivo ego et non ego, vivit vero in me peccatum, aut malus spiritus qui regnat in malis. Post sacrum, agendo gratias Deo Domino Nostro et virgini Mariae pro sua intercessione, consideravi perfectionem magnam quam semper habuit Domina Nostra, in sua propria natura, considerando etiam eam citra continuam motionem Sancti Spiritus, et actualem, licet, ut puto, non semper eodem modo. Quanquam etenim semper plena gratia esset, et Dominus esset cum ea, et essel benedicta super omnes, fieri tamen potest ut non semper eodem fervore Spiritus Sancti et eadem consolatione tangeretur; sed relinqueretur in ea locus humiliationis, et fames, et sitis magis placendi, et timor ut non esset, quantum vellet Deus, utilis. Eam igitur roga- bam ut impetraret mihi gratiam, ut ego possem corroborari, refectus et reformatus gratia Dei; qua, postea veniente privatione justa admodum et necessaria illius motionis actualis et cooperationis sensibilis Spiritus Sancti, ego non spargerer tam cito et perderem continentiam donorum Dei, nec essem tam negligens, tam carnalis, et tam non vigilans in spiritu ad alia spiritualia. Placeat divinae Bonitati me ita confirmari in essentiali gratia sua, ut quotidie fortior, sapientior, et melior ad bene operandum efficiar, etiam quando mihi quod advenerat subtractum fuerit; et ut tales habitus sint in anima, corpore et spiritu meo, quibus ego possim proficerein ejus gratia, cessantibus actu spiritualibus fervoribus. Die sequenti, scilicet Assumptionis, in quo feci commemorationem sancti Rochi, proposui eamdem commemorationem facere singulis annis, quia sic fit Parisiis. In eodem die, apud Carmelitanos, ego habui magnam devotionem magnumque sensum illorum verborum: Mariam sanctificans, Mariam gubernans, Mariam coronans; et in illis: Gloria in excelsis Deo. Et ita rogabam cum magna devotione, fide et spe, ut Do- mina mea vellet mihi impetrarae sanctitatem et munditiam castitatis, sobrietatis et totius puritatis, tum corporis, tum praecipue spiritus; qua ego possem regere et ordinare vitam meam in servitio Filii sui; et ut mihi impetraret pacem in omnibus virtutibus in hoc mundo, et gloriam in alio. Volens eodem modo adorare cum devotione sanctissimum Sacramentum, quod erat coram me in altari, recordatus sum qualiter virgo Maria, requiescendo super omnes choros angelicos, est illa quae magis veneratur divinam Majestatem quam aliae omnes creaturae purae, quae factae sunt manibus Altissimi; et adhuc quod ejus favor pro hominibus est multo major et superior quam ullius angeli, vel seraphim; quia non solum gaudet et regnat super omnes creaturas, verumetiam magnificat, laudat, et servit super omnes Filio, sanctissimaeque et individuae Trinitati, et est Domina, Mater, et Advocata, Procuratrix et Sollicitatrix renovationis omnium creaturarum, quae adhuc non pervenerunt, nec attigerunt scopum suae perfectionis essentialis et accidentalis; procurans mortalibus nova quotidie dona gratiae, pacis et gloriae, et novunt aliquid gloriae accidentalis. i q In festo divi Bernardi, ego habui infinitam dèvotionem in missa, cum multis lacrymis, considerans diminutionem honoris sancti Sacramenti, quae provenit ex tepiditate vitae christianae, et finaliter propter desolationem quam faciunt homines qui exeunt ab#*Ecclesia; item considerans damnum quod provenit animabus purgatorii, propter istarum falsarum opinionum causam; et postea aspexi qualiter tot irreverentiae fiant omnibus rebus piis, et praelatis; similiter murmurationes proximi contra proximum; et qualiter jam nemo potest ferre alterum, nisi quod sibi placet fiat.
units.en: On the feast of the Virgin Mary, at the time of matins, while I recited the said office, and heard the same being said in the church during the Mass I celebrated, I was throughout entirely in my own self — that is, without any stirring of a good or evil spirit; and so I felt my own frailty, and my own weight in reciting, in trying to be attentive. Nevertheless it afterwards seemed to me — though I persevered in the same state — that my own proper being was not so humble and abject, so incontinent and disorderly, as it would otherwise be found, when Our Lord left me in this way: in this way I was deprived of any spirit from without, and persevered in myself, yet with the sufficiency of his essential grace. May it please Our Lord to give me grace to grow daily, that I may become a more capacious vessel, more retentive and cleaner; ready in itself not to admit evil spirits and to receive good ones. Thus I remembered and noted how, for about a year, on the chief feasts I have always found myself without any devotion — without devotion, I mean, proceeding from an inward motion of the spirit, which is wont to change us out of our own essence into another far better, working in us by its presence; so that it seemed to me a great gift of God that a man should often find himself living, as it were, in himself, with essential grace, that he may better know and learn to distinguish his own spirit, which he has from his essential being, from the being he has in an adjoined spirit, whether it be good or evil. And it is a thing of great moment, for knowing and discerning between the good Spirit and the evil, to know, understand and feel in oneself what is high and what is low in each essence; and also for the increase or diminution which can befall us in each kind of life. Of these states the first is that in which, in a certain manner, I could say — rightly understood, not excluding the grace of God — I live, I now; in the second: Not I, but Christ lives in me; in the third: I live, and yet not I, for sin lives in me — or the evil spirit, which reigns in the wicked. After Mass, giving thanks to God Our Lord and to the Virgin Mary for her intercession, I considered the great perfection which Our Lady always had in her own nature, considering her even apart from the continual and actual motion of the Holy Spirit — though, as I think, this was not always in the same manner. For although she was always full of grace, and the Lord was with her, and she was blessed above all, it may yet be that she was not always touched with the same fervour of the Holy Spirit and the same consolation, but that there was left in her room for humiliation, and hunger, and thirst to please more, and fear lest she should not be as useful as God would wish. I prayed her therefore to obtain for me the grace to be strengthened, refreshed and reformed by the grace of God; so that afterwards, when there should come the just and most necessary withdrawal of that actual motion and sensible cooperation of the Holy Spirit, I might not so quickly be scattered and lose my hold of the gifts of God, nor be so negligent, so carnal, and so unwatchful in spirit towards other spiritual things. May it please the divine Goodness so to confirm me in his essential grace that I may daily become stronger, wiser and better for working well, even when what had come to me has been withdrawn; and that such habits may be in my soul, body and spirit by which I can make progress in his grace when the actual spiritual fervours cease. On the following day, that of the Assumption, on which I made a commemoration of Saint Roch, I resolved to make the same commemoration every year, because so it is done at Paris. On the same day, at the Carmelites, I had great devotion and a great sense of those words: Sanctifying Mary, governing Mary, crowning Mary; and of those: Glory to God in the highest. And so I prayed with great devotion, faith and hope, that my Lady would obtain for me holiness and cleanness of chastity, of sobriety and of all purity, both of body and above all of spirit, by which I might rule and order my life in the service of her Son; and that she would obtain for me peace in all virtues in this world, and glory in the other. Wishing in the same way to adore with devotion the most holy Sacrament, which was before me on the altar, I remembered how the Virgin Mary, resting above all the angelic choirs, is she who venerates the divine Majesty more than all other pure creatures made by the hands of the Most High; and further, that her favour for men is far greater and higher than that of any angel or seraph; for she not only rejoices and reigns above all creatures, but also magnifies, praises and serves, above all, the Son and the most holy and undivided Trinity; and she is Lady, Mother, Advocate, Procurator and Solicitor of the renewal of all creatures which have not yet arrived at, nor attained, the mark of their essential and accidental perfection; procuring for mortals daily new gifts of grace, peace and glory, and some new accidental glory. On the feast of Saint Bernard I had boundless devotion at Mass, with many tears, considering the diminution of the honour of the holy Sacrament which comes from the lukewarmness of christian life, and finally from the desolation wrought by the men who go out from the Church; likewise considering the harm that comes to the souls in purgatory by reason of those false opinions; and then I beheld how many irreverences are done to all pious things, and to prelates; likewise the murmurings of neighbour against neighbour; and how now no one can bear another, unless what pleases himself be done.

units.la: Eodem die magnam habui devotionem in offerendo me sancto Bernardo, orando ipsum ut me discipulum velit accipere, cum ipse tam integre placuerit virgini Mariae.
units.en: On the same day I had great devotion in offering myself to Saint Bernard, praying him to be willing to receive me as a disciple, since he so wholly pleased the Virgin Mary.

units.la: In festo sancti Ludovici,. episcopi et confessoris, habui ingentem devotionem, cogitans inter alia applicare sacrum pro omnibus negligentiis a me commissis, in ponderando et notando, oculis apertis et attentis, bona quae mihi offeruntur quotidie per medium operum divinorum, et per medium verborum interiorum et exterio- rum Domini, et praeterea per viam sui proprii corporis et personae, quod quotidie prae meis manibus et ante oculos meos habeo. Hinc secuta est mihi valde clara intelligentia, et magnum - desiderium, dignum quod semper esset in anima, illius versus: Revela ocos meos et considerabo mirabilia de lege tua. Similiter ad pro positum cujusdam admirationis meae, quae quotidie mihi veniebat super mutationem animae tristis et alacris: quare aliquando considerans meum defectum et alias misericordias Domini, ego habui, in offertorio, illius versus intelligentiam: Veritas mea et misericordia mea ċčum ipso. Et in hoc consolatus sum; ut si quis mihi diceret quod Deus modo utitur veri- tate, ostendens justitiam, modo signis miseri- cordiae; et in istis duobus exercet servos suos.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Louis, bishop and confessor, I had immense devotion, thinking among other things to apply the Mass for all the negligences committed by me in weighing and noting, with open and attentive eyes, the good things offered me daily by means of the divine works, and by means of the inward and outward words of the Lord, and moreover by way of his own body and person, which I have daily in my hands and before my eyes. Hence there followed for me a very clear understanding, and a great desire — worthy to be always in the soul — of that verse: Open thou mine eyes, and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law. Likewise, touching a certain wonder of mine which came to me daily over the change of the soul from sad to glad: for once, considering my defect and on the other hand the mercies of the Lord, I had, at the offertory, the understanding of that verse: My truth and my mercy shall be with him. And in this I was consoled — as if someone said to me that God uses now truth, showing justice, now signs of mercy; and in these two he exercises his servants.

units.la: In octava Assumptionis virginis Mariae, ego habui quamdam memoriam optimam super Passionem Domini, quae mihi causa fuit inveniendi devotionem in officio, et in solitis orationibus et meditationibus meis, maxime super illud: Tristis. est anima, mea. — Transeat a me calix iste. — Deus, Deus meus! ut quid de- reliquisti me? — Mulier, ecce filius tuus. — Pater, in manus tuas, ete. Et ita habui intelligentiam ad propositum Assumptionis, quod per medium compassionis virginis Mariae, ex Passione Filii (nempe cum ipsa Passio esset via perfecta et recta in caelum) ipsa fuit assumpta super omnes choros angelicos; et ita mihi vide-. batur conveniens medium, ad contemplandum Assumptionem Matris, contemplari prius Passionem Filii et compassionem Matris.
units.en: On the octave of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary I had a certain excellent remembrance of the Passion of the Lord, which was the cause of my finding devotion in the office, and in my accustomed prayers and meditations, above all on these words: My soul is sorrowful. — Let this cup pass from me. — God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? — Woman, behold thy son. — Father, into thy hands, and the rest. And so I had an understanding bearing on the Assumption: that by means of the compassion of the Virgin Mary, arising from the Passion of her Son (the Passion itself being the perfect and straight way into heaven), she was assumed above all the angelic choirs; and so it seemed to me a fitting means, for contemplating the Assumption of the Mother, first to contemplate the Passion of the Son and the compassion of the Mother.

units.la: In sacro habui quamdam considerationem circa illud quod fit ante consecrationem, et post consecrationem usque ad communionem, et eorum quae sunt post communionem; quae omnia tria sunt. Dico me habuisse memoriam, cum. abundantia boni spiritus, essè bonum eligere tria tempora circa Christum; videlicet: primum, ante Incarnationem; secundum, quando fuit in mundo; tertium, post Ascensionem. Similiter circa virginem Mariam: primum, usque ad Conceptionem Domini; secundum, usque ad mortem et Ascensionem Filii; tertium, postquam ascendit ad caelos usque ad ipsius mortem.
units.en: At Mass I had a certain consideration about what is done before the consecration, and after the consecration up to the communion, and what follows after the communion — which in all are three. I say that I had the remembrance, with abundance of good spirit, that it is good to choose three times concerning Christ: namely, the first, before the Incarnation; the second, when he was in the world; the third, after the Ascension. Likewise concerning the Virgin Mary: the first, up to the Conception of the Lord; the second, up to the death and Ascension of her Son; the third, after he ascended into heaven, up to her own death.

units.la: Et ad hoc concipiebam aliquot nova desideria: OOPONES NNER aut scilicet communicarentur mihi "novae gratiae ad cognoscendum eum melius et. amandum, videlicet per intercessionem Matris suae; et hoc ad propositum illorum quae mihi in missa contigerunt; ubi vellem mihi dari: 4° dona eorum quae data sunt usque ad Incarnationis tempus; quod denotabatur mihi in ea parte quae est usque ad consecrationem;. 2 ut darentur mihi dona ad propositum illius temporis ab Incarnatione usque ad Passionem; quod denotabatur mihi ex eo quod esset a consecratione usque ad communionem; 3omne illud quod est ad propositum a Passione usque ad Assumptionem.
units.en: And upon this I conceived some new desires: namely, that new graces might be communicated to me for knowing him better and loving him, through the intercession of his Mother; and this bearing on what had befallen me at Mass; where I would wish to be given: first, the gifts of those things which were given up to the time of the Incarnation — which was signified to me in that part which reaches to the consecration; second, that there be given me the gifts belonging to the time from the Incarnation to the Passion — signified to me by the part from the consecration to the communion; third, all that belongs to the time from the Passion to the Assumption.

units.la: Eodem modo pertinet ad devotionem quam ego habeo virginis Mariae, ut singulis annis ego habeam quaedam desideria ut Dominus Noster, secundum tempora quae sunt inter festum et festum virginis Mariae, daret mihi gratias similes illis quibus erat plena; accipiens unum tempus a Conceptione Virginis usque ad Annunciationem; et hic deberent esse continuae praeparationes, ut tandem cum affectu possem dicere: Ecce ancilla, Domini, jam facta taber- naculum Altissimi, etc. -Alio tempore, hinc scilicet usque ad mortem Fili, quod fuit tempus compassionis ipsius; et illinc usque ad Assumptionem; incipiens iterum a principio, ete. Ut Dominus Noster daret mihi gratiam sentiendi Christum praesentem per veram compassionem et imitationem; et postea sentiendi ejus absentiam, cum sanctis desideriis sequendi ipsum aq, gloriam, postquam hoc absolvero, faciendo ejus voluntatem.
units.en: In the same way it belongs to the devotion which I have to the Virgin Mary, that each year I should have certain desires that Our Lord, according to the seasons which lie between one feast of the Virgin Mary and another, would give me graces like those with which she was filled: taking one season from the Conception of the Virgin to the Annunciation — and here there should be continual preparations, so that at last I might say with affection: Behold the handmaid of the Lord, now made the tabernacle of the Most High, and so forth. Another season thence, namely, to the death of her Son, which was the time of her compassion; and thence to the Assumption; beginning again from the beginning, and so on. That Our Lord would give me the grace of feeling Christ present, through true compassion and imitation; and afterwards of feeling his absence, with holy desires of following him into glory, when I shall have finished this course, doing his will.

units.la: Eodem die, similiter ad propositum cogitandi qualiter Christi Passio et Gompassio Virginis fuit tanquam scalarum gradus, ad ascendendum ex deserto ad Ascensionem et Assumptionem, ego habui magnam devotionem, altam et infimam cognitionem omnium inferiorum et altorum, cum - desiderio quod Dominus Noster mihi det gratiam nunquam contristari nec laetari, nisi secundum quod Christus laetatus et contristatus est cum sua Matre.
units.en: On the same day, likewise bearing on the thought of how the Passion of Christ and the Compassion of the Virgin were as the steps of a ladder, for ascending out of the desert to the Ascension and the Assumption, I had great devotion, and a knowledge both high and lowly of all things below and above, with the desire that Our Lord may give me the grace never to be saddened nor gladdened except according as Christ was gladdened and saddened with his Mother.

units.la: In festo sancti Bartholomaei, ego inter alia applicavi sacrum pro omnibus laboribus quos haberent aliquando, et quocumque modo, fratres mei et amici eorum, pro laboribus, in- quam, non solum praesentibus sed et praeteritis et futuris, ut sacrificium tale sit supplementum in gratiarum actiones debitas, et ad petendum veniam et gratiam quas quaerere debent per viam talium tribulationum.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Bartholomew I applied the Mass, among other intentions, for all the labours which my brethren and their friends might at any time, and in whatever way, have — for their labours, I say, not only present but past and future; that such a sacrifice might be a supplement towards the thanksgivings that are due, and for asking the pardon and grace which they ought to seek by way of such tribulations.

units.la: Eodem modo habui devotionem et desiderium rei impossibilis, hoc est quod ego essem ante omnes martyres, et unicuique eorum possem dicere: Exaudiat te Dominus in die tribulationis, et tribuat tibi secundum cor tuum et omne consilium tuum confirmet. Impleat Dominus omnes petitiones tuas et holocaustum tuum pingue fiat. Hoc omne in bono sensu spiritus sensi.
units.en: In the same way I had a devotion and desire for an impossible thing: namely, that I might have stood before all the martyrs, and might have been able to say to each of them: May the Lord hear thee in the day of tribulation, and grant thee according to thine own heart, and confirm all thy counsel. May the Lord fulfil all thy petitions, and may thy burnt offering be made fat. All this I felt in a good sense of the spirit.

units.la: Eodem die, cum vellem dicere completorium, videns animam meam tam tristem et amaram, quia ab aliis vesperis veteres aliquae infirmitates et debilitates agitabant me, et videbatur mihi quod in tali die noluissem sentire tot agitationes spiritus et distractiones in meo officio; venit mihi quaedam consolatio: scilicet quod forsitan placebat Domino quod in similibus diebus invenirem me inferiorem et propinqùiorem veteribus meis plagis; ut tales-sancti occurrentes illas videant, et orent Dominum ut extrahat me ab hujusmodi iımperfectionibus. Et certum est quod abhinc uno anno, fere semper, in praecipuis festis, ego me inveni extra illum spiritum in quo est devotio, pax, etc. Itaque in hoc multam spem assumpsi, et rogabam Dominum ita fieret ut non solum Ipse, verum etiam Maler et Apostoli sui, et Joannes Baptista, et sanclae Anna.et Magdalena, cum aliis, certiores fierent per hane viam mearum necessita- tum spiritualium. i In festo sancti Ludovici Galliarum regis, ego habui multam devotionem applicando missam in nomine Cardinalis pro quo ego debebam eam dicere, volens satisfacere, ejus nomine, omnibus quae ipse potest debere ad honorem istius Sancti, et utilitatem totius Galliae, in qua tot bona gesta sunt et tot peccata remissa; et in qua sunt tot necessitates corporales et spirituales. Dico me applicavisse sacrum pro ipso et tota Gallia, praeterita; praesenti et futura, cum omnibus regibus, ducibus, comitibus, et aliis Dominis; pro Archiepiscopatibus, Episčopatibus, Abbatiis, Parochiis, Gymnasiis, et civitatibus cujuscumquë conditionis; et in hoe discursu sensi multam devotionem, desiderans quod Dominus Noster id concederet; faciens mentionem quod pro aliis regnis idem fieri desiderabam. Quodam die dominico, cum dicerem officium, adjungebam quaedam verba psalmorum, specialiter illa: Diligam te, Domine, fortitudo mea; item: Dominus firmamentum meum et refugium meum et liberator meus, Deus meus, adjutor meus, protector meus et cornu salutis meae et susceptor meus. Et ponderabam praedicta verba, cum fide et spe in Domino, et magno desiderio amandi Ipsum. Postea considerans humanam fragilitatem esse majorem, et ejus corruptionem faciliorem, et dissolutionem jam momentaneam super alia omnia corpora; considerando et animam. esse tam caecam, et spiritum tam perversum in seipso, ad judicandum suas necessitates, et quid sit necessarium ad quaerendum remedia carnis et animae suae; et mihi venit multa devotio, offerens mihi ut orarem Patrem omnipotentem, ut misereatur carnis et corporis, et ut illam corroboraret et sanctificaret, Filio suo commendando; et animam similiter, ut velit eam illuminare et sanctificare Spiritu Sancto; et commendabam etiam spiritum, ut velit ipsum sic bonum reddere ut nunquam obliviscatur officii sui: pro anima intelligendo partem sensitivam simul cum portione inferiori rationis, quae videlicet ratiodiscurrit circa ea quae per sensus accipiuntur; per spiritum autem, eam portionem superiorem quae circa divina occupatur, accipiendo per Spiritum Sanctum et per Angelos, et item per fidem ex auditu, suas. communicationes, et desideria atque affectus, etc. Rogavi etiam Filium, quatenus illa quae dixi mihi concederet, in sumptione corporis sui pretiosissimi, animae et divinitatis. suae in Sacramento existentium.
units.en: On the same day, when I was about to say compline, seeing my soul so sad and bitter — because since the previous vespers certain old infirmities and weaknesses had been shaking me, and it seemed to me that on such a day I would not have wished to feel so many agitations of spirit and distractions in my office — there came to me a certain consolation: namely, that perhaps it pleased the Lord that on such days I should find myself lower, and nearer to my old wounds, so that the saints of the day, meeting them, might see them, and pray the Lord to draw me out of such imperfections. And it is certain that for a year now, almost always, on the chief feasts I have found myself outside that spirit in which are devotion, peace, and the rest. And so in this I took much hope, and prayed the Lord that it might come about that not only He, but also his Mother and his Apostles, and John the Baptist, and Saints Anne and Magdalen, with others, might by this way be made aware of my spiritual needs. On the feast of Saint Louis, king of France, I had much devotion, applying the Mass in the name of the Cardinal for whom I was bound to say it, wishing to satisfy, in his name, all that he can owe to the honour of that Saint, and to the profit of all France, in which so many good deeds have been done and so many sins forgiven, and in which there are so many bodily and spiritual needs. I say that I applied the Mass for him and for all France — past, present and future — with all its kings, dukes, counts and other lords; for its archbishoprics, bishoprics, abbeys, parishes, schools, and cities of every condition; and in this round I felt much devotion, desiring that Our Lord would grant it; making mention that I desired the same to be done for the other kingdoms. On a certain Sunday, while saying the office, I joined to it certain words of the psalms, especially these: I will love thee, O Lord, my strength; likewise: The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer; my God, my helper, my protector, and the horn of my salvation, and my upholder. And I weighed these words, with faith and hope in the Lord, and a great desire of loving Him. Afterwards, considering that human frailty is greater, and its corruption easier, and its dissolution more momentary, than that of all other bodies; considering too that the soul is so blind, and the spirit so perverse in itself, at judging its own needs and what is necessary for seeking the remedies of its flesh and of its soul — much devotion came to me, prompting me to pray the almighty Father to have mercy on the flesh and body, and to strengthen and sanctify it, commending it to his Son; and the soul likewise, that he would deign to enlighten and sanctify it by the Holy Spirit; and I commended also the spirit, that he would deign to make it so good that it might never forget its office: understanding by the soul the sensitive part together with the lower portion of reason — the reason, namely, that runs upon the things received through the senses; and by the spirit, that higher portion which is occupied with divine things, receiving through the Holy Spirit and through the Angels, and likewise through faith by hearing, its communications, desires, affections, and the rest. I prayed also the Son to grant me what I have said, in the receiving of his most precious body, soul and divinity, present in the Sacrament.

units.la: In festo sancti Joannis decollati, inveniens me aliquantulum distractum, et videns difficultates redeundi ad me, ego habui multam devotionem, cogitando qualiter Sacramentum sanctissimum proprie est in quo gratia pro tali negotio invenitur, quod vult semper ingredi ad nos et ducere nos ad conversionem cordis nostri; ut sequendo ipsum: quotidie magis ac magis, ingrediamur. in profundum viscerum nostrorum. Sanctum Joan- nem orabam ut doceret me modum praeparandı viam Domini, cum ipse sit vox quae clamat in deserto: Parate viam Domini.
units.en: On the feast of the beheading of Saint John, finding myself somewhat distracted, and seeing the difficulties of returning into myself, I had much devotion in thinking how the most holy Sacrament is properly that in which grace for such a matter is found — which wills always to enter in to us and lead us to the conversion of our heart; that following it daily more and more, we may enter into the depth of our inward parts. I prayed Saint John to teach me the way of preparing the way of the Lord, since he is the voice that cries in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord.

units.la: Spiritus igitur haec duo a nobis maxime desiderat, scilicet ut proficiamus in elevatione spiritus nostri ad coelos, et intremus et penetremus nos ipsos quousque invenerimus Deum intra nos esse; quare in alia parte non debet quaeri regnum Dei quam intra nos et in caelis. Exaltatus est Christus in cruce et tandem ascendit ad caelos, ut nos omnes traheret ad seipsum. Dedit seipsum in sacrificio, ad cibum animae nostre ut viam haberemus qua ipsum ad nos traheremus, juxta illud: 4d eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus; et jūxta illud: Si quis mihi aperuerit, ego caenabo cum illo, etc.
units.en: The Spirit, then, desires these two things of us above all: that we make progress in the raising of our spirit to heaven, and that we enter and penetrate into ourselves until we find that God is within us; wherefore the kingdom of God is to be sought nowhere else than within us and in heaven. Christ was lifted up on the cross, and at last ascended into heaven, that he might draw us all to himself. He gave himself in sacrifice, as food for our soul, that we might have a way by which to draw him to us — according to that word: We will come to him, and make our abode with him; and that other: If any man open to me, I will sup with him, and the rest.

units.la: Dum faciebam officium sanctae Sabine mar: tyris, venit mihi devotio quaedam, ut simul haberem memoriam in omnibus horis sanctae Serapiae virginis et martyris, quae cum conversaretur in domo sanctae Sabine eam convertit.
units.en: While I was saying the office of Saint Sabina the martyr, there came to me a certain devotion, to keep in memory at all the hours, together with her, Saint Serapia, virgin and martyr, who, dwelling in the house of Saint Sabina, converted her.

units.la: Eodem die, considėrans qualiter peccata, non solum carnalia sed etiam fere omnia, fiant cum applicatione spiritus, cogitando in eorum mate- ria, loquendo, odiendo, etc., habui quemdam discursum ad rogandum Dominum, ut vellet impedire malignos. spiritus \ne tantum tentarent homines: quia super gulam hodie sunt tot verba, tot affectus, tot cogitationes, ex quibus colligitur spiritualis ista (ut ita dicam) comestio; et ita circa alia corporis, etiam licita, in quibus homines ponunt animam suam; quasi qui, ex nutrimento corporis et necessaria. provisione, velint nutrire ipsam animam et ipsi providere; quae alium debet habere cibum, et non delectari in eisdem in quibus corpus delectatur. Hinc fit quod ideo, hoc tempore, fornicatores aggravant peccata sua ex hoc, quod nimium. applicant ad illa peccata spiritum, et demergunt animam suam spurcitiis ipsius corporis, maritati quoque in hoe maculant sanctum thorum, quod et ipsi nimium spurcitiis commiscentur, quaerentes animae desideria simul cum desideriis carnis perficere; et hinc est etiam nimia alienatio et elongatio a rebus divinis. Hinc fit ut spiritus nequeat invenire proprium cibum. Potius autem fuerat trahendum corpus usque ad sensa spiritualis cibi animae suae ac spiritus; ita ut, dum videremus opus Dei aliquod, aut audiremus verba ipsius, aut tractaremus manibus nostris, spiritus in omnia illa totus ferretur, et secum traheret totam animam sensitivam ad illa percipienda. Hoc est enim vere egredi seipsum ad pascua. Verum est hoc non bene posse fieri, donec nos penitus omnino traxerimus ad interiora nostra; id est, totaliter collecti intus fuerimus, ibi parati morari: quo sic dum primum nitimur pervenire, separamur a sensibus spiritualibus, hoc est a sensualibus. Oportet igitur Deum deprecari, ut ita erigat nos ad alta et ad res omnino spirituales contemplandas, ut tandem in nobis caetera spiritualia omnia fiant, apprehendanturque modo spirituali; et hoc longe praestat quam-si nobis detur gratia spiritus, qua haec inferiora sancte sed tamen sensibiliter sentiamus.
units.en: On the same day, considering how sins — not only carnal but almost all — are committed with an application of the spirit, by thinking on their matter, speaking, hating, and so forth, I had a certain round of prayer, begging the Lord to be pleased to hinder the malignant spirits from tempting men so much: for concerning gluttony there are today so many words, so many affections, so many thoughts, out of which is gathered that spiritual (so to speak) eating; and so about the other things of the body, even lawful ones, in which men set their soul — as if from the nourishment of the body and its necessary provision they would nourish the soul itself and provide for it; whereas it ought to have another food, and not to delight in the same things in which the body delights. Hence it comes that in this age fornicators aggravate their sins by applying the spirit too much to those sins, and plunging their soul in the filth of the body; the married too in this defile the holy bed, in that they too mingle overmuch with impurities, seeking to fulfil the desires of the soul together with the desires of the flesh; and hence also comes too great an estrangement and distance from divine things. Hence it comes that the spirit cannot find its proper food. Rather ought the body to have been drawn up to the perceptions of the spiritual food of the soul and spirit; so that when we see some work of God, or hear his words, or handle them with our hands, the spirit might be borne wholly into all these, and draw with it the whole sensitive soul to perceive them. For this is truly to go out of oneself into pastures. True it is that this cannot well be done until we have first drawn ourselves wholly to our own interior — that is, until we are totally recollected within, ready to dwell there; for while we first strive to arrive there, we are separated from the spiritual senses, that is, from the sensual ones. We must therefore beseech God so to raise us to high things, and to the contemplation of things wholly spiritual, that at last all the other spiritual things may come to be in us, and be apprehended in a spiritual manner; and this far surpasses the granting of a grace of the spirit by which we should feel these lower things holily and yet sensibly.

units.la: Erige igitur mentem ad ea in quibus nihil est quod sensu ullo percipi potest, t-ut rest -divinitas Christi, quae eadem est el Patris et Spiritus Sancti; et personae omnes spiritualiter purae, maxime autem Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti.
units.en: Raise your mind, then, to those things in which there is nothing that can be perceived by any sense — such as the divinity of Christ, which is the same as that of the Father and of the Holy Spirit; and all the persons spiritually pure, but above all the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Quaere Deum ubi aliud inveniri non potest quam Deus, id est in seipso. Post hune sic in divina natura consideratum, quaere Christum hominem in coelo potius quam in terra; postea vero quaere beatam Virginem, et in utroque prius animam quam corpus. Post Virginem corpoream, sint spiritus angelici et reliquae beatorum animae quae sunt in caeoelo. Post haec, in ordine quo dixi, Pater noster in caelis quaerendus est et alloquendus, dum in seipso nequeat a nobis inveniri neque imaginari. In terra autem, dum conversari optas in Domino nesciens ad caeoeaelestia ascendere, Christus primum et verba ejus, et omnia verba sacra; et cruci affixus contemplandus est, si ad praeteritum respicias; et si ad futurum respicias, tanquam qui descensurus esset ad judicium. Deinde consequenter retrocedendo per vitam Christi, si in perfectionibus a spiritu nostro progressus quaeratur, post Christum nulla melior conversatio quam illa quae est cum vita et moribus beate Virginis: nullibi enim invenies tam efficax exemplum compatiendi Christo, et sequendi eum, et ipsi serviendi, etc. Post Virginem sintreliqui sancti, martyres, eremitae, caeterique qui mundum reliquerunt et bona hujus seculi contempserunt, in quibus etiam Deus ipse invenitur, et eo magis quo vita fuerint sanctiores et magis spirituales. Post homines sint caetera opera Dei, creationis et Redemptionis, et omnia alia in quibus est consideratio aliqua, in aedificationem. In angustiis, utroque modo proficitur, id est, in consideratione paenarum Christi et malorum aeternorum, et etiam in resurrectionis consideratione et gloriae; in prosperis autem magis proficitur in consideratione Passionis et eorum quae humiliant.
units.en: Seek God where nothing else can be found but God, that is, in himself. After him, thus considered in the divine nature, seek Christ as man in heaven rather than on earth; and afterwards seek the blessed Virgin — and in both, the soul before the body. After the Virgin in the body, let there be the angelic spirits and the other souls of the blessed which are in heaven. After these, in the order I have said, our Father in heaven is to be sought and addressed, since in himself he cannot be found or imagined by us. But on earth, when you desire to converse in the Lord and know not how to ascend to heavenly things, let Christ come first, and his words, and all sacred words; and he is to be contemplated fixed to the cross, if you look to the past; and if you look to the future, as one who is to come down to judgment. Then in order, going back through the life of Christ, if progress in perfections is sought by our spirit, after Christ there is no better converse than with the life and ways of the blessed Virgin: nowhere will you find so efficacious an example of suffering with Christ, and following him, and serving him, and so forth. After the Virgin let there be the other saints, martyrs, hermits, and the rest who left the world and despised the goods of this age, in whom too God himself is found — and the more, the holier and more spiritual their lives were. After men, let there be the other works of God, of creation and of Redemption, and all else in which there is any consideration that edifies. In afflictions, profit is made in both ways — that is, in the consideration of the pains of Christ and of the eternal evils, and also in the consideration of the resurrection and of glory; but in prosperity more profit is made in the consideration of the Passion and of the things that humble.

units.la: Eodem die sanctae Sabinae considerans Dominum Nostrum Jesum Christum in speciebus panis et vini, cogitavi cum magno quodam. devotionis sensu qualiter infinita ejus bonitas volebat accipere officium panis et vini materialis et eorum formam ad cibandum animas nostras et corpora reformanda ad meliorem essentiam quam non possunt causare materialis panis et vinum.
units.en: On the same day of Saint Sabina, considering Our Lord Jesus Christ in the species of bread and wine, I thought with a certain great feeling of devotion how his infinite goodness willed to take the office and form of material bread and wine, to feed our souls and to reform our bodies to a better essence than material bread and wine can produce.

units.la: In die sancti Aegidii abbatis, postquam fecissem parvam adhortationem coram quibusdam qui erant communicaturi, et postquam absolvissem missam, datus est mihi magnus spiritus in desiderio praedicandi sicut et hactenus frequenter; ideoque et tune proposui, firmius quam hactenus, in Germania me daturum esse omnem operam ut possim praedicare vel legere; magnum enim alioquin incommodum. enasciturum ex tanta et tam diuturna taciturnitate.
units.en: On the day of Saint Giles the abbot, after I had given a short exhortation before certain persons who were about to communicate, and after I had finished Mass, a great spirit was given me in the desire of preaching, as often before; and so I then resolved, more firmly than hitherto, that in Germany I would give all diligence to be able to preach or to lecture; for otherwise great harm would grow out of so long and so continued a silence.

units.la: Sensi etiam tunc quod oporteat melius attendere ad hoc, ut sim obediens ei spiritui qui me ad fervorem excitat, circa opera quae sunt in verbo Domini, puta exhortationes particulares, et publicas praedicationes; et non solum in ecelesia coram multitudine, sed circa domos, etiamsi pauci sint qui me possint audire;: item in mensis coram principibus et magnatibus.
units.en: I felt also then that I must attend better to being obedient to that spirit which stirs me to fervour in the works which lie in the word of the Lord — such as particular exhortations and public sermons; and not only in church before a multitude, but from house to house, even if they be few who can hear me; likewise at table, before princes and great men.

units.la: In Dominica prima Septembris, dum applicarem discursus meos, et praesertim discursum mysteriorum vitae et mortis, et resurrectionis Christi, ad animam cujusdam defuncti qui fuit Doctor de Cornibus, theologus parisiensis, cujus decessus mihi tum nuntiatus fuerat, ego dicturus missam pro ipso, sensi magnam devotionem in tali discursu, petendo veniam nomine ipsius, cum contritione magna, quod non imitatus fuerat Christum ipsum, neque eos qui ei serviebant et obediebant, adorando,. recognoscendo, audiendo, compatiendo, petendo ab eo gratias et omnia necessaria.
units.en: On the first Sunday of September, while I applied my rounds of prayer — especially the round of the mysteries of the life, death and resurrection of Christ — to the soul of a certain departed man, Doctor de Cornibus, a theologian of Paris, whose death had then been announced to me, being about to say Mass for him, I felt great devotion in that round, asking pardon in his name, with great contrition, for that he had not imitated Christ himself, nor those who served and obeyed him, in adoring, acknowledging, hearing, compassionating, and asking of him graces and all things needful.

units.la: Hic etiam sese mihi offerebant alia illa in quibus dictus defunctus potuit peccasse et defecisse a perfectione quam potuisset assequi; verbi gratia: petebam veniam pro. his omnibus in quibus forte deliquissèt circa obedientiam suam, paupertatem. et castitatem, quia erat monachus sancli Francisci. Item circa defectum in officiis H n a n= EAE suis, cum esset doctor et praedicatot. Item circa vanam gloriam quae solet sequi tantos viros. Et in eo loco ubi fit memoria defunctorum in missa, tempore quo delinebar in memento cum satis magna animi mei elevatione, sese mihi obtulit ut rogarem Patrem quatenus dignaretur in tali anima glorificari; et etiam Filium, et Spiritum Sanctum, et beatam Mariam yirgiginem. Item ut dignaretur ipsam animam admittere ad ordinem laureatorum doctorum, secundum: promissum illud, quod qui docti fuerint et ad justitiam erudierint multos, fulgebunt quasi stellae in perpetuas aeternitates.
units.en: Here there offered themselves to me also those other things in which the said departed man could have sinned and fallen short of the perfection he might have attained: for example, I asked pardon for all wherein he had perhaps failed as to his obedience, poverty and chastity, for he was a friar of Saint Francis; likewise as to failure in his offices, since he was a doctor and preacher; likewise as to the vainglory which is wont to attend such men. And at that place where the departed are remembered in the Mass, while I lingered in the memento with a considerable lifting of my mind, it was offered to me to beg the Father that he would deign to be glorified in that soul; and likewise the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and the blessed Virgin Mary; and that he would deign to admit that soul to the order of the laurelled doctors, according to that promise, that they who are learned, and have instructed many unto justice, shall shine as stars for perpetual eternities.

units.la: In festo sanctorum Cosmae et Damiani, sensi magna quaedam et intima desideria erga venerationem sanctissimi Sacramenti, et Sanctorum qui in. caelis sunt, et circa cultum impendendum imaginibus et reliquiis Sanctorum; voluissemque semper posse adesse coram sanctissimo Sacramento ubicumque reservatur in Germania; et similiter coram qualibet imagine Christi, vel Virginis Deiparae, vel cujuscumque Sancti vel Sanctae.
