Quod desiderium quia impleri non potest, rogabam Dominum ut per Angelos nos- tros custodes suppleat meos circa hujusmodi cultum defectus, et omnium aliorum, ita ut id quod deberet fieri per personas, tiat per Angelos eorum custodes.
units.en: On the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian I felt certain great and intimate desires towards the veneration of the most holy Sacrament, and of the Saints who are in heaven, and concerning the worship to be paid to the images and relics of the Saints; and I would have wished to be able to be always present before the most holy Sacrament wherever it is reserved in Germany, and likewise before every image of Christ, or of the Virgin Mother of God, or of any saint whatever. And because this desire cannot be fulfilled, I prayed the Lord that through our guardian Angels he would supply my defects in such worship, and those of all others, so that what ought to be done by the persons themselves may be done by their guardian Angels.

units.la: Dum etiam considerarem, cum quadam mentis elevatione, Christum, sedentem ad dexteram virtutis Dei Patris, videre etiam oculis humanitatis suae cuncta quae fiunt sub sole, tot opera ingratitudinis et malitiae; tot blasphemias contra Deum, etc.; sensi quamdam admirationem circa tanlam patientiam et bonitatem ipsiusChristi, tam potentis in coelo et in terra. Gousiderabam homines quasi crucifigere mortalem Agnum, et non aestimare, aut negligere, jam regnantem aut triumphantem. Patientia ergo ipsius viventis et jam regnantis talem in bonitate proportionem habere videri potest, sicut mala illa ad invicem proportionantur.
units.en: While I also considered, with a certain lifting of the mind, that Christ, sitting at the right hand of the power of God the Father, sees also with the eyes of his humanity all things that are done under the sun — so many works of ingratitude and malice, so many blasphemies against God, and the rest — I felt a certain wonder at the so great patience and goodness of Christ himself, so mighty in heaven and on earth. I considered that men, as it were, crucify the mortal Lamb, and take no account of, or neglect, him who now reigns and triumphs. The patience, then, of him who lives and now reigns may be seen to hold such a proportion in goodness as those evils bear to one another.

units.la: In festo sancti Michaelis Archangeli, ego habui multas contemplationes et affectiones pias ad propositum ipsius et omnium angelorum. Dicens officium, habui desiderium ut angeli laudarėnt Dominum Nostram quoties dicuntur talia verba, veluti illi qui melius illa et sentiunt et intelligunt.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Michael the Archangel I had many contemplations and devout affections concerning him and all the angels. Saying the office, I had the desire that the angels might praise Our Lord whenever such words are said, as those who both feel and understand them better.

units.la: Eodem modo desiderabam ut facerent Sancti, non solum qui nominantur in orationibus, verum etiam omnes ali; et ut mea recitatio, verba et cogitationes, essent semper occasio illis laudandi Dominum Nostrum, vel agendi, vel petendi gratias pro nobis; et ut, propter meam inadvertentiam, non relinquant ipsi notare verba bona quae mea lingua proferuntur; etsie de gestibus et signis propter Deum factis, quanquam saepe in sola fide Ecclesiae, aut in proprio tantum habitu valeant.
units.en: In the same way I desired that the Saints might do so — not only those named in the prayers, but all the others too; and that my recitation, words and thoughts might always be an occasion for them to praise Our Lord, or to give thanks, or to ask graces for us; and that, notwithstanding my inadvertence, they might not fail to mark the good words uttered by my tongue; and so too of gestures and signs made for God's sake, although often they avail only in the faith of the Church, or only in one's own habit.

units.la: In offertorio missae, habui quoddam desiderium ut suppleret et applicaretur ad gloriam sancti Michaelis et totius exercitus ejus, sic ac si in hoc mundo, accepto corpore, imitati essent Jesum Christum; ac ad meritum meum et aliorum virorum, sicuti si haberemus potestatem et scientiam Angelorum, et laudassemus hucusque Christum etiam in gloria quemadmodum tenes mur: Itaque ego gauderem quod, per gratiam Dei, mihi fieret possibile ut essem vicarius, in laboribus multis; nomine angelorum, et quod ipsi essent mihi excusatores omnium quorum ego debitor sam divinae Majestatis honori, cui millia millium ministrant et decies centena millia assistunt Sed bene sentiebam quod mihi sufficeret servire, laudare, et honorare Christum. Itaque eum consideravi modum in quo ipse in mundo sit; qualiter scilicet ipse tam paucis contentus esset, relinquens hic vicarios suos, - quos qui audit, ipsum audit, relinquens etiam pauperes,;de-quibus dicit: Quod uni ex minimis meis fecistis, mihi fecistis, etc.
units.en: At the offertory of the Mass I had a certain desire that it might supply, and be applied to, the glory of Saint Michael and of all his host, as though in this world, having taken a body, they had imitated Jesus Christ; and to the merit of myself and other men, as if we had the power and knowledge of the Angels, and had hitherto praised Christ even in glory as we are bound. And so I would rejoice if, by the grace of God, it were made possible for me to be a vicar in many labours in the name of the angels, and that they might be my excusers in all wherein I am debtor to the honour of the divine Majesty, whom thousands of thousands minister to and ten hundred thousand stand before. But I felt well that it would suffice me to serve, praise and honour Christ. And so I considered the manner in which he is in the world: how he is content with so little, leaving here his vicars — he who hears them, hears him — leaving also the poor, of whom he says: What you did to one of the least of mine, you did to me, and the rest.

units.la: In festo sancti Hieronymi, ego certior factussum, ad obtinendum favorem ejus, et aliorum Eai quọrum homo recordari potest, hoc esse multi valoris in effectu adjutori; scilicet ut ego acciperem multam ¿devotionem erga illum angelum qui eum in hoc mundo custodivit; et similiter erga omnes alios: angelos custodes quorumcumque sanctorum; et ita potest peti, talibus angelis communicari in spiritu cum. fide, quemadmodum et sanctis.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Jerome I was made certain that, for obtaining his favour, and that of the other saints whom a man can call to mind, this is of much worth for effectual help: namely, that I should take much devotion towards that angel who guarded him in this world; and likewise towards all the other guardian angels of all the saints; and so one may ask to communicate in spirit, with faith, with such angels, even as with the saints.

units.la: Cum dicerem ofticium, sensi multam devotionem, considerans qualiter, angeli et sancti possint accipere occasionem illorum verborum ad laudandum Deum, et ad me adjuvandum, et quod petimus obtinendum; et ita sensi rem esse valde utilem rogare illos cum devotione, ut velint assistere ad contemplandum et laudandum Deum, nempe cum videant i ipsum sicuti est; et proficit quod homo habeat: desiderium quod ipsi suppleant in omnibus pro nobis, et excusent defectusnostros linguis suis beatificatis.
units.en: While I said the office I felt much devotion, considering how the angels and saints can take occasion from those words to praise God, and to help me, and to obtain what we ask; and so I felt it to be a very useful thing to beg them with devotion to be pleased to assist us in contemplating and praising God — they indeed seeing him as he is; and it profits that a man have the desire that they supply in all things for us, and excuse our defects with their beatified tongues.

units.la: Inveni similiter magnum desiderium et gaudium, ut sancti qui iú coelis sunt, ut'itasdicam, habeant nunc modum, potestatem et scientiam et voluntatem; etc., ad faciendum et compensandum quod hic noluerunt, vel nescierunt, vel non potuerunt, circa res divinas, et proximorum tam vivorum quam mortuorum.
units.en: I found likewise a great desire and joy that the saints who are in heaven have now, so to speak, the manner, the power, the knowledge and the will, and the rest, to do and make good what here they would not, or knew not how, or could not, concerning divine things and the affairs of their neighbours, both living and dead.

units.la: Hic habui quoddam #desiderium ut possem exprimere opere vel verbis exterioribus, vel quovis alio modo, quo manifestum esset singulis sanctis atque angelis, omnia illa que Deus in hoc mundo fecit, et quaecumque ad nos hucusque misit, ut quisque sanctorum hoc modo posset cognoscere Štvini illis videre glorificationem suam, et suam majorem gloriam accidentalem quae potest augeri, sumpta etiam ex nobis occasione; nos enim possumus esse illis causa majoris gloriae accidentalis: Hic etiam notavi quamdam devotiònem, quam inveni causa crucifixi sanctae crucis de Moguntia, et aliarum imaginum quae dederunt sanguinem, sed praecipue istius crucifixi, quando perditus ille homo hujus truncavit caput, et tam male vulneravit. Unde penetravit me quaedam et quasi continua consideratio, quae est in gradu illius divinae Bonitatis; scilicet dare et spargere sanguinem toties peccatori qui eum offendit. Ita dedit eum pauperi caeco Longino postquam mortuus erat, et illuminatus fuit ab illo; et ita videtur mihi quod cum ego tot ineptias commiserim, et tot opera ingratitudinis, et malitiae contra Dominum meum, ipse nihil aliud facit propter vulnus nisi mihi dare gratiam, ut ex ipso sanguine sparso proficiam. Et sic contingit, dum in hoc mundo tot blasphemiae contra honorem Dei et Sanctorum suorum fiant, ut non cesset divina ejus Bonitas spargere signa sanguinis amoris sui super illos qui similia faciunt; permittens etiam se crudelius vulnerari; ut tandem dando aliquod abominabile vulnus, quum aliud remedium pro multis jam non sit, redeamus ad nos; et sentiamus crudelitatem nostram, et inveniamus sanguinem puriorem ad sanandam animàm nostram. l" ra A.
units.en: Here I had a certain desire that I might express by deed or outward words, or in any other way, so that it might be manifest to each of the saints and angels, all that God has done in this world, and whatever he has hitherto sent to us, so that each of the saints might in this way know and see in these things his own glorification, and his greater accidental glory which can be increased, taking occasion even from us; for we can be to them the cause of greater accidental glory. Here I also noted a certain devotion which I found by reason of the crucifix of the holy cross of Mainz, and of the other images which have shed blood, but chiefly of that crucifix, when that lost man struck off its head and wounded it so grievously. Whence there pierced me a certain almost continual consideration of the degree of that divine Goodness: namely, to give and shed blood so often for the sinner who offends him. So he gave it to the poor blind Longinus after he was dead, and he received light from it; and so it seems to me that, though I have committed so many follies, and so many works of ingratitude and malice against my Lord, he does nothing else on account of the wound but give me grace, that from that shed blood I may profit. And so it comes to pass, while in this world so many blasphemies are done against the honour of God and of his Saints, that his divine Goodness does not cease to shed the signs of the blood of his love upon those who do such things, allowing himself even to be wounded more cruelly; so that at last, by the giving of some abominable wound — since for many there is now no other remedy — we may return to ourselves, and feel our cruelty, and find the purer blood to heal our soul.

units.la: Dum haec considerarem de sanguine Jesu Christi agni immaculati, ego sensi magnam vim ipsius christianae mansuetudinis, quam Christus verbis et opere nos docuit: nulla est enim efficacior contra crudelitatem atque iram, et quidquid est charitati contrarium, quam si ita mansuetus sis, ut nullis ictibus resistens, sed omnes benigne et cum mansuetudine animi exepiens, permittas percussori quidquid velit. Tandem sic, aut alias nunquam, frangetur cor ejus et emollietur, videns patientiam tuam et viscera bonitatis tuae. O durum igitur me nimiumque crudelem, tardumque ad credendum et audiendum Christum Dominum, qui toties aquam lacrymarum et sanguinem pro me effuderit frustra! O anima mea misera et nimium crudelis, quare non te mollierunt ille lacrymae, quum primum eas intellexisti, quas Christus, mundum intrans et hujus tuae mortalis vitae sensum, jam statim pro te effudit? Propter te enim in hunc mundum exivit a Patre caelesti, et lacrymis prima hujus vitae miseranda mala significat. Et cum haec vidisti non es mota, sedexspectasti effusio- nem sanguinis; et ecce circumcisus lacrymas simul et, sanguinem effudit puer octo dierum, et tu nec sic es emollita! quare hoc? quia ille puer forte ibi erat sensum solius carnis et corporis tibi ostendens, et ideo tu exspectabas signa interni sensus Dei tui? Vide igitur lacrymas. Et haec aquae effusio pro te et super te est. Et quare igitur non moveberis? Quid exspectas? Exspecto, inquies, et exspectavi majores motus Dei mei, ut movear, et ipse melius sentiam. O miseram te et deplorandam, quae tam dura es! Vide igitur et agnosce lacrymas quas emittit Dominus super eversione futura et summa ingratitudine Hierosolymae. Item illas quas in cruce, dum emittebat spiritum, ipse effudit. Et si hoc non satis est, aut magis cupias emissionem sanguinis quam lacrymarum Domini, aspice sudorem sanguineum, ubi sunt duo simul commixta et vide insuper sanguinem ob ligamina, ob percussiones, ob verbera, ob coronationem, ex totius corporis extremitatibus profluentem; idque propter te, et quasi unus esses, haec omnia. Quod si nondum haec signa te moveant, veni usque ad venas, et considera quomodo pro te omnes evacuantur puriore sanguine Agni immolati; et si haec omnia non sufficiant, accipe sanguinem purissimum per se, et accipe seorsum aquam quae ex latere Domini profluxit, et cum Longino sana animam tuam; nec velis experiri majora signa divinae Bonitatis ex passionibus ipsius Humanitatis, quia post hoc non patitur Christus resurgens ex mortuis.
units.en: While I considered these things about the blood of Jesus Christ the immaculate lamb, I felt the great power of that christian meekness which Christ taught us by word and deed: for nothing is more efficacious against cruelty and anger, and whatever is contrary to charity, than to be so meek that, resisting no blows, but receiving all kindly and with meekness of soul, you allow the striker whatever he will. So at last, and otherwise never, his heart will be broken and softened, seeing your patience and the bowels of your goodness. O hard then am I, and too cruel, slow to believe and to hear Christ the Lord, who so often has poured out the water of tears and his blood for me in vain! O my wretched and too cruel soul, why did those tears not soften you when first you understood them — the tears which Christ, entering the world and the feeling of this your mortal life, at once shed for you? For your sake he came forth from the heavenly Father into this world, and by tears signified the first pitiable evils of this life. And when you saw this you were not moved, but waited for the shedding of blood; and behold, the child of eight days, being circumcised, shed tears and blood together — and not even so were you softened! Why is this? Because that child there perhaps was showing you the feeling of the flesh and body only, and you therefore waited for signs of the inward feeling of your God? Behold then his tears. And this pouring out of water is for you and over you. Why then will you not be moved? What do you wait for? I wait, you will say, and I have waited, for greater movings of my God, that I may be moved and myself feel better. O wretched and deplorable soul, that art so hard! See then and acknowledge the tears which the Lord sheds over the coming destruction and the utter ingratitude of Jerusalem; likewise those which he shed on the cross as he gave up his spirit. And if this is not enough, or you desire the shedding of the Lord's blood rather than of his tears, behold the sweat of blood, where the two are mingled together; and see besides the blood flowing from the extremities of his whole body — from the bonds, the blows, the scourges, the crowning; and that for you, as if you alone were the cause of it all. And if these signs do not yet move you, come to the very veins, and consider how for you they are all emptied of the purer blood of the immolated Lamb; and if all this does not suffice, take the most pure blood by itself, and take separately the water which flowed from the Lord's side, and with Longinus heal your soul; and do not wish to try greater signs of the divine Goodness from the sufferings of his Humanity, for after this Christ, rising from the dead, suffers no more.

units.la: Pridie festi sancti Francisci, dum celebrarem officium unius martyris relicti, ad quem dudum est mihi magna devotio, ego applicavi missae sacrificium parentibus meis vivis ac mortuis, omnibusque qui ex familia nostra profluxerunt; et consequenter pro omnibus familiis fratrum meorum qui sunt in Societate Jesu Christi. Haec dum facerem, venit in me magna et devota memoria eorum quibus obligati sumus naturaliter, scilicet parentibus. Unde visum est optimuñ futurum esse si invocavero angelos custodes. talium familiarum nostrarum, quibus secundum Deum sint agendae gratiae, per quos petendae sint excusationes propter peccata multa. quae commissa sunt hucusque a talibus familiis, et postulanda multa beneficia quibus nune indigent, et posthac indigebunt. i Optabam quoque ex animo ut, illo singulari sacrificio, ego excusari possem ab illis culpis quascumque ego contraxero; et eo quod pro posse et secundum opportunitatem non adjuvem fratres meos in orando, obsecrando, gratias agendo, et postulando pro ipsis, et pro illis quibus ipsi tenentur.
units.en: On the eve of the feast of Saint Francis, while I celebrated the office of a certain forgotten martyr, to whom I have long had great devotion, I applied the sacrifice of the Mass to my parents, living and dead, and to all who have sprung from our family; and consequently for all the families of my brethren who are in the Society of Jesus Christ. While I did this, there came upon me a great and devout remembrance of those to whom we are bound by nature, that is, our parents. Whence it seemed to me that it would be best to invoke the guardian angels of these families of ours, through whom, according to God, thanks should be given, through whom excuses should be sought for the many sins hitherto committed by such families, and many benefits begged which they now need and hereafter will need. I wished also from my heart that by that particular sacrifice I might be excused from whatever faults I have contracted, and from my failure to help my brethren, so far as I can and as occasion serves, by praying, beseeching, giving thanks, and petitioning for them, and for those to whom they are bound.

units.la: Post communionem, ego sensi magnum desiderium sicuti senseram quoque die praecedenti, post eumdem actum, ut Christus quem sumpseram me totum secum revocaret intra me ipsum; ut et cohabitarem, et cooperarer in mei ipsius reaedificatione, reparatione, ete. Petebam quoque ui ipse, sub quo sunt infiniti modi essendi, saltem accidentales, dignaretur revocare in me ipsum meum esse, vivere, et operari; ut novo modo sim \ in ordine ad ipsum, et ad omnia alia, et novo modo vivam, et me habeam in omnibus operibus meis, ita ut me quotidie mutet in melius, qui solus habet esse et vivere exactum per se immutabiliter.
units.en: After communion I felt a great desire — as I had felt the day before also, after the same act — that Christ whom I had received would call me back wholly with himself into my own inward self; that I might dwell with him, and work with him in my own rebuilding and repair. I asked also that he, under whom there are infinite modes of being, at least accidental ones, would deign to call back into himself my being, my living and my working; that I might stand in a new way ordered towards him and towards all else, and in a new way live and bear myself in all my works — he daily changing me for the better, who alone has being and life exact and unchangeable in himself.

units.la: In die sancti Francisci, inter alia bona desideria quae in orationibus et meditationibus sensi, ego maxime optavi, et idipsum cum satis spirituali et pio affectu a Deo petii, ut per virtutem sacrificii missae mihi concederetur, ut divus Franciscus et quivis alius sanctus posthac mei me-' minisset; idque tam efficaciter, ut si unumquemque in articulo mortis suae ego cum magna tribulatione cordis hoc ipsum petivissem illis verbis: Memento mei dum veneris in regnum Christi.
units.en: On the day of Saint Francis, among other good desires which I felt in prayers and meditations, I wished above all — and asked this same thing of God with a truly spiritual and devout affection — that by the virtue of the sacrifice of the Mass it might be granted me that Saint Francis, and every other saint, should hereafter remember me; and that as efficaciously as if, at the hour of each one's death, I had with great tribulation of heart asked this very thing in those words: Remember me when thou comest into the kingdom of Christ.

units.la: Dum cogitarem eodem die quaedam circa modum bene orandi, et modos quosdam bene operandi, et etiam quonam pacto bona desideria orationum sunt viae quaedam ad bona opera, hic ego annotavi et clare sensi in spiritu quod qui quaerit Deum in operibus bonis, -melius ipsum inveniet postea in oratione, ut postea inveniat in operibus. Qui quaerit igitur et invenit spiritum Christi in bonis operibus, ille multo solidius proficit quam qui negotiatur in sola oratione; -hic videlicet ipsum in affectu, et ille habet in effectu. Nitendum est igitar ut teipsum frangas et mortifices, vincas et aptes ađ opus bonum -Fr Bii 5 suscipiendum per bona opera. Fx hoc enim sen- ties frequenter hanc esse meliorem praeparationem ad orationem. mentalem. Vita igitur tua ita se habeat cum Martha et Magdalena; ita nitatur orationi et piis actionibus; ita denique commis- ceatur ex activa et contemplativa, ut si quando alterum propter alterum, et non propter se, sicut saepe accidit exercueris, id est orationem intenderis ut medium ad melius operandum, vel e contra opus propter orationem, dico quod ubi ista duo ad se invicem putabis esse ordinanda, melius erit, magis universaliter loquendo, ut ordines omnes orationes tuas ad thesauros bonorum operum, quam, contra, bona opera; id est, hoc intendere ut thesauros facias per orationes tuas: Secus esset si quis vitam ducat pure contemplativam, cujus scopus est exerceri in accumulatione thesaurorum divinae cognitionis et amoris; cui non tam universales petendae sunt gratiae, quae sunt necessariae iis qui in actione versantur. Hi etenim, quoniam multis modis se habent, et supra se, et prope se, et infra se, et ante, et retro, a dextris et a sinistris, per quae omnia varias virtutes operantes requirunt. Hinc fit ut hi multis virtutibus debeant perfici, alioquin defecturi. Ipsi habent opus quodam gradu patientiae, quodam humilitatis, quodam charitatis, et caeterarum virtutum in ordine ad inferiores suos aut etiam superiores; aliarum quoque virtutum praedictarum et aliarum gradibus, proùt in aliis et aliis versantur occasionibus, indigent; proindeque facile est ut isti videant ex operibus nimium multas necessitates etiam proprias, quae opus habent divinis virtutibus, unctionibus, variisque donorum Dei infusionibus; nec pro se tantum, sed pro proximis, quibus student. Pro quorum auxilis, juvaminibus indigemus, et multis spiritualibus luminibus, ac oculis, auribus, caeterisque sensibus; nec iis tantum, sed etiam fortitudine, sed pietate, virtute, liberalitate, diligentia caeterisque variis virtutibus animi et corporis. Quibus dum caremus, facile est videre haec duo incommoda, unum videlicet nostra ex parte, quod in nobis defectus sit, et alterum ex parte proximorum, quibus non bene,, sed multis modis malis, aut saltem minus bene prospicitur et providetur frequenter.
units.en: While on the same day I thought over certain things about the way of praying well, and certain ways of working well, and also how the good desires of prayers are ways towards good works, I noted and clearly felt in spirit that he who seeks God in good works will afterwards find him better in prayer, so as afterwards to find him in works. He, therefore, who seeks and finds the spirit of Christ in good works makes far more solid progress than he who deals in prayer alone: the one has him in affection, the other holds him in effect. Strive therefore to break and mortify yourself, to conquer and fit yourself for undertaking good work, by good works. For from this you will often feel that this is the better preparation for mental prayer. Let your life, then, keep company with both Martha and Magdalen; let it lean on prayer and on pious actions; in short, let it be so compounded of the active and the contemplative that, if ever you have exercised the one for the sake of the other and not for itself — as often happens: intending prayer, that is, as a means to work better, or contrariwise work for the sake of prayer — I say that where you think these two must be ordered to one another, it will be better, speaking more universally, to order all your prayers towards the treasures of good works, than, contrariwise, good works towards prayer — that is, to intend the making of treasures through your prayers. It would be otherwise if a man led a purely contemplative life, whose aim is to be exercised in the accumulation of the treasures of divine knowledge and love; such a one does not need to ask graces so universal as are necessary to those who are engaged in action. For these, since they stand in many relations — above themselves, near themselves, beneath themselves, before and behind, on the right hand and on the left — require various working virtues for all of these. Hence it comes that they must be perfected in many virtues, or else they will fail. They have need of a certain degree of patience, of humility, of charity, and of the other virtues, in relation to those under them and likewise those above them; and they need degrees of the aforesaid and of other virtues according as they are engaged in this or that occasion. And so it is easy for such men to see from their works exceedingly many needs, their own included, which require divine virtues, anointings, and various infusions of the gifts of God; and not for themselves only, but for the neighbours whom they serve. For whose help we stand in need of aids, and of many spiritual lights, eyes, ears and other senses; and not these only, but also fortitude, piety, virtue, liberality, diligence, and the other various virtues of soul and body. And while we lack these, it is easy to see these two harms: one on our side, that there is defect in us; the other on the side of our neighbours, who are frequently provided and cared for not well, but in many bad ways, or at least less well.

units.la: Igitur in hunc scopum intendendae erunt nos- trae orationes, potius quam contra, id est quam talia opera propter orandum. Dixerim haec in genere, et considerando scopum ipsius vitae hoc modo incaeoeptae; alıter enim, id est specialiter et magis particulariter loquendo, non potest fieri quin frequenter oremus in finem aliquorum bonorum operum; et etiam contra, frequenter operemur multa ut consequamur scopym aliquem aliquarum orationum.
units.en: To this mark, then, our prayers must be directed, rather than the contrary — that is, rather than such works directed to the end of praying. I have said this in general, and considering the aim of a life undertaken in this way; for otherwise — speaking specially and more particularly — it cannot be but that we often pray for the sake of certain good works, and also, contrariwise, often do many things in order to attain the aim of certain prayers.

units.la: Danda est autem opera ut non solum ad res pure spirituales, ut sunt contemplatio et oratio mentalis atque affectualis, quaeratur spiritus ut bene ac optime fiant; sed etiam totis viribus nitendum est ut mixtis quoque operibus externis, orationibus vocalibus, aut aliis collocutionibus particularibus, vel quae fiunt publice ad populum, idem inveniatur.
units.en: Care must be taken, however, that the spirit be sought not only for things purely spiritual, such as contemplation and mental and affective prayer, that they may be done well and excellently; but we must also strive with all our strength that the same be found in mixed outward works, in vocal prayers, and in other conversations, whether private or made publicly to the people.

units.la: Verum est multa quidem opera fieri posse, et multa verba dici, et facile, absque motione spiritus; et maxime cum non sunt opera agenda, aut verba dicenda contra proprium habitum, vel etiam propriam voluntatem. In iis autem ultimis magis aperte videtur et magis apparet necessitas spiritus, aut alias saepius omittentur.
units.en: True it is that many works can be done, and many words said, easily and without any motion of the spirit — above all when the works to be done or words to be said are not against one's own habit, or against one's own will. But in these last the necessity of the spirit is more openly seen and appears more plainly; otherwise they will very often be left undone.

units.la: Universaliter tamen quaerendus est spiritus ad intelligendum et promptius volendum illud bonum, quod in talibus actionibus inest; maxime vero in illis quae dixi magis esse difficilia et veteri homini contraria; quae sicut requirunt spiritum majorem ex quo procedant, ita quoque, dum fiunt, per ipsa major spiritus acquiritur, quam per alia quae non ita contraria sunt. Ex his etiam multo melius perspicies quid in homine sit, et quare indigeat spiritu, quam ex aliis quae facile fiunt et absque contradictione. Sic contingit in oratione mentali et affectuali, quia et ipsa requirit ipsum interiorem spiritualem et actualem spiritum; aloquin omnino mens divagatur, et non sequitur propositum orationis scopum.
units.en: Universally, however, the spirit is to be sought for understanding, and for willing more promptly, the good which lies in such actions; but above all in those which I have said are harder and contrary to the old man; which, as they require a greater spirit from which to proceed, so also, while they are being done, a greater spirit is gained through them than through others which are not so contrary. From these, too, you will perceive much better what is in man, and why he needs the spirit, than from other things which are done easily and without contradiction. So it happens in mental and affective prayer, for it also requires that inward, spiritual and actual spirit; otherwise the mind wanders altogether, and does not follow the intended aim of the prayer.

units.la: Erga hoc propositum quod est de operibus, notari potest triplicia esse opera, circa quae maxime nos oporteat exerceri; quaedam ad se ipsum, quaedam ad proximum, et quaedam ad Deum ipsum. Ad se ipsum, verbi gratia, ut sunt opera paenitentiae,: quae sunt in propriam morti-; ficationem aut abnegationem, castigationem et paenalitatem, veluti jejunia, peregrinationes, vigi- liae, dimissio aliquoram bonorum temporalium, aut etiam divitiarum, caeteraque hujusmodi quae corpus defatigant, et voluntatem circa propria convincunt. Ad proximum, sunt ea omnia quae ipsum juvant, consolantur, aut levant, ut eleemosynae, caeteraque omnia quae ad curam ipsius l corporalem aut spiritualem pertinent. Ad Deum, pertinent directe (quanquam omnia dicta ad ipsum etiam tendant) illa quae spectant ad ejus, rerumque ad ipsum et sanctos ejus pertinentium, honorem et cultum, ut sunt oblationes, ornatus templorum, decor sacramentorum, impensae luminariorum, etc.
units.en: On this subject of works it may be noted that the works in which we ought chiefly to exercise ourselves are threefold: some towards oneself, some towards one's neighbour, and some towards God himself. Towards oneself are, for example, the works of penance, which make for one's own mortification or self-denial, chastisement and penalty — such as fasts, pilgrimages, vigils, the giving up of certain temporal goods or even of riches, and other such things as weary the body and overcome the will in what concerns itself. Towards one's neighbour are all those things which help, console or relieve him, such as alms, and everything else that belongs to his bodily or spiritual care. To God belong directly (although all the foregoing also tend towards him) the things that concern the honour and worship of him and of the things pertaining to him and his saints — such as offerings, the adornment of churches, the beauty of the sacraments, the expenses of lights, and the rest.

units.la: In primo genere modorum trium dictorum tu praeparas teipsum, et quodam modo te tibi constituis contrarium ad victoriam tui. In secundo genere, tu evadis in hominem utilem proximo. In tertio vero, tu ostendis te pium erga ipsum Deum, et res sacras, et sanctos. Prima pars potest etiam quodam modo spectare ad opera paenitentiae, secunda ad opera charitatis, tertia ad opera pietatis, sed tamen omnia vere dici possunt opera paenitentiae, et omnia opera charitatis, et omnia opera pietatis.
units.en: In the first of the three kinds named you prepare yourself, and in a certain way set yourself against yourself, for the victory over yourself. In the second kind, you come forth as a man useful to your neighbour. In the third, you show yourself devout towards God himself, and holy things, and the saints. The first part may also in a manner be referred to works of penance, the second to works of charity, the third to works of piety; and yet all may truly be called works of penance, and all works of charity, and all works of piety.

units.la: Die quodam, dum celebraturus essem missam in templo Sanctae Crucis, pro defunctis benefactoribus et fundatoribus, et generaliter pro tota civitate Spirensi, dicturus autem eram missam de Sancta Cruce, propterea quod ibi sit Crux quaedam quae olim, dum esset in magna devotione, multa miracula operata est ex virtute divina, ad fidem commovendam et excitandam devotionem, et propter ipsam etiam fidem quae tunc inerat multis; dedit tunc mihi Dominus optimum spiritum et magnum affectum devotionis erga talem crucem, ut ipsam venerarer, et universaliter omne vexillum et omne signum crucis. Apprehendebam cum fide et fiducia mirabilem virtutem crucis contra daemones; et propterea desiderabam fieri posse ut ego semper et actualiter habere possem crucem, dico etiam materialem, spiritualiter, in mente mea, fide et spe; et similiter optabam de aqua benedicta, et pro omni re sanctificata in aliquo verbo Dei, aut aliquo signo crucis signata: Idem praeterea de imaginibus crucifixi; beate Virginis et sanctorum et de reliquiis sanctorum corporum, et similium. Imo etiam cupiebam posse fieri ut una aliqua tota matorialis ecclesia, cum omnibus aliis quae ibi cernuntur ad pietatem facientia, spiritualiter includeretur mente mea, et ut semper et actualiter haberetur intra me, et ego intra illam essem in spiritu meo, videns omnia supradicta cum fide et devotione, maxime autem ipsum corpus Domini ibi conservatum, cui ecclesiae assistit maxima virtutum omnium abundantia, propterea quod ibi corporaliter sit Ghristus et corpus ipsius, quod habitaculum est corporale et verum templum totius divinae virtutis, et omnis plenitudinis divinitatis.
units.en: On a certain day, when I was to celebrate Mass in the church of the Holy Cross for the departed benefactors and founders, and generally for the whole city of Speyer, and was to say the Mass of the Holy Cross — because there is there a certain Cross which of old, when it was held in great devotion, wrought many miracles by divine power, to stir up faith and awaken devotion, and also because of the faith which then was in many — the Lord gave me then an excellent spirit and a great affection of devotion towards that cross, so that I venerated it, and universally every standard and every sign of the cross. I apprehended with faith and confidence the wonderful power of the cross against the demons; and therefore I desired that it might be possible for me always and actually to have the cross — I mean even the material cross — spiritually in my mind, by faith and hope; and I wished the like concerning holy water, and every thing sanctified by some word of God or signed with some sign of the cross. The same, moreover, of the images of the crucifix, of the blessed Virgin and the saints, and of the relics of holy bodies, and the like. Nay, I even desired that it might be possible that some one whole material church, with all the other things seen in it that make for piety, should be spiritually enclosed in my mind, and always and actually held within me, and that I might be within it in my spirit, seeing all the aforesaid with faith and devotion — but above all the very body of the Lord there preserved; to which church there is attached a very great abundance of all powers, because Christ is there bodily, and his body, which is the bodily dwelling-place and true temple of all divine power, and of all the fulness of the godhead.

units.la: Hic ego, clare videbam et sentiebam spiritu, Christum non solum velle ut ipsum apprehendamus mente, sed et tractemus ea omnia quae ex ipso virtutem sumunt, et secundum fidem et pietatem credentium ex beneplacito Dei nobis sunt parata; tanquam praeambula ad ipsum qui ad haec nos movet; dans devotionem; piam äffectionem et fidem humilibus et simplicibus, quam fidem non utique daret, nisi esset ad ipsius honorem et nostram utilitatem: Fit autem aliquando ut ipsemet Deus faciat sentire et experiri virtutem aliquam sūam per res sanctas, nobis non cogitantibus, neque adhuc fidem circa talia habentibus, ita ut şuccurrat postea illud: Locus iste aut res ista sancta est, et ego nesciebam. Postea autem excitatur devotio et fides, visa prima operatione Dei, absque nobis aut fide nostra facta. Sic igitur clare videtur Deum ipsum honorificare res istas per se, et non solum nobis communicare suam virtutem, nec omnia pendere ex fide nostra originaliter. O et si igitur tu, anima mea, posses apprehendere et comprehendere, postquam res ipsas in animam immittere non valemus, non dico solum nomen Domini Nostri Jesu Christi in quo est tua salus, sed etiam nomem virginis Mariae matris Dei, quam solido gaudio gauderes! O si virtutem crucis cum signo ejus sentires! O si nomem sancli Petri mente cum re ipsa spiritualiter teneres super cor tuum; sane tu sentires varias divinitatis virtutes, quae iis rebus insunt 'et nominibus, quibus equidem si affecta esses et depicta aliud posses coram Deo et sanctis Angelis ipsius, et alud opereraris in demonibus et malignis s ugt p. A s spiritibus, qui non siħñe causa tantopere nituntur ut omnia sacra et sanctificata et vera signa deleantur de memoria hominum; sperantes hine posse fieri ut tandem ipsius Christi quoque memoria ẹt nominis ipsius, caeteris sublatis de medio, tolli possit. Cresce igitur, anima mea, in devotione venerationis omnium rerum sanctarum et sancltificatarum, et Crucis signo quocumque signatarum. Actualisa te ipsum in dies magis ac magis in his contemplandis, et cordi tuo admovendis, in fide et fiducia divinae virtutis coram talibus assıstentis. Ea in te primo infige et depinge, donec paretur tibi via ad fontes unde tales aquae nascuntur et tales rivuli tam sancli. Dum autem datur tibi aliquid haurire -de fontibus ipsiusmet Salvatoris, cave ne contemnas, aut non quanticumque potes facias, rivos Dei, et sanctorum, aliarumque virtutum quae ex caeteris rebus, sicut dixi, manant. Non tibi datur aqua fontis ac principii quasi in rivis, sed abundanter supra quam vel merearis vel operari possis; et ad hoc ut melius laudare possis fontem, non solum propter id quod est in se, sed etiam propter ipsius tantas et tam varias emissiones, et flumina divinorum liquorum, quos inde emanare et fluere experientia sensus spiritus tui didiceris.
units.en: Here I clearly saw and felt in spirit that Christ wills not only that we apprehend him with the mind, but also that we handle all those things which take their power from him, and which, according to the faith and piety of believers, are prepared for us by the good pleasure of God — as forerunners to himself, who moves us to them; giving devotion, pious affection and faith to the humble and simple, which faith he assuredly would not give unless it were to his honour and our profit. And it sometimes happens that God himself makes us feel and experience some power of his through holy things, when we are not thinking of it, and do not yet have faith about such things; so that afterwards that word comes home: This place, or this thing, is holy, and I knew it not. And afterwards devotion and faith are stirred up, when the first working of God has been seen, done without us or our faith. Thus, then, it clearly appears that God himself honours these things of himself, and does not only communicate his power to us through them, nor does everything depend originally on our faith. O my soul, if only you could apprehend and comprehend — since we cannot bring the things themselves into the soul — I do not say only the name of Our Lord Jesus Christ, in which is your salvation, but even the name of the Virgin Mary, Mother of God, with what solid joy would you rejoice! O if you felt the power of the cross with its sign! O if you held the name of Saint Peter in your mind, with the thing itself, spiritually upon your heart — truly you would feel the various powers of the divinity which are in these things and names; and if you were affected and imprinted with them, you would count for something else before God and his holy Angels, and would work something else upon the demons and malignant spirits; who not without cause strive so hard that all sacred and sanctified things and true signs may be blotted out from the memory of men; hoping that thus it may at last come about that the memory of Christ himself too, and of his name, the rest being taken out of the way, may be taken away. Grow therefore, my soul, in the devotion of venerating all things holy and sanctified, and signed with the sign of the Cross in whatever manner. Actualize yourself daily more and more in contemplating these things, and in bringing them to your heart, in faith and confidence of the divine power that stands by such things. Fix them and imprint them in yourself first, until the way be prepared for you to the fountains whence such waters spring, and such holy streams. But when it is given you to draw something from the fountains of the Saviour himself, beware of despising, or failing to value as much as you can, the streams of God and of the saints, and of the other powers which flow, as I have said, from the other things. The water of the fountain and source is not given you as it were in streams, but abundantly, beyond what you could deserve or work for; and to this end, that you may better praise the fountain, not only for what it is in itself, but also for its so many and so varied outpourings, and the rivers of divine liquors which you have learned, by the experience of the sense of your spirit, to issue and flow from it.

units.la: Quodam die, dum cogitarem et meditarer ad quoddam propositum verbum Christi: Auferetur sponsus ab eis, et: Numquid possunt filii sponsi lugere, quamdiu sponsus est cum illis? occurrit mihi maxima quaedam admiratio cum pio erga Christum spiritu, qua per modum excelamationis dicebam ipsi Christo: O Domine, quidnam est hoc quod in ordine ad discipulos tuos te voces spousum quası quo gaudeant ipsi, sicut et gaudent filii sponsi dum cum illis est sponsus, et tamen tu in ordine ad teipsum non ut sponsus deliciaris, sed potius ut omnium servus, ct in ordine ad omnes postremus ac infimus habearis, ita tu laboras, tu sudas, tu vituperaris et sperneris, usque ad damnationem; et passionem mortis crucis. Tu laboras, inquam, mi Domine; ut tui quiescant; tu tristaris, ut ipsi gaudeant; et tandem mori cupis pro ipsorum resurrectione i vere illud est simile quod poeta dixit: Sic vos, non vobis, vellera fertis, oves; Sic vos, non vobis, mellificatis, apes; Sic vos, non Vobis, nidificatis, aves, etc.
units.en: On a certain day, while I thought and meditated on a saying of Christ, on a certain occasion: The bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and: Can the children of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? — there came to me a very great wonder, with a devout spirit towards Christ, in which by way of exclamation I said to Christ himself: O Lord, what is this, that in relation to your disciples you call yourself the bridegroom, as one in whom they rejoice, as the children of the bridegroom rejoice while the bridegroom is with them; and yet in relation to yourself you take your delight not as a bridegroom, but rather are held as the servant of all, and in relation to all the last and lowest; so you labour, you sweat, you are reviled and despised, even to condemnation and the suffering of the death of the cross. You labour, I say, my Lord, that yours may rest; you are sorrowful, that they may rejoice; and at last you desire to die for their resurrection. Truly it is like what the poet said: So you, not for yourselves, bear your fleeces, O sheep; so you, not for yourselves, make honey, O bees; so you, not for yourselves, build nests, O birds.

units.la: Tu enim alis sponsus eras; tibi erat crux eontinua. Tu caeteris fuisti sponsus; caeteri tibi fuerunt onera, cruces atque tormenta. Sit nomen tuum, quod est Jesus, benedictum, Amen! et laudabile; et superexaltatum in secula, Amen!
units.en: For you were bridegroom to others; for yourself there was the continual cross. You were bridegroom to the rest; the rest were to you burdens, crosses and torments. Blessed be your name, which is Jesus. Amen! — and praiseworthy, and exalted above all for ever. Amen!

units.la: In die alio, qui erat Dominicae, mane dum dicerem officium et distraherer, indeque peterem auxilium Dei et beatae Virginis, ego recepi satis multa bona intervalla clarae devotionis, et responsa varia quae me exhortabantur ad desiderandum continuitatem actualis spiritus boni assis- - tentis; maxime autem ut consectarer majorem intractum Säāncti Spiritus, quo magis ad finem divini officii procedebam; intractum dico, quasi tractum intro, qui a Deo sit, nobis petentibus, ac omnibus modis nitentibus, ut melius capiamus yerba sancta, et illa capiant in nobis radices suas, et virtutem suam seminantem imprimant. Verbum etenim quodcumque, de ore Dei procedens, verum Dei semen est, Deum ipsum, quodam modo, quantum ex se est, in nobis producens ac generans. Desiderabam etiam, circa horas canonicas, ut possem ibi crescere, et eo amplius quo magis accedebam ad finem. Et ego considerabam quo pacto Christus, quanto magis accedebat ad finem vitae suae, eo amplius patiebatur, et majora tormenta ei inferebantur; propter hoc sentiebam crescere oportere in devotione horarum, ita ut cum perventum fuerit ad horam Nonae, sentiri possit vis ipsius mortis et expirationis Jesu Christi, quae hora nona accidit.
units.en: On another day, which was a Sunday, in the morning, while I said the office and was distracted, and thereupon asked the help of God and of the blessed Virgin, I received a good many intervals of clear devotion, and various answers exhorting me to desire the continuance of the actual good spirit assisting me; but above all to follow after a greater indrawing of the Holy Spirit the nearer I came to the end of the divine office — an indrawing, I say, as it were a drawing inward, which comes from God when we ask, and strive in every way, that we may better take in the holy words, and that they may take root in us, and imprint their seminal power. For every word proceeding from the mouth of God is a true seed of God, producing and begetting God himself, in a certain manner, so far as in it lies, within us. I desired also, as regards the canonical hours, that I might grow in them, and the more, the nearer I came to the end. And I considered how Christ, the nearer he came to the end of his life, suffered the more, and greater torments were laid upon him; on this account I felt that one ought to grow in devotion through the hours, so that when one comes to the hour of None, the power of the very death and expiring of Jesus Christ may be felt, which came to pass at the ninth hour.

units.la: In die sancti Dionysii Areopagitae et sociorum ejus, ego reperi multam devotionem, rogando ipsos ut mihi dignarentur impetrare aliquam gratiam permanentem a Patre caelesti, aliqùūam etiam a Filio ejus, aliquam etiam a Spiritu Sancto; item aliquam aliam a beata Virgine, et sie de aliis Sanctis, maxime ab aliquibus magis peculiaribus per quos nominatim discurrebam. Petebam etiam ab ipso sancto Dionysio spirituale auxilium, rogans ipsum quatenus impetraret mihi aliquod initium boni sensus, pro corde meo, in verbis timoris Domini, aut in verbis amoris, seu cujuscumque alterius virtutis, qua maxime ego egere possem. Pro oculis quoque petebam aliquid, et pro sensu auditus, tactus, gustus atque odoratus.. Sensi praeterea aliquod novum desiderium circa hoc, ut sanctissi- mum Sacramentum, intrans in stomachum meum, dignaretur cibare animam et eam nutrire, sicut ipsum corpus nutritur materiali cibo panis et vini.
units.en: On the day of Saint Denys the Areopagite and his companions I found much devotion, praying them to deign to obtain for me some abiding grace from the heavenly Father, some also from his Son, some also from the Holy Spirit; likewise some other from the blessed Virgin, and so of the other saints, above all from certain more particular ones through whom I ran by name. I asked also of Saint Denys himself spiritual help, praying him to obtain for me some beginning of good feeling, for my heart, in the words of the fear of the Lord, or in the words of love, or of whatever other virtue I might most need. For my eyes too I asked something, and for the sense of hearing, of touch, of taste and of smell. I felt besides a certain new desire in this: that the most holy Sacrament, entering into my stomach, would deign to feed my soul and nourish it, as the body itself is nourished by the material food of bread and wine.

units.la: In die sancti Cerbonii confessoris et pontificis, dum cogitarem circa processum vitae et mortis Jesu Christi Domini Nostri, venerunt mihi in mentem quaedam colloquia, cum quadam #eneritudine spiritus, ubi dicebam: O Jesu Christe, tua mors sit vita mea, et in tua morte sciam vitam invenire! tui labores sint quies mea! tua debilitas humana sit fortitudo mea! tua confusio sit mea glorificatio! passio, laetitia! tristitia, gaudum! in tua humiliatione sit mea exaltatio, et in summis malis tuis, cuncta bona mea! Tu enim, mi Domine, vitam, quae in. mortem tendebat absque remedio, reparasti; et mortem, quae semper duratura videbatur, destruxisti!
units.en: On the day of Saint Cerbonius, confessor and bishop, while I thought on the course of the life and death of Jesus Christ Our Lord, there came into my mind certain colloquies, with a certain tenderness of spirit, in which I said: O Jesus Christ, may your death be my life, and in your death may I know how to find life! May your labours be my rest! Your human weakness my strength! Your confusion my glorification! Your passion my delight! Your sadness my joy! In your humiliation be my exaltation, and in your utmost evils all my goods! For you, my Lord, repaired the life that was tending to death without remedy, and destroyed the death that seemed destined to last for ever!

units.la: In die quo celebravi officium sancti Marci confessoris, ego inveni multa sensa optima desideriorum, et inter caetera optabam ut omnia desideria, quae ipse beatus Marcus habuit super salutem, non solum Germanorum, sed omnium fidelium, dum viveret, adimpleantur in nostris temporibus. Idem quoque rogabam ut contingeret circa omnia omnium aliorum sanctorum desideria, ut sic tandem magis: universaliter impleatur dictum illud: Desiderium animae ejus tribuisti ei, etc., dum non solum desiderium, im quo nune vivit quilibet sanctus, gloriose videatur adimpletum, sed etiam quodlibet pium et sanctum aliud quod ipse habuit in vita, erga honorem Dei et salutem animarum.
units.en: On the day when I celebrated the office of Saint Mark the confessor, I found many excellent movements of desire, and among the rest I wished that all the desires which blessed Mark had for the salvation, not only of the Germans but of all the faithful, while he lived, might be fulfilled in our times. I prayed likewise that the same might come to pass with all the desires of all the other saints, so that at last that saying might be more universally fulfilled: Thou hast given him his soul's desire, and so forth — when not only the desire in which each saint now lives shall be seen gloriously fulfilled, but also every other pious and holy desire which he had in his life, towards the honour of God and the salvation of souls.

units.la: Eodem die, ego habui quoddam desiderium j dum essem celebraturus missam, ut Deus dignaretur acceptare tale sacrificium ad tantum gradum fructus spiritualis, pro hac civitate Spirensi, quantum posset esse ille fructus, quem hine usque ad mortem perseverando ego essen facturus cum alis meis sociis; quod desiderium sicut alia similia, licet nòn sit adimplendum ad modum mei captus. et voluntatis, non tamen ideo nùllum est apud Deum, ex quo manat et suggeritur spiritu ipsius.
units.en: On the same day, when I was about to celebrate Mass, I had a certain desire that God would deign to accept that sacrifice for this city of Speyer, to as great a degree of spiritual fruit as that fruit might be which I, persevering here until death with my other companions, should accomplish; which desire, like others of the kind, although it is not to be fulfilled according to the measure of my understanding and will, is not therefore nothing with God, from whom it flows and by whose spirit it is suggested.

units.la: Post missam, dum cogitarem modum quo in ipsa me habuissem, illud visum est mihi notatu dignissimum, ut videlicet peterem instanter a Deo memoriam mihi dari et:augeri, ad recogni- Doon SE is tionem cujuscumque praeteriti spiritualis exercitii, idque per meritum passionis Domini Nostri Jesu Christi, quod est memoriale maximum nostrum; et ut mihi daretur intellectus ad illa exercitia quae praesentia sunt; et voluntas bene. desiderans, ad illa quae sunt futura. Haec intelligo non quia separantur ipsae tres potentiae in talibus actibus, sed quia in praeterita respiciat memoria, ip praesentia intellectus et in futura desiderium.
units.en: After Mass, while I thought over the manner in which I had borne myself in it, this seemed to me most worthy of note: namely, that I should earnestly ask of God that memory be given me and increased, for the recognition of every past spiritual exercise — and that through the merit of the passion of Our Lord Jesus Christ, which is our greatest memorial; and that understanding be given me for those exercises which are present; and a rightly desiring will, for those which are to come. This I understand not as though the three powers were separated in such acts, but because memory looks to the past, understanding to the present, and desire to the future.

units.la: Die sequenti, dum dicerem officium sancti Stephani papae et martyris, cujus caput est in Ecclesia Spirensi venerabiliter conservatum, ego sensi magna desideria, et ea cum magna fide et spe circa adimplėtionem ipsorum, ut verbi gratia sanctus Stephanus dignaretur esse primus quùi nobis aperiret aliquod ostium circa res spirituales; dicebam autem sub his terminis, prout dabatur, et quia ita dabatur: Beatissime pater ẹt sanctissime in veritate, fac precibus tuis ut opus ipsum circa quod debeo versari aperiatur; quasi dicerem: Non sufficit quod ego aperiar et fiam dispositus ad opera messis Christi, sed oportet etiam ut ipsa opera aperiantur mihi et disponantur per Dei gratiam.
units.en: On the following day, while I said the office of Saint Stephen, pope and martyr, whose head is venerably preserved in the church of Speyer, I felt great desires, and those with great faith and hope of their fulfilment: as, for example, that Saint Stephen would deign to be the first to open to us some door in spiritual things; and I said it in these terms, as it was given me, and because it was so given: Most blessed father, and truly most holy, bring it about by your prayers that the work itself about which I must be engaged may be opened; as if I said: It is not enough that I be opened and made ready for the works of Christ's harvest, but the works themselves must also be opened to me and made ready by the grace of God.

units.la: Dum communicarem in missa, habui aliud desiderium, cum magna devotione, quo cupiebam (et ita petebam) ut illudsanctissimum Sacramentum dignaretur me facere quoddam instrumentum sui obediens, et item Matris suae, et omnium ac singulorum sanctorum, et omnium Angelorum, et animarum omnium purgalorii, et cujuslibet viventis; per quod instrumentum unusquisque posset operari secundum voluntatem suam, ad eum modum quo me cunctis obtuli. Hoc faxit Christus ut possim praestare, ut possim esse omnium, et non solum esse sed et vivere, et operari omnibus, et pro omnibus, et vice omnium dictorum, in laudem Dei et salutem omnium vivorum et mortuorum.
units.en: While I communicated at Mass I had another desire, with great devotion, in which I longed (and so I asked) that that most holy Sacrament would deign to make me an instrument obedient to itself, and likewise to his Mother, and to each and all of the saints, and to all the Angels, and to all the souls of purgatory, and to every living person; an instrument through which each one might work according to his will, in the same manner in which I offered myself to all. May Christ grant that I may perform this: that I may be all men's — and not only be, but live and work for all, and on behalf of all those named, to the praise of God and the salvation of all the living and the dead.

units.la: In die septem Fratrum ordinis minorum, dum celebrarem, et celebrando sentirem quemdam timorem ne animus meus obscuraretur in charitate, aut angustiaretur, sed cum desiderio ut dilataretur, erga aliquas personas, quarum defectus quidam veniebant in mentem, ego accepi hoc responsum intra me ipsum: Time potius ne Dominus, quem ante te vides, tibi claudat cor suae hilaritatis, et ne cor tuum erga ipsum et res ipsius reddatur angustiatum. Si enim remanseris dilatatus cum Deo et ipse tecum, facile fiet ut omnia alia erga te aperta videantur, et tu erga illa. Igitur bonam devotionem quaere erga Deum et Sanctos cjus; et facile invenies ea quae pertinent ad proximum tuum, amicum vel inimicum. Ubi vero aliquid esset quod pertineret ad faciendum aliquam actualem operam, vel locutionem ad reconciliationem cum proximo tuo, tunc illa primo et tanquam medium esset facienda ad consequendam cum Deo reconciliationem, juxta illud: Si frater tuus habet aliquid adversum te, etc. Sed hic quaestio est quando talia sensa proveniunt ex sola apprehensione mentis, et affectu spiritus, ubi opus est sola animi mutatione; et proinde reconciliatio spiritualis tantum requiritur, sicut contingit in variis amaritudinibus quae tollendae ‚sunt de cordibus nostris, ad hoc ut secum haþÞeat charitas sensum benignitatis, patientiae, sustinentiae, supportationis, et non sentiat irritationem ullam, neque perdat fidem erga personas, aut ipsam spem quam habet dum adest principalis Spiritus, sanctus, et rectus, et þo- nus, cum quo adest statim oai et cum devotione veniunt caetera bona quae dixi, maxime dilatatio cordis erga omnia et -erga omnes homines; tolliturque error qui erat in intellectu propter aliquas cogitationes malas aut etiam veras, juxta rationem humanam, propositas tamen a malo spiritu, et tollitur etiam error qui erat in voluntate propter divisiones non bonorum affectuum, aut saltem imperfectionum, quibus quies auferebatur. Cavendum igitur ut in his malis non queratur victoria per fagam, declinando res ipsas, aut personas circa quas contingit fieri tàlem spiritus ac mentis mutationem; sed potius approximandum est illis, imitando Christum qui ita approximavit malefactoribus suis, ut etiam post receptam mortem, perfossus lancea, effuderit in Longinum sanguinem; quod est signum evidentissimum, erga inimicòs, Ghristi continuae charitatis; ita ut, quo magis procedebat inimicus in odio, volens a se expellere Christum et virtutem ejus de medio tollere, eo magis ipse Jesusamore procedebat, non fugiens aut declinans ipsum corpore aut spiritu, sed omnino se totum ipsi inferens, dans carnenı percus- ae o a sori, et ad ejus curationem sanguinem effundens, non vivus tantum, sed etiam jam mortuus. Hoc modo voluit totus aperiri inimicis suis Christus. Quadam die Dominica mensis Octobris, quae fuit 22 ejusdem mensis, anno 1542, hac die, inquam, et die praecedenti, quae fuerat sanctae Ursulae et sociarum ejus, ego determinavi, et inveni apud Deum consilium, parens voļuntati Reverendissimi Domini Moguntini qui significaverat se velle ut irem cum aliis suis Theologis ad concilium Tridentinum, celebrandum et incipiendum in calendis proximis Novembris. Circa quod negotium, ego inveni varios spiritus et varias tristitias* antequam fuissem determinatus; sed de omnibus liberavit me Dominus, in virtute Sanctae et:caecae obedientiae, quae non habet videre neque propriam insufficientiam, neque negotiorium aut operum quae praecipiuntur magnitudinem ac pondus. Quidquid igitur ex hac mea deliberatione, aut potius obedientia, evenerit, id omne, dico, si bonum fuerit, sanctis undecim millibus virginum, secundum sancetissimam Trinitatem, Christum Ressuscilatum, et beatam virginem Mariam, referendum erit.
units.en: On the day of the seven Brothers of the order of friars minor, while I celebrated, and in celebrating felt a certain fear lest my soul be darkened in charity, or straitened — though with the desire that it might be enlarged — towards certain persons whose defects came to mind, I received this answer within myself: Fear rather lest the Lord, whom you see before you, close to you the heart of his cheerfulness, and lest your heart towards him and the things that are his be made strait. For if you remain enlarged with God, and he with you, it will easily come about that all other things appear open towards you, and you towards them. Seek therefore good devotion towards God and his saints, and you will easily find what belongs to your neighbour, friend or enemy. But where there were something to be done — some actual work or word towards reconciliation with your neighbour — then that should be done first, and as a means to obtaining reconciliation with God, according to that word: If thy brother hath aught against thee, and so forth. But here the question concerns those feelings that arise from the mere apprehension of the mind and affection of the spirit, where nothing is needed but a change of soul; and so only a spiritual reconciliation is required — as happens with the various bitternesses which must be taken out of our hearts, so that charity may have with it the sense of kindness, patience, endurance and forbearance, and may feel no irritation, nor lose faith towards persons, nor the hope it has while the principal Spirit is present, holy, right and good; with whom there comes at once, and with devotion, the other goods I have named, above all the enlarging of the heart towards all things and towards all men; and the error is removed which was in the intellect through certain thoughts, evil or even true according to human reason, yet proposed by an evil spirit; and the error is removed also which was in the will through the divisions of affections not good, or at least imperfect, by which quiet was taken away. Care must be taken, then, that in these evils victory be not sought by flight, turning aside from the things themselves, or the persons, about whom such a change of spirit and mind happens to arise; but rather one must draw near to them, imitating Christ, who so drew near to his evildoers that even after death received, pierced by the lance, he poured out his blood upon Longinus; which is a most evident sign of Christ's continual charity towards enemies; so that the further the enemy went in hatred, wishing to drive Christ from him and to take his power out of the way, the further Jesus went in love, not fleeing or turning from him in body or spirit, but bringing his whole self to bear upon him, giving his flesh to the striker, and pouring out his blood for his healing — not only living, but even already dead. In this way Christ willed to be wholly opened to his enemies. On a certain Sunday of the month of October, which was the 22nd of that month, in the year 1542 — on this day, I say, and on the day before, which was that of Saint Ursula and her companions — I made my determination, and found counsel with God, obeying the will of the Most Reverend Lord of Mainz, who had signified that he wished me to go with his other theologians to the council of Trent, to be celebrated and begun on the coming first of November. About this affair I found various spirits and various sadnesses before I was determined; but from all of them the Lord freed me, in the virtue of holy and blind obedience, which is not to look either at its own insufficiency, or at the greatness and weight of the affairs and works commanded. Whatever therefore shall come of this my deliberation, or rather obedience — all of it, I say, if it be good, must be referred to the holy eleven thousand virgins, after the most holy Trinity, the risen Christ, and the blessed Virgin Mary.

units.la: Eodem die mane, dum dicerem horas canonicas et distraherer ad dictum negotium, et ad quaedam responsa quae ego eram daturus Episcopo suffraganeo, ego habui clara quaedam documenta, quae dicerent oportere, in ipso officio, non admittere alios spiritus qui non sunt secundum verba et litteram officii, neque admittendas esse alias rerum, aut verborum, aut quorumcumque negotiorum intelligentias tali tempore; sic ut totus homo ibi sit ubi est lingua dicens divinas preces. Deus quidem permittit nos incidere eo tempore in varios spiritus, et in varias intelligentias multarum rerum, et varios quoque habere timores; sed nos, debemus quaerere principalem Spiritum ut in illo quiescamus; nos debemus adhaerere verbis, et intelligentiis, et voluntatibus ac desideriis, quae magis quam illa alia sunt secundum subjectam materiam immediate; ut appareat si solum Deum, aut ipsum super omnia et principali affectu diligamus ac timeamus. Magis autem cognoscitur intentio amoris nostri, aut cujuscumque pii erga Deum affectus, eo tempore, cum adsunt varıı venti desideriorum cordis et nostra- rum intentionum. Dum igitur videris te bene dispositum esse tempore officii, secundum corpus et secundum intellectum, ad praedicationem vel ad aliam aliquam collocutionem, memento. statim te esse extra dispositionem quae requiritur ad officium divinum, et ad res quae cum Deo habentur peragendas. Faxit Chrislus optimus maximus et secundum exigentiam rerum, et collocutionum, et verborum, in quibus variis modis, et secundum varia tempora, nos oportet occupari corporaliter, ita habeamus spiritus qui exiguntur, et intentiones nostrorum animorum, et omnia suo ordine, ut non confundamur in ordinatione operum nostrorum, verborum, neque cogitationum aut desideriorum.
units.en: On the same day in the morning, while I said the canonical hours and was distracted towards the said affair, and towards certain answers I was to give to the suffragan Bishop, I had certain clear instructions, saying that in the office itself one must not admit other spirits which are not according to the words and letter of the office, nor admit at such a time other understandings of things, or words, or any affairs whatever; so that the whole man may be there where the tongue is, saying the divine prayers. God indeed permits us at that time to fall into various spirits, and various understandings of many things, and to have various fears too; but we ought to seek the principal Spirit, that in him we may rest; we ought to cleave to the words, and understandings, and wills and desires, which more than those others belong immediately to the matter in hand; that it may appear whether we love and fear God alone, or him above all things and with the principal affection. For the intention of our love, or of any pious affection towards God, is better known at the time when the various winds of the desires of our heart and of our intentions are blowing. When therefore you see yourself, at the time of the office, well disposed in body and understanding for preaching or for some other discourse, remember at once that you are outside the disposition required for the divine office, and for the things that are to be transacted with God. May Christ, the best and greatest, grant that according to the demands of the things, and discourses, and words in which, in various ways and at various times, we must be bodily occupied, we may so have the spirits that are required, and the intentions of our minds, and all things in their order, that we be not confounded in the ordering of our works, words, thoughts or desires.

units.la: In hoc mense Octobris, die quadam, dum agerem in quodam castro et oppidulo diaecesis Spirensis, et surrexissem media nocte ad com- memorationem, egọ incidi in quaedam colloquia ad Deum, et beatam Virginem, et Sanctos, pro illo populo, quantum ad vivos et defunctos; et hoc magna cum devotione et multis lacrymis. Discursus autem qui mihi tunc dabatur, erat circa recognitionem universalem beneficio- rum quae ego animadvertebam recepisse illum populum; petendo veniam nomine omnium, agendo gratias in omnibus, et petendo varias gratias. Dolebam propter defectum eorum. Optabam ut omnia quae mihi Deus per se et per sanctos suos operatus fuerat et adhuc operabatur recognoscerentur. Dicebam ergo: O Domine Jesu Christe, quis recognovit bonitatem tuam, qua factum est ut hic essent tam multa bona temporalia, et hic tamdiu permanserint sacramenta Eucharistiae, et caetera, et verba et ritus doctrinae christianae? Parce, Domine 3 quod haec hic non cogitantur, quod non petuntur, quod'non honorantur. Parce, Domine, quod animae purgandorum non sunt iù memoria istorum prout egent. Conserva, Domine, huic populo omnia haec; nec ad ignorantias, negligentias, aut ingratitudines velis respicere: sed ad Christüm Redemptorem, et ad Angelos, et sanctas animas qu omnes recognoscunt pro nobis. Hac commemoratione, tam beneficiorum quam peccatorum qüae hactenus in iis locis essent commissa, ego includebam fructus terrae, pacem temporalem, fidem catholicam, templa, imagines, administrationes sacramentorum et ipsa sacramenta, aquam benedictam, reliquias sanctorum corporum, receptacula ossium mortuorum; et quod habuissent tamdiu successionem temporalium dominorum quibus tenerentur in pacifico bono, quod habuissent sacerdotes, episcopos et praedicatores. Optabam illis multa bona optima, ut scilicet cognoscant haec omnia; ut cognoscant bonum quod ipsis sit in Deo suo, et in Christo Jesu incarnato, nato, circumciso, mortuo, etc.; item in virgine Maria, in Angelis et Sanctis, in rebus sanctis, in mortuis qul sunt in Purgatorio, in Scripturis, ete.
units.en: In this month of October, on a certain day, while I was staying in a certain castle and small town of the diocese of Speyer, and had risen at midnight for the commemoration, I fell into certain colloquies with God, and the blessed Virgin, and the Saints, for that people, both the living and the departed; and this with great devotion and many tears. The round which was then given me was a universal acknowledgment of the benefits which I perceived that people to have received: asking pardon in the name of all, giving thanks in all things, and asking various graces. I grieved for their failure. I wished that all the things which God, by himself and through his saints, had wrought for me and was still working might be acknowledged. I said therefore: O Lord Jesus Christ, who has acknowledged your goodness, by which it has come to pass that there were here so many temporal goods, and that here the sacraments of the Eucharist have remained so long, and the rest, and the words and rites of christian doctrine? Pardon, O Lord, that these things are not thought on here, that they are not asked for, that they are not honoured. Pardon, O Lord, that the souls of those to be purged are not in the memory of these people as they need. Preserve, O Lord, to this people all these things; and do not look upon their ignorances, negligences or ingratitudes, but upon Christ the Redeemer, and upon the Angels and holy souls who all make acknowledgment for us. In this commemoration, both of the benefits and of the sins hitherto committed in those places, I included the fruits of the earth, temporal peace, the catholic faith, the churches, the images, the administration of the sacraments and the sacraments themselves, holy water, the relics of holy bodies, the resting-places of the bones of the dead; and that they had had so long a succession of temporal lords by whom they were kept in peaceful good, that they had had priests, bishops and preachers. I wished them many excellent goods: namely, that they might know all these things; that they might know the good that is theirs in their God, and in Christ Jesus incarnate, born, circumcised, dead, and the rest; likewise in the Virgin Mary, in the Angels and Saints, in holy things, in the dead who are in Purgatory, in the Scriptures, and so forth.

units.la: In die sanctorum Chrysanti et Dariae, mane, antequam incepissem officium diei, ego inveni magnam devotionem in qua me offerebam, et omnes labores quos usque ad mortem ego essem bene operaturus aut passurus, pro omnibus et singulis gradibus et particulis virtutum, quae vel mihi, vel quilibet alteri, in quolibet temporis puncto, et in quolibet mundi loco, essent necessariae futurae vel utiles ad gloriam Dei et Sanctorum, et salutem animae meae et Christiano- rūm omnium.
units.en: On the day of Saints Chrysanthus and Daria, in the morning, before I began the office of the day, I found great devotion, in which I offered myself, and all the labours which until death I should well perform or suffer, for each and every degree and particle of the virtues which, whether to me or to any other, at any point of time and in any place of the world, should be necessary or useful for the glory of God and the Saints, and the salvation of my soul and of all Christians.

units.la: EEE a o AT EUL. AOE o In hoc autem ego, cum magna claritate meritorum Jesu Christi, invocabam gratiam ipsius, qua meruit omnibus et singulis, etiam quotquot essent possibiles, omnia et singula quae sunt necessaria et convenientia, etiam abundanter supra quam dici possit, ad salutem in statu gratae et ad gloriam in statu patriae; ipse tamen nec absoluta sua voluntate, nec ex ordinatione voluntatis vult ut omnia omnibus applicentur. Rogabam igitur Dominum ut ipse per sua merita dignaretur mihi concedere hane gratiam et hanc etiam cuilibet ex sociis meis, ut ego totus sim, quatenus sum, ex Christo; et omnia opera mea bona per gratiam ipsius ita dignaretur acceptare, quasi omnia essent in qualibet mea necessitate possibili et futura, et cujuscumque alterius ubicumque terrarum esset, directa et praeordinata actualiter. Idem quoque de singulis virtutibus et donis Dei mihi aut cuilibet convenientibus Christiano. Hinc autem mihi datum est trahere merita vitae et passionum Christi, qui actibus suis in omnem sufficientiam salutis cujuscumque, se actualiter et ex infinita virtute extendebat, etiam cum adhue -mortalis esset.
units.en: And in this, with great clearness concerning the merits of Jesus Christ, I invoked his grace, by which he merited for each and all — even for as many as were possible — each and every thing that is necessary and fitting, even abundantly beyond what can be said, for salvation in the state of grace and for glory in the state of the fatherland; yet he does not will, either by his absolute will or by the ordinance of his will, that all things be applied to all. I begged therefore the Lord that he, through his merits, would deign to grant me this grace — and this also to every one of my companions — that I may be wholly, so far as I am, from Christ; and that he would deign so to accept all my good works, through his grace, as if they were all actually directed and preordained to every possible and future need of mine, and of any other person anywhere in the world. The same also of the several virtues and gifts of God fitting for me or for any Christian. Hence it was given me to draw upon the merits of the life and sufferings of Christ, who by his acts extended himself, actually and out of infinite power, to the full sufficiency of the salvation of everyone, even while he was still mortal.

units.la: = T ASNNSNNN DANAI EAN Sensi etiam satis vivum dolorem ex eo quod, ab finitio vitae meae, non pelierim, et in hoc non laboraverim, ut quod jam nune mihi datum est virtualiter, saltem tunc praetendissem; agebamque gratias ipsi Filio Dei qui perpetua charitate praetendisset et intendisset mihi ea bona quae jam percipio; et quod quemlibet laborem et dolorem, quem in humanitate sua pasṣus est, pro me et propter quodlibet meum -bonum fecerit, et in illud ordinaverit. Ipse igitur sit benedictus in saecula!
units.en: I felt also a keen enough sorrow that, from the beginning of my life, I had not asked, and had not laboured for, at least the intending then of what is now given me virtually; and I gave thanks to the Son of God himself, who with everlasting charity had intended and purposed for me those goods which I now perceive; and that every labour and grief which he suffered in his humanity he bore for me and for the sake of every good of mine, and ordered it to that end. Blessed be he for ever!

units.la: Hic memini cujusdam desiderii quod alias acceperam, quod erat sub hoc modo optativo: Utinam ego propter -Christum fuissem servus ipsius Adae, Abrahae, David, et ipsius tandem Mariae virgmis, quae ipsum concepit, peperit et nutrivit. Item ipsorum Apostolorum, et cujuslibet Pontificis Petri successoris, usque ad Paulum HI, qui nunc est et sub quo sumus, et deinceps. Hoc autem desiderium meum, quo voluissem fuisse servus tam multis propter Christum Dominum meum, ita distinguebatur, quod considerando etiam solam humanitatem ejus, ego voluissem servivisse om- - nibus patribus ex quibus ipse est secundum car- nem, idque in officiis et ministeriis corporalibus; g patribus autem novi testamenti qui servierunt Christo, èt ipsum nobis quodammodo genuerunt in ministeriis spiritualibus, his, inquam, ego optabam exhibuisse omnia officia circa res spirituales. i In die sancti Evaristi papae et martyris, dum surrexissem circa horam tertiam post mediam noctem, ego inveni multam devotionem in bona voluntate, et in multis piis desideriis quae mihi suggerebantur ad orandum pro necessitatibus proximorum in generali commemoratione circa Christianos, circa Judaeos, circa Turcas et Gentiles, circa hereticos, item et circa mortuos.
