Veniebant in mentem variae afflictiones hominum, infirmitates, peccata, obstinationes, desperationes, fletus, clades, fames, pestes, angustiae, etc., pro quibus mihi suggerebatur Christus redemptor, Christus consolator, Christus vivificator, illuminator, adjutor, ereptor, misericors et miserator Dominus Deus; quem orabam secundum vim talium nominum, ut cunctis dignaretur succurrere et subvenire. Hic quoque optavi et petivi, cum magna devotione et affectu quodam novo, ut F mihi detur tandem esse servum et ministrum Christi consolatoris, ministrum Christi adjutoris, ministrum Christi ereptoris, ministrum Christi salvatoris, liberatoris, ditantis et roborantis; administrare lumen non solum spirituale, sed etiam, si audere et praesumere in Deo liceat, corporale, et caetera quaecumque sint charitatis erga animam aut corpus cujuscumque proximi:: Et hic nota quod tibi, quemadmodum alias saepe, dabatur praesumere, non in te aut meritis tuis, sed in Christo, multa quae non possent fieri per naturam aut sine miraculo; sicut est sanare aegrotos, illuminare caecos, curare leprosos, expellere daemones de corporibus, consolari aliquos super mortuis suis. Ita animus tuus in omnia se extendebat, absque vanitate spiritus, tum Spirtu Sancto sic visitante animam tuam ad haec desideranda, et etiam, licet hoc fuerit alias magis vivaci spiritu et cum majore fide, speranda. Alias etenim contigit mihi frequenter invenisse majorem fidem circa talia impossibilia; non tamen nisi cum daretur per charitatem sentire aliquam possibilem necessitatem proximi, aut consolatio- nem, etc., aut aliquam rationem gloriae Dei quae esse potest in talibus piis operibus. Ex tali enim fide, etiamsi non esset nisi ut granum, et ex chartatei, solet oriri etiam fiducia absque temeritate et praesumptione. Aliter non est facile inveniri fidem quae prosit in salutem ipsius etiam operantis; si enim habuero fidem ut montes transferam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil mihi prodest, licet possit prodesse proximo. Oportet igitur fidem quae operatur sic magna circa proximum, nasci quodammodo aut suscitari per charitatem quae est circa proximum, cum qua apprehendatur et quasi comprehendatur proximi necessitas, utilitas, consolatio, absque alio affectu quam purae charitatis. Id quod magis usu venit in extremis articulis necessitatis proximorum, propter imperfectionem humanam, quae non facile comprehenditneque sentit parvas necessitates aut incommoda, sicut novit ponderare parva commoda ipsius. Amator quoque gloriae Dei, qui ponderat per gratiam Spiritus Sancti ea quae Dei sunt ad vivum, ille facilius fidem assequitur -ex dono ejusdem Spiritus, per quam magna ad laudem Dei operari, quomodo oportet, possit in propriis quoque necessitatibus, maxime in extre- mis, et usque ad intimam afflictionem cordis urgentibus. Facile est invenire fidem per quam, contra omnem humanam spem, tu possis assequi aliquam gratiam, circa animam et etiam circa corpus tuum, nempe aliquam liberationem a malo, vel adeptionem boni necessarii, quod aliter non occurrit posse habere, etc.
units.en: Here I remembered a certain desire which I had received at another time, which ran in this optative manner: Would that I, for Christ's sake, had been the servant of Adam, of Abraham, of David, and at last of the Virgin Mary herself, who conceived him, bore him and nursed him; likewise of the Apostles, and of every Pontiff, Peter's successor, down to Paul III, who now is and under whom we are, and onward. And this desire of mine, by which I would have wished to have been servant to so many for the sake of Christ my Lord, was thus distinguished: that considering even his humanity alone, I would have wished to have served all the fathers from whom he is according to the flesh, and that in bodily offices and ministries; but to the fathers of the new testament, who served Christ and in a certain manner begot him for us in spiritual ministries — to these, I say, I wished to have rendered all offices in spiritual things. On the day of Saint Evaristus, pope and martyr, having risen about the third hour after midnight, I found much devotion in good will, and in many pious desires suggested to me for praying for the needs of my neighbours, in a general commemoration: for Christians, for Jews, for Turks and Gentiles, for heretics, and likewise for the dead. There came to mind the various afflictions of men, sicknesses, sins, obstinacies, despairs, weepings, disasters, famines, plagues, distresses, and the rest; for which there was suggested to me Christ the redeemer, Christ the consoler, Christ the giver of life, the enlightener, the helper, the rescuer, the merciful and pitying Lord God; whom I prayed, according to the force of these names, that he would deign to succour and relieve all. Here too I wished and asked, with great devotion and a certain new affection, that it might at last be given me to be a servant and minister of Christ the consoler, a minister of Christ the helper, a minister of Christ the rescuer, a minister of Christ the saviour, the deliverer, the enricher and strengthener; to administer light not only spiritual but even — if one may dare and presume in God — bodily, and all other things whatsoever that belong to charity towards the soul or body of any neighbour. And note here that it was given you, as often at other times, to presume — not upon yourself or your merits, but upon Christ — many things which could not be done by nature or without miracle: such as healing the sick, giving light to the blind, cleansing lepers, driving demons out of bodies, consoling people over their dead. So your mind reached out into all these things, without vanity of spirit, the Holy Spirit so visiting your soul to desire these things, and even — though at other times this was with a livelier spirit and greater faith — to hope for them. For at other times it has often befallen me to find greater faith about such impossible things; yet never except when it was given me, through charity, to feel some possible need of my neighbour, or consolation, and so forth, or some ground of the glory of God which can lie in such pious works. For from such faith, though it were but as a grain, and from charity, confidence too is wont to arise, without rashness or presumption. Otherwise it is not easy for a faith to be found which profits to the salvation even of the worker himself; for if I have faith so as to remove mountains, but have not charity, it profits me nothing, though it may profit my neighbour. The faith, therefore, which works such great things for one's neighbour must in a manner be born, or stirred up, through the charity which is towards one's neighbour — with which the neighbour's need, profit or consolation is apprehended, and as it were comprehended, without any other affection than that of pure charity. This comes about most in the extreme necessities of our neighbours, because of human imperfection, which does not easily comprehend or feel small needs and discomforts, though it knows well how to weigh its own small comforts. The lover, too, of the glory of God, who by the grace of the Holy Spirit weighs to the quick the things that are God's, more easily attains, by the gift of the same Spirit, that faith by which he may work great things to the praise of God, as is fitting — even in his own necessities, above all in extreme ones, and those which press to the inmost affliction of the heart. It is easy to find the faith by which, against all human hope, you may obtain some grace, concerning your soul and even concerning your body — some deliverance from evil, or the gaining of a necessary good which otherwise there appears no way to have, and so forth.

units.la: In hoc autem oportet quam maxime ùt homo non amet seipsum propter se, sed ut jam sil totus ordinatus ad Dei gloriam, et salutem proprii spiritus, et in bonum proximi. Aemulare igitur melius charisma in omnibus, quae est charitas, el in hac te exerce, continuo crescens, et non contentus ex parte quae necessaria est ad salutem tuam aut proximi. Hoc enim faciens, et sic ad perfectum tendens, facile erit ut assequaris gratias alias non necessarias, sed abundantes ad bonum tuum et proximorum, nempe fidem et spem circa magna, ete.
units.en: But in this it is above all necessary that a man love not himself for his own sake, but that he be already wholly ordered to the glory of God, and the salvation of his own spirit, and the good of his neighbour. Strive then after the better gift in all things, which is charity; and exercise yourself in it, continually growing, and not content with the portion which is necessary for your own salvation or your neighbour's. For doing this, and thus tending to what is perfect, you will easily obtain the other graces, not necessary, but abundant, for your good and your neighbours' — namely faith and hope concerning great things, and the rest.

units.la: Pete gratiam pro minimis, et invenies eam etiam ad maxima operanda, credenda et speranda. Considera minima, et ea pondera et aestimato ad operandum ea, et Dominus dabit majora.
units.en: Ask grace for the least things, and you will find it also for the working, believing and hoping of the greatest. Consider the least things, and weigh them and value them so as to do them, and the Lord will give greater.

units.la: Extende te ipsum et totum te expandas ad ea quae tu potes cum parva gratia Dei, et Dominus tibi dabit magnam gratiam per quam poteris etiam illa quae supra teipsum sunt. Multi sunt, sicut et tu fuisti frequenter, qui auxili quaerunt gratias ad universalia bona opera facienda, et interim omittunt particularia, pro quibus facile fuerat invenire gratiam.
units.en: Stretch yourself out, and spread your whole self, towards the things you can do with a small grace of God, and the Lord will give you great grace, by which you will be able to do even the things that are above yourself. There are many — as you too have often been — who seek graces of help for doing universal good works, and meanwhile omit the particular ones, for which it had been easy to find grace.

units.la: Multi cogitant circa ea quae quasi impossibilia sunt, et interim non sunt solliciti de operibus - manuum suarum. Fides ideo tibi proponitur ut granum sinapis, et Charitas ut magnum et primum mandatum, quia oportet te cum parya cognitione et fide intellectus crescere secundum affectum non otiosum, sic ut non semper velis addiscere et semper crescere secundum intellectum, omisso. augmento quod est secundum volunfatem quae sit operativa. Sı unicum talentum cognitionis et fidei habes, operare in illo et lucrare, ut hac via duo talenta habeas. Cave autem ut non fodias illud in terra; sed nec dicas te prius velle habere,duo talenta cognitionis quam incipere operari. Oportet etenim, ut jam dixi, per negotiationem illius et operationem unius talenti, lucrari alterum, etc. Noli omittere praxim i n ocas operum praesentium et eorum quae juxta te sunt, pro contemplatione otiosa operum futurorum, et eorum quae longe a te adhuc posita sunt.
units.en: Many think about things which are all but impossible, and meanwhile are not solicitous about the works of their own hands. Faith is therefore set before you as a grain of mustard seed, and Charity as the great and first commandment, because you must, with small knowledge and faith of the intellect, grow according to an affection that is not idle; so that you be not always wanting to learn, and always to grow according to the intellect, while omitting the growth which is according to the will — which should be operative. If you have a single talent of knowledge and faith, work with it and gain, that by this way you may have two talents. But beware of burying it in the earth; and do not say that you wish first to have two talents of knowledge before beginning to work. For, as I have said, it is by the trading and working of the one talent that the other is to be gained, and so forth. Do not omit the practice of present works, and of those which are close to you, for the idle contemplation of future works, and of those which are still placed far from you.

units.la: = Desideria ipsa bona sunt, modo a Deo sint, et per ipsum, et in ipso, et ad ipsum; et hinc fit ut in orationibus frequenter desideremus ea etiam quae non sunt futura, ea quae sunt supra vires nostras, et ea quoque quae impossibile est naturaliter fieri; et haec desideria non displicent Deo a quo immittuntur, ad quem ordinantur, et in cujus Spiritu sentiuntur; imo ipse sic excitat ad fidem, ad spem et ad charitatem non solum internam, sed ad ipsius quoque opera pia, faciens nos saepe desiderare summa, ea videre et sperare, ut saltem mediocria absque pigritia atque diffidentia operemur; quandoque et ut apprehendamus bona, et favores qui nos possibiliter contingunt et accidere possunt. Quandoque vero accidit contrarium, scilicet ut apprehendamus mala quae nobis tantum possibiliter imminent. In priore dispositione, cavendum ne elevemur supra modum; in posteriore, ne dejiciamur plusquam oportet. Bonus spiritus noster utrumque horum temporum in alterius reme- é do EN PA K aA dium novit applicare: id est abundantiam contra penuriam, penuriam contra abundantiam. Malus autem spiritus ex utroque malum nostrum efficere nititur, nempe elationem atque praesumptionem ex abundantia, et pusillanimitatem atque dejectionem boni animi ex penuria.
units.en: Desires themselves are good, provided they be from God, and through him, and in him, and towards him; and hence it comes that in prayers we frequently desire even things that will never be, things above our strength, and things too which are naturally impossible; and these desires do not displease God, by whom they are sent in, to whom they are ordered, and in whose Spirit they are felt. Nay, he thus stirs us up to faith, to hope and to charity — not only inward, but to its pious works as well — often making us desire the highest things, see them and hope for them, that we may at least work the middling ones without sloth or distrust; and sometimes that we may apprehend the goods and favours which may possibly touch us and come to pass. But sometimes the contrary happens: namely, that we apprehend the evils which only possibly hang over us. In the former disposition we must beware of being lifted up beyond measure; in the latter, of being cast down more than is fitting. Our good spirit knows how to apply each of these times as a remedy for the other — that is, abundance against want, want against abundance. But the evil spirit strives to work our harm out of both: namely, elation and presumption out of abundance, and faint-heartedness and dejection of good courage out of want.

units.la: Tu frequenter, dum ad teipsum et ad ea quae exterius apparent respicis, credis te nihil posse, nihil scire, neque posse sperare erga proximos. Dominus autem, in contrarium, te in Spiritu suo ducens, ostendit innumera quae facilia factu apud ipsum videntur; dat quoque spem et omnem bonum affectum ad multo plura quam fieri etiam per omnes homines possint; ut sic exciteris animo ad opera, nec desperes de omnibus. Alius est tamen modus cognoscendi in spiritu aliqua esse possibilia, et alius dum suggeruntur tanquam ın veritate futura, in contrario etiam spiritu, id est in tuo proprio, vel in spiritu mali Angeli. Simile aliquid in contrarium sensum solet accidere, videlicet quaedam repraesentari tanquam possibilia mala et inconvenientia, quae tamen non sunt possibilia; quaedam etiam pro- ponuntur tanquam futura, et non sunt futura; A Ca Jef. z quia ibi fit facile ut inveniatur spiritus malus, et non solum malus sed etiam mendax. Spiritus autem Domini quidquid diceret futurum esse, revara futurum esset et semper evenirèt; nisi forte accidat contrarium in lis quae sunt de futuro contingenti dependentia, ex aliquibus mutationibus causarum liberi arbitrii. Cavendum tamen nobis est ne ea quae ostenduntur ut possibilia, ut apud nos, non cum aliqua temporis determinatione, accipiamus tanquam realiter futura nostro tempore et seculo. Tu saepe videbis in spiritu Domini aliquam personam, vel civitatem, aut aliam rem vel negotium, etc., sub quadam specie boni et pulchri, ut facile speres fructum magnum et eventum optimum circa talem rem, alioquin in seipsa quasi perditam: contra vero dum te agitaverit contrarius spiritūs, id est malus, tu plane desperabis de tali re, tibique videberis videre ruinam ejus rei. In illo igitur spiritu, id est, in. bono, credes Deo placere ut ille bonus status veniat in rem illam, licet forte non sit eventurus, propterea quod voluntas divina non habet illa instrumenta quae vellet habere, ad operandum et efficiendum in re ipsa illud quod tu vides et credis, et speras et desideras, cum illo spiritu bono. Noli ergo assentiri illis malis spiritibus, qui rerum malos exitus et malas formas depingunt, et malos fructus ipsarum portendunt; quales enim mali spiritus apud se sunt, tales ipsi depingunt res ipsas, quas volunt et optant pessime habere. Satage potius fieri instrumentum boni spiritus, qui tibi demonstrat tales status rerum et tales conditiones ipsarum, quales ipse optat, et paratus est ex parte, te instrumento promovere. Ubi autem, id quod possibile est, spiritus justus mitteret tibi desiderium, aut spem, aut etiam ipsam evidentiam circa ruinas spirituales aliquarum civitatum, aut populi, aut personae, videreturque tibi talis esse voluntas Domini, adhuc esset tibi quaerendus alius spiritus, alius, inquam, secundum effectum in te, in quo posses quaerere misericordiam, et credere illam non esse absolutam Dei voluntatem, sed conditionatam; nec ergo tibi desistendum ab eo quod hic posses, nec desperandum, etiamsi haberes verbum Dei dicens: Iste damnabitur. Loquitur enim Deus, non solum in nobis, sed etiam in scripturis, multa absolute (propter conditiones rerum ipsarum variabiles) quae tamen non vult absolute.
units.en: You frequently, when you look at yourself and at the things that appear outwardly, believe that you can do nothing, know nothing, and can hope nothing for your neighbours. But the Lord, on the contrary, leading you in his Spirit, shows innumerable things which appear easy to be done with him; he gives also hope and every good affection towards far more things than could be done even by all men together; that so you may be stirred in mind to works, and not despair of everything. Yet it is one thing to know in the spirit that certain things are possible, and another when they are suggested as truly to come — and that in a contrary spirit, that is, in your own, or in the spirit of the evil Angel. Something similar is wont to happen in the contrary sense: namely, that certain things are represented as possible evils and misfortunes which yet are not possible; certain things too are proposed as future which are not future; for there it easily happens that the spirit found is evil — and not only evil but lying. But whatever the Spirit of the Lord should say would be, would truly be, and would always come to pass; unless perhaps the contrary happen in things depending on future contingency, from certain changes of the causes of free will. We must beware, however, of taking the things that are shown as possible, as with God, without any determination of time, as though they were really to come in our own time and age. You will often see in the spirit of the Lord some person, or city, or other thing or affair, and so on, under a certain appearance of good and beauty, so that you easily hope great fruit and an excellent outcome for that thing, though in itself it be as it were lost; on the contrary, when the contrary spirit — that is, the evil one — has shaken you, you will utterly despair of that thing, and will seem to yourself to see its ruin. In that spirit, then — the good one — you will believe that it pleases God that that good state should come upon that thing, although perhaps it will not come to pass, because the divine will does not have those instruments which it would wish to have, for working and effecting in the thing itself that which you see and believe, hope and desire, with that good spirit. Do not, therefore, assent to those evil spirits who paint the evil ends and evil shapes of things, and portend their evil fruits; for as the evil spirits are in themselves, so they paint the things themselves which they wish and desire to have turn out worst. Strive rather to become an instrument of the good spirit, who shows you such states of things, and such conditions of them, as he himself desires, and is ready, for his part, to promote with you as his instrument. But where — which is possible — the just spirit should send you desire, or hope, or even evidence itself, concerning the spiritual ruins of certain cities, or of a people, or a person, and it should seem to you that such is the will of the Lord, you would still have to seek another spirit — another, I say, as to its effect in you — in which you might seek mercy, and believe that that is not the absolute will of God, but conditioned; and therefore you must not desist from what you could do here, nor despair, even if you had a word of God saying: This man shall be damned. For God speaks, not only in us but also in the scriptures, many things absolutely (because of the variable conditions of the things themselves) which nevertheless he does not will absolutely.

units.la: In vigilia apostolorum Simonis et Judae, dum surrexissem in noctis silentio ad orationem, ego sensi multam inspirationem circa hoc, ut satagerem et darem omnem operam, quatenus pauperes infirmi, qui vagantur per civitatem Moguntinam, colligantur et recipiantur in aliquod hospitale, ut ibi curentur et bene habeant.
units.en: On the vigil of the apostles Simon and Jude, having risen in the silence of the night for prayer, I felt much inspiration on this point: that I should busy myself and give all diligence that the poor sick who wander through the city of Mainz might be gathered and received into some hospital, to be cared for there and be well kept.

units.la: Sic quoque sensi clare multas negligentias meas, et obliviones, et incurias, circa quosdam pauperes plagosos, quos olim ego vidi, et aliquando adjuvi, sed negligenter et remisse. Quamvis enim tunc fuerim inops rerum, fieri tamen poterat per me ut ipsis per alios et alios succurreretur: ego potuissem ostiatim mendicare ipsis aliquod majus quam habebam sublevamen; ego potuissem convenire praelatos locorum, medicos atque chirurgos, dominos aut magistratus civitatum, ubi illi tales infirmi et similes male habebant. Hic movebar ut ex animo rogarem spiritus illorum infirmorum et omnium aliorum generaliter, qui male in hac vita habuerunt, ut ipsi dignarentur esse nunc advocati pauperum infirmorum, qui in hac civitate Moguntina et alibi superstites sunt, atque mihi aliquam novam gratiam pro hujusmodi pauperibus jūvandis a Deo impetrarent.
units.en: So too I clearly felt my many negligences, forgetfulnesses and carelessnesses towards certain poor men covered with sores, whom I once saw, and sometimes helped, but negligently and remissly. For although I was then without means, it could yet have been brought about through me that they should be succoured by this man and that: I could have begged from door to door some greater relief for them than I had; I could have approached the prelates of the places, the physicians and surgeons, the lords or magistrates of the cities where such sick men and their like fared ill. Here I was moved to beg from my heart the spirits of those sick men, and of all others generally who fared ill in this life, that they would deign to be now the advocates of the poor sick who survive in this city of Mainz and elsewhere, and would obtain for me from God some new grace for helping such poor folk.

units.la: In die apostolorum Simonis et Judae, ego habui multam consolationem post missam, in quibusdam meditationibus et colloquiis immediate ad ipsum Deum: et nunc quidem ad Patrem, nunc ad Filium, nunc ad Spiritum Sanctum; et etiam ad humanitatem Jesu Christi Dómini Nostri. In hujusmodi discursibus, orationibus, obsecrationibus et gratiarum actionibus, ego multo solidius consolabar quam in illis quae sunt circa proximi salutem, aut etiam circa Sanctorum invocationes. In quibus duobus ego hactenus soleo magis frequenter a Domino visitari quam in illis quae immediate faciunt ad ipsius cognitionem et amorem. Abunde autem mihi sufficit quod tantus Dominus et Deus per sanctos suos et in ipsis mihi sese communicet, ad profectum meum, et ad salutem proximorum; ad quorum amorem quanto ego remissior sum in cooperando, major sum in affectu; unde fit ut ego tanto magis laborem, ef torquear variis desideriis et affectibus, propter salutem proximorum et ipsorum profectum, quanto minus sufficienter in iis quae ʻego possem operari laboro. Sic itaque fit ut in externis operibus deficiam nimium frequenter, et in desideriis spiritus mei et affectibus superabundem.
units.en: On the day of the apostles Simon and Jude I had much consolation after Mass, in certain meditations and colloquies directed immediately to God himself: now to the Father, now to the Son, now to the Holy Spirit; and also to the humanity of Jesus Christ Our Lord. In such rounds, prayers, supplications and thanksgivings I was consoled much more solidly than in those which concern the salvation of my neighbour, or even the invocations of the Saints. In these two I have hitherto been wont to be visited by the Lord more frequently than in those which make immediately for the knowledge and love of himself. But it abundantly suffices me that so great a Lord and God communicates himself to me through his saints and in them, for my progress and for the salvation of my neighbours; towards whose love, the more remiss I am in co-working, the greater I am in affection; whence it comes that I labour and am tormented by various desires and affections for the salvation of my neighbours and their progress, the more, the less sufficiently I labour in the things I could actually do. And so it comes about that in outward works I fail too frequently, and in the desires and affections of my spirit I superabound.

units.la: Deus optimus maximus omnia ordinet et rectificet, et componat et justificet, secundum beneplacitum suae voluntatis; faciatque ut ġo non solum inquiram quisnam ipse est sed etiam quidnam ipse velit me facere, ipse quidem omnibus modisinfinitus est; supra omnem capacitatem et intelligentiam creatam infinitus, et infra omnem captum creatum; infinitus sub omni descensu captus creati; infinitus ab anteriori omnium creaturarum, et infinitus a posteriori omnium creaturarum, et infinitus intra profundum omnis creaturae est. At hoc, in sua substantia; in voluntate autem sua praeceptiva, tam humilis est et tam limitatus atque terminatus, ut nihil praecipiat ex necessitate quod sit supra vires illius quantumlibet infirmi hominis, adjuncta gratia ipsius quae in promptu est, et magis in promptu ipsi homini quam homo ipse sibi sit in promptu. Nihil vult praeceptive et obligatorie quod non sit intra vires easdem et infra ipsas; quod non sit infra terminos potentiae quam habet homo versus inferiora, versus anteriora, et versus posteriora. Est igitur in hoc uno multum laudandus Deus, qui cum in se, multa ex parte, sit infinitus et immensus, contentus tamen sit ea virtute nostra, quae omni ex parte est limitata et mensurata, ad omnia dans gratiam et favorem; ita ut nec extrema quidem potentiae et scientiae, et voluntatis nostrae, a nobis necessario exigat. Ipse sit benedictus in saecula saeculorum!
units.en: May God, the best and greatest, order and set right all things, compose and justify them, according to the good pleasure of his will; and grant that I may inquire not only who he is, but also what he wills me to do. He indeed is in every way infinite; infinite above all created capacity and intelligence, and infinite beneath all created grasp; infinite below every descent of the created mind's reach; infinite before all creatures, and infinite after all creatures, and infinite within the depth of every creature. But this, in his substance; in his preceptive will he is so humble, so limited and bounded, that he commands nothing of necessity which is above the strength of any man, however weak, when his grace is joined to it — which is at hand, and more at hand to the man himself than the man is at hand to himself. He wills nothing by precept and obligation which is not within and beneath those same strengths; which is not below the bounds of the power a man has towards things beneath him, before him, and behind him. In this one thing, then, God is much to be praised: that although in himself he is in great part infinite and immense, he is yet content with that virtue of ours which on every side is limited and measured, giving grace and favour for everything; so that he does not of necessity exact from us even the extremes of our power, our knowledge and our will. Blessed be he for ever and ever!

units.la: Dominica post festum sanctorum Simonis et Judae, post quamdam perplexitatem quae spiritui meo inciderat, et postquam. essem jam ab ea liberior restitutusque in serenitatem boni spiritus, ego sensi haec verba consolationis, videlicet: Ile qui novit auferre timores malorum, novit etiam et aeque potens est a nobis avertere illa mala, unde sunt tales timores atque animorum anzietates; et qui potest. per se dare spem bonam inter adversa, novit dare rem ipsam in quam tendit talis spes. Sit igitur ipse benedic- tus, qui tantum potest circa rerum ipsarum adver- sitates, sicut potens circa spirituum nostrorum mitigandas perturbationes; apud quem etiam non magis difficile est ut assequaris rerum prosperrimos exitus, quam ipsam spem circa tales illo- rum exitus.
units.en: On the Sunday after the feast of Saints Simon and Jude, after a certain perplexity which had fallen upon my spirit, and after I was now freer of it and restored to the serenity of a good spirit, I felt these words of consolation: He who knows how to take away the fears of evils knows also, and is equally able, to turn away from us those evils from which such fears and anxieties of mind arise; and he who can of himself give good hope amid adversities knows how to give the very thing to which such hope tends. Blessed then be he, who can do as much concerning the adversities of things themselves as he is mighty in calming the disturbances of our spirits; with whom also it is no harder that you should obtain the most prosperous issues of things, than the very hope concerning such issues.

units.la: In die festi Sanctorum omnium, ego sensi magnum desiderium ut, sicut in terris fit festum et solemnis memoria omnium civium caeoelestium, ita in caelis fieret solemnis in tali die memoria, cum misericordia et miseratione, omnium incolarum hujus mundi, et eorum mazime qui sunt peccatores: sic videlicet quod nullus sit in hoc mundo, neque in Purgatorio, cujus hoc die non fieret memoria in caelis ab ipsis sanctis; et eodem modo de animabus quae sunt in Purgatorio; maxime cum quilibet sanctus possit in speculo dillo divino videre et. recordari uniuscujusque eorum qui sunt in terris.
units.en: On the day of the feast of All Saints I felt a great desire that, as on earth a feast and solemn memory is kept of all the citizens of heaven, so in heaven on that day a solemn memory might be kept, with mercy and compassion, of all the inhabitants of this world, and above all of those who are sinners: so that there should be no one in this world, nor in Purgatory, of whom on this day memory would not be made in heaven by the saints themselves; and in the same way of the souls which are in Purgatory; especially since every saint can see and remember, in that divine mirror, each one of those who are on earth.

units.la: In die animarum, dicendo missam, et jam exquo me praeparassem ad ipsam, ego habui magnam devotionem, a prinęipio usque ad finem, qualem nunquam antea in tali die senseram circa defunctos; fiebat autem totum per spiritum qui me movebat ad compassionem habendam pro mortuis. Ibi fut magna abundantia lacrymarum: cogitabam autem circa parentes et consanguineos, circa fratres qui in Societate mortui sunt, circa benefactores, circa parentes omnium fratrum meorum; occurrebant etiam mihi in genere illi qui sunt commendati beatae. virgini Mariae; et sic de alis multis sanctis mihi magis peculiaribus; et de Angelis, qui et ipsi desiderant quosdam in speciali habere peculiares amicos in hac vita, ubi est status merendi.
units.en: On the day of the souls, saying Mass, and indeed from the moment I had prepared myself for it, I had great devotion from beginning to end, such as I had never before felt on that day concerning the departed; and it all came through a spirit which moved me to compassion for the dead. There was there a great abundance of tears: I thought of my parents and kinsfolk, of the brethren who have died in the Society, of benefactors, of the parents of all my brethren; there occurred to me also, in general, those who are commended to the blessed Virgin Mary; and so of many other saints more particular to me; and of the Angels, who also themselves desire to have certain special particular friends in this life, where is the state of meriting.

units.la: Habui etiam sensum quemdam in quadam bona humilitate spiritus mei, quo consolatus sum ex parte, tanquam responso quodam super mea continua siti et fame quam habeo ut possim servire Christo, imitando ipsum circa animarum salutem. Verba ipsa quae aderant cum dicto sensu fuerunt in hanc sententiam: Siquidem tu non sis dignus ut servias Christo ipsi qui Dominus domi- nantium est, et siquidem non merearis occupari circa messem animarum, in hoc saltem confortare, quod possis invenire quid agas propter Christum tanquam servus alicujus minoris domini quam ipse est; ut puta tu potes venerator esse alicujus privati sancti, aut potes servire animabus defunctorum quae torquentur in Purgatorio; et hoc est unum magnum negotium, cui soli aliqui olim deputati erant.
units.en: I had also a certain feeling, in a certain good humility of my spirit, by which I was in part consoled, as by a kind of answer concerning my continual thirst and hunger to be able to serve Christ, imitating him in the salvation of souls. The words which came with that feeling were to this effect: If indeed you are not worthy to serve Christ himself, who is the Lord of lords, and if you do not deserve to be occupied in the harvest of souls, take comfort at least in this, that you can find something to do for Christ's sake as the servant of some lesser lord than he is: you can, for instance, be the venerator of some particular saint, or you can serve the souls of the departed who are tormented in Purgatory; and this is one great business, to which alone some men of old were deputed.

units.la: Eodem die, animarum videlicet, ego post prandium, statim dicta nona diei, sensi magnam devotionem cum variis notitiis sancti luminis, circa quamdam divisionem congregationum, quae in genere possunt numerari quinque: quarum prima, et omnino perfecta, est caelestis, et tota beata; secunda est animarum quae sunt in Purgatorio, quae maximis contritionibus affliguntur, in maximisque tormentis ad tempus servantur; tertia est earum animarum quae sunt in Limbo, puerorum qui cum originali peccato decesserunt, suntque privati omnibus bonis quae per Christum consequi possunt Christiani, licet nullo sensu torqueantur sive externo, sive in- terno, nec unquam torquebuntur; quarta est eorum qui sunt condemnati ad paenas aeternales, qui sine remedio, omnibus modis se pessime habent et in aeternum habebunt; quinta est corum, qui sunt in hoc mundo, quique inter spem vitae caelestis et mortis infernalis metum ambulant; qui in seipsis remedia habent ut salvari, et in seipsis habent ut damnari possint; alterum ex se, alterum vero ex gratia diviņa, quae tam in nobis est, et tam nostra est, aut melius, quam ulla propria voluntas nostra. Considerando igitur istas congregationes quinque, ego sensi varios affectus, et maxime circa animas quae sunt in Purgatorio, et circa eos qui adhuc superstites sunt in hoc saeculo.
units.en: On the same day — namely of the souls — after dinner, immediately after saying none, I felt great devotion, with various perceptions of holy light, concerning a certain division of assemblies, which in general may be numbered five: of which the first, and altogether perfect, is the heavenly, and wholly blessed; the second is that of the souls in Purgatory, who are afflicted with the greatest contritions and kept for a time in the greatest torments; the third is that of the souls in Limbo — of the children who departed with original sin, who are deprived of all the goods which Christians can obtain through Christ, though they are tormented by no sense, outward or inward, nor ever will be; the fourth is that of those condemned to eternal pains, who without remedy fare in every way most ill, and will for ever; the fifth is that of those who are in this world, who walk between the hope of heavenly life and the fear of infernal death; who have in themselves the means to be saved, and have in themselves the means to be damned — the one from themselves, the other from divine grace, which is as much in us, and as much ours, or better, than any will of our own. Considering then these five assemblies, I felt various affections, and above all concerning the souls in Purgatory, and those who still survive in this age.

units.la: Hic quoque sensi magna desideria ad hoc; ut sancti orarent pro nobis, qui tam multa possunt in gloria sua. Item, ut animae quae sunt in Purgatorio, orarent etiam pro nobis, in suis gemitibus et contritionibus, quae alioțłui sibi nihil prosunt; quae si essent in corporibus adhuc mortalibus, non possent non mereri in minimo momento quidquid in caelis est. Proinde multum, et plusquam dici potest, valere possunt pro nobis qui credimus, et res ipsas sanctas non calcamus pedibus nostris, sed maximi facimus in fide, quae est argumentum rerum non apparentium. Faxit Christus ut intrent gemitus illi in conspectum suum pro nobis! Sensi etiam quod optimum esset ut animae de Purgatorio invocarentur apud Deum, ad hoc ut detur nobis cogintio vera et verus sensus peccatorum, diligentia bene operandi, sollicitudo facienid fructus paenitentiae, ac generaliter omnes illae gratiae pro quarum defectu ipsae patiuntur tantas paeoenas. Postridie diei animarum defunctorum fidelium, ego tempore matutino multa notavi, quae mihi occurrerunt circa intelligentiam quamdam nuditatis animae meae ac spiritus; propter quam causam, ego petivi cum satis bona devotione sensus et intellectus, ut Dominus per intercessionem omnium Sanctorum dignaretur me vestire veste puritatis, innocentiae, castitatis et munditiei, contra omnes calores sordium et macularum lubricae vitae, et veste fervoris amoris suil et proximi, contra omnia frigora malorum imminentium extrinsecus, propter pravıtates humanas, aut propter adversitates quas- libet.
units.en: Here too I felt great desires to this end: that the saints, who can do so much in their glory, might pray for us. Likewise, that the souls in Purgatory might also pray for us, in their groanings and contritions, which otherwise profit themselves nothing — souls which, if they were still in mortal bodies, could not fail to merit, in the least moment, whatever is in heaven. Hence they can avail much, and more than can be said, for us who believe, and who do not trample holy things under our feet, but hold them in the highest esteem in faith, which is the evidence of things that appear not. May Christ grant that those groanings enter into his sight for us! I felt also that it would be an excellent thing that the souls of Purgatory should be invoked before God, to the end that there be given us true knowledge and a true sense of our sins, diligence in working well, solicitude in bringing forth the fruits of penance, and generally all those graces for the lack of which they suffer such great pains. On the day after the day of the souls of the faithful departed, at the time of matins I noted many things which occurred to me concerning a certain understanding of the nakedness of my soul and spirit; on which account I asked, with good devotion of feeling and understanding, that the Lord, by the intercession of all the Saints, would deign to clothe me with the garment of purity, innocence, chastity and cleanness, against all the heats of the filth and stains of a slippery life; and with the garment of the fervour of love of himself and of my neighbour, against all the colds of the evils that threaten from without, through human depravities or through any adversities whatever.

units.la: De nuditate quoque animarum quae sunt in Purgatorio, habui quamdam cognitionem satis claram, quae me docebat ponderandas esse illas paenas magis quam fecerim hactenus, ad compatiendum ipsis animabus, quae hoc nomine, inter alia multa, dici possunt maxime nudae, quia omnia Mala quae patiuntur, ea in proprio spiritu et in anima corpore nudata patiuntur. Sicut enim anima quae nondum habet corpus glorificatum, melius sentit veram consolationem separata quam unita corpori, ita fit ut anima quae patitur extra corpus suum nondum omnino miserum, magis patiatur nuda, quam si esset in suo corpore mortali; profundior enim est dolor et longe magis intimus qui directe penetrat animam et spiritum quam qui mediante corpore, in ipsum pertingit; corpus enim mortale et sensus ipsi aliquas detinent et divertunt paenas corporales et etiam paeoenas spirituales quae, per organa aut per potentias animae corpori immersas, accipiuntur; ita ut non tam vere sentiantur ab anima, sicut cum absque corporis adminiculo et extra corpus adveniunt.
units.en: Concerning the nakedness also of the souls that are in Purgatory I had a certain quite clear knowledge, which taught me that those pains are to be weighed more than I have done hitherto, so as to have compassion on those souls; which on this account, among many others, may be called naked in the highest degree, because all the evils they suffer, they suffer in their bare spirit and in a soul stripped of the body. For as a soul which does not yet have its glorified body feels true consolation better when separated than when united to the body, so it comes about that a soul which suffers outside its body — a body not yet wholly wretched — suffers more when naked than if it were in its mortal body; for the grief that pierces the soul and spirit directly is deeper and far more inward than that which reaches it by means of the body; for the mortal body and the senses themselves detain and divert some part of the bodily pains, and even of the spiritual pains which are received through the organs, or through the powers of the soul immersed in the body; so that they are not felt by the soul so truly as when they come without the body's mediation and outside the body.

units.la: Alio quodam die intra octavas omnium Sanc- torum, ego coeaepi sentire novum quoddam et satis vivum desiderium ad extendendum me in omnibus ad anteriora, quae retro sunt obliviscendo; sic, verbi gratia, quod dum aliquid operatus fuero aut locutus, aut dum cogitavero, aut desideravero, intentio mentis et voluntatissemper niteretur ut tenderet in ea quae restant, et quae sunt meliora, altiora, utiliora, magis grata Deo.
units.en: On another day within the octave of All Saints I began to feel a certain new and quite lively desire to stretch myself out in all things towards what lies ahead, forgetting the things that are behind; so that, for example, whenever I have done or said something, or thought, or desired, the intention of my mind and will should always strive to tend towards the things that remain, and which are better, higher, more useful, more pleasing to God.

units.la: Dicendo officium illius diei, et dicendo missam, hocetiam mihi aliqua ex parte datum est, ut seilicet, circa sensus verborum quae a me dicebantur, niterer ad ulteriorem attentionem, -ulteriorem sensum; cum timore ne anima mea et spiritus distraheretur ad alia, sed potius semper niteretur ad profectum majoremet meliorem.; Hic quoque ego notavi quam saepe nobis expediat-non affici magna devotione; oportet eùàim ut cum parva gratia discamus operari, seu, ut alio: modo loquar, cooperari parvae gratiae Dei; ut exerceatur id quod in nobis:est et ex nobis.
units.en: Saying the office of that day, and saying Mass, this too was in some part given me: namely, that concerning the meanings of the words said by me I should strive after further attention, a further sense; with fear lest my soul and spirit be drawn away to other things, but rather always strive towards greater and better progress. Here too I noted how often it is expedient for us not to be affected with great devotion; for we must learn to work with small grace — or, to speak otherwise, to cooperate with the small grace of God, that what is in us and from us may be exercised.

units.la: Vult igitur frequenter Deus ut cum parvo adju- torio gratiae nitaris servare saltem aliquod bonum desiderium, aut aliquem bonum nisum intentionis tuae ad aliquod. opus, aut ad aliquem spiritua- ADA am lem fructum faciendum. Dat quoque quandoque aliquem timorem in hoc bonum, cujus continuatio saepe melior est quam aliquis fervor magnae devotionis. Non enim oportet ut magni faciamus solam. devotionem, sed etiam desiderium et inquisitionem ejus, et etiam dolorem quod ipsam non habeamus; in quibus tanquam in seminibus optimis crescendum est usque,ad messem fructus. Bonae ergo sunt illae inquisitiones spiritus, illae petitiones et pulsationes, licet sint cum parvo sensu gratiae devotionis. Hoc enim modo eundo, itur, et mittuntur semina. cum difficultate et lacrymis; itur, inquam, ad Deum ipsum; ubi autem jam adest manipulus devotionis aut consolationis, tunc quodam modo venitur et fit egressus quidam ex ipso Deo consolatore, qui quaerendo inventus est. Illud autem verbum Pauli, quod dicit, non esse nos sufficientes ex nobis tanquam ex nobis, ne cogitare ' quidem, non infert nos ex nobis, tanquam ex nobis, nihil posse; sed dicit, nos non sufficere ad aliquod tale bonum. Oportet enim ut gratia praeveniat nos, et comitetur et sequatur idipsum, quod ex nobis tanquam ex nobis est, licet insuf- ficiens; ita ut ipsa sufficientia etiam in minimis ipsi tribuatur. Requiritur autem nostra operatio quae cooperatur gratiae Dei, et ex ipsa suam sufficientiam accipit in prima boni ipsius apprehensione. Nemo igitur dicat se non posse benefacere semper et ubique; quambis etenim sufficientia nostra ex Deo sit in nobis, continuo est in nobis, licet non ex nobis; quia stat gratia ad ostium semper pulsans, qua proinde semper et ubique praeventi et expectatıi sumus, ut et in eo quod ex nobis est (datum tamen in ipsa creatione et aliis viis) cooperemur.
units.en: Frequently, then, God wills that with a small help of grace you strive to keep at least some good desire, or some good effort of your intention towards some work, or towards the making of some spiritual fruit. He gives also sometimes a certain fear towards this good, the continuance of which is often better than some fervour of great devotion. For we ought to prize not only devotion itself, but also the desire and search for it, and even the sorrow of not having it; in which, as in the best of seeds, we must grow until the harvest of fruit. Good, then, are those searchings of the spirit, those askings and knockings, though they be with small sense of the grace of devotion. For going in this way, one goes, and the seeds are sown with difficulty and tears; one goes, I say, to God himself; but where the sheaf of devotion or consolation is already present, then in a certain manner one comes, and there is a kind of going forth from God himself the consoler, who by seeking has been found. And that word of Paul, that we are not sufficient of ourselves, as of ourselves, even to think — it does not conclude that of ourselves, as of ourselves, we can do nothing; but it says that we are not sufficient for any such good. For grace must go before us, and accompany and follow that very thing which is from us as from us, though insufficient; so that the sufficiency, even in the least things, is ascribed to grace. Yet our working is required, which cooperates with the grace of God, and from it receives its sufficiency in the first apprehension of the good. Let no one therefore say that he cannot do well always and everywhere; for although our sufficiency is from God, it is continually in us, though not from us; because grace stands at the door, always knocking, and therefore we are always and everywhere forestalled and awaited, so that we may cooperate also in that which is from us (given, however, in creation itself and in other ways).

units.la: Quinta die infra octavas ejusdem festi Sanctorum, mane postquam me dedissem orationi et contemplationi illi quae mihi quotidiana circa discursum vitae Christi, ego sensi magnam devotionem circa sanctos Angelos, et alios Sanctos, et animas Purgatorii; et orabam Angelos omnium Sanctorum et omnium animarum Purgatorii, qui videlicet aliquando ipsorum custodes fuerant, ut mihi essent propitii per merita Christi Jesu, ut ego possim liberari ab omni maligħitate horum spirituum malorum, qui fuerunt permissi ipsis ad exercitium, Sentiebam enim aliqualiter quam durum esset incidere in manus et potestatem talium Angelorum malorum.
units.en: On the fifth day within the octave of the same feast of the Saints, in the morning, after I had given myself to that prayer and contemplation which is daily with me concerning the course of the life of Christ, I felt great devotion concerning the holy Angels, and the other Saints, and the souls of Purgatory; and I prayed the Angels of all the Saints and of all the souls of Purgatory — those, that is, who had once been their guardians — to be favourable to me through the merits of Christ Jesus, that I might be freed from all the malignity of these evil spirits who were permitted to them for their trial. For I felt in some measure how hard it would be to fall into the hands and power of such evil Angels.

units.la: Rogavi etiam Christum cum magna devotione, considerando quod se subjiceret potestati externae mali Angeli Herodis, Archelai, Annae, Caiphae, Pilati, Herodis, et aliorum qui ipsum in externis afflixerunt; item et Satanae tentatori qui exteriori violentia maxima tentavit ipsum in deserto, et super pinnaculo templi, et super monte; tentavit, inquam, volens allicere ad ea quae carnis sunt, et superbiae, et avaritiae. Optabam autem, per gratiam tante humilitatis, fieri posse ut daemones et mali Angeli non haberent potestatem in īnteriora mea, sed potius, si aliud non expediat, in exteriora. Hic veniebat in mentem quomodo daemones, per manus hominum, per flagella, per clavos, et caetera exteriora, potuerint quidem affligere Christum, sed non per cogitationes aut ullas malas immissiones, quae carnem vel spiritum ad malum sugillare possent. Similiter occurrebat menti, quomodo beata virgo Maria et multi Sancti, imo omnes, habuerint quidem afflictiones externas, sed non ita omnes internas, quamvis alii quidem Sancti et Sanctae (nunquam tamen virgo Maria) aliquando eis frequenter etiam internis tacti sint, circa mundi vanitates, et etiam circa passiones et dolores (de afflictionibus loquor et de sensu voluptatum quae sunt per ministerium malorum spirituum). Beata enim virgo Maria sensit tristitias magnas, juxta illud: Eż tuam ipsius animam pertransibit gladius.
units.en: I prayed Christ also with great devotion, considering that he subjected himself to the outward power of the evil Angel of Herod, of Archelaus, of Annas, of Caiaphas, of Pilate, of Herod, and of the others who afflicted him in outward things; likewise to Satan the tempter, who with the greatest outward violence tempted him in the desert, and on the pinnacle of the temple, and on the mountain — tempted him, I say, wishing to entice him to the things of the flesh, of pride, and of avarice. And I wished, through the grace of such humility, that it might come about that the demons and evil Angels should have no power over my inward parts, but rather, if nothing else may serve, over my outward. Here it came to mind how the demons, through the hands of men, through scourges, nails, and the other outward things, could indeed afflict Christ, but not through thoughts or any evil injections which could beat flesh or spirit towards evil. Likewise it occurred to my mind how the blessed Virgin Mary and many Saints — nay, all — had indeed outward afflictions, but not all in the same way inward ones; although some Saints, men and women (never, however, the Virgin Mary), have sometimes, indeed frequently, been touched even by inward ones, concerning the vanities of the world, and also concerning passions and pains (I speak of the afflictions, and of the sense of pleasures, which come by the ministry of evil spirits). For the blessed Virgin Mary felt great sorrows, according to that word: And thine own soul a sword shall pierce.

units.la: Die qua sepulturae traditus est canonicus Bartholomaeus Monsono, decima tertia scilicet Novembris, in oppido inferioris Ingelheim, duabus leucis a Moguntia, habui quasdam tristitias recogitando aliquo modo meas negligentias circa ipsius curam. Videbar enim mihi nihil illi fecisse. In quo habui tale responsum: Bonum esse quando in omnibus operibus ultra progreditur quisque voluntate, sic quod voluntas non defatigetur, aut gravetur propter operam. Aliud documentum sensi, cogitans aliquas repugnantias quae solent accidere his qui se exercent talibus charitatis operibus circa infirmos et maxime pauperes, propter pericula contagionum, propter foetores, et propter alia incommoda ex quibus possit quis in eadem aut alia incidere; et documentum fuit in hoc, scilicet, quod oporteat attendentem ad talia, aut alia quaevis opera bona, propter solum Christum. ita esse paratum animo, ut in quolibet tali bono opere, ubicumque sit, libenter velit finire vitam.
units.en: On the day when the canon Bartholomew Monsono was committed to burial — the thirteenth of November, in the town of Lower Ingelheim, two leagues from Mainz — I had certain sadnesses, thinking over in some manner my negligences concerning his care. For it seemed to me that I had done nothing for him. In this I had this answer: That it is good when in all works each one goes further in will, in such a way that the will is not wearied or burdened by the work. Another lesson I felt, thinking of certain repugnances which are wont to befall those who exercise themselves in such works of charity towards the sick, and above all the poor — because of the dangers of contagion, because of the stenches, and because of the other discomforts from which one might fall into the same or other ills; and the lesson was this: that he who attends to such works, or any other good works, for Christ's sake alone, ought to be so prepared in mind that in any such good work, wherever he may be, he would gladly be willing to end his life.

units.la: Hic quoque, dum mecum quaererem aliquam causam devotionis et gratiarum actionis, ex eo ipso quod praedictus canonicus dominus Bartholomaeus mortuus fuisset, post medium noctis diei dominicae, videlicet circiter secundam horam, illud mihi occurrit ad spem bonam, quod praedictus fuerat, et hoc certo sciebam: ex fine ipsius et ex socio optimo et continuo, ex multis annis devotissimus erga honorem sancti -Michaelis Archangeli; cdi quidem, cum omnibus aliis Angelis, dies lunae, per. specialem quamdam commemorationem, a multis ecclesiis dicata est. Gaudebam ergo quod talı die abiisset, et ex hoec consolabar. ii Die alio quodam, dum celebrarem officium missae principali intentione pro domino Alvaro Alphonso nostro, qui die praecedenti obierat Lovanii, ego tenens in manibus meis, indignus dignissimum Eucharistiae sacramentum, recognovi magnam erga me hactenus non cogitatam Dei beneficentiam, in hoc quod reliquisset mihi corpus meum instrumentum animae, quo possim adjuvari ad colendum multis modis ipsum Ĝhristum et Patrem ejus; quod corpus nisi esset, fieri facile posset ut ego multa mala facerem, a quibus retrahor, propterea quod corpus non obedit animae ad nutum ipsius, nec ad primos ipsius impulsus ac impetus ipsi subjicitur. Orabam itaque ipsum Christum ut dignaretur hanc gratiam concedere omnibus meis amicis et aliis, quatenus non prius sim emissurus spiritum ex hoc corpore, quam ipsa anima sit bene disposita ad hoc, ut mereatur recipi in manus Dei omnipotentis. Quo pacto enim posset resistere malis spiritibus, si ipsis pervia esset, et coram ipsis, corpore suo in quo latet privata? Et quis eam retineret, ne nimium vaga esset, si neque corpus proprium neque alius spiritus ipsam impediret ab executione motuum suae voluntatis? Nunc esset Romae, nunc in Hispania, nune in patria apud parèntes, nunc alibi. Bonum igitur et necessarium ipsi animae est ut retineatur in corpore, et ut non possit nisi per ipsum operari.
units.en: Here too, while I sought within myself some cause of devotion and thanksgiving out of the very fact that the said canon, Don Bartholomew, had died after the middle of the night of the Lord's day — about the second hour, that is — this occurred to me for good hope: that the said man had been, and this I knew for certain from his end and from his excellent and constant companion, most devout for many years towards the honour of Saint Michael the Archangel; to whom indeed, with all the other Angels, the day of the moon (Monday) is dedicated by many churches with a certain special commemoration. I rejoiced therefore that he had departed on such a day, and from this I took comfort. On another day, while I celebrated the office of the Mass with the principal intention for our Don Álvaro Alfonso, who the day before had died at Louvain, holding in my hands — unworthy — the most worthy sacrament of the Eucharist, I recognized a great kindness of God towards me, never before thought of: in this, that he had left me my body as the instrument of my soul, whereby I can be helped to worship in many ways Christ himself and his Father; for were it not for this body, it might easily come about that I should do many evils, from which I am held back precisely because the body does not obey the soul at its nod, nor submit itself to its first impulses and onsets. I prayed therefore Christ himself that he would deign to grant this grace to all my friends and to others: that I may not send forth the spirit from this body before the soul itself is well disposed for this, so that it may deserve to be received into the hands of almighty God. For how could it resist the evil spirits, if it lay open to them, and stood before them stripped of its body in which it lies hidden? And who would hold it back from wandering too far, if neither its own body nor another spirit hindered it from carrying out the motions of its will? Now it would be at Rome, now in Spain, now in its own country with its parents, now elsewhere. It is good, then, and necessary for the soul itself that it be held in the body, and that it can work only through it.

units.la: Sit igitur benedictus Deus, qui disponit omnia suaviter!
units.en: Blessed therefore be God, who disposes all things sweetly!

units.la: Die sanctae Catharinae Alexandrinae, fuit mihi singularis quaedam nolitia, quomodo, ad melius divinum officium recitandum, admodum juvaret, tibi persuadere, interea dum durabit attentio bona in verba divina, Dominum sollicitum esse tui circa ala negotia et opera tua; et quod ideo non debeas permittere te tunc distrahi ad quaecumque et quantumcumque bona opera et pia, ne impedias ipsum Deum quominus ipse sit attentus et sollicitus.
units.en: On the day of Saint Catherine of Alexandria there came to me a certain singular perception: how, for the better recitation of the divine office, it would greatly help to persuade yourself that, so long as good attention to the divine words lasts, the Lord is solicitous for you concerning your other affairs and works; and that therefore you ought not to allow yourself to be then drawn away to any works whatever, however good and pious, lest you hinder God himself from being attentive and solicitous.

units.la: Notavi etiam quantum conveniret ut, dum tu recitas tuum officium, considerares ex una parte tibi praesentem esse Deum, et bonum Angelum ejus qui notet et ponderet exactissime omnem profectum tuum et omnem laborem; et ex alia parte, inimicum hominem, id est, spiritum malignum, qui notet quaecumque errata committis, ut tandem accusare te valeat.
units.en: I noted also how fitting it would be that, while you recite your office, you should consider on the one side that God is present with you, and his good Angel, who marks and weighs most exactly all your progress and all your labour; and on the other side the enemy of man, that is, the malignant spirit, who marks whatever errors you commit, that at last he may be able to accuse you.

units.la: Pridie diei sancti Saturnini, cum celebrarem officium sancti Caesarii martyris qui mihi relictus fuerat, ego inveni magnum sensum devo- tionis circa praedictum sanctum Caesarium mar- tyrem, licet non haberem quidquam proprii circa ipsius vitam aut martyrium. Tune primo mihi datum est intelligere, per spiritum, quam bonum sit, si quis circa quodlibet festum cujuscumque sancti occurrentis, sumeret unam contemplationem de tali sancto, quae haberet, post praeparatoria consueta, quinque puncta: primum, ut agantur gratiae Deo Patri, Filio et Spiritui Sancto, quod talem sanctum velsanctam prae- destinaverit ab aeterno, ac deinde elegerit, voca- verit, justificaverit, magnificaverit, et tandem glorificaverit; secundum erit agere gratias beatae Virgini, beato Michaeli, et bono angelo illius sancti, et omnibus sanctis viris et mulieribus qui ipsum precibus, aut quibuscumque aliis modis, apud Deum adjuverunt ut salvaretur; tertium punctum erit orare Deum et ipsum sancWum pro omnibus animabus defunctis et vivis hominibus, qui devoti fuerunt et sunt. circa talem sanctum; quartum erit orare Deum (con- siderando quod bonum est ut ita fiat) ut digne- tur conservare -nobis eam doctrinam et eas scripturas, ex quibus possimus habere memo- riam aliquorum verborum, aut etiam actionum, a a prer Den quas ille sanctus in nostram aedificationem, dum viveret, exercuit; quintum erit considerare quam bonum èt quam utile est àut esset, ut reliquiae corporis talis Sancti vel Sanctae, ex toto, vel ex parte, haberentur aul habeantur, et cum maxima veneratione servarentur. Qui autem non invenerit materiam in his punctis ad exercendum intellectum, is exerceat voluntatem, cordis sui, ut desideret haec omnia esse et melius ac melius fieri.
units.en: On the eve of the day of Saint Saturninus, when I celebrated the office of Saint Caesarius the martyr, which had been left to me, I found a great sense of devotion towards the said holy martyr Caesarius, although I had nothing particular concerning his life or martyrdom. Then for the first time it was given me to understand, by the spirit, how good it is if, for the feast of any saint that occurs, one should take a contemplation on that saint, having, after the accustomed preparations, five points: the first, that thanks be given to God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, for having predestined such a saint from eternity, and then chosen, called, justified, magnified, and at last glorified him; the second will be to give thanks to the blessed Virgin, to blessed Michael, and to the good angel of that saint, and to all holy men and women who helped him with their prayers, or in any other ways, before God, that he might be saved; the third point will be to pray God and the saint himself for all the souls departed, and the living, who have been and are devoted to that saint; the fourth will be to pray God (considering that it is good that it be so) to deign to preserve for us that teaching and those writings from which we can have the memory of some words, or even deeds, which that saint, while he lived, wrought for our edification; the fifth will be to consider how good and how useful it is, or would be, that the relics of the body of such a saint, whole or in part, should be possessed, and kept with the greatest veneration. And he who finds no matter in these points for exercising the intellect, let him exercise the will of his heart, desiring that all these things be, and be done better and better.

units.la: In die sancti Saturnini, quae erat vigilia sancti Andreae apostoli, dum ego vellem celebrare missam, datum est mihi ut quae sequuntur ex animo bono peterem, videlicet, a Patre caelesti, gratiam et omnia quibus indiget mea memoria; a Filio, omnia quibus indiget intellectus meus; a Spiritu Sancto, ea quibus indiget voluntas. Sic commendabam summae Trinitati meas tres potentias. Praeterea commendabam animam meam ipsi animae Christi Domini Nostri et salvatoris; totum autem denique compositum meum, et eum qui dicitur homo, ipsi Christo homini facto pro nobis.
units.en: On the day of Saint Saturninus, which was the vigil of Saint Andrew the apostle, when I wished to celebrate Mass, it was given me to ask from a good heart the things that follow: namely, from the heavenly Father, grace and all that my memory needs; from the Son, all that my intellect needs; from the Holy Spirit, the things my will needs. Thus I commended to the supreme Trinity my three powers. Moreover I commended my soul to the very soul of Christ Our Lord and saviour; and finally my whole composite, and that which is called man, to Christ himself, made man for us.

units.la: Hic etiam in singulari quodam desiderio spi- ritus, et cum quadam speciali agnitione mea, ut dicam, reptilitatis ac demissionis spiritus mei, ego petebam gratiam elevationis mentis meae; et ut non jam, lta ut assuevit, remaneat deorsum, et circa haec infima inclinata; et ut ex spiritu suae infirmitatis erigatur per gratiam Jesu Christi, ut possit crescere, et in id quod est sursum aspicere.
units.en: Here also, in a certain singular desire of the spirit, and with a certain special recognition of the — so to speak — creeping lowness and dejection of my spirit, I asked the grace of the raising of my mind; that it might no longer, as it has been accustomed, remain downward, bent towards these lowest things; but that from the spirit of its weakness it might be raised up by the grace of Jesus Christ, that it may grow, and look towards that which is above.

units.la: Pro hac re, venit in mentem id quod alias frequenter venerat, id est, quod bonum sit si fiam devotus illius sanctae mulieris, quae per Christum liberata fuit a spiritu infirmitatis, quo prohibebatur ne etiam corporaliter sursum posset respicere, liberata vero potuit. Hoc die igitur firmius propositum qùam antea sumpsi, ut posthac Christum hoc miraculum operantem, et ipsam mulierem tantam gratiam recipientem, in memoria habeam; multum enim juvat ut, secundum exigentiam necessitatum nostrarum, consideretur Christus, quasi esset in administrandis illis gratiis, quas dum mortalis esset administrabat.
units.en: For this matter there came to mind what had often come at other times: that it would be good if I became devoted to that holy woman who was freed by Christ from the spirit of infirmity by which she was prevented from being able even bodily to look up, but being freed, she could. On this day, therefore, I took a firmer purpose than before, to keep henceforth in memory Christ working this miracle, and the woman herself receiving so great a grace; for it helps much that, according to the demands of our needs, Christ be considered as though he were engaged in administering those graces which he administered while he was mortal.

units.la: Juvat etiam non parum cos qui tales receperunt gratias invocare, ut nobis similia bona et eadem apud eumdem Dominum implorent et, ki hi impetrent. Non est igitur contra pietatem, imo secundum pietatem est ea doctrina, qua quis doceat pium esse ut specialiter quidam sancti pro gratiis quibusdam tam spiritualibus quam corporalibus invocentur. Licet enim Deus omnia per se, et per quemlibet sanctum aeque possit, atque per alium quemvis, non tamen vult facere omnia per unum medium. te Pea S A AGE AS Die sancti Eligii episcopi et confessoris, inveni bonam devotionem, aliquot invocationes multiplicans, ut mihi gratiam aliquam a Deo Domino Nostro impetraret; aliquas gratias, inquam, et maxime quae essent ad propositum illorum duorum verborum quae sunt in communi confessorum oratione, ubi petimus nobis augeri devotionem et salutem, ġquae duo verba ego solito melius sensi in missa, quae erat de ipso sancto Eligio. Post missam, súper quamdam petitionem, ego inveni adhuc majorem devotionem: forma autem petitionis ad Deum erat, ut dignaretur aspicere non ad merita. neque demerita mea, neque ad frigiditatem meorum bonorum desi- deriorum; sed ad meas necessitates, indigentias, miserias et utilitates. In missa quoque, hac forma mihi fuit datum uti: Domine, Jesu Christe, aufer a me omne malum et omnem imperfectionem quae potest impedire oculos tuae humanitatis ab aspectu meo, aures tuas ab auditu verborum meorum, olfactum tuum, ut ne avertatur a me propter faetores meos, gustum propter insipiditates. meas, et tactum propter frigiditatem malam et malam caliditatem, nimiam siccitatem et humilitatem infimam; rogo te, mi Domine, ut auferas a me quidquid me dividit, separat et removet a te, et te a me; aufer quidquid me facit immundum, quidquid me reddit aridum, quidquid me facit rigidum, devium, saucium, indignum tua visione, tua correptione, tua reprehensione, tua allocutione, tua communicatione, tuo denique amore ac benevolentia. ‚Miserere mei, Domine, et miserere super me, et remove illa omnia mala quae faciunt quominus te videre possim, audire, gustare, olfacere, tangere, timere, memorari, intelligere; sperare, amare, possidere, praesentem habere, ex parte frui. Quod autem mihi, Domine, de te et de tua divinitate aut humanitate concupisco, -oro saltem ut mihi concedatur in omni verbo quod procedit de ore tuo. Satis enim mihi esset quod verba Jesu Christi Domini mei in me manerent et ego illa omnibus modis sentirem.
units.en: It helps also not a little to invoke those who have received such graces, that they may implore and obtain for us like goods, and the same, from the same Lord. It is not, then, against piety — nay, it is according to piety — that teaching by which one teaches it to be a pious thing that certain saints be specially invoked for certain graces, spiritual as well as bodily. For although God can do all things by himself, and equally through any saint as through any other, he nevertheless does not will to do all things through one means. On the day of Saint Eligius, bishop and confessor, I found good devotion, multiplying several invocations, that he might obtain for me some grace from God Our Lord; some graces, I say, and above all such as bear on those two words which are in the common prayer of confessors, where we ask that devotion and salvation be increased in us — which two words I felt better than usual in the Mass, which was of Saint Eligius himself. After Mass, upon a certain petition, I found still greater devotion: the form of the petition to God was that he would deign to look not at my merits or demerits, nor at the coldness of my good desires, but at my necessities, wants, miseries and interests. At Mass also it was given me to use this form: Lord Jesus Christ, take from me every evil and every imperfection which can hinder the eyes of your humanity from looking on me, your ears from hearing my words, your smell, that it turn not from me because of my stenches, your taste because of my insipidities, and your touch because of my evil cold and evil heat, my excessive dryness and lowest dampness; I beg you, my Lord, take from me whatever divides, separates and removes me from you, and you from me; take away whatever makes me unclean, whatever renders me dry, whatever makes me rigid, wayward, wounded, unworthy of your sight, your correction, your reproof, your address, your communication, and finally your love and good will. Have mercy on me, O Lord, and have mercy over me, and remove all those evils which prevent me from being able to see you, hear, taste, smell, touch, fear, remember, understand, hope, love, possess, have you present, and in part enjoy you. And what I long for, Lord, concerning you and your divinity or humanity — I pray at least that it be granted me in every word that proceeds from your mouth. For it would be enough for me that the words of Jesus Christ my Lord should abide in me, and that I should feel them in every way.

units.la: Ex diebus sancti Andreae apostoli et dominicae primae adventus, et sanctae Barbarae, et sancti Eligu confessoris qui prima Decembris occurrit, ego coepi sentire quamdam gratiam, quam nunquam.in me senseram, usque ad diem sancti Sabbae abbatis. Haec autem Dei gratia erga me in eo est deprehensa, quod hactenus in distractionibus meis quas habeo circa orationes meas, distractionibus, inquam, non tam quibus abstrahar a bonis cogitationibus et sensibus (raro enim ab his distrahor) quam ab otio spiritus, sine fructu non permaneam. Hanc igitur in hac materia notavi differentiam inter illud quod iis diebus coepit esse et illud quod antea: magis frequens erat, quod videlicet tempore praeterito ego, ab extrinseco magis motore externo solitus sim revocari ex distractione, ad ipsam, ut sic loquar, intractionem; ab extrinseco, inquam, ut puta. ex vi tentationum malarum cogitationum, sine to CGE i n En MEERN A quarum verberibùs frequenter non redissem, nec petiissem gratiam redeundi ad cor. Item ex remorsu conscientiae, èx timore, ex multis denique reprehensionibus cogitationum, quibus angebar dum essem distractus, ex quibus omnibus causabatur in me dolor, qui et ipse me adigebat ad quaerendum devotionem et remedium contra distractiones. Haec igitur erant magis ordinaria in me, eaque magis ego deprehendebam; et tamen non deerant desideria et postulationes, quibus ego petebam a Domino gratiam istam, quam nunc sentire coepi mihi ex parte dari, id est, quod ex intimis fieret revocatio de meae, si quando discederet a pace ipsius, et quod prima retractio esset ex visceribus et ex corde. His diebus itaque hoc magis notavi quam unquam: sensi enim frequenter, dum a quiete spiritus mei ad aliquodcontrarium distraherer, sensi, inquam, intractionem. et recollectionem incipere ab intrinseco. Magnam itaque devotionem inveni, dum applicarem ad hane gratiam petendam discursum vitae Christi, qui 'et ipse incaepit intrare ad nos per interna, dum praeser- vavit Matrem ab omni originalis mali culpa, et dum factus est homo in utero ipsius, visitans in utero, et tandem veniens ad externa incrementa. À Hic notavi quomodo Christus, in triginta circiter annis quos exegit antequam inciperet verbis docere mundum, docuerit factis, oportere. hominem exacte sibi attendere, ut in seipso perficiatur; ita ut ante omnia discat imitari eos Christi actus qui fuerunt, dum abscondebatur in utero, absque usu humanitatis, intelligendi, memorandi, desiderandi, videndi, audiendi, gustandi, odorandi ac tangendi experimentaliter. Considerandum quoque ad imitandum hoc quod voluerit prius venire ad usum videndi et sentiendi externis suis sensibus, quam vellet venire ad experimentalem usum veri ratiocinii humani; et quod praeterea ante voluerit audire quam scire usum loquendi; ante voluerit subjici quam dominari; esse discipulus quam magister; esse, inquam, et non solum dici; regi, quam regere.
units.en: From the days of Saint Andrew the apostle and the first Sunday of Advent, and of Saint Barbara, and of Saint Eligius the confessor, which falls on the first of December, I began to feel a certain grace which I had never felt in myself, until the day of Saint Sabas the abbot. And this grace of God towards me was perceived in this: that now, in the distractions I have about my prayers — distractions, I say, not so much by which I am drawn from good thoughts and feelings (for I am rarely drawn from these) as of an idleness of spirit — I do not remain without fruit. In this matter, then, I noted this difference between what began to be in those days and what before was more frequent: namely, that in time past I was wont to be called back from distraction to what I may call the in-drawing by some outward mover — from without, I say, as for instance by the force of temptations of evil thoughts, without whose lashes I should often not have returned, nor asked the grace of returning to my heart; likewise by remorse of conscience, by fear, and by the many reproaches of my thoughts, with which I was distressed while distracted; from all of which was caused in me a grief which itself drove me to seek devotion and a remedy against distractions. These, then, were the more ordinary things in me, and these I perceived the more; and yet there were not lacking desires and petitions by which I asked of the Lord that grace which now I have begun to feel in part given me: namely, that the calling back should come from within, whenever my soul departed from its peace, and that the first drawing back should be from the bowels and from the heart. In these days therefore I noted this more than ever: for I frequently felt, when I was being drawn from the quiet of my spirit to something contrary, that the in-drawing and recollection began from within. I found great devotion, then, when I applied to the asking of this grace the round of the life of Christ, who himself also began to enter in to us by inward ways, when he preserved his Mother from all guilt of the original evil, and when he was made man in her womb, visiting from the womb, and at last coming to outward growth. Here I noted how Christ, in the thirty years or so which he passed before he began to teach the world by words, taught by deeds that a man must attend exactly to himself, that he may be perfected in himself; so that before all things he should learn to imitate those acts of Christ which were his while he lay hidden in the womb, without the use of his humanity for understanding, remembering, desiring, seeing, hearing, tasting, smelling and touching by experience. It is to be considered also, for imitation, that he willed to come to the use of seeing and perceiving with his outward senses before he would come to the experiential use of true human reasoning; and that moreover he willed to hear before he would know the use of speaking; willed to be subject before to rule; to be a disciple before a master — to be, I say, and not only to be called; to be governed, before governing.

units.la: Hoc die sancti Sabbae abbatis, dum vellem celebrare pro confessario meo, ego sensi magnam memoriam et gratiam magnae et insolitae grati- aam ay omnes. confessarios quos unquam b d i EISES habui; item erga eum qui me baptisavit; erga eum qui me confirmavit; erga eos qui contulerunt mihi sacros ordines, et generaliter quaecumque sacramenta. Adfuit etiam memoria generalis erga praeceptores, et in summa erga eos qui ministraverunt mihi aliquam Dei gratiam, sive in verbis, sive in signis, sive alio modo quocumque. Idem feci nomine omnium fratrum meorum, - cupiens in hac parte, in fide Jesu Christi, supplere s vicem ipsorum, sicut et ipsi in multis supplent vicem meam, et me in multis apud Deum excusant, tanquam membra de membro. Sicut enim Deus nonnulla forte mihi, ad aliquam recognitionem, aut gratiarum actiones communicat, quae caeteris omnibus non communicat, ita e diverso maxime multa erunt quae alii recognoverunt, de quibus ego nunquam cogitaverim. Habui etiam magnum desiderium erga salutem omnium eorum, qui vel sacramenta, ut dixi, vel quaecumque alia Dei dona ac bona mihi unquam communicarint.
