Desiderabam etiam ut ipse Deus dignaretur eos omnes facere mihi gloriae suae ministros et bonorum caelestium, quos mihi voluit esse minis- tros gratiae et bonorum temporalium. Datum est etiammihi ut cum bono sensu humilitatis opta- rem hoc aliud postulatum, id est, ut mihi conce- deretur, per gratiam et misericordiam Jesu Christi quatenus illi omnes possent esse gloriosi benefici mei, qui fuerunt gratiosi benefici in hac vita, et ut merear esse subjectus gloriosa quadam servitute iis omnibus quibus quocumque modo fuerim subjectus in hae vita servitute quae est in statu gratiae. Amen.
units.en: On this day of Saint Sabas the abbot, when I wished to celebrate for my confessor, I felt a great remembrance, and the grace of a great and unwonted gratitude, towards all the confessors I have ever had; likewise towards him who baptized me; towards him who confirmed me; towards those who conferred on me holy orders, and generally all the sacraments. There was present also a general remembrance towards my teachers, and in sum towards all who have ministered to me any grace of God, whether in words, or in signs, or in any other way whatever. The same I did in the name of all my brethren, desiring in this matter, in the faith of Jesus Christ, to supply their place, as they too in many things supply mine, and in many things excuse me before God, as members for a member. For as God perhaps communicates to me some things for acknowledgment or thanksgiving which he does not communicate to all the rest, so contrariwise there will be very many things which others have acknowledged, of which I have never thought. I had also a great desire for the salvation of all those who have ever communicated to me either the sacraments, as I said, or any other gifts and goods of God. I desired also that God would deign to make all those the ministers to me of his glory and of heavenly goods, whom he willed to be my ministers of grace and of temporal goods. It was also given me, with a good sense of humility, to wish this further petition: that it might be granted me, through the grace and mercy of Jesus Christ, that all those might be my glorious benefactors who were my gracious benefactors in this life; and that I may deserve to be subject, by a certain glorious servitude, to all those to whom in this life I have been in any way subject by that servitude which belongs to the state of grace. Amen.

units.la: In diebus solemnitatis piissimae virginis Mariae ego sensi novam quamdam soliditatem etstabilitatem cordis et interiorum meorum; unde fieri videbam ut minus penetrabilis essem advenientibüs extrinsecus tentationum fluctibus. Non sensi magnam devotionem ex parte apprehensionum, quae me moverit ad magnas commotiones et vivos sensus devotionis; sed nec sensi pro solito more me penetrari a cogitationibus immundi aut mali spiritus; quia subjectum ipsum per gratiam esse sentiebam, nescio quo modo novo, solidatum in se et stabilitum. Hoc perinde est ac si diceret quis. domům suam solidatam aliqua de parte respectu fundamenti, aut parietum ac columnarum, et relique materiae, licet ornatus ipse non sit auctus. Alias frequenter sensi in me sanctos quosdam influxus et divinarum motionum et inspirationum bonarum; et tamen tunc sentiebam simul maximas quasdam debilitates, et inconstantiam ipsius subjecti. Faxit Jesus optimus et Sanctus sanctorum, per intercessionem Matris suae et omnium angelorum et sanctorum caelestium, ut quotidie utrumque, in me renovari possit, id est subjectum meum ipsum, et ornatus, diminutioque imperfectionum. Utinam renovetur ipsum esse, ipsum vivere, ipsum sentire, ipsum denique posse; deinde et qualitates, et quaecumque sancta accidentia ipsi subjecto ad aeternam et coelestem vitam necessaria sunt et Deo placentia.
units.en: In the days of the solemnity of the most loving Virgin Mary I felt a certain new solidity and stability of my heart and of my inward parts; whence I saw it come about that I was less penetrable to the waves of temptations coming from without. I did not feel great devotion on the side of apprehensions, such as might move me to great stirrings and lively feelings of devotion; but neither did I feel myself, as had been usual, penetrated by the thoughts of the unclean or evil spirit; for I felt that the subject itself had by grace been — I know not in what new way — made solid in itself and established. It is as if one should say that his house had been made solid in some part as to its foundation, or its walls and pillars and the rest of its fabric, although the ornament itself has not been increased. At other times I have often felt in myself certain holy influxes of divine motions and good inspirations; and yet I felt at the same time certain very great weaknesses, and the inconstancy of the subject itself. May Jesus, the best, and the Holy of holies, grant, by the intercession of his Mother and of all the angels and saints of heaven, that both may daily be renewed in me: that is, my subject itself, and the adornment, and the diminishing of imperfections. Would that my very being were renewed, my living, my feeling, and my power itself; then also the qualities, and whatever holy accidents are necessary to the subject for eternal and heavenly life, and pleasing to God.

units.la: Eodem tempore, id est festi Conceptionis, ego hoc unum notavi, circa tentationes meas, me videlicet esse quodammodo magis lucidum -in me, et quasi ex parte quadam eductum de mea propria et nativa confusione et indistinctione; memoriam quoque magis capacem et retinentem esse; et me nońita ut solebam alias turbari. Utinam haec sint initia ad hoc bonum ut tan- dem aliquando exire possim ex meis tenebris ad Lumen illud inaccessibile, ex profundo meae confusionis propriae ac debilitatis et infirmitatis ad illam distinctissimam Vitam, plenam omnis fortitudinis et omnis soliditatis. Novit Dominus quantitatem et qualitatem mei proprii esse et mei posse: novit etiam deformationes meas proprias, et maculas, caeteraque omnia mala et vilissima accidentia; sed beata virgo Maria, Mater nostra et advocata, tota pulchra et tota sine macula, et quantum ad materiam, et quantum ad omnes formas, haec, inquam, Domina Nostra potens est apud Patrem, et Filium, et Spiritum Sanctum, ut suis precibus mihi impetrare possit gratiam, qua et materia subjecti mei reformetur, et etiam depingatur, informeturque sanctis accidentibus; fiat, fiat! Quidquid autem tandem fuerit, id profluet ex potentia Patris, administrabitur per sapientiam Filii, et donabitur in bonitate Spiritus Sancti; fiat, fiat!
units.en: At the same time, that is, of the feast of the Conception, I noted this one thing about my temptations: that I am in a certain manner more lucid within myself, and as it were in some part led out of my own native confusion and indistinctness; that my memory also is more capacious and retentive; and that I am not troubled as I used to be at other times. Would that these might be beginnings towards this good: that at some time I may at last go out from my darkness to that inaccessible Light, from the depth of my own confusion and weakness and infirmity to that most distinct Life, full of all strength and all solidity. The Lord knows the quantity and quality of my own being and of my power; he knows also my own deformities and stains, and all the other evil and most vile accidents; but the blessed Virgin Mary, our Mother and advocate, all fair and all without stain, both as to matter and as to all forms — she, I say, Our Lady, is powerful with the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, to obtain for me by her prayers the grace by which the matter of my subject may be reformed, and also painted and informed with holy accidents. So be it, so be it! And whatever at last shall be, it will flow from the power of the Father, be administered by the wisdom of the Son, and be given in the goodness of the Holy Spirit. So be it, so be it!

units.la: In nocte sacratissima in qua natus est Jesus Christus Dominus Noster, dum essem in matutinis apud Ecclesiam cathedralem, ante faciem reliquiarum, et dicerem officium nocturnum, sensi magnam devotionem et magnam lacrymarum -aa O T, ie f zt A 5 effusionem, idque a principio usque ad finem. Verba illa Jeremiae prophetaee me maxime penetrarunt, quae ibi leguntur ad primum nocturnum. Magna desideria mihi data sunt ut optarem ex animo bene nasci ex Deo, et non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri.
units.en: In the most sacred night in which Jesus Christ Our Lord was born, while I was at matins in the cathedral church, before the face of the relics, and said the night office, I felt great devotion and a great pouring out of tears, and that from beginning to end. Those words of the prophet Jeremiah pierced me most which are read there at the first nocturn. Great desires were given me to wish from my heart to be born well of God, and not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man.

units.la: Optavi etiam ex animo sitienti et bene. affecto ut ea nocte nascerentur aliqua bona et efficacia media ac remedia contra mala nostri saeculi. Sensi item magnum affectum ad hoc ut ego ex nunc nascerer ad omne bonum opus, ad salutem meam faciendam, et ad honorem Dei et utilitatem proximi. Hoc autem esset, si dederit mihi Dominus spiritum, in quo et per quem me totum referrem et ordinarem ad unumquodque tale bonum opus, imitando Illum qui unicuique totus conceptus: est, et unicuique natus et mortuus, etc. Hoc in spiritu debemus velle vivere reliquum vitae nostrae, et agere omnia ad usum proximi nostri, aut ad laudem Dei; sufficit enim, et nimium est, praeteritum tempus nostrum in hoc fuisse ut nobis nostrisque commodis temporali- þus vixerimus, quasi nobis solis essemus nati.
units.en: I wished also, with a thirsting and well-affected heart, that in that night there might be born certain good and efficacious means and remedies against the evils of our age. I felt likewise a great affection towards this: that I might from now on be born to every good work, for the working of my salvation, and for the honour of God and the profit of my neighbour. And this would be, if the Lord should give me the spirit in which and through which I would refer and order my whole self to each such good work, imitating Him who was conceived whole for each one, and for each one born, and died, and the rest. In this spirit we ought to will to live the remainder of our life, and to do all things for the use of our neighbour, or for the praise of God; for it is enough, and too much, that our past time was spent in living for ourselves and our temporal comforts, as though we had been born for ourselves alone.

units.la: Nota quod tria concurrerunt ad nostram corporalem nativitatem: primum quidem, materia illa sanguinum ex qua sumus; secundum, voluntas carnalis, et concupiscientia parentum gignentium; tertium, intentio atque alia voluntas parentum qui volunt filios suos esse tandem divites in mundo, propter quam voluntatem saepe appetunt filiorum generationem temporalem. Qui ergo rursus nasci debet, ex Deo ipso cujus natura per- fectissima est, et cujus omnis voluntas rectissima est atque sanctissima, nasci debet, et ita vivere ut non jam feratur secundum inclinationem corruptae naturae suae, quam ex sanguinibus habet; neque secundum appetitus carnales moveri jam debet, aut secundum eos motus voluntatis, qui sunt humani atque mundani viri. Ex. talibus fructibus sumenda erunt signa verae nativitatis, id est, ejus qūae ex Deo existit.
units.en: Note that three things concurred to our bodily birth: first, that matter of blood from which we are; second, the carnal will and concupiscence of the begetting parents; third, the intention and that other will of parents who wish their children to be one day rich in the world — for the sake of which will they often desire the temporal begetting of children. He, then, who must be born again ought to be born of God himself, whose nature is most perfect and whose every will is most right and most holy, and so to live that he is no longer carried along according to the inclination of his corrupted nature, which he has from blood; nor ought he now to be moved according to carnal appetites, or according to those motions of the will which belong to the human and worldly man. From such fruits are to be taken the signs of the true birth — that is, of the birth which is from God.

units.la: Missam primam, quae silicet fuit in media nocte, applicui quantum ex mea intentione fuit, ad Societatem nostram, cuı desideranter: optabam omnium bonorum desideriorum et totius sanctitatis et justitiae coram Deo nativitatem, et quod unusquisque toti mundo nasceretur. Haec fuit dicta in summo templo. Secundam dixi in monasterio Carmelitarum, pro felici partu omnium - bonorum desideriorum R= Moguntini et pro spirituali nativitate totius tractus Rhenani mihi 'commendati; tertiam vero in templo divae Virginis ad Gradus, ubi ego habui occasionem contemplandi circa solemnitatem puerperii ejusdem beatissimae Virginis. Hanc. missam, dixi pro nativitate remediorum quibus indigent haec calamitosa tempora, id est, pro pace inter Christia-, nos principes, pro expulsione haeresum, et pro reliquis bonis universalibus.
units.en: The first Mass, which was at midnight, I applied, so far as lay in my intention, to our Society, for which I longingly desired the birth of all good desires and of all holiness and justice before God, and that each one might be born for the whole world. This was said in the cathedral. The second I said in the monastery of the Carmelites, for the happy bringing to birth of all the good desires of the Most Reverend of Mainz, and for the spiritual birth of the whole Rhine country entrusted to me; and the third in the church of the holy Virgin ad Gradus, where I had occasion to contemplate the solemnity of the child-bearing of the same most blessed Virgin. This Mass I said for the birth of the remedies which these calamitous times need: that is, for peace among Christian princes, for the driving out of heresies, and for the other universal goods.

units.la: In prima missa, dum sentirem me frigidum ante communionem, et dolerem quod non esset melior dispositio habitationis meae, venit in me spiritus satis vivus, in quo habui hoc responsum, cum intrinseco sensu devotionis usque ad lacrymas: Hunc spiritum convenire ad stabulum. Si enim jam ferventissimus esses, hic non videres humanitatem Domini tui, quia non. esset tanta ratio in te spiritualis stabuli. Consolatus fui itaque in Christo Domino, qui dignaretur venire ad tam frigentem domum. Volebam, ut domus mea essetornata, ita ut super ea pos- sem consolari; et vidi conditionem ipsius Do- mini, in qua sum consolatus. Utinam mihi posthac detur ut dum non potero videre in. meipso eum modum, eam formam; eum habitum quem ego vellem habere ad ipsum Deum meum Jesum, aut Matrem vel sanctos ejus, utinam, inquam, dum hoc negabitur justa de causa, mihi detur videre et sentire eum habitum, eam formam, eumque modum quo se habet ille erga me.
units.en: At the first Mass, when I felt myself cold before communion, and grieved that the disposition of my dwelling was not better, there came upon me a spirit lively enough, in which I had this answer, with an inward sense of devotion even to tears: that this spirit befits the stable. For if you were now most fervent, you would not see here the humanity of your Lord, because there would not be in you so much the character of the spiritual stable. I was consoled therefore in Christ the Lord, who would deign to come to so cold a house. I wished my house to be adorned, so that I might take comfort in it; and I saw the condition of the Lord himself, in which I was comforted. Would that hereafter it may be given me, when I cannot see in myself that manner, that form, that habit which I would wish to have towards my God Jesus, or his Mother, or his saints — would that, I say, when this is denied for a just cause, it may be given me to see and feel the habit, the form and the manner in which he bears himself towards me.

units.la: Hactenus ego semper magis studui quaerere ornatum in quo ad Deum aut sanctos ejus accederem, quam cognitionem in qua possem sentire quo ornatu ipsi me vel respiciunt, vel despiciunt, aut amant, aut tolerant, aut juvant. Quaesivi semper aliqua indumenta devotionis, aut reliquos quosque apparatus, quibus possem illos ad me vocare, et ut essem illis amabilis et acceptus; non autem vicissim quaesivi modum quo possem ad illos accedere, quod facilius fieret, siquidem possem contemplari ea ipsa bona quae in se habent et quibus tam sunt per se amabiles et acceptabiles. Det omnipotens Pater, et Filius, et Spiritus Sanctus, mihi gratiam, ut ego simul utrumque horum sciam, et possim, et velim inquirere et petere, id est, amaria Deo et sanctis ejus, et amare Deum et sanctos ejus. Magis autem posthac satagendum est id quod meliùs ac magis liberale. est, et quod ego minus feci, id est velle amare magıs quam vellẹ amari. Quaerenda igitur erunt signa, quibus significari possit me amare, magis diligenter quam illa uibus significatur me amari. Haec erunt labores propter Christum et propter proximum, juxta illud Christi ad Petrum: Diligis me plus his? Pasce oves meas. Vide igitur ut sis Petrus prius, ut postea sis Joannes, qui plus diligitur, et iù quo 'est gratia. Hactenus voluisti esse primo Joannes, et deinde Petrus. Haec scribebam in die sancti Stephani, dictis jam vesperis beati Joannis Evangelistae.
units.en: Hitherto I have always studied rather to seek the adornment in which I might approach God or his saints, than the knowledge in which I might feel with what disposition they look on me, or look away, or love, or tolerate, or help me. I have always sought certain garments of devotion, or whatever other preparations, by which I might call them to me, and be lovable and acceptable to them; but I have not in turn sought the way by which I might approach them — which would be easier done, if I could contemplate the very goods which they have in themselves, and by which they are of themselves so lovable and acceptable. May the almighty Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit give me grace to know, and be able, and will to seek and ask both of these together: that is, to be loved by God and his saints, and to love God and his saints. But henceforth I must strive more after that which is better and more generous, and which I have done less: that is, to will to love rather than to will to be loved. I must seek, then, the signs by which my loving may be shown, more diligently than those by which my being loved is shown. These will be labours for Christ's sake and for my neighbour's, according to that word of Christ to Peter: Lovest thou me more than these? Feed my sheep. See therefore that you be Peter first, that afterwards you may be John, who is the more loved, and in whom is grace. Hitherto you have wished to be first John, and then Peter. This I wrote on the day of Saint Stephen, vespers of blessed John the Evangelist being already said.

units.la: In die sancti Joannis Evangelistae, ego dixi missam pro necessitatibus quibusdam spiritualibus, et contra quaedam frigora malignorum spirituum, qui frequenter ita me disponunt erga quosdam proximos, et illos erga me, ut nesciamus nos alterutrum ferre nec corripere. Inveni in hoc satis magnam, devotionem et magnam spem contra molestias daemonum, eas, inquam, molestias, quibus fit ut homines sibi invicem claudant corda sua, et quibus fieri solet ut alter alterum nesciat supportare, aut dum non supportandum est, ipsum nesciat nec velit corripere; sed magis velit omnino dividipropter illam agitationem illius spiritus divisionis.
units.en: On the day of Saint John the Evangelist I said Mass for certain spiritual necessities, and against certain colds of the malignant spirits, who frequently so dispose me towards certain neighbours, and them towards me, that we know not how to bear with one another, nor to correct one another. I found in this a good measure of devotion, and great hope against the vexations of the demons — those vexations, I mean, by which it comes about that men close their hearts to one another, and by which it commonly happens that one knows not how to bear with another, or, when he ought not to bear, knows not how, and will not, correct him; but rather wishes to be altogether divided, through that agitation of the spirit of division.

units.la: Hic rogabam ex animo Angelos hominum custodes, et omnes alios, ut cum Ghristo dignarentur nobis nasci; et ita de sanctis Dei hominibus, ae mulieribus, aut animabus in caelo regnantibus; idem -octabam quoque de his qui sunt in hac vita, ut pote quod et ipsorum quilibet suae et omnium proximorum saluti nasceretur, hoc est, nunc inciperet ex animo se totum ordinare et referre in utilitatem omnium proximorum, spiritualem primo; deinde: et corporalem.
units.en: Here I begged from my heart the guardian Angels of men, and all the others, that with Christ they would deign to be born for us; and so of the holy men and women of God, and the souls reigning in heaven; and I wished the same of those who are in this life: namely, that each of them might be born for his own salvation and that of all his neighbours — that is, might now begin from his heart to order and refer his whole self to the profit of all his neighbours, spiritual first, and then bodily too.

units.la: In missa dum legerem verbade: dilectione Jesu erga Joannem, sensi magnum quoddam desiderium reamandi et honorandi: ipsum Joannem, intelligens in'hoc fieri rem gratam ipsi Domino, quem qui vult amare, debet omnia quae ipse amat. amare; ante: omnia autem salu- tem et spiritualem vitam, ac consolationem et refectiohem animarum, id est, ovium ipsius et agnorum, juxta commendationem quam fecit Pètro, ad quem tertio replicaverat: Diligis His diebus natalitiorum, hoc unum bonum in quamdam spiritualem nativitatem meam videor mihi consecutus, ut videlicet nova quadam curà cupiam quaerere signa amoris Dei et Christi, ac rerum suarum, quibus fiat ut deinceps magis cogitem, magis desiderem, libentius loquar et operer ea quae Dei sunt. Hactenus ego maxime anxius eram circa ea sensa quibus significatio sumi potest:de eo quod est amari a Deo et a sanctis ejus; maxime enim volebam intelligere quomodo se haberent erga me, et hoc est non malum, imo primum quod occurrit ad Deum pergentibus, aut (ut melius dicam) Deum sibi conciliantibus. Nec enim statim ab initio, et multo minus ante initium conversionis nostrae, supponendum est, aut certa fide (ut quidam male opinantur) assumendum, ipsum Deum et Christum ejus oninemque coelestem illum coetum nobis esse placatissimum, €x maxime irato; sed nec quando placatus est quantum ad minas aeternarum paenarum, tenendum est quod ideo nihil aliorum laborum paenitentiae nobis minetur; quum dixerit de Paulo electo in vas electionis: Ostendam illi quanta oporteat eum pro nomine meo pati. Solemus igitur, non 'male procedendo in principiis nostris bene vivendi, esse maxime solliciti, ut placeamus Deo in nobis ipsis praeparando habitaculum corporale et spirituale, in corpore nostro et in spiritu nostro. Est tamen certum tempus (quod per seipsam sola unctio Spiritus Sancti unumquemque recte proficientem docet) in quo jam nobis detur, et a nobis requiratur, ut nos jam principaliter studeamus amare ipsum, hoc est, ut non jam quaeramus quomodo se habeat in se et in caeteris rebus, quidque ipsi absolute placeat ac displiceat in rebus suis. Illud primum dictum erat trahere Deum ad nos; hoc vero est nos ipsos trahere ad Deum. In priore quaerimus ut ipse meminerit et sit totus sollicitus nostri; in secundo autem quaerimus meminisse ejus et esse toti solliciti eorum quaecumque ipsi placent; in primo est via ut perficiatur in nobis timor ac reve- rentia filialis; in hoc secundo progressu est via perfectionis et charitatis. Det igitur mihi Dominus, et omnibus, duos pedes, quibus innitendum est ambulando hanc scalam viae Dei, idest, verus timor et verus amor. Hactenus quidem mihi videtur timor fuisse dexter pes, et amor sinister. Nunc jam cupio ut amor sit dexter atque principalis, et timor sinister ac minus principalis fiat. Et utinam adhuc nunc sim natus, et in hoc crescam in virum perfectum!
units.en: At Mass, while I read the words about the love of Jesus towards John, I felt a certain great desire of loving in return and honouring John himself, understanding that in this a thing is done pleasing to the Lord; for he who would love him must love all that he loves — before all, the salvation and spiritual life, the consolation and refreshment of souls, that is, of his sheep and his lambs, according to the charge he gave to Peter, to whom he had said the third time: Lovest thou me? In these days of the Nativity I seem to have obtained this one good, towards a certain spiritual birth of my own: namely, that with a certain new care I desire to seek the signs of the love of God and of Christ and of the things that are theirs — whereby it may come about that henceforth I think more, desire more, more gladly speak and work the things that are God's. Hitherto I was most anxious about those feelings from which an indication may be taken of what it is to be loved by God and by his saints; for above all I wished to understand how they stood towards me — and this is not evil; nay, it is the first thing that occurs to those who are going towards God, or (to speak better) who are winning God to themselves. For it is not to be supposed at once from the beginning — much less before the beginning of our conversion — nor to be assumed with certain faith (as some wrongly opine) that God himself and his Christ and all that heavenly company are most appeased towards us, when he is most angered; nor, when he is appeased as regards the threats of eternal pains, is it to be held that he therefore threatens us with none of the other labours of penance; since he said of Paul, chosen as a vessel of election: I will show him how much he must suffer for my name. We are wont, then — not proceeding badly in the beginnings of our living well — to be most solicitous to please God by preparing in ourselves a bodily and spiritual dwelling, in our body and in our spirit. Yet there is a certain time (which the anointing of the Holy Spirit alone, of itself, teaches everyone who makes right progress) in which it is now given us, and required of us, that we now study principally to love him — that is, that we no longer ask how he stands in himself and in other things, and what absolutely pleases and displeases him in his own affairs. That first way was to draw God to us; but this is to draw ourselves to God. In the former we seek that he may remember us and be wholly solicitous for us; in the second we seek to remember him and to be wholly solicitous for whatever pleases him. In the first is the way by which filial fear and reverence are perfected in us; in this second progress is the way of perfection and of charity. May the Lord then give me, and all, the two feet on which we must lean in climbing this ladder of the way of God: that is, true fear and true love. Hitherto, indeed, fear seems to me to have been my right foot, and love the left. Now I desire that love be the right and principal one, and fear become the left and less principal. And would that even now I may be born, and grow in this into a perfect man!

units.la: In die Qircumasionis Domini Nostri Jesu Christi et in primis vesperis ejus, in ecclesia, majore Aschafemburgi, inveni magnam devotionem ex auditu vesperarum et ex visu ornatus hujus templi; adfuerunt multa desideria circa innovationem anni, et pro me in particulari, et pro universo in variis gentibus, in pace scilicet, in firmitate et restitutione fidei catholice ac divini cultus.
units.en: On the day of the Circumcision of Our Lord Jesus Christ, and at its first vespers, in the great church of Aschaffenburg, I found great devotion from hearing the vespers and from seeing the adornment of that church; many desires were present concerning the renewal of the year, both for myself in particular and for the whole world among the various nations — namely for peace, for the strengthening and restoration of the catholic faith and of divine worship.

units.la: Mane in missa, ego sensi in vivo quodam spiritu bono, quam bonum sit et quam pacificum probari soli Deo, èt videri ab ipso solo, quin aliud boninobis detur.!
units.en: In the morning at Mass I felt, in a certain lively good spirit, how good and how peaceful a thing it is to be approved by God alone, and to be seen by him alone, even should no other good be given us.

units.la: Notavi et illud, Christum non ante voluisse in. facie Ecclesiae Judaeorum habere nomen suum, JESUS, quam effunderet sanguinem. Proinde F: igitur videbatur maxime rogandus ut det nobis gratiam qua fiat, ut sic circumcidatur quidquid in nobis ad perfectum fructum non facit, ut nomen aliquod bonum sub Christo habere mereamur. Nullum autem nomen in hac vita nobis quaeramus quod non sit sub nomine Jesy, id est, Salvatoris. Qui enim quaerit nomen patris, non in ratione salutis filiorum, ille non recte procedit; sic de magistro, sic de pastore, sic de domino, sic de episcopo, sic de procuratore, sic de rege, duce, imperatore, et reliquis nominibus, quae omnia rationem suam habent sub ratione Jesu comprehensam.
units.en: I noted also this: that Christ would not have his name JESUS before the face of the Church of the Jews until he had shed blood. Therefore it seemed that he was above all to be begged to give us the grace by which whatever in us does not make for perfect fruit may be so circumcised that we may deserve to have some good name under Christ. And let us seek for ourselves no name in this life which is not under the name of Jesus, that is, of the Saviour. For he who seeks the name of father, but not for the sake of the salvation of the children, does not proceed rightly; so of master, so of pastor, so of lord, so of bishop, so of procurator, so of king, duke, emperor, and the other names — all of which have their meaning comprehended under the meaning of Jesus.

units.la: Desiderio quodam bono hic desideravi ut in anima mea hoc anno spiritualiter fiant quatuor tempora; id est, primo spiritualis hyems, ad hoc ut divina semina terrae animae meae demandata foveantur, radicesque capere possint; secundo ver spirituale, ad hoc ut terra mea germinare bene possit fructum suum; tertio aestas spiritualis, ut fructus maturescere possint in optimam messem; quarto autumnus spiritualis, ut fructus maturi colligi possint, et in horreis divinis congregati atque servati non pereant.
units.en: With a certain good desire I here desired that in my soul this year there might spiritually come the four seasons: that is, first a spiritual winter, that the divine seeds committed to the earth of my soul might be cherished and take root; second a spiritual spring, that my earth might well bring forth its fruit; third a spiritual summer, that the fruits might ripen into an excellent harvest; fourth a spiritual autumn, that the ripe fruits might be gathered, and, stored and kept in the divine granaries, might not perish.

units.la: Optavi etiam ut per gratiam Domini Nostri Jesu Christi circumcisi in carne sua, et tandem in eadem mortui, in signaculum pacti obedientialis ad Deum Patrêm, mihi concederetur vera aliqua circumcisio spiritus, ut esset per Spiritum Sanctum in signum et in arrham praecipue dilectionis meae erga Christum et ejus erga me.
units.en: I wished also that through the grace of Our Lord Jesus Christ, circumcised in his flesh and at last dead in the same, as the seal of the covenant of obedience to God the Father, there might be granted me some true circumcision of the spirit, that it might be, through the Holy Spirit, a sign and pledge above all of my love towards Christ and of his towards me.

units.la: In vesperis, dum oculis aspicerem modestiam depictam in una imagine virginis Mariae, ego sensi aliquo modo quantum valeat illa gratia Dei, qua fit ut quis totus in hoc sit, ut placeat soli Deo, et teneat ac retineat in se omnem gratiam suam, quasi qui nescit per sul apertam et explicatam communicationem trahere quem- uam mortalium ad se amandum, aut de se cogitandum, etc. Sic igitur omnis pulchritudo Mariae ab intus erat et intus Deo abscondebatur.
units.en: At vespers, while I looked with my eyes on the modesty painted in an image of the Virgin Mary, I felt in some measure how much that grace of God avails by which one is wholly bent on pleasing God alone, and keeps and retains in himself all his grace — like one who does not know how, by an open and displayed communication of himself, to draw any mortal to love him or think of him, and so forth. Thus all the beauty of Mary was from within, and within was hidden for God.

units.la: In die octavae sancti Stephani, ego celebravi missam in capella R"! Domini Moguntini, quae propter me' fuit ornata solemniter omnibus reliquiis eț thesauris suis. In die vero sequenti quae fuit octava sancti Joannis Evangelistae, ego cele- þravi in altera capella, quae est in sede ejus- dem R=, in majore Ecclesia, quae erat ipsa solem- = niter ornata. In his ergo locìs et his modis orna- tis cum accessi ad altare, ego parvam ad modum devotionem intra meipsum inveni; quin potius totus aridus intravi ad altare, et ibi permansı, et exivi; unde factum est per gratiam Jesu Christi crucifixi, ut totus hic refriguerim circaomnem appetitum quaerendi mihi tot et tantas causas externas ad devotionem et ad melius inveniendum Christum crucifixum.
units.en: On the day of the octave of Saint Stephen I celebrated Mass in the chapel of the Most Reverend Lord of Mainz, which for my sake had been solemnly adorned with all its relics and treasures. And on the following day, which was the octave of Saint John the Evangelist, I celebrated in another chapel, which is at the seat of the same Most Reverend in the greater church, and which was itself solemnly adorned. In these places, then, and adorned in these ways, when I came to the altar I found very little devotion within myself; rather I entered the altar wholly dry, and so remained, and so went out; whence it came about, by the grace of Jesus Christ crucified, that I here grew wholly cold towards every appetite of seeking for myself so many and so great outward causes of devotion and of better finding Christ crucified.

units.la: Frequenter enim fit, sicut hic mihi accidit, ut dum quis invenit gratiam maximam apud homines, ille.sit magis destitutus interius apud Christum et Spiritum ejus. Hic ego sensi quam- = dam in animo meo fugam humanorum favorum et gratiae ejus quae est apud summos, videns quam sit efficacius medium ad habendam gratiam Dei, si quis destituatur, et fiat crucifixo propinquissimus. Humanus igitur favor omnis, si quis quaerendus est vel acceptandus offertur, ad proximorum aedificationem referendus aut intendendus est, non autem ad seipsum; cum absque omni favore melius inveniri possit Jesus animarum nostrarum. Tendendum igitur semper est et declinandum animo in eam partem viae f quae est versus crucem. Christus enim crucifixus vera via est ad gloriam animae nostrae et corporis, nec solum via, sed et veritas et vita. Tu igitur, quando tibi studebis, et tuam ipsius aedificationem aut veram consolationem quaesieris, sive proprium profectum, vide ut semper renitaris humanae gratiae et favoribus hominum ad inferiora te extendens, id est, ad ea quae sunt crucis.
units.en: For it frequently happens, as befell me here, that when one finds the greatest favour among men, he is the more destitute inwardly with Christ and his Spirit. Here I felt in my soul a certain flight from human favours and from the grace which is with the great, seeing how much more efficacious a means it is for having the grace of God, if one be left destitute and become nearest to the crucified. All human favour, then, if any is to be sought, or is offered to be accepted, must be referred and directed to the edification of our neighbours, not to oneself; since without any favour Jesus, the Jesus of our souls, can be better found. We must always tend, then, and incline in mind towards that side of the way which is towards the cross. For Christ crucified is the true way to the glory of our soul and body — and not only the way, but also the truth and the life. You, therefore, when you attend to yourself and seek your own edification or true consolation, or your own progress, see that you always resist human favour and the favours of men, stretching yourself towards the lower things, that is, towards the things of the cross.

units.la: Alius erit qui usque ad, certum gradum, per aeternam pulchritudinem, potentiam, ac bonitatem, quae sibi offertur, melius proficiet in gratiarum actionibus et melius forte movebitur ad glorificandum Deum omnipotentem et omnibus modis infinitum. Oportet tamen tändem si non fiat ab initio ut veniamus ad crucem eam, in qua pependit salus nostra. In Christo enim crucifixo est salus nostra, nostra vita, et nostra resurrectio. Haec autem tria ordine quodam praecedunt gloriam nostram, quae in celis nos exspectat; quae et ipsa est per eumdem, et ex eodem, et in eodem Christo glorificato. Quaerenda est itaque primo virtus Christi crucifixi, et postea virtus Christi gloriosi, et non e contrario. Virtus illi in eo fuit quod ipse voluerit spontanee mori, et pati quaecumque voluerunt inimici ejus; qua virtute destructa est mors nostra, quae maxime statuebatur, et statuitur, ac quodam modo aedificatur per timorem passionum et moriendi. Ipse solvit, destruxit, et quasi ad nihilum redegit mortem, qui solus sponte corpus assumpsit pro nobis, et ipsum pro nobis passionibus mortique obtulit deponendum. Sic nos eadem cogitatione atque voluntate armare debemus; id est, ut nos sponte propter ipsum passionibus et morti offeramus ad destitutionem corporis peccati, ut tandem inveniamus corpus gratiae et gloriae Dei, in Christo Jesu Domino Nostro, in* quo oportet ut inveniatur esse nostri spiritus, et suum vivere, et suum movere, ete.
units.en: There will be another who, up to a certain degree, will profit better in thanksgivings through the eternal beauty, power and goodness offered to him, and will perhaps be better moved to glorify God almighty and in every way infinite. Yet at last, if it is not done from the beginning, we must come to that cross on which our salvation hung. For in Christ crucified is our salvation, our life, and our resurrection. And these three in a certain order go before our glory, which awaits us in heaven; and that glory itself is through the same, and from the same, and in the same Christ glorified. First, then, is to be sought the virtue of Christ crucified, and afterwards the virtue of Christ glorious, and not contrariwise. His virtue lay in this, that he willed of his own accord to die, and to suffer whatever his enemies willed; by which virtue our death was destroyed — the death which was chiefly set up, and is set up, and in a manner built, by the fear of sufferings and of dying. He loosed, destroyed, and as it were brought to nothing death, who alone of his own will took a body for us, and offered it for us to sufferings and to death, to be laid down. So ought we to arm ourselves with the same thought and will: that is, to offer ourselves willingly, for his sake, to sufferings and death, for the stripping off of the body of sin, that at last we may find the body of the grace and glory of God, in Christ Jesus Our Lord; in whom the being of our spirit must be found, and its living, and its moving, and the rest.

units.la: In die Epiphaniae, quod est festum Regum, ego sensi magnas consolationes spirituales: et primo in solito discursu litaniarum mearum, dum omnia traherem ad hoc ut omnes sancti dignarentur adorare nomine meo Deum omnipotentem, et Christum ejus Jesum Dominum Nostrum. Hic ex bono animo 'optavi ut omnes externae corporis mei, et caeterorum moltiones, quae in Deum intuentur, acceptae semper sint ipsi Deo, etiam si cor ipsum et spiritus ipse a carne magis liber quandoque nesciatassurgere sursum.
units.en: On the day of the Epiphany, which is the feast of the Kings, I felt great spiritual consolations: and first in the accustomed round of my litanies, while I drew everything to this, that all the saints would deign to adore in my name God almighty, and his Christ, Jesus Our Lord. Here from a good heart I wished that all the outward motions of my body, and of the rest, which look towards God, might always be accepted by God himself, even if the heart itself, and the spirit that is freer than the flesh, sometimes knows not how to rise upward.

units.la: Hic sensi quamdam compassionem circa vituperia Jesu Ghristi Domini Nostri, quae passus est invita sia usque ad mortem, tam in contrarium ejus quod recepit a tribus Magis.
units.en: Here I felt a certain compassion over the revilings of Jesus Christ Our Lord, which he suffered in his life even to death — so contrary to what he received from the three Magi.

units.la: Hic ego habui desiderium quoddam ut mihi concederetur gratia, qua fieret me nunquam gaudere nisi in Deo aut in proximo; et nunquam tristem esse ob incommoda mea temporalia, sed solum in his quae sunt proximorum et ad Deum ipsum.
units.en: Here I had a certain desire that the grace might be granted me by which it would come about that I should never rejoice except in God or in my neighbour; and never be sad for my own temporal discomforts, but only in those things which concern my neighbours and God himself.

units.la: Hic ego sensi quasdam optimas aestimationes et ponderationes bonorum operum variarum personarum, quae circa me, vel circa alios, vel circa Deum laborando quovis modo occupantur.
units.en: Here I felt certain excellent estimations and weighings of the good works of the various persons who, in any way whatever, are occupied in labouring for me, or for others, or for God.

units.la: Magnum quoque desiderium, dum essem in missa quae cantabatur in altari trium Regum, sensi; quod erat ut daretur mihi gratia relinquendi post me varias memorias, etiam externas, Dei et Sanctorum ejus; quod si debeat perire haec memoria in his partibus, égo prius desinam esse in memoria vivorum etin hoc mundo! Quid enim mihi esset. in terra (mihi videbatur) si mihi non sit memoria Dei mei ac Sanctorum ejus? Haec veniebant per occasionem imaginum sanctorum et picturarum variarum externarum Christi mysteriorum, quibus variae rerum sanctarum memoriae et intelligentie mihi et tunc et alias semper subministrari solent. In mèpropter haec crescebat amor et veneratio R= domini Alberti Archiepiscopi et principis Moguntini, qui tantam curam in omni vita sua habuerit et habet circa reliquias sanctorum, et circa ipsorum memoriam conservandam et in posteros relinquendam; quae exterior memoria tanto magis est necessaria, quanto magis homines eam parvi pendunt et sunt frigidi. Tunc enim, nisi imagines et caetera quae divinarum rerum et personarum habent specimen ac figuras, essent in maximo ornatu, facile esset ut homines omnia spernerent. Quomodo enim non contemnerentur omnia sacra, si absque dignitate et decore tractarentur, quum quasi ex toto spernantur, dum sunt maximo cum ornamento administrata?
units.en: I felt also a great desire, while I was at the Mass which was sung at the altar of the three Kings: it was that the grace might be given me of leaving behind me various memorials, even outward ones, of God and his Saints; and if this memory must perish in these parts, may I first cease to be in the memory of the living and in this world! For what would there be for me on earth (so it seemed to me), if I should not have the memory of my God and of his Saints? These things came by occasion of the images of the saints and the various outward pictures of the mysteries of Christ, by which various memories and understandings of holy things are wont to be supplied to me, both then and always. In me, on this account, there grew love and veneration for the Most Reverend Lord Albert, Archbishop and prince of Mainz, who all his life has taken, and takes, such care for the relics of the saints, and for preserving their memory and leaving it to posterity; which outward memory is the more necessary, the more men make little of it and are cold. For then, unless the images, and the other things which bear the likeness and figures of divine things and persons, were kept in the greatest adornment, it would easily come about that men would despise everything. For how would all sacred things not be despised, if they were treated without dignity and beauty, seeing that they are almost wholly despised even when administered with the greatest ornament?

units.la: Īn missa, ego sensi magnum desiderium ut Alvarus Alphonsus, qui est Coloniae, posset habere specialem memoriam supplendi. vices meas apud corpora trium Regum quae ibi servantur; et non solum ut vices meas suppleret, sed etiam omnium sociorum meorum. Idem quoque sentiebam et desiderabam ut facerent reliqui omnes qui sunt in aliquibus locis, ubi coluntur Sancti qui apud nos habentur in tanta veneratione.
units.en: At Mass I felt a great desire that Álvaro Alfonso, who is at Cologne, might keep a special remembrance of supplying my place before the bodies of the three Kings which are preserved there; and not only my place, but that of all my companions. The same I felt and desired that all the others might do who are in places where those Saints are venerated who are held among us in such honour.

units.la: In dominica infra cctavam Epiphaniae, ego applicui missam, inter caetera, ut esset sacrificium et oblatio in gratiarum actiones quas ego debeo,- et nunquam satis habui, nec possem sufficienter agere pro variis donis fidei et humilitatis spiritus, mihi sicut et aliis catholicis infusis, non solum ad propriam petitionem, sed ad postulationes Ecclesiae et ex fide ejus.
units.en: On the Sunday within the octave of the Epiphany I applied the Mass, among other things, that it might be a sacrifice and oblation towards the thanksgivings which I owe — and have never adequately made, nor could sufficiently make — for the various gifts of faith and humility of spirit poured into me, as into other catholics, not only at my own petition, but at the petitions of the Church and out of her faith.

units.la: Hic notavi et sentiebam quo pacto illi qui recedunt ab Ecclesia, primo incipiunt tepescere in operibus et exercitiis quae sunt secundum Dei gratias et differentes ejus devotiones, et ex. consequenti parvi facere et nihili aestimare quae- cumque ipsi non. deprehendunt se acquisivisse ex proprio judicio. Sic fit ut incipiant quaerere rationes fidei suae et spei, adducendo omnia in dubium; et hoc modo effundunt infusiones Spiritus Sancti, et amittunt veram fidem, quae nitebatur fidei catholicae et communioni Sanctorum. His vero effusis, ipsi incipiunt velle statuere et quaerere fidem suam propriam ex judicio proprio: quaerunt enim rationes, et illas examinant, unusquisque per seipsum; quaerunt et Scripturas, et earum interpretationes, et judicant sensus; sicque colligunt fidem suam, aut potius opiniones et errores. Dum autem volunt trahere quemquam ad suos errores, hoc primum quaerunt ex ipso tanquam principium ac suppositionem, ut scilicet ille deponat omnem passionem; sic enim vocant adhaesionem qua quis inhaeret firmiter, et ut decet verum catholicum christianum, Ecclesiae sententiis ac placitis, et doctorum Ecclesiae auctoritati. Quid est autem hominem, ad modum eorum, deponere illam passionem, nisi effundere et propria sponte amittere fidem catholicam, et simplicitatem et humilitatem intellectus captivati in obsequium fidei? Ex hac sancta et necessaria captivitate dum eduxerunt hominem, aoaaa d a a a tunc petunt ut communiter quaeratur fides per Scripturas et per rationes, nullo adhibito judice praeter proprium uniuscujusque arbitrium. Dum quis autem hoc modo quaerendo deprehendit se, vel jam perdidisse, vel sensim perdere fidem quam habuerat, tunc ipsi dicunt quaerendam esse a Deo fidem, et quaerendum judicium ad bene judicandum per se ipsum de Scripturis et caeteris; fidem enim esse Dei, et non omnium esse fidem, et similia, quae verissima quidem sunt, sed quae in hanc partem, aut inhunc locum ad Aeaedificationem non ideo veniunt. Hic enim conveniebat potius cognovisse haec dona posse ab unoquoque perdi et amitti. Qui igitur sua sponte amisit fidem, quam habuerat quandiu erat juratus in verba et in sensus Ecclesiae catholicae, nec abjuraverat catholicos doctores, is mirari non debet, dum videt se aliis viis, quae sunt secundum proprium judicium, quaerere fidem et non invenire; nec debet causare Deum nolle sibi dare; vult enim dare fidem uniculque, sed non extra Ecclesiam vivere volenti, ubi non est salus, neque vita, neque vera resur- rectio: Multiplices sensus et varia dona gratiarum habet quilibet fidelis Ecclesiae catholice christianus; quorum omnium singulorum rationes, et Scripturas aut verba sacra quibus innituntur, si per se quaereret, et quaerendo per se judicare vellet, varia detrimenta pateretur. Eva magnum donum gratiae ad credendum verbo praecepti Dei, per verbum Adamisibi facto, acceperat; sed statim audita cum attentione quaestione serpentis, qua quaerebatur cur praecepisset Deus, etc., dum, inquam, ipsa quaerit rationes ad respondendum ei qui nec aedificari nee aedificare poterat, sicut sunt plerique haeretici, ipsa donum fidei perdidit; quo effuso, facile fuit eam decipi, et persuaderi ut faceret id quod fecit. Sic ergo illa quae absque ratione, sed ex infusione gratiae, in verbo Adami, acceperat fidem quod quacumque hora comedisset esset moritura, in ratiocinationibus et in proprio judicio accepit errorem illum, qui erat ut per esum ejusdem pomi esset as- secutura conditiones Deorum immortalium, et scientiam boni et mali. Recognoscenda sunt igi- tur, cum multis gratiarum actionibus, ea dona quae habemus et accepimus ex Dei gratia, absque proprio judicio, et nobis etiam non petentibus aut intelligentibus, sicut factum est in baptismo, in fide Ecclesiae et parentum, infusis in nos seminibus catholicae et orthodoxae fidei, spei, et charitatis, reliquarumque virtutum; et item in aliis sacramentis, in quibus omnibus dantur gratiae non juxta mensuram captus nostri, nec secundum intellectum et sensum quem habemus de forma et materia ipsorum sacramentorum, sed supra quam petimus, et etiam sciamus Cogitare vel desiderare. Dum quis te interrogabit, qui nec te aedificare potest aut paratus est, nec a te aedificari potest aut vult, cum eo ne sermonem misceas, sed evita.aut declina eum ut serpentem. et scorpionem; noli respondere ad ejus interrogata: quia si bene responderis, ille non aedificabitur; sin autem male, ille non te docebit vel erudiet.
units.en: Here I noted and felt how those who withdraw from the Church first begin to grow lukewarm in the works and exercises which follow the graces of God and his different devotions, and consequently to make little of, and count as nothing, whatever they do not find themselves to have acquired by their own judgment. So it comes that they begin to seek the reasons of their faith and hope, calling everything into doubt; and in this way they pour away the infusions of the Holy Spirit, and lose the true faith which rested on the catholic faith and the communion of Saints. And when these have been poured away, they begin to want to establish and seek a faith of their own out of their own judgment: they seek reasons, and examine them, each for himself; they seek the Scriptures too, and their interpretations, and judge the meanings; and so they gather their faith — or rather their opinions and errors. And when they wish to draw anyone to their errors, this is the first thing they ask of him, as a principle and presupposition: namely, that he lay aside all passion — for so they call the adherence by which one cleaves firmly, as befits a true catholic christian, to the judgments and decisions of the Church and to the authority of the doctors of the Church. But what is it for a man, after their fashion, to lay aside that passion, except to pour away and of his own accord lose the catholic faith, and the simplicity and humility of an intellect made captive in the obedience of faith? When they have led a man out of this holy and necessary captivity, then they ask that faith be sought in common through the Scriptures and through reasons, with no judge admitted except each man's own judgment. And when one, seeking in this way, finds that he has either already lost, or is little by little losing, the faith he had, then they say that faith must be sought from God, and that judgment must be sought to judge well for oneself of the Scriptures and the rest; for faith is of God, and not all men have faith, and the like — things which are indeed most true, but which do not on that account belong in this place or serve here for edification. For here it would rather have been fitting to recognize that these gifts can be lost and forfeited by anyone. He therefore who of his own accord has lost the faith he had, so long as he was sworn to the words and meanings of the catholic Church and had not abjured the catholic doctors, ought not to wonder when he sees himself seeking faith by other ways, according to his own judgment, and not finding it; nor should he plead that God will not give it to him; for God wills to give faith to everyone, but not to one who wills to live outside the Church, where there is no salvation, nor life, nor true resurrection. Every faithful christian of the catholic Church has manifold perceptions and various gifts of graces; and if he were to seek by himself the reasons of each one of them, and the Scriptures or sacred words on which they rest, and in seeking wished to judge by himself, he would suffer various harms. Eve had received a great gift of grace for believing the word of God's command, through the word of Adam spoken to her; but as soon as she listened with attention to the serpent's question, in which it was asked why God had commanded, and so on — when, I say, she sought reasons to answer one who could neither be edified nor edify (as is the case with most heretics) — she lost the gift of faith; and when that was poured away, it was easy for her to be deceived, and persuaded to do what she did. Thus she who, without reasoning, but by the infusion of grace, had received on Adam's word the faith that in whatever hour she ate she would die, received in reasonings and in her own judgment that error, which was that by eating of that same apple she would attain the condition of the immortal gods, and the knowledge of good and evil. We must therefore acknowledge, with many thanksgivings, those gifts which we have and have received from the grace of God, without our own judgment, and even without our asking or understanding — as was done in baptism, in the faith of the Church and of our parents, when the seeds of catholic and orthodox faith, hope and charity, and of the other virtues, were poured into us; and likewise in the other sacraments, in all of which graces are given not according to the measure of our grasp, nor according to the understanding and sense we have of the form and matter of the sacraments themselves, but beyond what we ask, or even know how to think or desire. When one questions you who neither can nor is ready to edify you, nor can nor will be edified by you, do not join speech with him, but avoid him, or turn from him as from a serpent and a scorpion; do not answer his questions: for if you answer well, he will not be edified; and if badly, he will not teach or instruct you.

units.la: Eodem die, dum essem in missa, tenens pretiosissimum corpus Domini, ego habui quamdam vivam apprehensionem de eo quod est assistere sacramento veritatis, et sacro signo in se continenti omnem veritatem et omnem bonitatem; ad quod sacramentum non oportet accedere, nisi post multam sui purgationem et examinationem, Qui enim accedit sine reconciliatione prius facta apud eum qui est vicarius Christi in foro paenitentiae, ille inveniet judicium in manducatione et. potu salutaris cibi. Sume similitudinem de eo cui factum est mandatum nomine principis terreni, ut debeat exulare propter peccatum aliquod, ex quo incurrit iram principis: is enim, si contempto eo praecepto, et nolens curare illud ac fugere donec sit reconciliatus, praesumit insuper addere ad superbiam suam ut velit venire ad conspectum principis, clarum est quod judicium suum accipiet, si irreconciliatus accedat, et absque retractatione et impetratione veniae praecedentis criminis; quod quidem crimen tanquam malum, ac multis modisnon ferendum, princeps illè nolebat esse coram se, sed ejici; ille vero superbus magis ac magis satagit, dum propius accedit, ut peccatum suum et faetor ille versetur ob oculos principis. Sic est qui oneratus peccatorum suorum faeoetoribus, propter quae exulaverat a gratia Dei, ipse se offert irreconciliatus conspectui Jesu Christi quem sumit. Hoc est perinde ac si cui dictum sit: Aufer rem talem faetentem ab oculis meis ne videam; et illam a A T E E obtrudat ita ut non tantum debeat videri, sed etiam osculo tangi. Hic virtualiter dicit: Sciot te non posse ferre visum mei, sed ego volo ut me osculeris; scio, mi Domine, te non posse stare ante conspectum externorum meorum, sed volo ego te etiam in interiora mea, unde est faetor et immundities, introducere.
units.en: On the same day, while I was at Mass, holding the most precious body of the Lord, I had a certain lively apprehension of what it is to stand before the sacrament of truth, the sacred sign containing in itself all truth and all goodness; to which sacrament one ought not to approach except after much purgation and examination of oneself. For he who approaches without reconciliation first made with him who is the vicar of Christ in the tribunal of penance, will find judgment in the eating and drinking of the saving food. Take a comparison from one to whom command has been given in the name of an earthly prince that he must go into exile because of some sin by which he incurred the prince's anger: if he, despising that command, and refusing to heed it and to flee until he be reconciled, presumes besides to add to his pride by wishing to come into the prince's sight, it is clear that he will receive his judgment if he approaches unreconciled, without retraction and without having begged pardon for his preceding crime — a crime which the prince, as an evil not to be borne in many ways, would not have before him, but cast out; while that proud man, the nearer he approaches, strives more and more that his sin and its stench be set before the prince's eyes. Such is he who, loaded with the stenches of his sins, for which he had been exiled from the grace of God, offers himself unreconciled to the sight of Jesus Christ whom he receives. It is as if one were told: Take that stinking thing away from my eyes, that I may not see it — and he should thrust it forward, so that it must not only be seen but even touched with a kiss. Such a man virtually says: I know that you cannot bear the sight of me, but I will have you kiss me; I know, my Lord, that you cannot stand before the sight of my outward parts, but I will bring you even into my inward parts, whence come the stench and the uncleanness.

units.la: Tertia die infra octavas Epiphaniae Domini, venit in memoriam quidam discursus quem prius acceperam, circa processum earum gratiarum quas jampridem intellexi esse quaerendas et petendas, juxta ordinem mearum litaniarum; hoc autem fuit per comparationem quamdam sumptam ex quopiam, qui debet esse aulicus servus apud maximum aliquem principem, cujus aliquae bonae conditiones hoc ordine possent annotari Quidem et ante omnia ut possit, sciat, 6t velit servire; juxta quae tria, sumi possunt ea tria quae petimus ex -Trinitate personarum divi- narum; ut videlicet possimus, sciamus, et velimus servire Jesu Christo Domino Nostro. 2 Is futurus servus opus 'habet gratia, alioquin enim ineptus deprehendetur; ipsa autem gratia maxime notatur et exprimitur ex virtute humilitatis; et juxta hoc rogamus beatam virginem Mariam, ut ipsa quae est tota et semper fuit gratiosa, impetret ipsam pro nobis, ut placere possint omnia servitia nostra Deo et Sanctis ipsius. 3° Requirilur ut talis servus sit diligens, et ad ministrandum aptus; et juxta conditionem hanc desiderabimus, ut angeli, qui sunt spiritus admınistratorii, nobis impetrent hanc aptitudiņpem et sedulitatem in serviendo. 4° Oportet ut is servus sit amator honestatis et omnis ornatus, ne quid occurrat Domino. transeunti quod oculos ejus offendat; in timore itaque semper erit, et in desiderio ut omnia sint decentia et bene praeparata; et juxta hanc similitudinem, petemus intercessionem patriarcharum et prophetarum, ut parare possimus omnes vias Domini tanquam boni praecursores Christi. 5° Oportet illum servum promptum esse; ut sequatur curiam quocumque ierit. Nos igitur juxta formam apostolorum, quaeremus gratiam sequendi Dominum Nostrum secundum ejus beneplacitum. 6° conditio servi aulici est ut sit attentissimus:ad singula verba Domini sui; juxta quod petemus intercessionem discipu- lorum ut esse possimus vere discipuli Ghristi, attentique ipsius et sanctorum omnium auditores. 7conditio in eo est ut talis servus semper caveat ne quem ex omnibus qui in aula vivunt offendat; quin potius. omnibus modis studeat esse utilis, nulli autem nocuus, ut nemo unquam de ipso queri possit apud Dominum: juxta quod quaeremus gratiam sanctorum Innocentium, ut nunquam quemquam laedamus, aut scandalisemus, aut infirmemus. 8° conditio est ut servus sit paratus pati, etiam usque ad mortem, pro honore, et pro rebus, et pro omni justa defensione atque salute Domini sui. Juxta hoc invocabimus martyres, ut nobis impetrent virtutem patientiae; id est, ut esse possimus prompti ad subeundas tribulationes quascumque pro Domino Nostro Jesu Christo, pro honore scilicet ejus et ipsius voluntate facienda. talis servus fuġiat diligenter et evitet omnes Tetun O OUNTE a aaa ' voluptates ac recreationes, loca, conversationes, et caetera omnia quae ipsi impedimento esse possent ad recte faciendam voluntatem Domini sui; et secundum hanc formam sumemus invocationem sanctorum monachorum et eremitarum, qui se abdicarunt ab omnibus placitis suis, ut voluntatem Domini sui sibi ostensam possent adimplere. 14> est ut ejusmodi servus studeat omnibus modis esse mundus in se et ornatus, ita ut possit amari a Domino suo; juxta hoc invocabimus auxilium Virginum sacrarum quae soli Christo sponso suo placere omnibus modis studuerunt. 12> est ut, si quidem dilectus fuerit et in privatum Domini assumptus,* studeat fidelis esse, nec abutatur amore Domini sui, sed respondeat ei; juxta hoc invocabimus sanctas quae fuerunt fideles in matrimonio. 13* conditio est in hoc ut dum servus caret praesentia benefici sui Domini, imo eliamsi ad tempus esset ab eo separatus, nunquam alienetur ipse, nec convertatur ad alias consolationes quibus impediretur facile ne curare posset de reunione ad Dominum necessaria. Hinc accipiemus formam petitionis ultimae pro qua quaeremus auxi- lium viduarum et continentium, ut scilicet nobis impetrent hanc gratiam ne ullam (extra divinam) consolationem quaeramus; quin potius, dum non dabitur frui Domino Nostro, semper et ubique malimus lugere et maesti esse ob carentiam ejus, quam converti ad praesentiam cujuscumque alterius voluptatis, quae non sit ex ipso derivata ac missa in nos, per ipsum subministrata, et in ipso terminata. Amen.
units.en: On the third day within the octave of the Epiphany of the Lord there came to memory a certain round which I had received before, concerning the sequence of those graces which I have long understood are to be sought and asked according to the order of my litanies; and this was by a certain comparison taken from one who is to be a court servant with some very great prince, whose good qualities might be noted in this order. First and before all, that he be able, know how, and be willing to serve; and according to these three may be taken the three things we ask of the Trinity of divine persons: namely, that we may be able, know how, and be willing to serve Jesus Christ Our Lord. Second, this future servant has need of gracefulness, for otherwise he will be found unfit; and this grace is chiefly marked and expressed by the virtue of humility; and accordingly we beg the blessed Virgin Mary that she, who is wholly and always full of grace, may obtain it for us, that all our services may be able to please God and his Saints. Third, it is required that such a servant be diligent, and apt for ministering; and according to this condition we shall desire that the angels, who are ministering spirits, obtain for us this aptness and sedulity in serving. Fourth, the servant must be a lover of seemliness and of all good order, lest anything meet the Lord as he passes that offends his eyes; he will therefore always be in fear, and in the desire that all things be decent and well prepared; and after this likeness we shall ask the intercession of the patriarchs and prophets, that we may prepare all the ways of the Lord like good forerunners of Christ. Fifth, that servant must be prompt to follow the court wherever it goes. We therefore, after the pattern of the apostles, shall seek the grace of following Our Lord according to his good pleasure. The sixth condition of a court servant is that he be most attentive to every word of his Lord; according to which we shall ask the intercession of the disciples, that we may be true disciples of Christ, and attentive hearers of him and of all the saints. The seventh condition is that such a servant always beware of offending anyone of all who live at court; nay rather, that he study in every way to be useful, and harmful to none, so that no one can ever complain of him to the Lord; according to which we shall seek the grace of the holy Innocents, that we may never hurt, or scandalize, or weaken anyone. The eighth condition is that the servant be ready to suffer, even unto death, for the honour, the possessions, and every just defence and welfare of his Lord. According to this we shall invoke the martyrs, that they may obtain for us the virtue of patience: that is, that we may be prompt to undergo any tribulations whatever for Our Lord Jesus Christ — for his honour, that is, and for the doing of his will. The ninth: that such a servant diligently flee and avoid all pleasures and recreations, places, conversations, and everything else that could hinder him from rightly doing the will of his Lord; and after this pattern we shall take the invocation of the holy monks and hermits, who renounced all their own likings, that they might fulfil the will of their Lord shown to them. The tenth is that such a servant study in every way to be clean in himself and well ordered, so that he may be loved by his Lord; according to this we shall invoke the help of the holy Virgins, who studied in every way to please Christ their bridegroom alone. The eleventh is that, if he should be beloved and taken into the Lord's privacy, he study to be faithful, and not abuse the love of his Lord, but respond to it; according to this we shall invoke the holy women who were faithful in marriage. The twelfth condition is that when the servant lacks the presence of his kind Lord — nay, even if for a time he were separated from him — he never become estranged, nor turn to other consolations by which he might easily be hindered from caring for the necessary reunion with his Lord. Hence we shall take the form of the last petition, for which we shall seek the help of the widows and the continent: namely, that they obtain for us this grace, that we seek no consolation (outside the divine); but rather, while it is not given us to enjoy Our Lord, that we prefer always and everywhere to mourn and be sorrowful for the lack of him, than to turn to the presence of any other pleasure which is not derived from him and sent into us, ministered through him, and terminated in him. Amen.

units.la: Alia die infra easdem octavas Epiphaniarum harum Domini, ego sensi quemdam spiritum bonum, in quo admiratus sum gratiam Dei, qua factum est ut ego jam septem et triginta vicibus haec festa Epiphaniarum in hac vita viderem; et sic discurrebam per alios festos dies, qui mihi tot revolutis annis illuxerunt; ego vero tam parum fructus ex ipsis accepi, nec unquam fui satis gratus ut saltem recognoscerem benignitatem Dei, qua factum est ut haec bona et similia mihi toties 1n septem et triginta annis, qui jam sunt mutati, superreplicarentur, et ob oculos revolutis temporibus proponerentur, ad hauriendam inde salutem, et ut id quod neglectum fuisset in praecedentibus, resarciri posset reiteratis gratiis. Agebam igitur gratias et agnoscebam meam ingratitudinem et arŘŮ—— — — Í IESE meam incuriam, atque negligentiam et incogitantiam. Benedictus Deus qui haec dedit agnoscerê; et faciat ut ego, post haec, in omni genere sanctae agnitionis Christi manifestati, et toties ac tam multis modis. nobis declarati, crescere possim. Propter hujusmodi clementiam Dei erga me, et erga totum genus humanum abundantes misericordias, et propter meas et omnium mortalium ad haec recognoscenda negligentias, ego obtuli sacrificium laudis et propitiationis in holocaustum et in hostiam pro peccatis. Deus Pater gratum ipsum dignetur habere. Post matutinum, dum venissem ad missam, ego sensi quamdam vivam intelligentiam super Puero nato nobis et dato. Cognoscebam enim ipsum tunc primum opèra Divinitatis suae exercuisse, cum nondum esset aptus ad opera humanitatis suae, quia erat infans et impotens. Agnoscebam etiam generaliter tunc in sua Divinitate traxisse ad se pastores, spiritu distantissimos a cognitione tantae et tam absconditae in carne Divinitatis; item Magos, qui licet spiritu et ingenio non essent rudes, tamen secundum ea quae sunt humanae carnis erant valde distantes, propter magnitudinem suam, a Christo infante et parvo. Praeterea cogitabam quomodo Pueri innocentes per ipsum, absque ulla sua operatione, ad martyrium fuerint vocati. Orabam ipsum Jesum Christum, qui his modis apparuit et manifestatus est his qui longius aberant ab eo quam ut eum possent per se requirere, ut ipse dignetur acceptare quaecumque suffragia et bona, quae fiunt nomine eorum qui per se nesciunt aut non possunt requirere salutem suam, quae est in ipso. Sic dabatur spiritus ut ego devote orarem pro omnibus parvulis, etiam qui sunt adhuc in uteris matrum, qui pro se nesciunt nec possunt requirere salutem suam, quae est in ipso. Sic dabatur spiritu orare, aut operari, aut recognoscere bona data ac danda per ipsum Dominum Nostrum Jesum Christum.
units.en: On another day within the same octave of these Epiphanies of the Lord, I felt a certain good spirit, in which I wondered at the grace of God, by which it has come about that I have now seen these feasts of the Epiphany thirty-seven times in this life; and so I ran through the other feast days which have shone on me through so many revolving years; while I have taken so little fruit from them, and have never been grateful enough even to acknowledge the kindness of God, by which these goods and the like have been repeated over me so many times in the thirty-seven years now passed, and set before my eyes as the seasons returned, that I might draw salvation thence, and that what had been neglected in the preceding ones might be made good by the repeated graces. I gave thanks, then, and acknowledged my ingratitude, my carelessness, negligence and thoughtlessness. Blessed be God who gave me to acknowledge these things; and may he grant that I may hereafter grow in every kind of holy recognition of Christ manifested, and so many times and in so many ways declared to us. For this clemency of God towards me, and his abounding mercies towards the whole human race, and for my negligences, and those of all mortals, in acknowledging them, I offered the sacrifice of praise and propitiation, as a holocaust and as a victim for sins. May God the Father deign to hold it accepted. After matins, when I came to Mass, I felt a certain lively understanding concerning the Child born to us and given to us. For I recognized that he then first exercised the works of his Divinity, when he was not yet apt for the works of his humanity, because he was an infant and powerless. I recognized also that then, in his Divinity, he drew to himself the shepherds, in spirit most distant from the knowledge of a Divinity so great and so hidden in flesh; likewise the Magi, who, though not rude in spirit and mind, were yet, according to the things of human flesh, very distant, by reason of their greatness, from Christ, an infant and small. Moreover I thought how the innocent Children were called to martyrdom through him, without any act of their own. I prayed Jesus Christ himself, who in these ways appeared and was manifested to those who were too far from him to be able of themselves to seek him, that he would deign to accept whatever suffrages and good things are done in the name of those who of themselves know not, or cannot, seek their salvation, which is in him. So the spirit was given me to pray devoutly for all little ones, even those still in their mothers' wombs, who for themselves know not, nor can, seek their salvation, which is in him. So it was given by the spirit to pray, or to work, or to acknowledge the goods given and to be given through Our Lord Jesus Christ himself.

units.la: Post missam venerunt mihi in mentem varii usus salutares, propter quos sese nobis dedit et nobis a Patre datus fuit. Datus est enim in medicinam, in cibum, in potum, in hostiam, in medicum, in sacerdotem, in reparatorem, in vitam denique corporis et ànimae, in mortem, in resurrectionem, et denique, quod gravius est, dedit se ut occideretur:a nobis, et ut fieret sibi quidquid SENSON OSSES V voluerunt hominesmali. Hic igitur dolebam ex animo quod ego nullo adhuc modo satis bene me ipsi dederim, ut de me faceret quidquid velit aut voluerit, sive per vitam, sive per mortem.
units.en: After Mass there came into my mind the various saving uses for which he gave himself to us and was given to us by the Father. For he was given as medicine, as food, as drink, as victim, as physician, as priest, as restorer, as the life indeed of body and soul, in death, in resurrection; and finally — which is the weightier thing — he gave himself to be slain by us, and that there should be done to him whatever evil men willed. Here, then, I grieved from my heart that I have as yet in no way given myself well enough to him, that he might do with me whatever he will or would, whether by life or by death.

units.la: Rogabam itaque ut jamjam me et omni opera mea uteretur omni modo, prout sibi videbitur ad gloriam suam et utilitatem proximorum meorum, et ad salutem animae meae; et ut quidquid, ipse. dat, et dederit, et dedit mihi et caeteris omnibus, velle, cogitare et sentire, det aliquando perficere ante mortem, juxta ordinem suae voluntatis, et sapientiae, etc.
units.en: I begged, therefore, that even now he would use me and all my works in every way, as shall seem good to him, for his glory and the profit of my neighbours, and for the salvation of my soul; and that whatever he gives, and shall give, and has given to me and to all others to will, to think and to feel, he may one day grant to be brought to completion before death, according to the order of his will, and wisdom, and the rest.

units.la: Post festum Epiphaniae, die 45° Januarii, in qua ego celebravi festum de sacratissimo nomine Jesu, ego inveni satis magnam devotionem êt affectus varios ad hoc mellifluum nomen. Dixi tunc missam pro tota Societate nostra, propterea quod ipsa dicitur Societas Jesu Christi Domini Nostri. In his diebus, ego caeoepi invenire speciale quoddam auxilium ad reducendum cor meum in viam rectam, dum orandum est: auxilium autem fuit in singulari quadam memoria et assistentia Christi in cruce pendentis et proferentis illa verba: Mulier, ecce Filius tuus; — Pater, dimitte illis; — Deus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? — Hodie mecum eris in Paradiso; — Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum; — Sitio; etc. Sentiebam itaque dum cogitarem talia verba et talem considerationem Christi in cruce pendentis, sentiebam, inquam, cor meum sensi- bili quodam attractu tranquillari, et venire ad meliorem quietem, imo et elevari ad attentionem ofācii mei.
units.en: After the feast of the Epiphany, on the 15th of January, on which I celebrated the feast of the most sacred name of Jesus, I found a good measure of devotion, and various affections towards this honey-flowing name. I said Mass then for our whole Society, because it is called the Society of Jesus Christ Our Lord. In these days I began to find a certain special help for bringing my heart back into the right way when prayer is to be made: the help was in a certain singular remembrance and presence of Christ hanging on the cross and uttering those words: Woman, behold thy son; — Father, forgive them; — God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? — Today thou shalt be with me in Paradise; — Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit; — I thirst; and the rest. I felt, then, when I thought on such words and on such a consideration of Christ hanging on the cross — I felt, I say, my heart calmed by a certain sensible attraction, and coming to a better quiet, nay, even raised to attention to my office.

units.la: Sub hos dies venit a summo Pontifice bulla Jubilaei; juxta cujus tenorem ego me praeparavi ad susceptionem ejus gratiae quam sonabat ipsa bulla, ad quam rem Dominus dedit mihi varios gradus infusionis fidei et spei circa talia bona spiritualia. Rogabam Dominum ut mihi concederet gratiam qua fieri posset ut, quaecumque bona animae meae ego unquam alienavi aut vendidi, aut perdidi, illa valeant redire ad me. Hoc erat desiderium sumptum juxta figurale jubilaeum Judaeorum, in quo unusquisque redibat ad bona terrae suae quomodocumque alienatae. Varii affectus quoquè venerunt in animum meùm circa reconciliationem cum Deo. Optabam ut culpae omnes, sive essent per ignorantiam, sive propter culpabilem fragilitatem, sive propter malitiam, sive propter immunditiam, vel ingratitudinem, aut denique propter quamlibet labem animae, spiritus, vel corporis, contractae delerentur; ita ut ntmhilin me jam remaneret quod Deum, Matrem ejus, aut sanctos offendat. Circa paeoenas quoque temporales quas incurri, optabam variis affectibus ut fieret etiam perfecta reconciliatio mea apud Deum et sanctos ejus; item quod nulla mala publica propter peccata mea debeant amplius esse in mundo: frequenter enim fit, imo quasi semper, ut mala communia, sicut sunt pestis, bella, fames, ete., eveniant propter cumulos peccatorum multorum hominum; ita scilicet quod unusquisque, ex parte, in causa est hujusmodi malorum.
units.en: About these days there came from the supreme Pontiff the bull of the Jubilee; according to whose tenor I prepared myself for the reception of that grace of which the bull spoke; for which thing the Lord gave me various degrees of infusion of faith and hope concerning such spiritual goods. I begged the Lord to grant me the grace by which it might come about that whatever goods of my soul I have ever alienated, or sold, or lost, might avail to return to me. This was a desire taken after the figure of the Jubilee of the Jews, in which each one returned to the goods of his land, however alienated. Various affections also came into my soul concerning reconciliation with God.
