I wished that all faults — whether contracted through ignorance, or through culpable frailty, or through malice, or through uncleanness, or ingratitude, or finally through any stain whatever of soul, spirit or body — might be blotted out; so that nothing might now remain in me to offend God, his Mother, or the saints. Concerning also the temporal pains I have incurred, I wished with various affections that my reconciliation with God and his saints might be made perfect; likewise that no public evils ought any longer to be in the world on account of my sins: for it frequently happens — nay, almost always — that common evils, such as plague, wars, famine, and the rest, come about through the heaps of sins of many men; so that each one is, in part, a cause of such evils.

units.la: In sabbato praecedenti immediate dominicam Septuagesimae, sub noctem, dum orarem mihi dimitti omnia mala, at maxime dum rogabam ut nullum peccatum unquam permittatur in me accidere propter demerita praeterita, hic ego sensi magnam quamdam consolationem, apprehendendo quodammodo gaudium quod esset ei cui Deus et Mater ipsius et sancti essent placati, et sese ipsi, aliquibus vel minimis signis, tales ostenderent.
units.en: On the Saturday immediately preceding Septuagesima Sunday, towards night, while I prayed that all evils might be forgiven me, and above all when I begged that no sin might ever be permitted to befall me on account of past demerits, I felt a certain great consolation, apprehending in a manner the joy which would be his towards whom God and his Mother and the saints were appeased, and should show themselves such to him by some signs, even the least.

units.la: Videbantur tunc intra me esse verba Christi et Virginis, et nonnullorum sanctorum mihi peculiarium; sed sensus talis erat magis de ipsis tanquam possibilibus quam de praesentibus, juxta verba quibus quis diceret: O si sentires verba talis amici sancti!
units.en: There seemed then to be within me words of Christ and of the Virgin, and of some saints particular to me; but the sense of them was rather as of things possible than of things present, after the manner of words in which one might say: O if you could feel the words of such a holy friend!

units.la: In die sanctae Agnetis virginis gloriosae ac martyris, dum cogitarem atque sentirem varias necessitates hominum mortalium, in quibus plurimi non habent sublevamen nisi a Deo per Christum et Sanctos ejus, ego sensi magnum desiderium in hoc, ut scilicet sancti qui sunt in coelis, unusquisque specialiter pro his qui laborant in sua patria et pro animabus suae regionis, dignentur orare, et excusare nos. Pro hac re offerens ego missam rogabam etiam Patrem coelestem ut, quotiescumque pronuntiarem nomen Filii sui, id est Jesus, ipse dignaretur respicere ad omnes eos qui aliqua parte salutis indigent, sive in hoc mundo, sive in Purgatorio; item quod semper recordetur omnium meritorum ipsius Jesu, et omnium desideriorum quae ipse, quandiu vixit in vita mortali, habuit in salutem hominum.
units.en: On the day of Saint Agnes, glorious virgin and martyr, while I thought on and felt the various necessities of mortal men, in which very many have no relief except from God through Christ and his Saints, I felt a great desire in this: namely, that the saints who are in heaven — each one specially for those who labour in his own country, and for the souls of his own region — would deign to pray, and to excuse us. Offering the Mass for this, I begged also the heavenly Father that, as often as I should pronounce the name of his Son, that is Jesus, he would deign to look upon all those who stand in need of any part of salvation, whether in this world or in Purgatory; likewise that he would always remember all the merits of Jesus himself, and all the desires which he, while he lived in mortal life, had for the salvation of men.

units.la: Hoc die, dum semel venisset in mentem meam quod instaret tempus in quo nos possemus egere rebus quae ad victum necessarium pertinent, ego sensi magnum et vivum desiderium nihil habendi praesentialiter; et ita rogavi ex intimo corde Christum in altari coram oculis meis existentem, ut siquidem fuerit ipsius voluntas et beneplacitum, mihi in perpetuum, id est quandiu fuero in hac vita mortali, nullus transeat annus in quo saltem semel non accidat, juxta illud desiderium, aliquid tale: sic videlicet quod quolibet anno debeam evacuari omnibus praesentibus, et inveniri in eo quod realiter nihil eorum habeam quae ad praesentem vitam pertineant, neque pro me, neque pro aliis quibuscumqueQuod si haec gratia, quam ego magnam reputarem, non venerit ex parte ipsarum rerum, detur mihi cognoscere utrum ipsi Deo placeat ut ego talem regulam voveam quantum ex meest, id est me effecturum esse hoc ipsum, privando me semel in anno omnibus praesentibus, et sic reducendo ad effectum veram et actualem paupertatem. Voluntas hoc efficiendi per gratiam Dei jamdiu 'in me fuit. Utinam igitur det Deus cognoscere in omnibus quid expediat in laudem suam, et ut fiat in omnibus ipsius voluntas bona, beneplacens et perfecta. Supradictum desiderium respiciebat non tam ad meam personam, quam facta suppositione quod essemus multi in eadem familia, vel domo, vel alias. Pro me enim jamdiu Dominus dedit sentire voluntatem quae esset ut quemlibet pastum deberem per meipsum ostiatim mendicare, ubicumque terrarum essem quae voluntas mea, sicut caeterae omnes quae ad abnegationem et abjectionem conferunt, et quidquid est virtutis ac gratiae, utinam semper in me crescant, et tam bene, quum ipsis actualiter non dabitur uti, ac si semper ipsis actualiter et directe uterer. Multi enim sunt qui, dum aliquandiu desuescunt ab actuali paupertate ac mendicitate,. caeterisque sanctis actibus crucis Christi, facile perdunt affectus ipsos ad tales actus exercendos. Orandus autem Jesus Christus crucifixus, ut per nulla exercitia dimoveamur aut retrahamur, sed nec retardemur, ab eo cursu quo debemus sempèr ferri ad crucem ipsius et ad mortem. Domini Nostri Jesu Christi. Quis- quis enim huc fertur, ad salutem fertur, et ad CoS o oLa es Aa a a a aar aaa a veram vitam, et ad veram resurrectionem. Amatores autem vitae hujus temporalis difficiles vias et periculosas sequuntur.
units.en: On this day, when once it came into my mind that a time was at hand in which we might lack the things that belong to necessary sustenance, I felt a great and lively desire of possessing nothing in the present; and so I begged from my inmost heart Christ, present on the altar before my eyes, that — if it were his will and good pleasure — for ever, that is, so long as I am in this mortal life, no year might pass in which at least once there should not befall, according to that desire, something of this kind: namely, that in every year I ought to be emptied of all present things, and be found in a state of really having none of the things that pertain to the present life, neither for myself nor for any others whatever. And if this grace, which I should count a great one, should not come from the side of the things themselves, may it be given me to know whether it would please God that I should vow such a rule so far as lies in me: that is, that I would bring this very thing about, depriving myself once a year of all present things, and thus reducing to effect a true and actual poverty. The will to effect this has, by the grace of God, long been in me. May God then grant to know in all things what is expedient for his praise, and that in all things his good, well-pleasing and perfect will may be done. The aforesaid desire looked not so much to my own person as to the supposition that we should be many in the same family, or house, or otherwise. For as for myself, the Lord long ago gave me to feel a will that I ought to beg every meal for myself from door to door, wherever in the world I might be; and may this will of mine, like all the others which make for self-denial and abasement, and whatever there is of virtue and grace, ever grow in me — and as well, when it shall not be given to use them actually, as if I were always using them actually and directly. For there are many who, when they have for some time grown unaccustomed to actual poverty and begging, and to the other holy acts of the cross of Christ, easily lose the very affections for exercising such acts. But Jesus Christ crucified must be prayed that by no exercises may we be moved away or drawn back, nor even delayed, from that course by which we ought always to be borne towards his cross and towards the death of Our Lord Jesus Christ. For whoever is borne hither, is borne to salvation, and to true life, and to true resurrection. But the lovers of this temporal life follow difficult and dangerous ways.

units.la: In festo sanctae Emerentianae virginis, causam cognovi quamobrem deberet anima mea benedicere Domino Deo Jesu Christo, qui illam martyrem et virginem, catechumenam adhuc, ad se tali die traxit. Ejus precibus puto factum esse ut senserim magnam et multam devotionem, tam in officio dicendo quam in missa; in qua missa mihi data fuit abundantia consolationis, cum effusione multarum lacrymarum. Hic maxime optavi ut Dominus meminisset, cum sacrificio nostro, ejus sacrificii quod in beata Emerentiana tali die ipsi oblatum fuit, at non meminissėt peccatorum eorum hominum qui ipsam sanctam lapidarunt. Et ita sensi bonum esse coram Deo si quotidie, dum per Christum offertur memoria martyrum et aliorum sanctorum, repraesentemus bòna-:opera et merita talium sanctorum, ut eorum intuitu placari possit nobis Deus, qui nihil tale per nos facimus; simul autem rogantes ipsum ne meminerit iniquitatum et malitiarum quae fuerunt contra ipsos sanctos.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Emerentiana the virgin, I learned the reason why my soul ought to bless the Lord God Jesus Christ, who drew to himself on such a day that martyr and virgin, while yet a catechumen. By her prayers I think it came about that I felt great and abundant devotion, both in saying the office and at Mass; in which Mass an abundance of consolation was given me, with the shedding of many tears. Here I wished above all that the Lord would remember, with our sacrifice, that sacrifice which was offered to him on such a day in blessed Emerentiana; and that he would not remember the sins of those men who stoned that saint. And so I felt that it is good before God if daily, when through Christ the memory of the martyrs and other saints is offered, we represent the good works and merits of such saints, that in regard of them God may be appeased towards us, who do nothing of the kind ourselves; at the same time begging him not to remember the iniquities and malices which were committed against those saints.

units.la: E AEA E N EN E E ea In hoc die, dum in puncto quodam bonae consolationis spiritualis venisset in me desiderium quo vellem talem consolationem communicatam cuidam personae et aliis omnibus, subito advenit aliud desiderium respondens: Sed utinam tu ipse posses gustare et particeps fieri ejus consolationis quam tibi vellet communicatam Jesus, aut illius cujus te participem libenter faceret beata virgo et martyr Emerentiana. Hic quoque habui vivum quemdam sensum et apud me novum, gui erat juxta haee verba: O utinam, Deus meus, ego possem distincte cognoscere tuam voluntatem in omnibus operibus meis! Haec mihi enim esset suavissima vita, etc.
units.en: On this day, when at a certain point of good spiritual consolation there came upon me the desire that such consolation might be communicated to a certain person and to all others, suddenly another desire came in answer: But would that you yourself could taste, and become partaker of, that consolation which Jesus would wish communicated to you, or that of which the blessed virgin and martyr Emerentiana would gladly make you partaker. Here too I had a certain lively feeling, new to me, which ran according to these words: O would, my God, that I could distinctly know your will in all my works! For this would be to me a most sweet life, and so forth.

units.la: Die Purificationis Dominae Nostrae, multam recepi cognitionem super evangelio, multam devotionem super officio benedictionis candelarum, et magnum habui desiderium non moriendi donec bene cognoscam Dominum Jesum Christum et videam ipsum in anima mea, omnino pacificantem eam, contra omnes impugnationes, liberantem eam ab omnibus periculis, illuminantem eam prorsus in omnibus que ad ipsius obsequium pertinent, et dantem ei gloriam contra omnes ejus confusiones, tristitias et perturbationes. Hoc die etiam multis 'modis sensi miserias mearum imperfectionum atque defectuum, maxime eorum quibus deficio in rebus agendis. Hoc igitur mihi fuit ad quamdam confortationem spiritus contra tales tristitias, quod viderem Deum esse mihi propitium; quem ego si tenuero et sensero in me ipso, me facere possit quidquid esse possum et debeo. Sensi etiam quoddam gaudium in hoc die, dum considerarem me tam nudum esse et privatum spiritu, quia videlicet beata virgo Maria occasionem haberet miserendi mihi, videns defectus meos, Hoc quoque die proposui in corde meo frequentare orationem hanc, scilicet: Domine Deus omni- potens, des mihi gratiam ut, dum moriar, habeam pacem, quae constat ex visione tui salutaris, ex lumine omnium gentium, et ex gloria tuae plebis christianae. Hoc enim dum haberetur, cognosceretur perfecte Christus ut salvator, ut illuminator, et ut glorificator. Quodam die propinquo Purificationi virginis Mariae, ego sensi ex intimis meis verba illius sententiae Christi, quibus dicit derelinquenti patrem et matrem, etc., quod vitam aeternam possidebit: Cum magno pondere sentiebam quid- nam sit possidere aeternam vitam. Hoc die, super quadam mea interrogatione interna circa rationem temporis, ego sensi quod Deus exacturus sit rationem temporis, ipse videlicet qui solus nobis tempus dare potest. Alius quispiam potest exigere rationem aliquarum rerum quas ipse mihi crediderit; sed Deus etiam temporis, quod nemo neque dare neque prolongare cuiquam potest, rationem petet, sicut et caeterarum rerum omnium quas ipse dederit.
units.en: On the day of the Purification of Our Lady I received much knowledge on the gospel, much devotion at the office of the blessing of the candles, and had a great desire not to die until I should know well the Lord Jesus Christ, and should see him in my soul, wholly giving it peace against all assaults, freeing it from all dangers, thoroughly enlightening it in all that belongs to his service, and giving it glory against all its confusions, sadnesses and disturbances. On this day too I felt in many ways the miseries of my imperfections and defects, above all of those by which I fail in things to be done. This, then, was to me a certain strengthening of spirit against such sadnesses: that I saw God to be favourable to me; and if I hold him and feel him in myself, he can make of me whatever I can and ought to be. I felt also a certain joy on this day, when I considered that I was so naked and stripped of spirit — because, that is, the blessed Virgin Mary would have occasion of pitying me, seeing my defects. On this day also I purposed in my heart to use often this prayer: Lord God almighty, give me the grace that, when I die, I may have peace, which consists in the vision of thy salvation, in the light of all nations, and in the glory of thy christian people. For while this is had, Christ would be perfectly known as saviour, as enlightener, and as glorifier. On a certain day near the Purification of the Virgin Mary I felt from my inmost being the words of that sentence of Christ, in which he says of him who leaves father and mother, and the rest, that he shall possess eternal life. With great weight I felt what it is to possess eternal life. On this day, upon a certain inward questioning of mine about the account of time, I felt that God will demand an account of time — he, namely, who alone can give us time. Another may demand an account of certain things which he has entrusted to me; but God will ask an account even of time, which no one can give or prolong to anyone, as of all the other things which he has given.

units.la: Circa dies carnis-privii, ego sensi satis grande pondus tristitiarum ex meis humanis 'imperfectionibus procedentium, et non tam ex ipsis imperfectionibus quam ex ipsarum consideratione quae mihi suggerebatur, non jam de solito per spiritum meum principalem, sed. potius - per meum humanum et proprium, aut per illum qui mihi datus est ad colaphizationem exercitativam. Fui igitur in hoc tempore multum remissus in bonis actionibus, distractus et ab= stractus a vivis et intimis intelligentiis atque sensu rerum supernarum. In hoc igitur solo ferme consolabar quod hoc mihi videretur crux mea, jamdiu nota, quae scilicet crux habet ferme semper has tres partes: unam quidem ex pro- E EAE ES S EE E fundo meo, dum considero carnis meae tantam inconstantiam circa sanctimoniam; alteram ex parte ejus quod est circa me a dextris et a sinistris, dum video defectus meos circa opera charitatis proximi; tertiam vero ex parle superiore, quae causabatur ex cognitione meae indevotionis et abstractionis a rebus quae immediate sunt circa Deum et sanctos ejus. Horum itaque trium malorum meorum humana consideratio crucem mihi jamdiu posuit in humeros, quam frequenter sentio cum magno gravamine, ut discam ègo tolerare et sciam aliam crucem meam quae placeat magis Deo, videlicet magnos et continuos labores circa amorem Dei ac laudem, circa mei ipsius sanctificationem et circa proximorum salutem: circa Deum quidem ascendendo; circa me semper descendendo; circa proximos vero quotidie me a dextris et a sinistris dilatando, et extendendo manus operatrices. Sed quoniam hanc crucem non tollo diligenter, fit ut alteram patiar et sentiam in. spiritu meo.
units.en: About the days of carnival I felt a considerable weight of sadnesses proceeding from my human imperfections — and not so much from the imperfections themselves as from the consideration of them, which was suggested to me not now, as usual, by my principal spirit, but rather by my human and own spirit, or by that one which has been given me for a buffeting that exercises me. I was therefore at this time much slackened in good actions, distracted and drawn away from the living and inward understandings and sense of things above. In this alone, then, I found almost my only comfort: that this seemed to me to be my cross, long known to me — a cross which has almost always these three parts: one from my own depths, when I consider the great inconstancy of my flesh with regard to holiness; another from what is about me on the right hand and on the left, when I see my failures in the works of charity to my neighbour; and the third from the upper part, caused by the knowledge of my want of devotion and my abstraction from the things which immediately concern God and his saints. The human consideration of these three evils of mine has long laid a cross on my shoulders, which I often feel with great heaviness, so that I may learn to bear it, and may know that other cross of mine which pleases God more: namely, great and continual labours about the love and praise of God, about my own sanctification, and about the salvation of my neighbours — towards God, by ascending; towards myself, by always descending; towards my neighbours, by daily enlarging myself to right and left, and stretching out working hands. But because I do not take up this cross diligently, it comes about that I suffer and feel the other in my spirit.

units.la: In festo sanctae Dorothee virginis et martyris, ego sensi magnum quoddam desiderium circa salutem proximorum afflictorum, aut in necessitate qualibet positorum; unde ego rogavi ex intimis Deum, ut ipse aperiret sensum omnium eorum qui male habent, sic quod 1u possint invocare ipsius misericordiam super miseriis suis; et hic dolui quod viderem multos, multis modis mala habentes, nescire repraesentare miserias suas ipsi Deo et sanctis suis, sed semper recurrere ad humana remedia et tempo- ralia, in quibus non est salus. Effundamus erg semper coram illo corda nostra afflicta, quia ipse laborem et dolorem considerat, ponderat, et penitus novit aestimare qualis et quantus sit.
units.en: On the feast of Saint Dorothy, virgin and martyr, I felt a certain great desire for the salvation of afflicted neighbours, or of those placed in any need whatever; whence I begged God from my inmost heart that he would open the understanding of all who fare ill, so that they might invoke his mercy upon their miseries; and here I grieved to see that many, faring ill in many ways, know not how to set their miseries before God and his saints, but always have recourse to human and temporal remedies, in which there is no salvation. Let us therefore always pour out our afflicted hearts before him, for he considers toil and grief, weighs them, and knows thoroughly how to estimate of what kind and how great they are.

units.la: In die sanctae Appolloniae, ego inveni satis bonam devotionem applicando missam ad eam personam, quaecumque sit in mundo, quae maxime omnium optat precibus Ecclesie adjuvari. Optavi quoque liberationem a paeoenis purgatorii ei animae, quaecumque sit, quae justissime omnium de me conqueri possit, et majori jure exigere orationes meas. In hoc eodem die sanctae Appolloniae, ego habui memoriam quamdam quod, cum essem parvulus, solebam legere quamdam orationem de hac sanctissima virgine, quam orationem ego inchoaveram propter dolo- rem dentium. Quo postea non fui afflictus. Agebam igitur gratias huic ipsi virgini, quae potuit mihi facile impetrare conservationem hujus sanitatis, et petebam ut in futurum fieret, per intercessionem et merita ipsius apud Christum, quatenus ègo et quilibet sociorum meorum possemus conservari ab his et caeteris omnibus morbis. Rogabam etiam hanc eamdem sanctam ut ipsa oraret pro nobis alios sanctos, unumquemque juxta ministerium quod habet a Christo circa curam fidelium, non solum quantum ad impetrandas nobis virtutes et salutem spirituum nostrorum, sed etiam in particulari quantum ad virtutes, et curationes, et conservationes circa corpus et partes corporis. Optabam itaque ut unus aliquis mihi impetraret verbi gratia humilitatem, continuam mei curam circa hoc habendo; alius patientiam, alius salutem corporis, ete. Et hoc modo dilatabar circa Societatem meam, discurrendo etiam usque ad minima, cum spiritu sanctae pietatis, et cum fide simplici ac spë bona.
units.en: On the day of Saint Apollonia I found quite good devotion, applying the Mass for that person, whoever in the world it may be, who most of all desires to be helped by the prayers of the Church. I wished also deliverance from the pains of purgatory for that soul, whichever it may be, which with the greatest justice of all could complain of me, and with greater right demand my prayers. On this same day of Saint Apollonia I had a certain memory that, when I was a little boy, I used to read a certain prayer about this most holy virgin, a prayer I had begun on account of toothache — with which I was afterwards not afflicted. I gave thanks therefore to this virgin, who could easily have obtained for me the preservation of this health, and asked that in future it might come about, through her intercession and merits with Christ, that I and every one of my companions might be preserved from these and all other diseases. I begged also this same saint to pray for us to the other saints, each according to the ministry which he has from Christ for the care of the faithful — not only for obtaining for us virtues and the health of our spirits, but also in particular for virtues, and cures, and preservations of the body and the parts of the body. I wished, then, that some one might obtain for me, for example, humility, keeping continual care of me in this; another patience, another health of body, and so on. And in this way I enlarged myself over my Society, running down even to the least things, with a spirit of holy piety, and with simple faith and good hope.

units.la: Det Deus, qui nos et omnia creavit, gra- tiam ut possimus recognoscere, per Spiritum ipsius, quaecumque ab ipso sunt nobis idonea, et recognoscendo gratias agere. Utinam sentiremus ea quae ipse operatùr in nobis, sive in corpore, sive in spiritu, et hoc per se immediate, aut per şuos ministros. Utinam tandem aliquando videamus eum qui est et qui operatur omnia in nobis; et illum per quem omnia sunt et aguntur; et illum in quo omnia sunt! f Sed veniendum erit ad hoc summum et primum principium, ac causam omnium rerum, per mediatas causas, et sicut ad summum ac primum mediatorem, per mediata media; et sicut ad primum finem ac terminum formamque omnium rerum, per alios fines mediatos ac per formas mediatas. Primus a quo, Pater est; primus per quem, Filius; primus autem in quo, Spiritus Sanctus. Pater. quidem a quo omne esse creatum est; Filius per quem omnia fiunt; et Spiritus Sanctus in quo omnia perficiuntur. Haec quidem attriÞþutive intelligenda sunt, quia unicum omnium creatorum et factorum et perfectorum principium sunt Pater et Filius et Spiritus Sanctus; a quo uno principio processerunt omnia, et per quod administrantur omnia, et in quo subsistunt omnia, quod sit benedictum in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
units.en: May God, who created us and all things, give grace that we may recognize, through his Spirit, whatever things from him are fitted for us, and in recognizing give thanks. Would that we felt the things he works in us, whether in body or in spirit, and that both immediately by himself and through his ministers. Would that at last we may some day see him who is, and who works all things in us; and him through whom all things are and are done; and him in whom all things are! But we must come to this supreme and first principle and cause of all things through mediate causes, and to the supreme and first mediator through mediate means; and to the first end and term and form of all things through other mediate ends and mediate forms. The first from whom, is the Father; the first through whom, the Son; the first in whom, the Holy Spirit. The Father, from whom all created being is; the Son, through whom all things are made; and the Holy Spirit, in whom all things are perfected. These things are to be understood by way of attribution, for the one principle of all things created and made and perfected is the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit; from which one principle all things have proceeded, and through which all things are administered, and in which all things subsist — which be blessed for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: In festo beatae Scholasticae virginis, ego celebravi missam de ipsa pro me ipso. Hic ego notavi et sensi esse perquam necessarium et conveniens valde, ut in similibus. festis sanctarum Virginum, quaerantur gratiae que faciunt ad propriam perfectionem. Ipsae omnes sanctae Virgines, quae maximo studio operam dederunt ut in seipsis aedificarent templum sanctum in Spiritu Sancto, et voluerunt fieri vasa sanctitatis ad placendum sponso suo Jesu Christo cui se devoverunt, ipsae, inquam, tales animae maxime optant ut nos omnes ornemus in nobis, et ut in omni sanctitate ac justitia, liberati a -> maculis quae displicent oculis divinis, placeamus Deo nostro. Unde fit ut sollicitae sint hae virgines pro nobis, dum hujusmodi gratias per ipsarum intercessionem postulaverimus. Alii quoque sancli convenienter invocari possunt, unusquisque juxta ordinem suum, et juxta viam meritorum et gratiarum in quibus magnificati sunt a Deo inhac vita, et per quas consecuti Daaa ja OUO TENE sunt gloriam sempiternam in Christo Jesu Domino Nostro et suo. Deus enim hune ordinem non tollit a sanctis suis, qùi est ut unusquisque vėlit Deum suum omnibus sicut sibi communicatum: alius autem ab alio diversum tenuit ordinem dum -viveret; nec omnes eisdem gra tiis fuerunt dotati;.nec voluit Deus ut omnes ioe eisdem operibus bonis ac sanctis exercitiis erudirentur. Quare ergo non conveniret unumquemque sanctum velle Deum laudari ac cognosci eo modo quo sibi gratum fuit eum colere et cognoscere? Et quare non vellet illa opera bona, in quibus ipse invenit Deum, esse in usu apud aliquos saltem eorum qui in hac vita ipsum invocant?
units.en: On the feast of blessed Scholastica the virgin I celebrated the Mass of her for myself. Here I noted and felt that it is exceedingly necessary and very fitting that on such feasts of the holy Virgins the graces be sought which make for one's own perfection. All those holy Virgins, who with the greatest zeal laboured to build up in themselves a holy temple in the Holy Spirit, and wished to become vessels of holiness to please their bridegroom Jesus Christ to whom they devoted themselves — such souls, I say, desire above all that we all should adorn ourselves within, and that in all holiness and justice, freed from the stains which displease the divine eyes, we may please our God. Hence it comes that these virgins are solicitous for us when we ask such graces through their intercession. The other saints too may fittingly be invoked, each according to his order, and according to the way of merits and graces in which they were magnified by God in this life, and through which they attained everlasting glory in Christ Jesus, Our Lord and theirs. For God does not take from his saints this order, which is that each wills his God to be communicated to all as to himself; but one held a different order from another while he lived; nor were all endowed with the same graces; nor did God will that all should be formed by the same good works and holy exercises. Why then should it not be fitting that each saint should wish God to be praised and known in that way in which it was pleasing to himself to worship and know him? And why should he not wish those good works, in which he himself found God, to be in use among at least some of those who invoke him in this life?

units.la: In prima dominica Quadragesimae, dum optarem et peterem a Deo ut longe a me expelleret omnes inimicos meos, accepi hoc responsum: Da operam tu ut Dominus te elevet a locis inimicorum tuorum; tua enim habitatio non est hic: hic autem ipsorum est locus.
units.en: On the first Sunday of Lent, when I wished and asked of God that he would drive all my enemies far from me, I received this answer: Do you rather labour that the Lord may lift you up away from the places of your enemies; for your dwelling is not here: this, however, is their place.

units.la: Hoc quoque die, dum dicerem officium meum et aptarem horologium absque ulla necessitate, venit in mentem meam quaerere a Deo gratiam qua ipse me aptaret et ordinaret ad bene orandum; esse enim ipsi magis facile, quam mihi aptare vel ordinare qualemcumque rem materialem manibus meis. Ex hoc assumpsi occasionem reprehendendi meipsum, quod hactenus nimium frequenter, dum debui esse dttenitn dka adaptatus, et ordinatus circą orationes meas aut bonas meditationes, diverti me ad tangendum, vel videndum, vel ad ordinandum aliquid aliud absque necessitate; cum tamen tota cura mea tunc debuerit esse ad aptandum me et componendum, ad bene faciendum opus quod habebam in manibus meis, vel in lingua, vel in mente. Tunc autem optime fiunt hujusmodi bona exercitia, cum a toto homine, -concurrentibus cunctis potentiis requisitis, fiunt; ubi autem concurrit omnis. homo, facile crederem quod bonus angelus non deerit; et dum ipse adest,Spiritus Sanctus qui Deus est non longe abest, ut actum nostrum perficiat.
units.en: On this day too, while I said my office and was adjusting my clock without any necessity, it came into my mind to seek from God the grace that he would adjust and order me for praying well; for that is easier for him than for me to adjust or order any material thing with my hands. From this I took occasion to reprove myself, that hitherto too frequently, when I ought to have been attentive, adjusted and ordered for my prayers or good meditations, I have turned aside to touch, or look at, or set in order something else without necessity; whereas all my care ought then to have been to fit and compose myself for doing well the work I had in my hands, or on my tongue, or in my mind. And such good exercises are done best when they are done by the whole man, with all the required powers concurring; and where the whole man concurs, I could well believe that the good angel will not be absent; and while he is present, the Holy Spirit, who is God, is not far off, to perfect our act.

units.la: In die quo mihi contigit celebrare festum translatum de beata Martina virgine et martyre, ego concepi, ex occasione lectionum ipsius, magnam fidem, quod. ipsa multa possit apud sanctos Angelos, et multa contra malos, quorum templa ante ipsam consistere non poterant nec ipsa idola daemoniorum. Concepi igitur in missa magnum propositum invocandi illam contra malignos spiritus; proposuique me habiturum hujus desiderii rationem omnibus secundis feriis, in quibus soleo facere spiritualem memoriam Angelorum bonorum. Sicut enim juvat invocare bonos Angelos et fieri devotus ipsorum, ita quoque, juvabit tali die spiritualem invocare gratiam et auxilium Dei, et ipsorum Angelorum, contra malos spiritus qui tam multis modis nos agitant, et decipiunt, et perdunt. Utinam igitor mihi semper adsit favor hujus þeatae virginis, cujus festum celebravi hoc die lunae post dominicam primam Quadragesimae, ad. hoc ut singulis diebus secundarum feriarum habeam hanc memoriam, non solum videlicet bonorum. Angelorum, id quod jamdiu habui, sed etiam malorum Angelorum in eorum perniciem. Hoc secundum ego nunquam antea senseram tam ex intimis. Sit benedictus ille a quo, et per quem, etin quo talia sensa et tales notitias accipimus.
units.en: On the day when I happened to celebrate the transferred feast of blessed Martina, virgin and martyr, I conceived, on occasion of her lessons, a great faith that she can do much with the holy Angels, and much against the evil ones, whose temples could not stand before her, nor the very idols of the demons. I conceived therefore at Mass a great purpose of invoking her against the malignant spirits; and I resolved to keep account of this desire on all Mondays, on which I am accustomed to make a spiritual memory of the good Angels. For as it helps to invoke the good Angels and become devoted to them, so also it will help on such a day to invoke the spiritual grace and help of God, and of those Angels, against the evil spirits who in so many ways agitate us, and deceive, and destroy. May the favour of this blessed virgin, whose feast I celebrated on this Monday after the first Sunday of Lent, be always with me, so that on every Monday I may keep this memory — not only, that is, of the good Angels, which I have long kept, but also of the evil Angels, to their destruction. This second thing I had never before felt so from my inmost heart. Blessed be he from whom, and through whom, and in whom we receive such feelings and such knowledge.

units.la: In die sancti Valentini martyris, quae fuit 14° Februarii, Stephanus a nobis recessit Romam versus. Ego sensi magnam devotionem circa invocationem boni Angeli ipsius et aliorum pro ipso, ad concipiendum spem majorem contra omnia pericula viarum; ego sensi magnum desiderium ut multi boni et patientes eas peragerent, quorum patientia et orationes impetrarent a Deo gratiam pro caeteris post eum profecturis et peregrinaturis.
units.en: On the day of Saint Valentine the martyr, which was the 14th of February, Stephen left us for Rome. I felt great devotion in invoking his good Angel, and the others, for him, so as to conceive greater hope against all the dangers of the roads; and I felt a great desire that many good and patient men might travel those ways, whose patience and prayers might obtain grace from God for the others who after him are to set out and journey.

units.la: Ex occasione hujus discessus, sensi etiam quemdam bonum spiritum, considerando quomodo Angelus ipsius bonus tamdiu mansisset in societate nostra domestica, a me non cognitus, et quod nunc discederet localiter a nobis. Dolui ego quod non admisissem ipsum circa curam juvenis sibi commissi quantum potuissem, cum tamen ipsemet Angelus humiliasset mihi et obedientem conservasset juvenem, non permittens ut malus spiritus ipsius mihi molestaret - quantum ego merebar. Hic dum multa considerassem de officio Angelorum circa homines A clare sensi quam necessarium sit. ut Spiritus ille qui omnia perfectissime continet, adaptet ipsis animas nostras ex intimis, et eas moderetur per infusionem donorum suorum. Rogandus est igitur Christus ut ille nobis conservet Spiritum suum, sine cujus operatione etiam boni Angeli nostri non sufficerent ad moderationem spirituum nostrorum. Sine tactibus namque divinis, caetera omnia verba viderentur, quae efficaciam non habent usque ad penelrationemintimorum nostrorum. Est autem sermo Dei vivus et efficax, et penetrabilior omni gladio ancipiti, discretor spirituum et intentionum cordis, usque ad divisionem carnis et spiritus et medullarum. Haec, inquam, efficit divinus sermo, si per Spiritum Sanctum doceatur et suggeratur.
units.en: On occasion of this departure I felt also a certain good spirit, considering how his good Angel had remained so long in our domestic company, unrecognized by me, and that now he was departing from us in place. I grieved that I had not admitted him, so far as I could have, into the care of the young man entrusted to him — although that very Angel had humbled the youth for me and kept him obedient, not permitting his evil spirit to trouble me as much as I deserved. Here, having considered many things about the office of the Angels towards men, I clearly felt how necessary it is that that Spirit who contains all things most perfectly should fit our souls to them from within, and govern them by the infusion of his gifts. Christ therefore must be asked to preserve to us his Spirit, without whose working even our good Angels would not suffice for the governing of our spirits. For without the divine touches, all other words would seem words that have no efficacy reaching to the penetration of our inmost depths. But the word of God is living and effectual, and more piercing than any two-edged sword, a discerner of the spirits and intentions of the heart, even to the dividing of flesh and spirit and marrow. This, I say, the divine word effects, if it be taught and prompted by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: In hoc die, post missam, dum considerassem diversitatem spirituum qui me frequenter agitarunt, et varium esse fecerunt circa possibilitatem faciendi fructum in Germania, notavi non esse adhaerendum ullo modo verbis illius qui omnia facit impossibilia et semper adducit inconvenientia, sed potius verbis et sensibus illius qui ostendit possibilitatem, et dat animum; sed tamen etiam cavendum ne nimium curramus in dexte- ram: sumenda enim tandem est discretio; ut in medio quòdam consistamus inter dextrum et sinistrum; sic videlicet ut nec in nostra spe misceatur inanis abundantia, nec in metu nostro - aggravetur penuria. Quod si nequeat fieri quin vel in hanc vel in illam partem declinetur, tutius, et minus periculosum est, si juxta tempus potius abundantiae ambulemus, ac speremus, quam si jūxta modum tristitiae nos adaptaverimus, ubi mille errores ac deceptiones, mille sursum germinantis amaritudinis labyrinthi, ete. Qui autem noverit spiritum abundantiae et verba ejus, 1tem spiritum tentantem et turbantem et verba ejus, is poterit ex utraque parte doceri. Sumendus enim erit et retinendus, et dum amissus fuerit, semper requirendus spiritus abundantiae; servanda erit illa laetitia et consolatio, ac confortatio et tranquillitas, et reliquae dispositiones quae se tenent ex parte boni affeċlus, et ad has redeundum erit nt tandem firmius haereant: Verba autem omnia quae accidunt non ita sumenda erunt quin possent quaedam admisceri non vera, propterea quod et malus spiritus possit induere speciem lucidi Angeli. Circa spiritum autem contrarium et verba ejus, contradictorio modo faciendum est: spiritus.- quidem ıste quantum ad omnes partes suorum sensuum expellendus est ac fugiendus; non autem omnia verba, quia multa posses accipere ad multas cautelas, et ex ipsis reddi circa res humanas prudentior; quia sunt multa vera et utilia, si postea informäta fuerint alio spiritu.
units.en: On this day, after Mass, having considered the diversity of spirits which have frequently agitated me and made me waver about the possibility of bearing fruit in Germany, I noted that one must in no way cleave to the words of that spirit who makes everything impossible and always brings forward difficulties, but rather to the words and feelings of that one who shows possibility and gives courage; and yet we must also beware of running too far to the right hand: for discretion must in the end be used, that we may stand in a certain middle between right and left; so that neither may an empty abundance be mingled in our hope, nor the want be aggravated in our fear. And if it cannot be but that one lean to one side or the other, it is safer, and less dangerous, to walk and hope according to the season of abundance, than to conform ourselves to the manner of sadness, where are a thousand errors and deceptions, a thousand labyrinths of bitterness springing upward, and the rest. But he who knows the spirit of abundance and its words, and likewise the tempting and troubling spirit and its words, can be taught from both sides. For the spirit of abundance is to be taken and kept, and, when lost, always to be sought again; that gladness and consolation, that strengthening and tranquillity, and the other dispositions which stand on the side of good affection, are to be preserved, and to these we must return, that at last they may cleave more firmly. Yet all the words that come are not so to be taken but that some untrue ones may be mingled in, since even the evil spirit can put on the appearance of an angel of light. With the contrary spirit and its words we must deal in the contradictory way: that spirit indeed, as to all the parts of its feelings, is to be driven out and fled from; but not all its words, for many you might take as so many cautions, and from them be made more prudent about human affairs; for many are true and useful, if they be afterwards informed by another spirit.

units.la: In die quo celebravi officium translatum de sancto Hygino papa et martyre, dum dicturus essem missam pro summo pontifice Paulo HI, venil in mentem meam bona quaedam admiratio super bonitate Jesu Christi: in hoc videlicet quod fuerit tam liberalis ut seipsum totum communicaverit, tam variis modis, non solum bonis et gratis, sed etiam malis, cum in caeoena. totum sese communicaverit etiam traditori suo. Admonebar igitur hic ut, quoniam Christus sese mihi quotidie celebranti communicat, et paratus est omnibus aliis modis seipsum communicare, puta ın orationibus caeterisque piis operibus, ego quoque me omnibus modis ipsi deberem communicare ac resignare; et non ipsi tantum, sed propter ipsum omnibus proximis meis, bonis et malis; communicare inquam, alloquendo, docendo, benefaciendo, pro ipsis laborando, patiendo, totum me (in quañtum utile esset) omnibus aperiendo, ad consolationem, et denique me totum et omnia mea omnibus distribuendo. Fiat, fiat!
units.en: On the day when I celebrated the transferred office of Saint Hyginus, pope and martyr, when I was about to say Mass for the supreme pontiff Paul III, there came into my mind a certain good wonder at the goodness of Jesus Christ: in this, namely, that he was so liberal that he communicated his whole self, in such various ways, not only to the good and grateful, but even to the wicked, since at the supper he communicated his whole self even to his betrayer. I was admonished here, then, that since Christ communicates himself to me daily as I celebrate, and is ready to communicate himself in all other ways — as in prayers and other pious works — I too ought to communicate and resign myself to him in every way; and not to him only, but for his sake to all my neighbours, good and bad: to communicate, I say, by speaking with them, teaching, doing good, labouring for them, suffering, opening my whole self (so far as it might be useful) to all, for their consolation, and finally distributing myself and all that is mine to all. So be it, so be it!

units.la: In die quo mihi contigit celebrare festum beatae Birgittae, multa sensi circa curam salutis animarum, quae me angebant; maxime dum meminissem quod in hae provincia sint tot Ecclesiae parochiales catholicae, quae nullum habent pastorem particularem, neque etiam ullum sacerdotem, sive dignum sive indignum. Multum quoque affectus spiritualis recepi, dum considerassem quo modo sancta Birgitta fuerit mulier tam sanctorum desideriorum circa salutem animarum, sicut scripta ipsius et orationes quae nobis relictae sunt testantur. Hic inveni gratiam, ut ex animo possem gratias agere Deo pro omnibus beneficiis quae per eamdem sanctam Birgittam Ecclesiae suae contulit et confert.
units.en: On the day when I happened to celebrate the feast of blessed Bridget, I felt many things concerning the care of the salvation of souls, which distressed me; above all when I remembered that in this province there are so many catholic parish churches which have no particular pastor, nor even any priest, worthy or unworthy. I received also much spiritual affection when I considered how Saint Bridget was a woman of such holy desires for the salvation of souls, as her writings and the prayers left to us bear witness. Here I found grace to give thanks from my heart to God for all the benefits which through the same Saint Bridget he has conferred and confers on his Church.

units.la: In die quo celebravi officium translatum de sançto Gilberto confessore, in-missa inveni maximam devotionem circa animas defunctorum, et magnos sensus compassionis pro ipsis; ita ut, durante missa, semper adfuerint lacrymae.
units.en: On the day when I celebrated the transferred office of Saint Gilbert the confessor, I found at Mass the greatest devotion concerning the souls of the departed, and great feelings of compassion for them; so that, while the Mass lasted, tears were present throughout.

units.la: Ante missam, ego optaveram satis efficaciter, quantum in me erat, ut possem communicare in Christo. Ibi igitur, in missa, sensi quod bona pars communicandi cum ipso est sentire ea quae sentiebat ipse in passione, non solum in corpore suo, sed in anima, in qua erat dolor propter animarum pericula aeterna, et etiam propter pericula paenarum temporalium, maxime autem earum quae suntin Purgatorio. Haec verba şupradicta non fuerant mihi suggesta in quantum ad intellectum, nec quantum ad memoriam, quasi nova, sed sensus ipse fuit novus ac insolitus.
units.en: Before Mass I had wished, quite efficaciously so far as in me lay, that I might communicate in Christ. There, then, at Mass, I felt that a good part of communicating with him is to feel what he felt in the passion — not only in his body, but in his soul, in which there was grief for the eternal dangers of souls, and also for the dangers of temporal pains, above all of those which are in Purgatory. These words had not been suggested to me as new, either to the understanding or to the memory; but the feeling itself was new and unwonted.

units.la: In cathedra sancti Petri, dum essem in missa, et sentirem quasdam amaritudines meas ex meis imperfectionibus nascentes, ego recepi responsum, per satis bonam cogitationem, quod non deberem tanti facere tales imperfectiones, nec ita esse attentus ad eas ut solebam, quia contemptae facile possunt evanescere, et quoniam saepe fit ut illarum contemplatio sola me reddat imperfectum illo modo.
units.en: On the Chair of Saint Peter, while I was at Mass and felt certain bitternesses of mine born of my imperfections, I received an answer, through a good enough thought: that I ought not to make so much of such imperfections, nor be as attentive to them as I used to be; for when despised they can easily vanish away; and because it often happens that the mere contemplation of them makes me imperfect in that very way.

units.la: In die quo ego celebravi festum sanctae Geno-. vefae virginis ac protectricis Parisiensium, dum mille suggererentur difficultates, quae non erant ex me dependentes, ego afficiebar taedio quodam, et perturbatione quae me impediebat circa spem bonam quam semper habui. Pro eadem tristitia tollenda mihi datum est considerare et sentire ea quae sequuntur: primo, quod non debeo facile permittere me extrahi extra opera quae ad mė pertinent et in quibus jam versor; secundo, quod non debeo humanam et propriam sollicitudinem meam tam late extendere; tertio, quod circa illa opera quae mihi sunt prae manibus, debeam intendere omnes vires meas; quarto, ut procedam in his operibus charitatis, sicut qui per ea sola quae tractat sibi facere velit viam ad caetera. Ea igitur impedimenta et defectus, qui ex me et ex his qui sunt in mea potestate procedent, sunt tollenda, ut spes faciendi fructùs augeatur. eTe N In die quo celebravi festum Angelorum custodum nostrorum, qui fuit primus Martii, ego inveni magnam devotionem, praesertim in missa quam dizi pro Societate nostra, rogando Dominum ut dignaretur illam circumdare et protegere Angelico sanctorum spirituum praesidio, tanquam sepe fortissima, ipsi tribuens custodiam.
units.en: On the day when I celebrated the feast of Saint Geneviève, virgin and protectress of the Parisians, while a thousand difficulties were being suggested which did not depend on me, I was affected by a certain weariness, and a disturbance which hindered me in the good hope I have always had. For the removing of that sadness it was given me to consider and feel what follows: first, that I ought not easily to allow myself to be drawn out of the works which belong to me and in which I am already engaged; second, that I ought not to stretch my human and personal solicitude so wide; third, that upon those works which are in my hands I ought to bend all my strength; fourth, that I should go forward in these works of charity as one who, by those things alone which he handles, would make his way to the rest. Those hindrances and defects, then, which proceed from me and from those who are in my power, are to be removed, that the hope of bearing fruit may be increased. On the day when I celebrated the feast of our guardian Angels, which was the first of March, I found great devotion, especially in the Mass which I said for our Society, begging the Lord that he would deign to surround and protect it with the Angelic guard of the holy spirits, as with a most strong hedge, giving it into their keeping.

units.la: In die quo celebravi officium et missam de sancto Brunone Patre Cartusiensium, ego sensi magna desideria et viva circa integrationem illius ordinis, et omnium aliorum ordinum, monasteriorum et eremitarum; et propter hoc dixi missam pro Societate nostra, cum magno desiderio ut ipsa aliquando posset, secundum voluntatem Dei Jesu Christi, et cum favore Patrum omnium sanctorum ordinum, ut possit, inquam, laborare et efficere aliquid in ipsam reformationem talium institutorum, et reliquorum omnium quae sunt secundum Ecclesiae romanae ordinationem, approbationem, concessioneni.
units.en: On the day when I celebrated the office and Mass of Saint Bruno, Father of the Carthusians, I felt great and lively desires for the restoration to wholeness of that order, and of all other orders, monasteries and hermits; and for this I said the Mass for our Society, with a great desire that it might one day be able, according to the will of God, of Jesus Christ, and with the favour of the Fathers of all the holy orders — that it might, I say, labour and accomplish something towards the reformation of such institutes, and of all the rest which stand according to the ordinance, approbation and concession of the Roman Church.

units.la: Hic sensi magnum desiderium ut inveniantur multi qui velint se humiliare propter Christum ad quaevis etiam minima opera, sintque multi ita exercitati in rebus spiritualibus, ut spiritu prompti sint obeundo cuilibet officio, et qui se habeant servos ad omnia paratos. Optabam etiam ut inveniri possint multi quibus gloriosum lucrum videretur ministrare sacerdotibus et ipsis respondere cum devotione, Fiat, fiat.
units.en: Here I felt a great desire that many might be found who would be willing to humble themselves for Christ's sake to any works, even the least; and that there might be many so exercised in spiritual things as to be prompt in spirit for undertaking any office whatever, bearing themselves as servants ready for everything. I wished also that many might be found to whom it would seem a glorious gain to minister to priests and to answer them with devotion. So be it, so be it.

units.la: Hoc die, animadverti quod utile sit cuilibet homini esse in memoria justi, ın charitate et cum claro spiritu Deum orantis: proinde mazime optabam ut sancti, qui Deo semper adstant, memoriam mei hàbeant in desideriis suis.
units.en: On this day I observed how profitable it is for any man to be in the memory of a just man who prays to God in charity and with a clear spirit: hence I wished above all that the saints, who always stand before God, might keep the memory of me in their desires.

units.la: Habui etiam nonnulla circa modum quem habent res omnes ¢reatae in Christo: si enim quidquid est in Deo ipsemet Deus est, non -po- test non fieri quin quodcumqùe est in Christo quantum ad humanitatem sit pulcherrimum; proindeque maxime cupiendum est et orandum ut ipse dignetur nos admittere ad memoriam suam, quatenus inibi existentes Deo placeamus, et ex hoc fiat in nobis dilectio, qua et ipsi contemplari et vicissim amare Deum ipsum et Jesum Christum Dominum Nostrum possimus. Circa curam Societatis nostre, quam Semper habeo juxta quod mihi datur a Domino, ego habui quoddam desiderium quod alias quoque mihi suggestum est cum magna devotione. Desiderabam autem aliquando fieri posse ut Societas nostra ila crescere posset numero et virtutibus, in quantitate spirituali personarum, et in qualitate ipsarum, quatenus tandem restaurare valeat ruinas Religionum omnium praesentes, et futuras brevi nisi Deus averteret. Pro hac optabam ut inveniri possint innumerabiles personae saeculares et ecclesiasticae, quae relictis omnibus se vellent offerre ad obedientiam omnium quaecumque secundum Ecclesiam romanam ordinata sunt; ex quibus alii pro una Religione eligi possent et probari, et alii pro aliis. Deus det hoc fieri, et det personas quae possint probare spiritus qui a Ieo sint; quinam ad unum ordinem et statum vivendi, et quinam sint ad reliquos status apti. Det Jesus personas tam universaliter catholicas in fide, in spe, in charitate, et tam alis spiritibus dilatatas in restitutionem omnium priorum statuum in Ecclesia, ut repleri possint ad hunc modum omnia monasteria et omnium monasteriorum sedes; et denique, id quod primum in ratione finis est, ut omnes et omnium intellec- ' tus, memoriae, voluntates, corda et corpora, sanctificari et perfici in Christo Jesu valeant. Alio quodam die, dum celebrarem officium de sancto Rocho, confessore, ego sensi nonnulla circa utilitatem, veritatem, et necessitatem externi cultus Christi et sanctorum ipsius. Hinc factum est ut sentirem magnum dolorem quod haeretici adeo contemnant externas caeremonias et ritus sanctae Christi Ecclesiae, qui sunt tam necessarii ad retinendos homines in humilitate, in concordia, in charıtate, et denique in omni sanctitate religionis. Si enim vetus testamentum habuit tam varia circa sacrificia animalium irrationabilium, et reliqua caeremonialia, quae carne consummabantur, et quae omnia complenda erant in corpore Jesu Christi vero et mystico, nunquid erit contra divinam voluntatem, si in novo testamento habuerimus caeremonias et externum cultum, circa corpus ejusdem Domini Nostri et sanctorum ejus? Caeremoniae enim veteris testamenti erant figurae caeremoniarum aliarum, futurarum in novo testamento. Caeremoniae autem novi testamenti sub se continent sola spiritualia. Vetus quoque testamentum non solum adumbravit spiritum Christi, sed etiam corpus ejus sanctum. Per corporales igitur novi testamenti ritus, nos observamus id quod fuerat figuratum, et veneramur sanctitatem Christi corporati, etimitamur Christum, non tantum spiritu sed etiam corpore, quia corpora nostra templa sunt Sancti Spiritus. Ili offerebant carnem animalium, nos offerimus corpus Christi; illi lavabant carnem corporum suorum aqua materiali, ut nos intelligamus lavandum esse veterem hominem nostrum aqua spirituali. Nos igitur habemus externum cultum per quaedam sensibilia opera, tanquam complementum veteris legis et figurarum ejus, at non jam ut aliquid aliud figuremus quod in hac vita expectari debeat. Habemus quoque cultum per verba Dei ac Christi et Ecclesiae, et simul per Spiritum Sanctum. Illi igitur qui nihil curant externum cultum, Christi humanitatem non intelligunt, nec eam sanctitatem curant quae - debet esse et corporum et carnis nostrae. Nonnulla etiam habet caeremonialia nova lex, quae sunt adumbracula quorumdam pertinentium ad gloriosum et caelestem cultum divinum.
units.en: I had also some thoughts about the manner which all created things have in Christ: for if whatever is in God is God himself, it cannot but be that whatever is in Christ as regards his humanity is most beautiful; and therefore it is above all to be desired and prayed that he would deign to admit us to his memory, so that, being there, we may please God, and from this there may arise in us that love by which we too may contemplate, and in turn love, God himself and Jesus Christ Our Lord. Concerning the care of our Society, which I always carry according as it is given me by the Lord, I had a certain desire which at other times also has been suggested to me with great devotion. I desired that it might some day come about that our Society might so grow in number and in virtues, in the spiritual quantity of its persons and in their quality, that it might at last avail to restore the present ruins of all the Religious orders — and the future ones, soon to come unless God avert them. For this I wished that there might be found innumerable persons, secular and ecclesiastical, who, leaving all things, would offer themselves to the obedience of everything that is ordained according to the Roman Church; of whom some might be chosen and tested for one Religious order, and others for others. May God grant this to be done, and give persons able to test the spirits, whether they be from God — who are apt for one order and state of living, and who for the other states. May Jesus give persons so universally catholic in faith, in hope, in charity, and so enlarged by other spirits, for the restoration of all the former states in the Church, that in this way all monasteries and the seats of all monasteries may be filled again; and finally — which is first in the order of the end — that all men, and the intellects, memories, wills, hearts and bodies of all, may be sanctified and perfected in Christ Jesus. On another day, while I celebrated the office of Saint Roch the confessor, I felt some things concerning the usefulness, truth and necessity of the outward worship of Christ and of his saints. Hence it came that I felt great grief that the heretics so despise the outward ceremonies and rites of the holy Church of Christ, which are so necessary for keeping men in humility, in concord, in charity, and in short in all the holiness of religion. For if the old testament had such various things concerning the sacrifices of irrational animals, and the other ceremonial matters, which were consummated in flesh, and all of which were to be fulfilled in the true and mystical body of Jesus Christ, shall it be against the divine will if in the new testament we have ceremonies and outward worship concerning the body of the same Our Lord and of his saints? For the ceremonies of the old testament were figures of other ceremonies to come in the new testament; but the ceremonies of the new testament contain beneath them only spiritual things. The old testament, moreover, foreshadowed not only the spirit of Christ, but also his holy body. Through the bodily rites of the new testament, then, we observe that which had been prefigured, and venerate the holiness of Christ embodied, and imitate Christ not only in spirit but also in body, because our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit. They offered the flesh of animals; we offer the body of Christ. They washed the flesh of their bodies with material water, that we might understand that our old man must be washed with spiritual water. We therefore have an outward worship through certain sensible works, as the completion of the old law and of its figures — yet not so as to prefigure something else still to be awaited in this life. We have also a worship through the words of God and of Christ and of the Church, and at the same time through the Holy Spirit. Those, then, who care nothing for outward worship do not understand the humanity of Christ, nor do they care for that holiness which ought to belong to our bodies and our flesh. The new law also has some ceremonial things which are foreshadowings of certain things belonging to the glorious and heavenly divine worship.

units.la: In die sancti Gregorii Episcopi et Confessoris, summique Pontificis et Doctoris Ecclesiae, ego sensi quasdam. bonas et vivas gratiarum actiones, pro eo quod tantus Doctor et Pontifex, abundantius quam omnes alii doctores, nobis reliquerit doctrinam illam quae est necessaria pro animabus defunctorum. Nisi enim tam clare plurima ille fuisset locutus de Purgatorio et de illis quae pertinent ad levamen defunctorum, facile fieret ut adhuc plures nostris temporibus essent de tanta pietate increduli. Benedictus igitur sit Deus, qui tantum Doctorem divinitus instruxit ad hane animarum pietatem, et qui ipsis purgandis tantum dedit advocatum suum Jesum Christum. Hic ego propositum sumpsi quod vellem posthac ma- jorem quam hactenus in memoriis defunctorum habere hujus sancti Papae memoriam; et non solum habere, sed etiam praedicare; quo fiat ut qui devoti sunt hujus Sancti, devoti sint et defunctorum, et e contrario, qui devoti sunt defunctorum, meminerint in tali negotio invocare istius Pontificis auxilium.
units.en: On the day of Saint Gregory, bishop and confessor, supreme Pontiff and Doctor of the Church, I felt certain good and lively thanksgivings, because so great a Doctor and Pontiff, more abundantly than all other doctors, left us that teaching which is necessary for the souls of the departed. For had he not spoken so clearly and so much of Purgatory, and of the things that pertain to the relief of the departed, it might easily be that still more in our times would be unbelieving about so great a work of piety. Blessed therefore be God, who divinely instructed so great a Doctor for this piety towards souls, and who gave to those being purged so great an advocate, his own Jesus Christ. Here I took the resolve that I would henceforth, in my memorials of the departed, keep a greater memory of this holy Pope than hitherto; and not only keep it, but preach it; so that those who are devoted to this Saint may be devoted also to the departed, and contrariwise, that those who are devoted to the departed may remember, in that business, to invoke this Pontiff's help.

units.la: In die sancto Passionis Dominicae, ego notavi et sensi ea quae sequuntur: et primo, illud anum l adverti quod in tota Quadragesima ego fui agitatus variis motibus agitationum et spirituum, in quibus videbantur renovari plagae miseriarum mearum ac imperfectionum, quibus fiebat ut, licet vellem, nescirem tamen dolere nisi super me et super filiis meis, propter imperfectiones mei ipsius et operum meorum, quae sunt vel in ordine ad Christum, vel in ordine ad proximum, vel in ordine ad meipsum. Spiritus meus totus erat distractus a rebus in quibus jampridem novit esse pacem suam. Caro autem tota erat in illis in quibus ab ineunte aetate deprehensa est mors sua et inquietudo. Inordinationes porro actionum mearum, et torpor, et ignorantia revixisse videbantur: omnia denique mala sensa mea, que mortua pene putabantur, renasci in hac Quadra- gesima visa sunt. Merito igitur dolebam; merito ergo incessi tristis et afflictus inter tot motus, male tractantes spiritum et animam et corpus meum.
units.en: On the holy day of the Lord's Passion I noted and felt what follows: and first, I observed this one thing, that through the whole of Lent I was agitated by various motions of agitations and of spirits, in which the wounds of my miseries and imperfections seemed to be renewed; whereby it came about that, though I wished it, I yet knew not how to grieve except over myself and over my children — on account of the imperfections of myself and of my works, whether in relation to Christ, or to my neighbour, or to myself. My spirit was wholly distracted from the things in which it has long known its peace to lie; while the flesh was wholly in those things in which from my earliest age its death and unrest have been found. The disorders of my actions, moreover, and torpor, and ignorance seemed to have revived: in short, all my evil feelings, which were thought almost dead, seemed in this Lent to be born again. Justly therefore I grieved; justly I went sad and afflicted among so many motions, ill-treating my spirit and soul and body.

units.la: Dum autem venit haec dies Passionis Dominicae, et caeperam haec recolere, factum est ut non sine confortatione spiritus senserim haec omnia fuisse mihi utilia. Dies enim hic et tempus hoc de Passionibus Jesu Christi, tempus est in quo plage Christi corporales, et afflictiones, et mors, et vita plena ignominia et opprobriis rememorantur. Utile igitur fuerit quod plage meae spirituales et vestigia infirmitatum mearum nondum bene sanatarum hoc tempore quasi renoventur. Hinc factum est per gratiam Dei ut ego ex animo bene petiverim a Domino, per Jesum Christum crucifixum et mortuum, quod fiat ut tot et tantae infirmitates curari possint. Orabam ut virtus effusi in terram sanguinis Domini pacificaret sanguines meos; illos, inquam, a quibus cupio liberari, dicendo: Libera me de sanguinibus, Deus, Deus salutis meae! Orabam ut virtus carnis corporis Christi in sepulcro. positi adju- varet infirmitates carnis et corporis mei.. Orabam praeterea animam Christi, quae separata a Christi corpore descendit ad inferos, sanctificare spiritum meum et animam meam, expellendo ab ea omnem virtutem et potestatem ex qua hactenus vivificari videbar ad peccatum, id est inclinari ad male sentiendum secundum meipsum. Ad haec ego, eodem die veneris, proposui offerre sacrificium missae quam die Sabbati sequentis seram dicturus, qua possem impetrare a Deo gratiam alicujus bonae contritionis atque renovationis mei ipsius; idque per mortem Christi Jesu, qua factum est ut templum illud sanctum suum destrueretur; destrueretur, inquam, ita ut totus sanguis effusus sit, et sic remanserit in una parte corpus, in ala parte anima usque ad Resurrectionem. Hic caepi desiderare, spirituali quadam devotione et consideratione, ut fiam devotior ejus orationis qua oratur: Anima Christi, sanctifica me; corpus Christi, salva me; sanguis Christi, inebria me; aqua lateris Christi, lava me. Maxime vero tactus sum singulari quadam cognitione circa beatitudinem ac virtutem animae Christi abstractae a corpore et Divinitati conjunctae, qualem videbant sancti Patres qui erant in limbo, et illi qui purgabantur, quando descendit ad inferos. Dum etiam considerarem exanimatum corpus Christi in sepulcro, unitum tamen Divinitati, ego habui magnum desiderium, quo petebam veram quamdam exanimationem ab omni vi peccati, vanitatis et erroris, et gratiam qua possim vivificari a Deo, per Christm Dominum Nostrum qui surrexit a mortuis.
units.en: But when this day of the Lord's Passion came, and I had begun to recall these things, it came about, not without a strengthening of spirit, that I felt all this to have been useful to me. For this day, and this season of the Sufferings of Jesus Christ, is the time in which the bodily wounds of Christ, and his afflictions, and death, and a life full of ignominy and reproaches, are remembered. It was fitting, then, that my spiritual wounds, and the traces of my infirmities not yet well healed, should at this season be as it were renewed. Hence it came, by the grace of God, that from my heart I earnestly asked of the Lord, through Jesus Christ crucified and dead, that so many and so great infirmities might be healed. I prayed that the virtue of the Lord's blood poured out upon the earth might pacify my bloods — those, I mean, from which I long to be freed, saying: Deliver me from bloods, O God, God of my salvation! I prayed that the virtue of the flesh of Christ's body laid in the sepulchre might help the infirmities of my flesh and body. I prayed moreover the soul of Christ, which, separated from Christ's body, descended to the lower regions, to sanctify my spirit and my soul, driving out from it every power and force by which I have hitherto seemed to be quickened towards sin — that is, inclined to feel wrongly according to myself. To this end, on the same Friday, I resolved to offer the sacrifice of the Mass which I was to say late on the following Saturday, that I might obtain from God the grace of some good contrition and renewal of myself; and that through the death of Christ Jesus, by which it came to pass that that holy temple of his was destroyed — destroyed, I say, in such wise that all the blood was poured out, and so there remained in one place the body, in another the soul, until the Resurrection. Here I began to desire, with a certain spiritual devotion and consideration, to become more devoted to that prayer in which one prays: Soul of Christ, sanctify me; body of Christ, save me; blood of Christ, inebriate me; water from the side of Christ, wash me. But above all I was touched by a certain singular knowledge concerning the blessedness and virtue of the soul of Christ withdrawn from the body and joined to the Divinity, such as the holy Fathers saw who were in limbo, and those who were being purged, when he descended to the lower regions. And while I considered the lifeless body of Christ in the sepulchre, yet united to the Divinity, I had a great desire, in which I asked for a true un-souling from all the power of sin, of vanity and of error, and the grace by which I may be quickened by God, through Christ Our Lord who rose from the dead.

units.la: In die Sabbati quae est vigilia Paschae, ego inveni quasdam optimas considerationes circa illos duos articulos fidei: Passus sub Pontio Pilato, crucifixus, mortuus et sepultus, descendit ad inferos, tertia die resurrexit a mortuis. Datum est quoque mihi, juxta hoc, optare aliquid pati pro Christo, ferre crucem meam quotidie, peccato mori, ac mundo sepeliri in privatione omnium sensuum hujus vitae temporalis, et resurgere in novitate spiritus et carnis; ut agam secundum formam Jesu Christi Domini Nostri qui mortuus est propter peccata nòstra et resurrexit propter justificationem nostram, ut peccatis mortui, Christi justitiae vivamus; et ita vivamus, ut non jam moriamur in peccata recidendo, nec permitta- mus mortem peccati nobis ultra dominari; quia Christus resurgens ex mortuis jam non moritur. Mors illi ultra non dominabitur. In die sancto Dominicae\ Resurrectionis, ego sensi quamdam insolitam consolationem in missa; et tamen mihi non aderat sensibilis devotio illa, quam nimium frequenter ad propriam satisfactionem, et etiam ad aliorum aedificationem, appetitu quodam in quo aliquid esset de meo concupiscebam; aut saltem movebar ad concupisťendam illam inordinato aliquo impetu, inordinato, inquam, quantum ad ipsam quantitatem desiderii insurgentis.
units.en: On the Saturday which is the vigil of Easter I found certain excellent considerations concerning those two articles of the faith: Suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead and buried; he descended into hell; the third day he rose again from the dead. It was also given me, in accord with this, to desire to suffer something for Christ, to bear my cross daily, to die to sin, and to be buried to the world in the privation of all the senses of this temporal life, and to rise again in newness of spirit and flesh; that I may act after the pattern of Jesus Christ Our Lord, who died for our sins and rose for our justification, that being dead to sins we may live to the justice of Christ; and so live as not to die again by falling back into sins, nor allow the death of sin any longer to lord it over us; for Christ rising from the dead dies now no more. Death shall no more have dominion over him. On the holy day of the Lord's Resurrection I felt a certain unwonted consolation at Mass; and yet there was not present to me that sensible devotion which too frequently, for my own satisfaction and also for the edification of others, I used to covet with a certain appetite in which there was something of my own; or at least I was moved to covet it with some inordinate impulse — inordinate, I mean, as to the very quantity of the desire arising.

units.la: Hic sensi quamdam admirationem, cum satis clara. cognitione, considerando glorificationem totius humanitatis Christi Divinitati unitae. Admirabile enim est instrumentum operandi circa corporalia omnia, corpus humanum unitum Divinitati; admirabilius quoque verum principium illud corporis quod est anima rationalis, dum ipsi Divinitati immediate unitum est. Qualis enim et quantus actus ad vitam sensibilem atquerationalem est actus corporis physici, organici, omnipotentis Dei Deitati conjunctus? Spiritus autem ipse humanus, id est, eadem anima quatenus abstracta circa aeterna et spiritualia versatur, longe major apparere potest, dum consideratur et ipse cum Deo omnipotente unitus, ab ipso omnibus modis agi ac dirigi.
units.en: Here I felt a certain wonder, with a knowledge clear enough, in considering the glorification of the whole humanity of Christ united to the Divinity. For a wonderful instrument for working upon all bodily things is a human body united to the Divinity; more wonderful still that true principle of the body which is the rational soul, when it is immediately united to the Divinity itself. For what an act, and how great, towards the sensible and rational life, is the act of a physical, organic body joined to the Deity of almighty God! And the human spirit itself — that is, the same soul in so far as, withdrawn, it is occupied with things eternal and spiritual — can appear far greater, when it too is considered as united with God almighty, moved and directed by him in every way.

units.la: Hic mihi datum est ex animo orare Deum, per Jesum Christum qui resurrexit a mortuis, ut aliquando fiat per gratiam ipsius quod corpus meum et anima meå et spiritus meus glorificentur ad lau- dem ipsius, a quo, et per quem, etin quo est omnis gratia et gloria, et meum esse bonum naturale. Hic etiam optavi ut omnia corpora hominum et animae ipsorum et spiritus, quae. sunt tam capacissima vasa, sibi a Deo datis repleri possint gratiis; hocque per defluxum ab illo summo vase quod est Christi humanitas, quae capit tantam Divinitatis plenitudinem. Utinam igitur ex hac abundantia repleamur et nos per ipsam! Applicabam quatuor dotes corporis Christi glorificati ad hoc ut peterem quasdam dotes pro spiritu meo; scilicet quod per gratiam fieret ut ego ad omnia bona opera facienda et mala toleranda sim postea magis agilis, magis subtilis, magis illuminatus et clarus, et minus sensitivus malorum quod est fieri impassibilis.
units.en: Here it was given me to pray God from my heart, through Jesus Christ who rose from the dead, that some day it may come about by his grace that my body and my soul and my spirit be glorified to the praise of him, from whom, and through whom, and in whom is all grace and glory, and my good natural being. Here also I wished that all the bodies of men, and their souls and spirits, which are such most capacious vessels, might be filled with the graces given them by God; and this by an overflowing from that supreme vessel which is the humanity of Christ, which holds such fulness of the Divinity. Would that from this abundance we too might be filled through it! I applied the four endowments of the glorified body of Christ to asking certain endowments for my spirit: namely, that by grace it might come about that for the doing of all good works and the enduring of evils I might hereafter be more agile, more subtle, more illumined and clear, and less sensitive to evils — which is to become impassible.

units.la: In secúnda feria Paschae, post dictum matutinum officium, ego incidi in meam jamdiu solitam crucem, quae est tristari triplici ex causa: prima quidem quod non sentiam, prout desidero, signa divinae dilectionis erga me; secunda, quod sentiam signa veteris Adae in meipso plusquam optarem; tertia, quod non possim facere fructum quem cupio circa proximorum salutem. In his enim tribus fere concluduntur affectiones spiritus mei, proinde quod crediderim ex his constare crucem meam. Hoc igitur die, dum isthuc sic discurrissėm, ego sensi quasi responsum in meipso dicens: Tu quidem saepe optasti deponi de cruce antequam sis mortuus; Christus autem ipse in cruce sua mortuus est. Quare igitur el tu non incipies velle mori in ipsa hac cruce tua? Sed tu velles solum corripi et emendari, ut in eadem vita possis renovari. Vivificatio enim spiritus tui, quantum ad consolationes accidentales, quas tu solas concipis et sentis, illa, inquam, vivificatio tua fuit in laetitia quam accipiebas ex eo quod sentires te devotum ad Deum, et te non male inclinatum juxta veteris Adae conditiones, et dum videres aliquem fructum manuum tuarum de quo posses edere tu, et videntes opera tua bona. Nunc jam opta mori huic tuae vitae, quia nimium caduca, nimium inconstans atque. mutabilis est. Sic autem bene mori non poteris nisi per mortem crucis, huic vitae contrariam, quae est in tribus sequentibus: primo, ut ex animo in hoc obdormias quod nullam accidentalem devotionem penitus sentire optes ex proprio affectu; secundo, ut nihil velis turbari, etiamsi totus vetus homo tuus, quantus fuit unquam, in te surrexerit per suas radices et concupiscentias, quae sunt circa peccatum mortale ac veniale; tertio, in hoc quod nihil movearis, si nullus fructus externorum operum e manibus tuis deprehenditur, vel a te, vel ab aliis qui te inspiciunt ac aspiciunt ad imitandum vel gaudendum super benefactis tuis, sive ab his qui te inspiciunt ad calumniandum, sive ab his qui te despiciunt. Ubi hac morte fueris mortuus in illa cruce, publice, quantum ex affectu tuo est; ubi fueris in hoc tanquam sepultus, extra considerationem conspectus, sive respectus, sive suspicioniş, sive despectionis, aut etiam expectationis hominum quorumcumque; tune dabitur desiderare saltem atque instituere novam aliquam formam consolationis tui spiritus, ex qua senties aliam quamdam vitam per resurrectionem corporis, animae, ac spiritus; aliam, inquam, vitam cujus radix et ipse fructus, et folia et frondes non ejusdem conditionis erunt; sed permänentius unum quodque per se in uno eodem statu. invenietur, Tu hactenus plas consolationis in magnitudine arboris, quae procedit ex*divina gratia, quam in radice ipsius in qua est potissima virtus, quaesivisti; ad frondes attendebas, ad folia, ad flores et ad fructus, quorum omnium maxima pars mutabilis est, quia tendunt ad perfectionem. - Hinc fit ut non possit esse constans ac firma consolatio.
