Noli igitur radicem hujus arboris quaerere propter fructus illos; sed potius fructus et reliqua propter radicem. Quaere permanentem majoremque in dies ac majorem radicationem tui ad radices hujus arboris, non autem ita permanentem ipsius fructum in te: non enim per viam fructus venies ad gloriam arboris, sed potius per viam radicis. Appone igitur ad radicem quicquid poteris; quia aliquando radix ipsa apparebit glorificata; sicut primum apparuit glorificata, intra ipsam terram, dum descendit ad inferos Christi anima, vera radix creata, quae facta est summus omnium creaturarum rationabilium fructus gloriosus. Sicque inversa est arbor haec, ut radix in summum locum venerit, dimissis omnibus fructibus sub se, influens virlutem suam a superioribus ad inferiora. In futuris igitur bonis gloriae Dei, id est, bonis coelestibus, illud erit secundum quod fructus ipse qui est radix vera et glorificata, ille, inquam, fructus melior erit quam reliquum corpus arboris, cum sit conditio illius vitae bealae, ut in eo quod per essentiam: melius est majores quoque fructus et meliora accidentia collocentur: Sed non ita est in hac vita misera, quae requirit ut quae meliora sunt, illa magis sint cooperta laboribus, magisque obtecta, sicut accidit in radice qualibet; quod cum per essentiam melior sit, non tam perfectiora habet accidentia, sed potius magis imperfecta. Si ergo quaeris fructus, quaere illos qui sunt alterius vitae; ita tamen ut nobis prius sit sentire accidentia talium fructuum, quam accidentia earum sanctarum radicum; quae tamen suni glorificandae, et in fructum commutandae.
units.en: On Easter Monday, after the morning office was said, I fell into my long-accustomed cross, which is to be sad for a threefold cause: first, that I do not feel, as I desire, the signs of the divine love towards me; second, that I feel the signs of the old Adam in myself more than I would wish; third, that I cannot produce the fruit I long for in the salvation of my neighbours. For in these three are contained almost all the affections of my spirit, so that I have believed my cross to consist of them. On this day, then, when I had run over these things thus, I felt as it were an answer within myself, saying: You indeed have often wished to be taken down from the cross before you are dead; but Christ himself died on his cross. Why then will not you too begin to will to die on this your cross? But you would wish only to be corrected and amended, that you might be renewed in the same life. For the quickening of your spirit, as regards the accidental consolations, which alone you conceive and feel — that quickening of yours lay in the gladness you received from feeling yourself devoted to God, and not ill-inclined after the conditions of the old Adam, and when you saw some fruit of your hands of which you might eat, you and those who saw your good works. Now, rather, desire to die to this life of yours, because it is too perishable, too inconstant and changeable. And you cannot die well in this way except by the death of the cross, contrary to this life, which lies in the three things following: first, that you fall asleep from the heart in this — that you desire to feel absolutely no accidental devotion from your own affection; second, that you be willing to be troubled by nothing, even if the whole of your old man, at his greatest, should rise up in you by his roots and concupiscences, which concern mortal and venial sin; third, that you be moved by nothing, if no fruit of outward works is found coming from your hands — whether by yourself, or by others who watch you and look to you, to imitate you or to rejoice over your good deeds, or by those who watch you to calumniate, or by those who despise you. When by this death you shall have died on that cross, publicly, so far as your affection goes; when you shall have been in this as it were buried, beyond consideration of the sight, or regard, or suspicion, or contempt, or even the expectation of any men whatsoever — then it will be given you at least to desire, and to establish, some new form of consolation of your spirit, from which you shall feel another kind of life through the resurrection of body, soul and spirit; another life, I say, whose root, and fruit itself, and leaves and branches will not be of the same condition as before; but each one, abiding more permanently in itself, will be found in one and the same state. Hitherto you have sought more consolation in the greatness of the tree, which proceeds from divine grace, than in its root, in which is the chief virtue; you attended to the branches, the leaves, the flowers and the fruits, the greatest part of all of which is changeable, because they tend towards perfection. Hence it comes that consolation cannot be constant and firm. Do not, then, seek the root of this tree for the sake of those fruits, but rather the fruits and the rest for the sake of the root. Seek a permanent and daily greater rooting of yourself into the roots of this tree, and not so much its permanent fruit in you: for it is not by the way of the fruit that you will come to the glory of the tree, but rather by the way of the root. Apply then to the root whatever you can; for one day the root itself will appear glorified — as it first appeared glorified, within the earth itself, when the soul of Christ descended to the lower regions, the true created root, which became the supreme glorious fruit of all rational creatures. And thus this tree has been inverted, so that the root has come to the highest place, all its fruits left beneath it, pouring its virtue from the things above to the things below. In the future goods, then, of the glory of God — that is, in the heavenly goods — this will hold: that the fruit itself, which is the true and glorified root, will be better than the rest of the body of the tree; since it is the condition of that blessed life that in what is by essence better, the greater fruits and the better accidents should also be placed. But it is not so in this wretched life, which requires that the things which are better be the more covered over with labours and the more hidden, as happens with any root; which, though by essence better, has not the more perfect accidents, but rather the more imperfect. If therefore you seek fruits, seek those which are of the other life; yet so that we must first feel the accidents of such fruits, before the accidents of those holy roots — which are nevertheless to be glorified, and changed into fruit.

units.la: Alio quodam die infra has octavas Paschae, dum primum inciperem habitare domum quam conduxi, ego habui varia sensa mentis et spiritus, circa: desiderium prosperi ingressus in illam novam habitationem. Hic ego, in singulis habitaculis et diverticulis domus, genibus flexis, oravi orationem illam: Visita quaesumus, Do- mine, habitationem istam; et omnes insidias inimici ab ea longe repelle; Angeli tui sancti habitent in ea, qui nos in pace custodiant; et benedictio tua sit super nos semper. Per Christum Dominum Nostrum. Hoe feci cum bona devotione, sentiens quod esset conveniens et bonum ita fieri, quando de novo quemlibet locum ingredimvur. Angelos praeterea bonos qui sunt custodes vicinorum hujus domus ego invocavi, et sensi quod hoc quoque est conveniens et bonum, dum sic transitur in aliquam viciniam. Optabam etiam orando ut nec mihi, nec mecum habitaturis, nocere valeant mali spiritus vicinorum; maxime autem spiritus fornicationis, quos non dubium est esse cum meretricibus et fornicatoribus, caeterisque turpibus personis quales audivi esse in hac vicinia. Invocavi etiam sanctam Otiliam, sanctum Jodocum, et sanctam Luciam, quibus dicata est capella domui ei quam conduzi propinqua. Ubi sensi varios tactus doloris spiritus, videns dictam capellam ita destructam, et quodammodo, propter fornicationes varias transeuntium per viam, conspurcatam. Ex hoc factum est ut senserim magna desideria circa reparationem ipsius, et circa resuscitationem cultus divini in praedictis sanctis, quorum nulla est in supradicta capella devota commemoratio, aut memoria pietatis in illos; cum tamen olim aibi fuerit maxima devotio et fides i in praesidium ipsorum. Ego celebravi missam applicans ipsam in hoc ut esset remedium contra peccata circa defec- tum hujusmodi cultus facta, et simul ut restitui posset et reparari. Utinam Deus, per intercessionem eorum sanctorum et omnium aliorum, istam det mihi gratiam, ut possim aliquid in tali reparatione, tam in eo quod visibile ac manifestum est, quam in eo quod est spirituale. Eodem die sub noctem, dum primum mihi in ipsa domo esset dormiendum, et sensissem, nescio quam corporalem mutationem, et nescio quam miseriam in corpore meo, ex qua oriebatur quaedam tristitia in spiritu, ego incepi rogare Dominum ut daret mihi prosperitatem aeris domus, aut (si voluntas ipsius magis id fieri vellet) quicquid cogitationis mihi expediret; proximis autem, et hospiti, et vicinis omnibus, ego ex animo devoto petivi omnem prosperitatem aeris, totius viciniae defensionem a morbis et caeteris malis, et denique ut meus adventus ad ipsos omnibus modis ipsis vicinis prosper et faustus esse posset. Praeservationes quoque ubique a caeteris incommodis, quae nunquam nisi justa de causa demittuntur aut permittuntur, optavi nobis fieri, in fructu meritorum sanctae Luciae. Unum datum est, circa istam materiam, cum gratiarum actione cogitare: id est, cum tot et varia hospitia ego mutaverim, in toto tempore vitae meae, satis peregrinae juxta Dei (ut credo) nutum, et propter quem solum tot hospitia, ex quo meipsum novi, habitavi; considerans itaque tantam hospitiorum mutationem (haec autem non fuit quia vel quaererem commodiora corpori meo, vel quia fugerem incommoda) gratias Deo agebam quod nunquam mihi contigisset hactenus, propter talem mutationem, vel mori, vel infirmari, aut male habere; et tamen fieri non potest quin perfrequenter ego inciderim in loca variis periculis corporalibus affecta et subjecta. Fui enim saepe in hospitalibus parum mundis, saepius in diversoriis pessimae habitationis, quandoque etiam in multo frigore, quandoque in loco ubi praeter tectum domus, vel faenum, vel paleas, nihil erat. Sed et mihi contigit sub dio dormire. Qui igitur in habitationibus èt caeteris ejusdem conditionis ac differentiae conservat, ipse sit benedictus in saecula. Pro his gratias agebam, sperans quod in hac nova habitatione mihi non esset defuturus; et quum mihi voluerit adesse per mortem, non minus propter hoc bonum mihi volet Deus vitae et mortis adesse, quam pro reliquis bonis quae de manu ejus hactenus suscepi.
units.en: On another day within this octave of Easter, when I first began to inhabit the house which I had rented, I had various movements of mind and spirit, in the desire of a prosperous entry into that new dwelling. Here, in each room and corner of the house, on bended knees, I prayed that prayer: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling; and drive far from it all the snares of the enemy; let thy holy Angels dwell in it, to keep us in peace; and let thy blessing be upon us always. Through Christ Our Lord. This I did with good devotion, feeling that it is fitting and good so to do whenever we enter any place anew. Moreover I invoked the good Angels who are the guardians of the neighbours of this house, and felt that this too is fitting and good when one thus passes into some neighbourhood. I wished also, in prayer, that the evil spirits of the neighbours might not be able to harm me, or those who were to dwell with me; above all the spirits of fornication, which without doubt dwell with the harlots and fornicators and other base persons such as I have heard are in this neighbourhood. I invoked also Saint Ottilia, Saint Judoc, and Saint Lucy, to whom is dedicated the chapel near the house I rented. There I felt various touches of grief of spirit, seeing that chapel so ruined, and in a manner defiled through the various fornications of those passing along the road. From this it came that I felt great desires for its repair, and for the revival of divine worship towards those saints, of whom there is in that chapel no devout commemoration, nor any memorial of piety towards them; though of old there was there the greatest devotion and faith in their protection. I celebrated Mass, applying it to be a remedy against the sins committed through the failure of such worship, and at the same time that it might be restored and repaired. May God, through the intercession of those saints and of all the others, give me the grace to be able to do something in such a reparation, both in what is visible and manifest and in what is spiritual. On the same day at nightfall, when I was first to sleep in that house, and had felt I know not what bodily change, and I know not what misery in my body, from which arose a certain sadness in spirit, I began to beg the Lord to give me wholesome air in the house, or (if his will preferred) whatever thought might be expedient for me; and for my neighbours, and my host, and all the neighbourhood, I asked from a devout heart all wholesomeness of air, the defence of the whole neighbourhood from diseases and other evils, and finally that my coming to them might be in every way prosperous and fortunate for those neighbours. I wished also that preservations from other misfortunes — which are never sent or permitted except for a just cause — might everywhere be granted us, in the fruit of the merits of Saint Lucy. One thing was given me to think over, in this matter, with thanksgiving: namely, that having changed so many and various lodgings in the whole time of my life — a life sufficiently that of a pilgrim, according, as I believe, to God's good pleasure, for whose sake alone I have dwelt in so many lodgings since I came to know myself — considering, then, so great a changing of lodgings (and it was not because I sought greater comfort for my body, or fled discomforts), I gave thanks to God that it had never yet befallen me, through such change, to die, or fall sick, or fare ill; and yet it cannot be but that I have very often come into places touched and subject to various bodily dangers. For I have often been in hospices none too clean, more often in inns of the worst lodging, sometimes in great cold, sometimes in a place where besides the roof there was nothing but hay or straw; and it has befallen me even to sleep under the open sky. He therefore who preserves me in dwellings and in all else of the same condition and variety — blessed be he for ever. For these things I gave thanks, hoping that in this new dwelling he would not fail me; and when it shall be his will to be present to me through death, God of life and death will be no less willing to be present to me for that good, than for the other goods which I have hitherto received from his hand.

units.la: Hic quoque oravi pro omnibus quibus vel contigerit hactenus, vel posthac continget divertere vel demorari, in quocumque locorum eorum ubi aliquando vel me recepi, vel fui receptus, ad divertendum, aut habitandum, aut orandum. Deus meus qui sentire ac desiderare haec et şimilia dedit, omnia dignetur implere secundum vocem Verbi sui sancti, et sancti sui Spiritus, non autem ad libram mearum propriarum cogitationum ac juxta sensum mei proprii spiritus. Eodem die, dum scriberem ad comitissam a Monfor et ad dominum Vicarium 1n spiritualibus Reverendissimi Epicopi Spirensis, ego intellexi quaedam, et ea primum sensi, circa resurrectionem quae nondum contigerat. Haec autem fuerunt quaedam documenta sumpta ex eo quod animae nostre prius beatae futurae sint extra corpus, sicut et Christus apparuit prius beatus in spiritu quam in corpore glorificatus. Dum enim consideramus animam nostram posse esse, imo et de facto futuram esse beatam absque suo corpore et extra ipsum, facilius spernimus ipsa corpora, et melius sentimus quod non sumus debitores carni ut secundum ipsius voluntatem vivamus; clarius agnoscimus non ita studendum esse corporis necessitatibus ut fit, quia ipsum, non tam necessarium -sit nobis quam credere videmur propter operam quam carni inpendimus quasi sine illo, nec beati esse possimus nec miseri; cum tamen e contra contingat, id est, quosdam esse prius beatos in anima, et non per corpuš, aut in ipso, sive cum ipso; quosdam vero esse miseros ac infelices, cum nondum resumpserint corpora sua. Faxit igitur Jesus qui mortuus est, et qui primum sanctos patres beatificavit antequam resurrexisset a mortuis, faxit, inquam, ut nos jam discamus vivere vitam spiritus separati a corpore: non miseram illam quae est in male cogitando, memorando, appetendo; sed contrariam illam, secundum quam sentit per tres ipsius animae potentias, memoriam, voluntatem et intellectum.
units.en: Here too I prayed for all those who either have hitherto happened, or shall hereafter happen, to turn aside or stay in any of those places where I have at any time either taken myself in, or been received, to lodge, or dwell, or pray. May my God, who gave me to feel and desire these and like things, deign to fulfil them all according to the voice of his holy Word and of his holy Spirit — not by the scales of my own thoughts, nor according to the sense of my own spirit. On the same day, while I wrote to the Countess of Montfort and to the lord Vicar in spirituals of the Most Reverend Bishop of Speyer, I understood certain things — and felt them then for the first time — concerning the resurrection which has not yet come to pass. These were certain lessons drawn from the fact that our souls are to be blessed first outside the body, as Christ too appeared blessed in spirit before he was glorified in body. For when we consider that our soul can be — nay, in fact will be — blessed without its body and outside it, we more easily despise the bodies themselves, and feel better that we are not debtors to the flesh, to live according to its will; we recognize more clearly that we ought not to study the body's needs as is commonly done, since it is not so necessary to us as we seem to believe — judging by the labour we spend upon the flesh — as though without it we could be neither blessed nor wretched; whereas the contrary happens: that is, some are blessed first in soul, and not through the body, or in it, or with it; and some are wretched and unhappy before they have taken up their bodies again. May Jesus, then, who died, and who first beatified the holy fathers before he rose from the dead — may he grant that we now learn to live the life of a spirit separated from the body: not that wretched life which lies in thinking, remembering, desiring evil; but that contrary life, according to which it feels through the three powers of the soul itself — memory, will and intellect.

units.la: In die sancti Georgii martyris, dum dicerem missam in ecclesia sancti Christophori, et facerem memoriam cujusdam personae tunc recens defunctae, cujus depositionis dies primus -celebrabatur, ego magnam sensi consolationem, in quadam. viva apprehensione glorificationis' animarum per Christum faciendae. Particulariter illam Christi sentiebam liberalitatem, quam ostendit suis, super operibus suis quae fecerunt, reddendo praemia unicuique juxta opera sua quae fuerunt in fide ipsius. Non poterit enim non magnum esse praemium cujuslibet cperis facti in gratia. Eorum namque quae non fuerunt facta in gratia Christi, nulla in eo loco ipse habebit praemia a Deo; cum ipse omnipotens debeat illa ponderare et aestimare juxta charitatem et liberalitatem suae humanitatis, et praemiare per infinitam suam potentiam divinitatis. Quia enim Christi infinita humilitas est, fieri non potest ut quantumlibet minima opera facta ïn gratia obliviscatur; quia vero simul in infinitum dives est, non potest non munificentissime praemiare. Hic sensi quemdam bonum dolorem, ex eo quod his temporibus sic detractum est bonis operibus, quodque nulla jam ferme sit mentio praemiorum bonorum operum: ex quo sequitur quod neque malorum operum retributionem timeant. Sic tollitur spes inveniendi ea quae in lacrymis seminantur; et tollitur metus peccatorum singulorum, quia non videtur paena tali peccato respondens. In summa, dum tollitur respectus eorum quae corporaliter, sive bene, sive male, exercentur, ab hominibus quoque tollitur notitia Humanitatis divinae; quia ideo par incarnationem apparuit, ut salus nostra humaniter perageretur per Christum Deum et hominem, qui judicaturus est vivos et mortuos, et recogniturus ea quae quisque gesserit in corpore, in Humanitate illa in qua ascendens in coelum visus est, juxta illud: Sic veniet quemadmodum vidistis illum ascendentem in caelum. Quidquid igitur humanae gratitudinis, et gratiae, et liberalitatis, in homi- nibus mortalibus intelligi potest erga servos et officiales, hoc ipsum convenientissime debet credi.
units.en: On the day of Saint George the martyr, while I said Mass in the church of Saint Christopher and made memorial of a certain person then lately dead, whose first day of burial was being kept, I felt great consolation, in a certain lively apprehension of the glorification of souls which Christ is to accomplish. In particular I felt that liberality of Christ which he shows to his own over the works they have done, rendering rewards to each according to his works done in faith in him. For the reward of any work done in grace cannot fail to be great. Whereas of the works not done in the grace of Christ, he will there hold no rewards from God; since he, the almighty, must weigh and value them according to the charity and liberality of his humanity, and reward them through the infinite power of his divinity. For because the humility of Christ is infinite, it cannot be that he should forget even the least works done in grace; and because he is at the same time infinitely rich, he cannot but reward most munificently. Here I felt a certain good grief, that in these times good works have been so disparaged, and that there is now hardly any mention of the rewards of good works; from which it follows that men do not fear the retribution of evil works either. Thus the hope of finding what is sown in tears is taken away; and the fear of individual sins is taken away, because no pain is seen answering to such a sin. In sum, when regard for what is done in the body, whether well or ill, is taken away, the knowledge of the divine Humanity is also taken from men; for he appeared through the incarnation precisely that our salvation might be humanly accomplished through Christ, God and man, who is to judge the living and the dead, and to acknowledge what each has done in the body — in that Humanity in which he was seen ascending into heaven, according to the word: He shall so come as you have seen him going into heaven. Whatever therefore of human gratitude, and graciousness, and liberality can be conceived in mortal men towards their servants and officers, this same is most fittingly to be believed of him.

units.la: Clarum est autem unum aliquem mortalem principem posse mirabiliter consolari unum ex minimis servis suis, ex sola consideratione operis ipsius, ita ut ille servus, in magno gaudio suo, rapiatur in admirationem quamdam ex tanto sui principis respectu, quem habuerit ad hujusmodi opera, quae alioquin servus ille nihili faciebat.
units.en: Now it is clear that some mortal prince can wonderfully console one of the least of his servants by his mere consideration of the servant's work; so that that servant, in his great joy, is caught up into a kind of wonder at the great regard his prince has had for works which the servant himself otherwise counted as nothing.

units.la: Quare igitur tam male nobiscum agitur ut non praedicetur in Christo humana sed divina huma- nitatis suae conditio? Aut quare tolluntur similes comparationes et similitudines inter Deum et homines, dum non tollitur ab ipso nostra caro quam assumpsit? Ipse voluit esse in nobis corporaliter, factus servus ei cui erat aequalis, ut nos in nostra vilitate nati, Dei similitudinem nobis promissam facilius crederemus, et sic eorum rationem melius teneremus, habentes Deum et hominem quem colimus ut Deum nostrum, et cui servire debeamus non solum spiritualiter ut spiritui, sed etiam corporaliter ut corporato Domino Nostro, homini simili nobis in natura in qua passus est, in qua nunc regnat sedens ad dexteram Dei Patris omnipotentis. Quam equidem naturam nostram, a Deo sic exaltatam, oportet ut nos veneremur in sanctitate et justitia, videntes illam esse Divinitatis perfectum instrumentum, ad redemptionem nostram, ad vocationem, justificationem, sanctificationem et glorificationem, quae est et templum totius Divinīitatis.
units.en: Why then are we so ill served, that there is preached in Christ not the human but only the divine condition of his humanity? Or why are such comparisons and likenesses between God and men taken away, so long as our flesh, which he assumed, is not taken from him? He willed to be among us bodily, made a servant to him to whom he was equal, so that we, born in our lowliness, might more easily believe the likeness of God promised to us, and so hold their meaning better, having a God and man whom we worship as our God, and whom we ought to serve not only spiritually as spirit, but also bodily as our embodied Lord — a man like ourselves in the nature in which he suffered, in which he now reigns, sitting at the right hand of God the Father almighty. And this our nature, so exalted by God, we ought to venerate in holiness and justice, seeing that it is the perfect instrument of the Divinity for our redemption, our calling, justification, sanctification and glorification, and that it is also the temple of the whole Divinity.

units.la: Luminis Angelus noluit descendere sub istam naturam, ut sic descendens, per Humanitatem, ut medium, esset subjectus Altissimo; sed voluit propria virtute intrare in gaudium et in gloriam Domini Dei sui. Propositum est illi mysterium ab aeterno ordinatum, id est, Filii Dei humilitas, qua ab aeterno voluit et decrevit fieri homo, et hoc pacto humiliari sub eo qui ipsum ab aeterno genuit sibi aequalem. Lucifer supra se abiit, quia noluit se humiliare sub humanatum Deum, qui est Christus, ex summo factus minimus. Ille igitur, dum per fidem et gratiam, in qua creatus est, non vult humiliari usque sub hanc naturam assumendam, destituitur - gratia fidei suae, supra se abeundo, dicens: Ascendam et ero similis Altissimo; qui ascensus fut illi ruina et descensus.
units.en: The Angel of light would not descend beneath that nature, so that, thus descending, he might through the Humanity, as a means, be subject to the Most High; but he wished by his own power to enter into the joy and glory of the Lord his God. There was set before him the mystery ordained from eternity: that is, the humility of the Son of God, who from eternity willed and decreed to become man, and in this manner to be humbled under him who from eternity begot him equal to himself. Lucifer went above himself, because he would not humble himself under the God made man, who is Christ, made least from being highest. He therefore, while by the faith and grace in which he was created he refuses to be humbled even beneath this nature that was to be assumed, is stripped of the grace of his faith, going above himself and saying: I will ascend, and I will be like the Most High — which ascent became to him ruin and descent.

units.la: In die sancti Marci evangeliste, mane ante missam quam eram celebraturus, ego sensi quemdam spiritum deorsum ducentem; et cum subintraverit in me tristitia propter hujusmodi motum, dolui usque ad lacrymas, quod in carne mea esset adhuc occasio ejusmodi agitationum, quas parere posset spiritus ille cujus proprium est movere spiritum nostrum retrorsum, et carnem deorsum. Petivi igitur in spiritu compunc- tionis a Domino, id quod alias saepe cognovi h o A AT a a esse ad remedium verum talium tentationum, ut det mihi gratiam qua fiat ut sim conversus in ea bona quae ante me restant, et supra me; et si quidem dolendum sit et oporteat, magis compungar propter defectus virtutum quae desunt, quam propter defectus commissionis eorum, quae sunt in sensibus, peccatorum; id est, ut ista desideria, quae sunt ad perfectionem, me ita occupent in sui acquisitione vel inquisitione, ut non restet locus memoriae eorum quae vel deorsum ducunt vel retrorsum. Hic etiam clare cognovi, sicut et alias. frequentissime, quam sit necessarium ut, per desiderium cognoscendi et sentiendi, apprehendantur varii gradus nondum possessi; inque apprehensis, simus in continuo motu ad illa bona habenda, vel pacifice possidenda; non quia velimus ibi quiescere, sed quia hoc modo quaeramus nobis stabilire gradus ad ascensum nostrum. Proficiendum est autem tripliciter, juxta triplicem modum virtutum: primo, quantum ad ea quae sunt divinae cognitionis et affectuum qui ad ipsum Deum directe spectant, etc.; secundo, quantum ad illa quae tan- gunt proximum. Clarum est enim quotidie nos indigere novis cognitionibus et novis et renovatis affectibus, circa proximorum nostrorum utilitatem et necessitatem spiritualem, et etiam corporalem. Ex his omnibus autem resultat profectus noster, licet non debeamus praetendere ex illis nostram perfectionem, sed potius hanc desiderare et hanc ordinare ad ipsum Deum, et propter Deum ad ipsum proximum. Sed quoniam in nostra ipsorum perfectione necessario includitur: expoliatio veteris hominis, et non solum indumenta novi hominis, ideo (velimus, nolimus) quia expedit, habendae erunt tentationes et stimuli in spiritu et in carne; et non solum tentationes illae et illi stimuli qui nos excitant et aptant ad ea quae sunt virtutis et pacis, sed etiam quae sunt ad mortem et ad peccata; alioquin nesciremus videre arenam nostram, super quam aedificari nos contingeret, Christo lapide in nobis nondum posito, qui non potest formari nisi vetus fuerit evacuatus. Hoc igitur patienter. ferènńdum erit; et juxta quod supra dictum est, nitendum erit nobis, omnibus viribus nostris, ad ea quae restant; et patiendum erit, dum per- miserit Dominus, stimulos peccatorum. Sed quo- niam haec non ita observantur, ideo non sunt curandae hujusmodidistinctiones terminorum, quia sunt novae nec usitatae apud doctores positivos aut etiam scholasticos.
units.en: On the day of Saint Mark the evangelist, in the morning before the Mass I was to celebrate, I felt a certain spirit leading downward; and when sadness crept into me because of that motion, I grieved even to tears that in my flesh there should still be occasion for such agitations as that spirit can breed whose property it is to move our spirit backward and our flesh downward. I asked therefore, in a spirit of compunction, from the Lord — what I have often at other times known to be the true remedy of such temptations — that he give me the grace to be turned towards those goods which remain before me and above me; and if grief there must be, that I be pricked rather for the lack of the virtues that are wanting, than for the faults of commission of those sins which are in the senses; that is, that those desires which are towards perfection may so occupy me in their acquisition or pursuit, that no room be left for the memory of the things that lead downward or backward. Here also I clearly knew, as at other times most frequently, how necessary it is that, through the desire of knowing and feeling, various degrees not yet possessed be apprehended; and that, once apprehended, we be in continual motion towards having those goods, or peacefully possessing them; not that we would rest there, but that in this way we may seek to establish for ourselves steps for our ascent. And progress must be made in three ways, according to the threefold manner of the virtues: first, as to the things of divine knowledge and of the affections which look directly to God himself, and so forth; second, as to the things that touch our neighbour. For it is clear that we daily need new knowledge, and new and renewed affections, concerning the profit and the spiritual — and also bodily — need of our neighbours. From all these results our progress; although we ought not to claim our perfection from them, but rather to desire it, and to order it towards God himself, and for God's sake towards our neighbour. But since in our own perfecting there is necessarily included the stripping off of the old man, and not only the putting on of the new, therefore (will we, nill we), because it is expedient, temptations and stings must be had in spirit and in flesh; and not only those temptations and stings which rouse and fit us for the things of virtue and peace, but also those which are towards death and sins; otherwise we should not know how to see our own sand, upon which we should be found building, the stone Christ not yet laid in us — who cannot be formed unless the old has been emptied out. This, then, must be borne patiently; and, as was said above, we must strive with all our strength towards the things that remain; and we must suffer, so long as the Lord permits, the stings of sins. But since these things are not commonly so treated, one need not trouble about such distinctions of terms, for they are new and not in use among the positive or even the scholastic doctors.

units.la: Cavendum est autem maxime ne recedamus a communi modo loquendi Doctórum catholicorum, nec est multiplicanda lectio librorum, praesertim sacrorum, secundum spiritus multiplicationes, cum sciamus eamdem lectionem capere varios spiritus. Quod si unusquisque studeat facere scripturas et scribere libros. juxta terminos suarum conceptionum, hine erunt, prout jam sunt, infinitae sectae doctrinarum, infiniti modi definiendi res, et ipsas sacras, et dividendi et distinguendi. Opus igitur est ut trahamus, non Scripturas jam approbatas ad nostros terminos, sed nostros terminos ad ipsas. Quidquidautem sensus spiritualis et quicquid spiritus reduci non poterit ad Ecclesiae catholicae doctrinam et Doctores approbatos, hoc non erit recipiendum.
units.en: But we must beware above all of departing from the common manner of speaking of the catholic Doctors; nor is the writing of books to be multiplied — especially of sacred ones — according to the multiplications of the spirit, since we know that the same reading receives various spirits. For if each one should set himself to make writings and compose books according to the terms of his own conceptions, there will arise, as there already are, infinite sects of doctrines, infinite ways of defining things — even sacred things — and of dividing and distinguishing them. There is need, then, that we draw not the Scriptures already approved to our terms, but our terms to them. And whatever spiritual sense, and whatever spirit, cannot be brought back to the doctrine of the catholic Church and the approved Doctors, is not to be received.

units.la: In die sanctorum martyrum et pontificum Cleti et Marcellini, post dictum officium matutinum, ego inveni magnam quamdam devotionem,: considerando misericordiam Christi, quafactum est ut sanctus pontifex Marcellinus, qui timore mortis semel conversus fuisset ad cultum idolorum, statim redierit ad cor christianissimi martyris, sicque mercedem et coronam martyris acceperit.
units.en: On the day of the holy martyrs and pontiffs Cletus and Marcellinus, after the morning office was said, I found a certain great devotion, considering the mercy of Christ, by which it came about that the holy pontiff Marcellinus, who through fear of death had once turned to the worship of idols, straightway returned to the heart of a most christian martyr, and so received the reward and crown of a martyr.

units.la: Hic mihi datus est quidam bonus spiritus ad deplorandum varias retrocessiones et retrospectiones et. retroventiones meas, quas nunquam satis deploraveram. Coepi etiam mirari quamdam Dei erga me sive misericordiam, sive. justitiam, quae in hoc fuit quod aut raro aut nunquam senserim Spiritum ipsius sanctum me arguen- tem, minantem mihi debitas paenas, aut impro- perantem mihi peccata mea ac defectus; sed quod - ita fecerit ut reprehensiones quas communiter in meipso hactenus contra me audivi ac sensi, fuerint vel per propriam conscientiam, vel per spiritum ad exercitium mihi datum. Hinc igitur mihi datum est ex animo petere ac velle quaerere gratiam hane ab ipso Altissimo, quae est ut jam deinceps possim sentire verba ac correctiones. quae a. Spiritu ipsius sunt. Dicebam ad hoc:' Domine Deus meus, hactenus videris tacuisse super peccatis meis praeteritis, et super "oO ee N praesentibus defectibus et imperfectionibus; videris mihi adhuc nullum werbum de ore tui ipsius protulisse ad animam meam et ad cor meum, super materiam peccatorum, cum tamen multis jam modis me docueris facere bona et sequi consilia tua. Incipe igitur a principio, et novo quodam modo, id est, immediate per Spi-- ritum tuum, suggerere mihi verba et" sensa verae ac perfectae contritionis; move animum ad deplorandum peccata mea in tuo Spiritu, sicut hactenus dedisti deplorare per alios spiritus. Sensi autem hoc desiderium, non occasione aliqua gravaminis peccatorum; aut quia sentirem remordentem me conscientiam, quasi non esset satis pacata et quieta, sed quia sentiebam illum altiorem Spiritum Dei in me; in quo ego optabam denuo ab initio renovari me, ad novum sensum circa peccata, et circa ipsius Dei offensi cognitionem.
units.en: Here a certain good spirit was given me for bewailing my various goings-back, lookings-back and turnings-back, which I had never sufficiently bewailed. I began also to wonder at a certain mercy — or justice — of God towards me, which lay in this: that rarely or never have I felt his holy Spirit accusing me, threatening me with the pains I deserve, or upbraiding me with my sins and defects; but that he has so ordered it that the reproofs which I have commonly heard and felt in myself against myself have come either through my own conscience, or through the spirit given me for my exercise. Hence it was given me to ask from my heart, and to wish to seek from the Most High himself, this grace: that from now on I may feel the words and corrections which are from his Spirit. To this end I said: Lord my God, hitherto you seem to have kept silence over my past sins, and over my present defects and imperfections; you seem as yet to have uttered no word from your own mouth to my soul and to my heart on the matter of my sins, although you have already in many ways taught me to do good and to follow your counsels. Begin therefore from the beginning, and in a certain new way — that is, immediately through your Spirit — to suggest to me the words and feelings of true and perfect contrition; move my soul to bewail my sins in your Spirit, as hitherto you have given me to bewail them through other spirits. And I felt this desire not by occasion of any burden of sins, nor because I felt conscience gnawing me, as though it were not sufficiently pacified and quiet, but because I felt that higher Spirit of God in me; in which I wished to be renewed anew from the beginning, to a new sense concerning sins, and concerning the knowledge of God himself offended.

units.la: Alio quodam die, dum visitassem magistrum Petram Gueldriensem, qui exercebatur juxta modum Exercitiorum nostrorum, ego habui quaedam argumenta magnae evidentiae, quibus clarius quam unquam intellexi quam plurimum. referre ad discretionem spitituum, an cogitationes ac locutiones internas attendamus, an ad ipsum spiritum, quiper desideria, per affectus, per fortitudinem animi vel debilitatem, per tranquillitatem, vel, inquietudinem, per laetitiam vel tristitiam, et similes affectus spirituales sese prodere solet. Per haec sane facilius judicari potest de anima et ejus spiritibus, quam per ipsas cogitationes. Quidam autem sunt, qui per multas ac varias diversorum. exercitiorum spiritualium contemplationes aut orationes, vix possunt deprehendere varietatem spirituum diversorum, sedsemper videntur agitari uno et eodem spiritu, licet hoc fiat secundum magis ac minus. Efficacissimum autem medium, ad excitandum hanc distinctionem, est propositio electionis vitae et status; deinde in eodem varii gradus ad perfectionem tendentes; et generaliter quo quis altiorem, ad agendum, vel sperandum, vel credendum aut amandum, rem proposuerit, vel ad ipsam sese applicuerit affectualiter et effectualiter, eo facilius dederit argumenta excitandi differentiam spiritus boni ac mali. In quibusdam quo- que ideo non agnoscitur spiritus malus, et maxime in piis et diu versatis in devotione et extra peccata, quia non habeant cogitationes extra limites veritatis et bonitatis, neque affectus manifeste inordinatos. Hos tamen, quantumlibet sancti sint, si induxeris ut sese examinent 1n aliquo gradu perfectioris vitae ac conversationis, in. statu proprio (si immutabilis fuerit) aut inalio statu magis perfecto, facile erit videre utrumque ipsorum spirituum, confortatorem ac debilitatorem, illuminatorem ac offuscatorem, justificatorem ac maculatorem, id est, bonum et eum (qui est bono adversarius.
units.en: On another day, when I had visited Master Peter of Guelders, who was exercising himself after the manner of our Exercises, I had certain arguments of great evidence, by which I understood more clearly than ever how very much it matters for the discernment of spirits whether we attend to the thoughts and inward speeches, or to the spirit itself, which is wont to betray itself through desires, through affections, through strength or weakness of soul, through tranquillity or disquiet, through gladness or sadness, and like spiritual affections. By these, surely, one can judge of the soul and its spirits more easily than by the thoughts themselves. There are some who, through many and various contemplations or prayers of different spiritual exercises, can scarcely detect the variety of the different spirits, but seem always to be moved by one and the same spirit, though in greater or less degree. But the most efficacious means for bringing out this distinction is the proposal of an election of life and state; then, within the same, the various degrees tending to perfection; and generally, the higher the thing a man has proposed to do, or hope, or believe, or love, or the more he has applied himself to it in affection and in effect, the more easily will he have given grounds for rousing the difference of the good and the evil spirit. In some also the evil spirit is not recognized — above all in the devout, and those long practised in devotion and free from sins — because they have no thoughts outside the limits of truth and goodness, nor affections manifestly inordinate. Yet even these, however holy they be, if you lead them to examine themselves upon some degree of a more perfect life and conversation, whether in their own state (if it be unchangeable) or in another more perfect state, it will be easy to see both of those spirits — the strengthener and the weakener, the enlightener and the darkener, the justifier and the stainer; that is, the good spirit, and him who is the good one's adversary.

units.la: In die dominicae quintae post Pascha, ego notavi quaedam, quorum ordo et ratio in die veneris praecedente mihi fuerat satis clare ostensa, et.haec erant ad propositum eorum quae in singulis colloquiis Exercitiorum, circa varietatem quatuor hebdomadarum, et quadrifariam distinctarum materiarum Exercitiorum, peti solent aut commode possent. In prima hebdomada, recte et convenienter juxta materiam peccatorum, petuntur illae tres gratiae, scilicet: vera cognitio ac contritio peccatorum totius vitae anteactae, et haec est prima; secunda, cognitio inordinationis Are ora a a a ipsius vitae; tertia, cognitio et propositum verae emendationis vitae, et verae ordinationis ipsius in futurum. In secunda hebdomada, juxta scopum contemplationum vitae Christi, qui est ipsum cognoscere ad imitandum, ponuntur satis rationa- biliter istae tres gratiae in colloquiis (loquor semper de tribus colloquiis principalibus, ad.
units.en: On the fifth Sunday after Easter I noted certain things, whose order and reason had been shown me quite clearly on the preceding Friday; and these bore on what is usually asked — or could fittingly be asked — in the several colloquies of the Exercises, according to the variety of the four weeks and the four distinct matters of the Exercises. In the first week, rightly and fittingly, according to the matter of sins, those three graces are asked: namely, true knowledge of and contrition for the sins of one's whole past life — this is the first; the second, knowledge of the disorder of that life; the third, knowledge of, and resolve for, a true amendment of life, and its true ordering for the future. In the second week, according to the aim of the contemplations of the life of Christ, which is to know him so as to imitate him, these three graces are quite reasonably set in the colloquies (I speak always of the three principal colloquies, to the

units.la: Virginem, ad Christum, et ad Patrem): abnegatio sui, prima; secunda, contemptus mundi perfectus; tertia, perfectus amor servitii Christi Domini Nostri. Multi enim sibi bene sentire videntur de Christo, et ipsius personam diligere, quibus tamen non satis arrident negotia in quibus consistit Christi servitus. Hi proinde saepe, non sine consolatione multa, cogitant de Christo et de ipsius virtutibus atque perfectionibus; nihil aut parum interea cogitantes de operibus illis variis, in quibus ipse optat suos ministros occupari et se sequi, ut ubi ipse fuit illi sint, qui pòstea futuri sunt ubi ille nune est. In tertia hebdomada, quae est circa materiam Passionis, mihi satis apte videntur apponi illae tres gratiae, juxta materiam, videlicet: ut prima sit compassio Christi circa paeoenas corporales; secunda, com- passio Christi circa paupertatem atque omnium propriorum destitutionem; tertia, compassio circa vituperia et ignominias. Multae enim sunt paenae quas nescimus sentire in spiritu proprio. In quarta autem Exercitiorum hebdomada, convenienter juxta materiam resurrectionis, cujus scopus est cognoscere Christum gloriosum et glorificatum, ponuntur illae tres gratiae, generaliter multa vina optima complectentes: prima est amor Dei et Christi; secunda, gaudium perfectum in Christo solo; tertia, pax vera, quae etiam non nisi in ipso solo est.
units.en: Virgin, to Christ, and to the Father): denial of self, the first; second, perfect contempt of the world; third, perfect love of the service of Christ Our Lord. For many seem to themselves to feel rightly about Christ, and to love his person, to whom nevertheless the affairs in which the service of Christ consists are not sufficiently pleasing. Such men often think of Christ, not without much consolation, and of his virtues and perfections, while thinking nothing, or little, of those various works in which he desires his ministers to be occupied and to follow him — that where he was, they may be, who are afterwards to be where he now is. In the third week, which concerns the matter of the Passion, those three graces seem to me very aptly set down, according to the matter: namely, that the first be compassion with Christ in his bodily pains; the second, compassion with Christ in his poverty and the loss of all his own; the third, compassion in his revilings and ignominies. For there are many pains which we know not how to feel in our own spirit. And in the fourth week of the Exercises, fittingly, according to the matter of the resurrection, whose aim is to know Christ glorious and glorified, those three graces are set down, which in general embrace many excellent wines: the first is the love of God and of Christ; the second, perfect joy in Christ alone; the third, true peace, which likewise is nowhere but in him alone.

units.la: In vigilia Ascensionis Domini, dum solito more conturbarer et desolarer, considerando quaedam generalia mala in quibus videbatur obscurari servitium Christi, non solum in genere, sed etiam in particularibus. per me ope- randis, ego sensi quamdam confortationem specialem per opposita: in qua quidem confir- matione ego coepi consolari. Hic autem mihi datum est videre non minus fugiendas esse hujusmodi consolationes quae sunt in solis accidentibus, aut etiam in possibilibus prosperitatibus rerum spiritualium, quam contrarias desolationes: dico quantum ad extremum, quod frequenter solet nimium esse, et respiciendo ad ipsam cor- OT O a dis veram stabilitatem, quae utroque modo impeditur, id est, per, tristitiam vanam, et etiam per laetitiam vanam; et nonnunquam magis per ipsam laetitiam; licet plus juvet ad bene operandum ipsa laetitia cui et aliquid vanitatis spiritualis superveniát, quam ipsa tristitia cui alıquid perturbationis est permixtum. Quae quidem perturbatio solet ortum suum habere a malo spiritu, licet in bonum spiritum soleat terminari; sicut laetitia, e contrario, solet quidem ortum habere per spiritum bonum et terminari in malum. Sicut enim bonus spiritus solet ex tristitiis sumere argumenta trahendi nos ad id quod solidum est et bonum, ut nos vere consoletur, ablata falsa aut vana laetitia; ita et solet inimicus sumere occasionem ex laetitiis, ut nos ad vanum gaudium deducat, ex quo postea sequitur tristitia. Caveantur igitur, id est, observentur extrema horum excessuum, sive principia, sive fines; ut cognoscantur spiritus suggestores, et promotores, et terminatores talium motuum animae atque impressionum spiritualium.
units.en: On the vigil of the Ascension of the Lord, while I was troubled and desolate after my accustomed manner, considering certain general evils in which the service of Christ seemed to be darkened, not only in general but also in the particular things to be worked by me, I felt a certain special strengthening through the opposites; and in that confirmation I began to be consoled. But here it was given me to see that consolations of this kind, which lie in mere accidents, or even in the possible prosperities of spiritual things, are no less to be shunned than the contrary desolations: I mean as regards their extreme, which is often too much, and with regard to the true stability of the heart, which is hindered in both ways — by vain sadness, and also by vain gladness; and sometimes more by the gladness; although that gladness upon which some spiritual vanity supervenes helps more towards working well than that sadness with which some disturbance is mingled. And such disturbance is wont to have its origin from the evil spirit, though it commonly ends in the good spirit; as gladness, contrariwise, is wont indeed to have its origin through the good spirit and to end in the evil. For as the good spirit is wont to take from sadnesses arguments for drawing us to what is solid and good, so as truly to console us when the false or vain gladness has been taken away; so also the enemy is wont to take occasion from gladnesses to lead us to vain joy, upon which sadness afterwards follows. Let the extremes of these excesses, then, be guarded against — that is, observed — whether beginnings or ends; that the spirits may be known which suggest, promote, and terminate such motions of the soul and spiritual impressions.

units.la: In die Ascensionis mihi contigit quidam bonus intellectus de eo quod est quaerere Deum et w n 4 iý - Christum extra et supra omnem creaturam, et velle cognoscere in seipso. Et datum est quoque intelligere quasdam differentias, 'et sentire eas in spiritu, circa illud quod est apprehendere creaturam in ipso Deo, Deum in ipsa creatura, et Deum absque creatura. Iste autem est verus ascensus mentis et spiritus, ut per cognitionem creaturarum et affectus ascendamus ad Creatorem agnoscendum et amandum, in creaturis solis nullo pacto consistentes. Secundo veniendum est ad Creatorem, quatenus ipse est, et vivit, et operatur in creaturis. Sed nec ibi consistendum adhuc est, sed quaerendus est Deus in seipso, seorsum, supra omnem creaturam et extra, non exclusus tamen ab illa creatura. Postea in ipso creaturae cognoscantur omnes longe perfectius quam fuerint in seipsis notae; imo etiam per-. fectius quam in seipsis extiterint. O utinam, brevi veniat tempus quo nulla creatura absque Deo a me cernatur et ametur, aut timeatur!
units.en: On the day of the Ascension there came to me a certain good understanding of what it is to seek God and Christ outside and above every creature, and to wish to know him in himself. And it was given me also to understand certain differences, and to feel them in spirit, concerning what it is to apprehend the creature in God himself, God in the creature itself, and God without the creature. And this is the true ascent of mind and spirit: that through the knowledge of creatures and through the affections we ascend to acknowledge and love the Creator, in no wise resting in the creatures alone. Secondly, we must come to the Creator in so far as he is, and lives, and works in creatures. But neither must we stop there; God must be sought in himself, apart, above every creature and outside — yet not excluded from that creature. Afterwards, in him, all creatures may be known far more perfectly than they were known in themselves; nay, even more perfectly than they existed in themselves. O may the time soon come when no creature shall be seen or loved or feared by me without God!

units.la: Hinc mihi fiat ascensus ad cognoscendum ipsum in seipso, et tandem in Ghristo omnia, ut ipse sit in aeternum mihi omnia in omnibus. Pro gradibus his, nitendum erit ut Christus, qui est via et veritas et vita, inveniatùr in centro cordis mei, et infra, id est, intra meipsūm; et deinde inveniatur supra meipsum per mentem, et extra me per sensus. Ad haec, petendum erit ut Pater, qui supra dicitur, det potentiam; et Filius qui extra, quadam ratione, propter humanitatem dici potest, det sapientiam; et ut Spiritus Sanctus, qui quodammodo infra, id est, intra nọş dici potest, det bonitatem. Alioqui enim nec interiora nosira aperiri poterunt, ut intra Deus videatur a mundo corde; nec superiora nostra elevari ad invisibilia Dei, quae super omnia sunt; nec membra nostra mortificari, ut sentiatur ille qui est extra omnia et super omnia.
units.en: Hence may there be for me an ascent to knowing him in himself, and at last all things in Christ, that he may be to me for ever all in all. For these steps we must strive that Christ, who is the way and the truth and the life, be found in the centre of my heart, and beneath — that is, within myself; and then that he be found above myself through the mind, and outside me through the senses. For this we must ask that the Father, who is called above, give power; that the Son, who in a certain sense, because of the humanity, may be called outside, give wisdom; and that the Holy Spirit, who may in a manner be called beneath — that is, within us — give goodness. For otherwise neither can our inward parts be opened, that God may be seen within by the clean of heart; nor our higher parts be raised to the invisible things of God, which are above all; nor our members be mortified, that he may be felt who is outside all things and above all things.

units.la: Postridie Ascensionis, dum ageretur sanctissimae Crucis festum, ego celebravi in Ecclesia quae dicitur Sanctae Crucis, extra civitatem Moguntinensem; ubi est memoria illorum insignium miraculorum quae quondam contigerunt: quorum alterum fuit in crucifixo illo qui inibi servatur, et qui inventus est super flumen Rheni, et natabat contra tractum fluminis ascendendo; alterum est de altero crucifixo qui ibi quoque est, qui dum percussus fuisset a quodam lusore, caput ipsius ampvtatum emisit sanguinem, qui usque 1n hodiernum diem clarissime cernitur manasse per imaginem.!
units.en: On the day after the Ascension, the feast of the most holy Cross being kept, I celebrated in the church called of the Holy Cross, outside the city of Mainz; where is the memory of those famous miracles which once happened there: one of which concerned the crucifix preserved there, which was found on the river Rhine, and floated upward against the current of the river; the other concerns another crucifix which is there also, which, when it had been struck by a certain gambler and its head cut off, poured forth blood, which to this day is most clearly seen to have flowed down the image.

units.la: Ibi igitur dum celebrassem, ego inveni nobilissimam devotionem, et magnum sensi dolorem quod talia miracula jam sint in oblivione apud homines. Proinde orabam Dominum, ut mihi daret spiritum in quo, omnium nomine, possem cognoscere talia ipsius beneficia, et quod acciperet sensa mei spiritus, quasi ab omnibus nostrae Societatis et ab omnibus piis quos ego unquam novi, et quasi ab omnibus offerretur hoc sacrificium, in laudis et gratiarum actiones, ut propitiaretur pro his et omnibus similibus maximis Dei beneficiis.
units.en: There, then, when I had celebrated, I found a most noble devotion, and felt great grief that such miracles are now forgotten among men. Accordingly I prayed the Lord to give me a spirit in which, in the name of all, I might acknowledge such benefits of his; and that he would receive the feelings of my spirit as though they came from all of our Society and from all the devout whom I have ever known, and as though this sacrifice were offered by all, in praises and thanksgivings, that he might be propitiated for these and all similar very great benefits of God.

units.la: Feci etiam hic votum redeundi ad eamdem Ecclesiam una alia vice antequam sim abiturus e Germania, ut possem celebrare in altari superioris crucifixi, ejus scilicet qui super aqua per se natavit.
units.en: I made also here a vow to return to the same church once more before I depart from Germany, that I might celebrate at the altar of the upper crucifix — of that one, namely, which floated of itself upon the water.

units.la: In festo apparitionis divi Michaelis Archangeli, inciderunt mihi quaedam notabiles gratiarum actiones ad Deum, pro beneficiis factis ipsis An- gelis singulariter.. Ego autem agnoscebam pro Tooo SUEN a a magno beneficio quod Angeli nunquam fuerint circumdati infirmitatibus corporum humanorum, sicut sunt animae nostrae intra ergastula corporum suorum immersae et circumscriptae; unde fit in ipsis tanta sensuum diversitas atque etiam contrarietas, quibus saepe impugnantur et sollicitantur ad mala, quae non possunt sentire simplices illae naturae. Magnum quoque momentum ad bonum affert ipsis angelis non habere istam duplicitatem et multiplicitatem in. agendo; unde fit ut intra ipsos non fuerint bella, etiam antequam essent in bono confirmati, licet oppugnarentur a contrariis spiritibus. In nobis autem tanta est varietas ut, licet aliqua pars videatur esse bona, multae tamen ad malum tendant. Nec enim intellectum statim comitatur plena voluntas; neque contra ipse intellectus voluntatem; sensus quoque ipse aliorsum nimium saepe tendit quam ratio proponit. Fit igitur ut non statim totus: homo bonus ac rectus sit, cum una aliqua ipsius portio recta - aut bona fuerit. Hic tamen mihi etiam datum est ut recognoscerem in hoc magna beneficia facta esse homini, quod ita sit diversus in agendo, ita discontinuus atque etiam mutabilis. Ex eo enim factum est ut, licet una aliqua ipsius portio apprehensa a malo aut etiam infecta fuerit, non statim totus ipse homo sit perditus; item quod, licet ad tempus sit totus perditus, quia tamen mutabilis est et flexibilis, non in aeternum sit perditus. Saepe sensualitas tota videtur infecta, cum tamen ratio ipsa ac spiritus dissentientes non corrumpantur. Haec autem in angelis non poterant contingere, etiam antequam essent confirmati; unde maximum periculum inerat ut ruerent sicut caeteri apostatae. Statim enim ut apprehendissent malum, propter simplicitatem naturae, factum fuisset ut ipsorum natura fuisset infecta; nec fuisset locus ut una in ipsis parte consentiente aliqua alia dissensisset; sed oportebat statim aut totam naturam esse perfusam bono, aut totam malo plenam atque infectam. Ego igitur, quod ad me attinet > quandiu sum tam inclinatus ad malum et circumdatus tam multis coinquinationibus carnis, mundi, et malorum spirituum, multum gaudeo quod natura mea non sit adhuc simplex. Si enim simplex esset, nimium cito fieret ut tota anima mea esset a malo aliquo spiritu penetrata, proindeque tota inficeretur. Nunc vero, licet aliquis malus spiritus penetret, verbi gratia, carnem meam, aut intellectum, aut appetitum, et caetera, non tamen statim fit ut totus sim malus; quia possem nolle talia mala, et eis per voluntatem dissentiendo contradicere. Optarem quidem a bono et optimo spiritu totus et totaliter et in omnibus penetrari atque optime affici ab ipso, et Sic ipsi tali bono spiritui esse omnino simplex, et unum continuum, et in se immutabile; sed dum 1ngruunt spiritualia nequitiae, et circumstantia me undique peccata, a quibus periculum est attingi, quando haec, inquam, incidunt, tunc malo inveniri non simplex, et ens per se non ita continuum atque immutabile: nimium enim periculum esset ut ne totus statim inficerer, et ne, si caderem, irreparabiliter caderem.
units.en: On the feast of the apparition of Saint Michael the Archangel there came to me certain notable thanksgivings to God, for the benefits bestowed on the Angels in particular. For I acknowledged it as a great benefit that the Angels were never hedged about with the infirmities of human bodies, as our souls are immersed and confined within the prisons of their bodies; whence arises in us such diversity, and even contrariety, of feelings, by which we are often assailed and solicited to evils which those simple natures cannot feel. It is also of great moment towards good for the angels that they do not have this doubleness and multiplicity in acting; whence it came that there were no wars within them, even before they were confirmed in good, although they were assailed by contrary spirits. But in us there is such variety that, though some one part seem good, many parts nevertheless tend to evil. For the full will does not at once accompany the intellect, nor conversely the intellect the will; and sense itself too often tends elsewhere than reason proposes. Hence it comes that the whole man is not at once good and upright when some one portion of him is upright or good. Yet here it was also given me to recognize great benefits bestowed on man in this: that he is thus diverse in acting, thus discontinuous and even changeable. For thereby it comes about that, though some one portion of him be seized or even infected by evil, the whole man is not at once lost; likewise that, though for a time he be wholly lost, yet because he is changeable and pliable, he is not lost for ever. Often the whole sensuality seems infected, while yet reason and the spirit, dissenting, are not corrupted. But these things could not happen in the angels, even before they were confirmed; whence there was the greatest danger that they should fall like the other apostates. For as soon as they had apprehended evil, by reason of the simplicity of their nature it would have come to pass that their whole nature was infected; nor was there room, when one part in them consented, for some other part to dissent; but it must needs be that either the whole nature was suffused with good, or the whole full of evil and infected. As for me, then, so long as I am so inclined to evil, and beset with so many defilements of the flesh, the world, and evil spirits, I greatly rejoice that my nature is not yet simple. For were it simple, it would too quickly come about that my whole soul was penetrated by some evil spirit, and so wholly infected. But now, though some evil spirit penetrate, for example, my flesh, or my intellect, or my appetite, and the rest, yet it does not at once follow that I am wholly evil; for I can refuse such evils, and contradict them by dissenting with the will. I could wish indeed to be wholly and totally and in all things penetrated by the good and best spirit, and excellently affected by him, and so to be altogether simple for that good spirit, one continuous whole, unchangeable in itself; but while the spiritual powers of wickedness press in, and sins beset me on every side, by which there is danger of being touched — when these things fall upon me, I prefer to be found not simple, and a being not so continuous and unchangeable in itself: for the danger would be too great that I should at once be wholly infected, and that, if I fell, I should fall irreparably.

units.la: Benedictus igitur Dominus Noster Jesus Christus incarnatus et mortuus, per quem facti sumus tam multiplices tamque variabiles, dum versamur in malis accidentibus; per cujus gratiam fiet tandem ut veniamus ad omnimodam simplicitatem et ad immutabilitatem, boni quidem in bonis coeaelestibus damnati autem in malis: sic se e A quod sancti totaliter penetrabuntur ab ipso summo Bono, cui in aeternum unientur; et mali ab ipsa miseria iniquitatis, cui in sempiternum etiam conjungentur.
units.en: Blessed therefore be Our Lord Jesus Christ, incarnate and dead, through whom we have been made so manifold and so variable while we dwell among evil accidents; through whose grace it shall at last come to pass that we arrive at complete simplicity and unchangeableness — the good in heavenly goods, but the damned in evils: so that the saints will be totally penetrated by the supreme Good itself, to which they will be united for ever; and the wicked by the very misery of iniquity, to which they too will be joined everlastingly.

units.la: In die sancto Pentecostes, ego quaedam viva desideria habui ad Deum, ut mihi daretur, per Spiritum, spiritualiter spiritualia intelligere et velle. Petebam esse spirituale, vivere spirituale, sentire spirituale, et ipsum ratiocinari spirituale. Pro quibus verbis magnum sensum habui. Videbam etiam quamdam latissimam differentiam quae est inter commotiones divinas, quae esse possunt in homine quantum ad spiritum vitalem, et illas quae esse possunt. quantum ad spiritum animalem, et illas quae esse possunt qüantum ad spiritum rationalem; item considerabam quan- tum differat sentire aliquid in carne, aut sentire in spiritu; esse in carne, aut esse in spiritu; vivere in carne, aut vivere in spiritu.
units.en: On the holy day of Pentecost I had certain lively desires towards God, that it might be given me, through the Spirit, to understand and to will spiritual things spiritually. I asked for a spiritual being, a spiritual living, a spiritual feeling, and a spiritual reasoning itself. For these words I had a great feeling. I saw also a certain very wide difference between the divine movements which can be in a man as regards the vital spirit, and those which can be as regards the animal spirit, and those which can be as regards the rational spirit; likewise I considered how much it differs to feel something in the flesh, or to feel it in the spirit; to be in the flesh, or to be in the spirit; to live in the flesh, or to live in the spirit.

units.la: Hic quoque multis precibus datum est petere gratiam Spiritus Sancti, ut deinceps transferri possit meum esse, vivere, et sentire, ad ipsum spiritum; ut sit negotium animae meae, in illis intimis quae patent Spiritui Sancto; et ut liberari oo a U a possim ab eo quod est sentire carnalia et corporalia corporaliter; scilicet, ut ita loquar, per corporales ac carnales cogitationes aut motiones, idque in ipsa carne vel in ipso corpore. Tunc enim res vere sentiuntur, cum spiritu attinguntur rationali; maxime cum ipsae sint spirituales, et per Spiritum Sanctum suggerantur.
units.en: Here too it was given me, with many prayers, to ask the grace of the Holy Spirit, that henceforth my being, living and feeling may be carried over to the spirit itself; that the business of my soul may be in those inward depths which lie open to the Holy Spirit; and that I may be freed from that which is to feel carnal and bodily things bodily — that is, so to speak, through bodily and carnal thoughts or motions, and that in the very flesh or body. For things are truly felt when they are touched by the rational spirit; above all when they are themselves spiritual, and are suggested by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Hic quoque notavi modum quo tam saepe sensi carnalia carnaliter et in carne. Aliquando autem contingit hoc sic, quod carnalia per carnem sentiantur in carne; aliquando vero quod carnalia per spiritum malum sentiantur in carne; et, aliquando quod carnalia sentiantur per eumdem spiritum màlum in ipso spiritu vitali, aut animali, aut etiam rationali ipsius hominis.. Possūnt quoque spiritualia quandoque satis carnaliter apprehendi, sicut corporalia spiritualiter contingit intelligi et sentiri.
units.en: Here too I noted the manner in which I have so often felt carnal things carnally and in the flesh. Sometimes it happens thus, that carnal things are felt through the flesh in the flesh; sometimes that carnal things are felt through the evil spirit in the flesh; and sometimes that carnal things are felt through the same evil spirit in the vital spirit itself, or the animal, or even the rational spirit of the man. Spiritual things also can sometimes be apprehended quite carnally, just as bodily things happen to be understood and felt spiritually.

units.la: Rogandus est igitur mazime Spiritus Sanctus ut ipse dignetur moderari, omnem spiritum in nobis: tam eum spiritum in quo vita in nobis administratur, et eum in quo sensatio causatur, quam eum ipsum per quod cogitationes ac affectus procurantur; idque fiat donec veniat tempus illud et illa felicitas, cum Deus erit omnia in omnibus ac perspicietur, Alia quadam vice infra octavas Pentecostes, ego sensi magnam devotionem in quibusdam discursibus postulationum donorum Spiritus.
units.en: The Holy Spirit therefore is above all to be begged that he would deign to govern every spirit in us: both that spirit in which life is administered in us, and that in which sensation is caused, and that through which thoughts and affections are procured; and may this be done until that time and that happiness come, when God shall be all in all, and shall be seen clearly. On another occasion within the octave of Pentecost, I felt great devotion in certain rounds of petition for the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Sancti, considerando quidnam importet donum seu spiritus intellectus, spiritus sapientiae, spiritus timoris, scientiae, consilii, pietatis et fortitudinis. Item et mihi suggerebatur quidam modus orandi Spiritum Sanctum in quantum procedit ex Patre, et in quantum procedit ex Filio. Item in quantum ipse est ductor et sanctificator animae Christi; imo et in quantum ipse est de quo ipse Christus conceptus est. Item quantum est dotator virginis Mariae, Angelorum, Prophetarum, Apostolorum, Martyrum, Confessorum, Monachorum, Virginum, Continentium, Viduarum, etc. Item in quantum ipse destructor est daemoniacarum impressionum; et, in summa, in quantum ipse est omnia replens, et in quo sunt omnia, in quo vivunt, et in quo omnibus modis moventur. Magnum quid sensi esse, et maximam gratiam habere, favorem tanti et tam intrinseci omnium rerum principii, medii et finis. j p d Habui et satis bonas orationes ad Spiriturn Sanctum, desiderando ipsius aeternum patrocinium et tutamen; imo esse ipsum, et vivere, et sentire, et ratiocinationes contra malignos spiritus, id est, contra ipsorum malas impressiones, quascumque illi possunt et volunt immittere, sicut sunt malae cogitationes, malae affectiones, occultae virtutes, malignitates ac confortationes, ut malum possint melius operari aut sentire. Multa enim possunt mali spiritus in corpora ipsa, contra quae:nos munit Spiritus Sanctus per se et bonos spiritus angelicos.
units.en: Considering what is imported by the gift or spirit of understanding, the spirit of wisdom, the spirit of fear, of knowledge, of counsel, of piety and of fortitude. Likewise there was suggested to me a certain way of praying to the Holy Spirit in so far as he proceeds from the Father, and in so far as he proceeds from the Son; likewise in so far as he is the guide and sanctifier of the soul of Christ; nay, even in so far as he is the one of whom Christ himself was conceived; likewise as the endower of the Virgin Mary, of the Angels, Prophets, Apostles, Martyrs, Confessors, Monks, Virgins, Continent, Widows, and so on; likewise in so far as he is the destroyer of demoniacal impressions; and, in sum, in so far as he is the one who fills all things, and in whom all things are, in whom they live, and in whom they are moved in every way. I felt it to be a great thing, and a very great grace, to have the favour of so great and so intimate a principle, means and end of all things. I had also quite good prayers to the Holy Spirit, desiring his eternal patronage and protection; nay, his very being, and living, and feeling, and reasonings against the malignant spirits — that is, against their evil impressions, whatever they can and will send in, such as evil thoughts, evil affections, hidden powers, malignities and reinforcements, that they may the better work or make felt their evil. For the evil spirits can do much upon our very bodies, against which the Holy Spirit fortifies us by himself and by the good angelic spirits.

units.la: In diè superexcellentissimae Trinitatis, sensi magnum desiderium ut hoc festum solemne celebraretur, cum complectatur tres illas Personas, quibus nihil dignius potest excogitari nec credi.
units.en: On the day of the most super-excellent Trinity I felt a great desire that this solemn feast should be celebrated, since it embraces those three Persons, than whom nothing worthier can be conceived or believed.

units.la: Habui autem quasdam postulationes, quibus petebam ut omnes vires meae'et omne posse meum per Patrem laboraret; ut in me lumen et claritas, et ordo, et compositio, et ars, per Filium dirigerentur, expulsis omnibus contrariis; et ut omnes affectus, desideria, appetitus, inclinationes, ac formae accidentales, purifica- rentur per Spiritum Sanctum, expulsis cunctis malis impressionibus carnis et spiritus.
units.en: And I had certain petitions, in which I asked that all my strength and all my power might labour through the Father; that in me light and clarity, and order, and composition, and skill might be directed through the Son, all contraries being driven out; and that all affections, desires, appetites, inclinations and accidental forms might be purified through the Holy Spirit, all evil impressions of flesh and spirit being expelled.

units.la: Dum considerarem et satis bene comprehenderem quomodo Deus, Pater, et Filius, et Spiritus Sanctus, est undequaque extra omnia, et intra omnia, et per omnia, et in omnibús nobis, ego sensi bonam devotionem, petendo gratiam ut ipse dignaretur mihi dare gratiam quaerendi illum omnibus modis et inveniendi. Hic. notabam quoque et sensi quomodo Deus dicitur omnipotens; id est, tantus ut omnia possit facere esse, quaecumque per se esse non possunt, in omni modo possibili, corporali aut spirituali, et, ut generalius dicatur, substantiali aut accidentali, simpliciter, vel composite. Hic habui quemdam discursum circa ordinem qui est. a rebus imperfectioribus ad perfectiores: in quo ordine occurrebant primo omnia accidentia, quorum perfectio ex subjectis quibus adhaerere nota sunt, colligi et ordinari etiam potest; secundo, occurrebat materia rerum corporalium; tertio, formae - substantiales inanimatorum Corruptibilium; quarto, formae caelorum; quinto, formae animatorum corruptibiles, ut plantarum et brutorum animalium; sexto, composita inanimala, et etiam vegetabilia corruptibilia; septimo, composita coelestia et coeli corporales; octavo, animalia bruta; nono, animae rationales; decimo, homo ipse; undecimo, Angelus. Post haec, super omnia, Deus superbenedictus, Pater, Filius, et Spiritus Sanctus, tres in personis et unum in substantia omnibus modis perfectiŝsima.,, Feria tertia post festum sanctisimae Trinitatis, pro officio matutino, ego sensi quamdam gratiam quam nunquam fueram expertus tam evidenter, licet frequenter mihi datum fuit desiderium illam habendi. Ipsa autem erat in hoc, quod mens mea firmius et stabilius solito elevaretur ad conspectum Dei qui est in caelis. Alias ego saepe sensi majorem devotionem, circa intelligentiam verborum, aut in aliquo spiritu qui animam. meam vel compungeret, vel quocumque modo devotam faceret. Hic vero fuit elevatio apicis mentalis, in quo dabatur apprehendere potentiam Dei, prout ipse habitat in templo suo caelesti; et sic coepi hic desiderare, et omnino proponere, quod posthac velim quaerere. ut augeatur talis gratia, ad dicendas quascumque orationes meas vocales aut mentales. Difficilis nonnihil videbatur talis mentis intentio ad ipsum Deum; sed spes bona erat quod gratia confortatura esset mentem meam.
units.en: While I considered, and comprehended well enough, how God — Father, Son and Holy Spirit — is on every side outside all things, and within all things, and through all things, and in all of us, I felt good devotion, asking the grace that he would deign to give me the grace of seeking him in every way and finding him. Here I noted also, and felt, how God is called almighty: that is, so great that he can make to be all things whatsoever that cannot be of themselves, in every possible mode, bodily or spiritual, and, to speak more generally, substantial or accidental, simply or compositely. Here I had a certain round concerning the order which runs from the more imperfect things to the more perfect: in which order there came first all accidents, whose perfection can be gathered and ranked from the subjects to which they are known to adhere; second came the matter of bodily things; third, the substantial forms of inanimate corruptible things; fourth, the forms of the heavens; fifth, the corruptible forms of animate things, as of plants and brute animals; sixth, inanimate compounds, and also corruptible vegetable ones; seventh, the heavenly compounds and the bodily heavens; eighth, brute animals; ninth, rational souls; tenth, man himself; eleventh, the Angel. After these, above all, God super-blessed, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, three in persons and one in a substance in every way most perfect. On the Tuesday after the feast of the most holy Trinity, at the morning office, I felt a certain grace which I had never experienced so evidently, though the desire of having it had frequently been given me. It lay in this: that my mind was raised more firmly and stably than usual to the contemplation of God who is in heaven. At other times I have often felt greater devotion in the understanding of the words, or in some spirit which either pricked my soul or made it devout in some way. But this was an elevation of the summit of the mind, in which it was given me to apprehend the power of God as he dwells in his heavenly temple; and so I began here to desire, and altogether to resolve, that henceforth I would seek the increase of such a grace for the saying of all my prayers, vocal or mental. Such a directing of the mind to God himself seemed somewhat difficult; but there was good hope that grace would strengthen my mind.

units.la: Facilius quoque videbatur posse tempore orationis figi mens vel in ipsum crucifixum, quasi esset coram me, vel in virginem Matrem, aut etiam aliquem sanctorum, et etiam quandoque in Deum prout est in caeoelo.
units.en: It seemed also that at the time of prayer the mind can more easily be fixed either on the crucified himself, as though he were before me, or on the Virgin Mother, or even on some one of the saints, and even at times on God as he is in heaven.
