units.la: Hic notavi tria esse summopere necessaria ut apprehendantur ab orante sive mentaliter sive vocaliter: primo, ut ipsa persona ad quam funditur oratio velut collocetur in memoria; secundo, significatio verborum quae sumenda sunt ad orandum; tertio, spiritus in quo omnia sentiantur ex affectu. Pro consummata igitur oratione est habendus in memoria thronus majestatis Dei Patris, et ipsa memoria eo usque elevanda; inintellectu vero habenda est illustratio sapientiae Filii, quo omnia intelliguntur; in voluntate autem cordis, Spiritus Sanctus, sine quo nihil sentitur ex intimis. Det Deus et Jesus gratiam ut ad haec pervenire quotidie crescendo valeamus.
units.en: Here I noted that three things are supremely necessary to be apprehended by one who prays, whether mentally or vocally: first, that the person to whom the prayer is poured out be as it were set in the memory; second, the meaning of the words which are to be taken for praying; third, the spirit in which everything is felt from the affection. For a consummate prayer, then, the throne of the majesty of God the Father must be held in the memory, and the memory itself raised to that height; in the intellect must be held the illumination of the wisdom of the Son, by which all things are understood; and in the will of the heart, the Holy Spirit, without whom nothing is felt from the depths. May God and Jesus give grace that we may be able to arrive at these things, growing daily.

units.la: Hoc mihi expediens esse visùm est; et simul visum est quod hactenus nunquam exercueram supremam partem animae mee, id est, mentis apicem, circa hujusmod intentionem 1n alterum; quin potius quod habuerim illam hactenus totam conversam adhuc et intentam circa intima mea, id est, totam reflexam et recurvatam circa considerationem infirmitatum carnis meae et spiritus mei. Intelligentia autem quam habui circa hané materiam (quod fuit in hac tertia feria post festum Trinitatis) recognoscenda erit tanquam descendens ab ipsa sanctissima Trinitate, et quasi reliquiae festi ipsius, mente altissime reponenda. Hic quoque vere decernendum est ut profectum cujuslibet anni in die sanctissimae Trinitatis referas; ibique initium recollectionis fructuum tuorum annalium, et finis omnium profectuum animae tuae, et aedificationis templi tui, quod praeparandum est in habitaculum sanctum et in mansionem aeternam sanctissimae hujus Trinitatis, in quam terminantur omnia mysteria Christi, et per Ecclesiam ordinate solemnitates festorum dierum et dominicalium.
units.en: This seemed to me expedient; and at the same time it appeared that hitherto I had never exercised the supreme part of my soul — that is, the summit of the mind — in such a directing towards another; but rather that I had kept it hitherto wholly turned and intent upon my own inward things, that is, wholly bent back and curved upon the consideration of the infirmities of my flesh and of my spirit. And the understanding which I had on this matter (which was on this Tuesday after the feast of the Trinity) must be acknowledged as descending from the most holy Trinity itself, and, as it were relics of its feast, to be laid up most high in the mind. Here too it is truly to be resolved that you refer the progress of each year to the day of the most holy Trinity; and let there be there the beginning of the gathering of your yearly fruits, and the end of all the progresses of your soul, and of the building of your temple, which is to be prepared as a holy dwelling and an eternal mansion of this most holy Trinity, in whom all the mysteries of Christ are terminated, and, through the Church, the ordered solemnities of the feast days and Sundays.

units.la: In festo sacratissimi sacramenti corporis Christi Jesu Domini Nostri, ego sensi varias intelligen- tias circa ipsius solemnitatem celebrandam, circa ipsius adorationem, et circa ipsius permanentiam. In processione dum portabatur, ego tactus fuivariis modis, et commotus ad devotionem, videns tam varia adhiberi ad ornatum et ad celebrationem talis processionis. Gaudebam quod tam multi homines concurrerent, tam multa operantes ad laudem Christi. In summa ego maxime afficiebar ad illum aeternum cultum, ad quem cultum omnes homines possunt aliquid expendere, vel operum, Vel rerum suarum, vel affectuum animi, aut gèstuum corporis. Ad quem item cultum omnes sensus exerceri possunt cor- poraliter, omnes artes mechanicae possunt subser- vire, membra corporum humanorum possunt exerceri utiliterque abhiberi. Inibi esse possunt cantus humanae vocis, instrumenta varia manibus humanis confecta. Rustici herbas, frondes, et serta ex his confecta adferunt ad hunc cultum; artifices variis modis ad eumdem se quoque exercent. Sic itaque fit ut omnes omnino homines possint Servire. Deo eliam corporaliter, omniaque membra sua ejus obsequio exhibere, a quo ipsa habent.
units.en: On the feast of the most sacred sacrament of the body of Christ Jesus Our Lord, I felt various understandings concerning the celebration of its solemnity, concerning its adoration, and concerning its permanence. In the procession, while it was carried, I was touched in various ways, and moved to devotion, seeing such varied things employed for the adornment and celebration of such a procession. I rejoiced that so many men came together, working so many things to the praise of Christ. In sum, I was most drawn towards that eternal worship, on which all men can spend something — of their works, or of their possessions, or of the affections of the soul, or of the gestures of the body; for which worship likewise all the senses can be exercised bodily, all the mechanical arts can serve, the members of human bodies can be exercised and usefully employed. There can be there the singing of the human voice, and the various instruments made by human hands. Countryfolk bring herbs, boughs, and garlands woven of them, to this worship; craftsmen in their various ways exercise themselves for the same. Thus it comes about that absolutely all men can serve God even bodily, and offer to his service all their members, from whom they have them.

units.la: Eodem die ego sensi magnam devotionem et bonum spiritum ad offerendum me totum in cultum Christi. Offerebam memoriam, intellectum et voluntatem, et quinque sensus exteriores, et quicquid est in me. Offerebam, inquam, haec omnia ipsi ad glorificandum et colendum ipsum; deinde etiam ad serviendum et obediendum ipsi in sanctificationem; et tertio in hoc quod, propter ipsum velim totus exerceri et expendi ad utilitatem proximi, propter charitatem ipsius.
units.en: On the same day I felt great devotion and a good spirit for offering my whole self to the worship of Christ. I offered memory, intellect and will, and the five outward senses, and whatever is in me. I offered, I say, all these to him, to glorify and worship him; then also to serve and obey him unto sanctification; and thirdly in this, that for his sake I would be wholly exercised and spent for the profit of my neighbour, for the sake of his charity.

units.la: Dabatur quoque ut optarem, secundum omnes partes animae et corporis, imitari ipsum Christum corporaliter,. in his duobus, scilicet in hoc quod me totum possem expendere et consumere in bonis operibus propter ipsum, et praeterea quod possem secundum me totum et quamlibet partem exerceri in passionibus, sicut ille omnibus membris suis pro me et pro omnibus passus est usque ad mortem crucis. j In die octavo ejusdem festi, mihi datum est ut cum maxima animi anxietate super defectibus meis, peterem gratiam qua fieri posset ut deinceps mihi omnes paenae remittantur peccatorum, quae sunt ex propriis habitibus malis aut inclina- tionibus caeterisque tentationibus quae ex propriis concupiscentiis proveniunt.
units.en: It was also given me to wish, according to all the parts of soul and body, to imitate Christ himself bodily in these two things: namely, that I might spend and consume my whole self in good works for his sake; and moreover that I might, in my whole self and in every part, be exercised in sufferings, as he suffered in all his members, for me and for all, even to the death of the cross. On the octave day of the same feast it was given me, with the greatest anxiety of soul over my defects, to ask the grace by which it might come about that henceforth all the pains of sins might be remitted me — those which come from my own evil habits or inclinations, and the other temptations which arise from my own concupiscences.

units.la: Sensi etiam quodammodo quam mirabiliter Christus exercitatam velit Ecclesiam suam sponsam, ex occasione tanti tamque admirandi sacramenti corporis sui et sanguinis. Dum enim sub speciebus illis sensibilibus credimus esse corpus Domini, et rursus sanguinem, exercemur in fide eorum quae non videntur; credentes adsistentem, realem, et veram corporis Christi praesentiam sub specie panis; et de sanguine sub speciebus vini adsistente; et de concomitantiis corporis et animae, et totius pulehritudinis divinitatis; et eodem quoque modo de transsubstantiatione. Exercemur praeterea in actibus colendi variis modis tale sacramentum; non solum in spiritu et intra nos per fidem et devotionem, sed etiam per actus latriae, tanquam ipse esset visibilis in eodem loco. Tertio exercemur circa sanctificationem nos- tram utendo tali cibo ad animae nostrae sustentationem, confortationem, illuminaātionem, consolationem, et omnimodam perceptionem thesaurorum coelestium. Nimium igitur miseri sunt, qui nolunt huic sacramento tanta deferre, quanta deferrent propriae personae visibili corporaliter ipsius Christi. Nihil enim nobis minus relictum est quam fuit illud quod datum est in caena apostolica. Eis vero datum est corpus quod mox erat tradendum et crucifigendum: non mortuum, quia mortuum non tradebatur corpus Christi; sed vivum; nec jam mortuum erat cum crucifigeretur, sed vivens.
units.en: I felt also, in a manner, how wonderfully Christ wills his bride the Church to be exercised, by occasion of so great and so admirable a sacrament of his body and blood. For while we believe the body of the Lord to be under those sensible species, and again the blood, we are exercised in the faith of things that are not seen: believing the assisting, real and true presence of the body of Christ under the species of bread; and of the blood assisting under the species of wine; and of the concomitances of body and soul, and of the whole beauty of the divinity; and in the same way of transubstantiation. We are exercised, moreover, in acts of worshipping such a sacrament in various ways: not only in spirit and within ourselves through faith and devotion, but also through acts of latria, as though he were visible in that very place. Thirdly, we are exercised in our own sanctification, using such food for the sustenance of our soul, its strengthening, illumination, consolation, and every kind of perception of the heavenly treasures. Too wretched, then, are they who will not pay to this sacrament as much as they would pay to the visible bodily person of Christ himself. For nothing less has been left to us than was that which was given at the apostolic supper. To them indeed was given the body which was presently to be betrayed and crucified: not dead — for the body of Christ was not betrayed dead — but living; nor was it dead when it was crucified, but living.

units.la: Dominica quarta post Pentecosten, dum irem ad missam, datum est mihi petere gratiam qua possit anima mea et spiritus defendi a malis spiritibus daemonum, et etiam a malis spiritibus hominum. Hic notavi quod frequenter mihi hactenus acciderunt turbationes et maximae desolationes, ex consideratione malorum spirituum humanorum; id est, ex contemplatione malorum animorum hominum, qui sese mihi offerebant cum variis suspicionibus, imaginando ipsos homines et spiritum malum insidiari animae meae et spiritui meo, et considerare instanter penurias meas spirituales et humanas. Sentiebam sane magnam debilitatem ad pugnandum contra tales malos animos imaginatos; ita quod mihi vide-. batur longé levius si omnes homines intenderent suas vires corporales in persecutionem coporis mei; quam si unus solus homo, per spiritum suum malum niteretur persequi infirmitates animae meae. Hic et intelligebam multa de persecutionibus quaspaļimur in spiritu per malos spiritus daemonuni et hominum. A Hic etiam notavi et ponderavi tormentum illud meum, quod mihi continuum est ex quo novi Germaniam, super defectione talis hujus nationis. Avertat Deus ne hoc eveniat in re ipsa, quod toties apparuit in spiritu meo, non quidem per spiritum bonum, sed potius per spiritum difidentiae, qui tam multis modis me hactenus vexavit, hoc potissimum conjectans ut omnino desperarem de fructu faciendo, et arriperem fugam in animo primum, et deinde ut optarem abire extra sortem hanc Rhenicam mihi deputatam. Notavi etiam hic homini cuilibet summe cavendum esse, ut non se permittat penetrari a ventis illis frigidis, qui sunt ex attenta consideratione alienorum defectuum. Ex his enim saepe con- tingit ut spes quae est de salute proximi per- datur, et bona opinio de ipso, credulitas erga ipsum, amor et charitas. Oportet in calore spiritus superare haec mala, non solum apprehensa, sed etiam, si fieri potest, illa quae sunt in proximo, ut vincatur in bono malum nec desistat a communicatione et cura ejus propler mala ipsius. Propter hoc autem summe necessarium fuerit, in similibus casibus, ut non consideretur res in seipsa, sed in Deo, et in signis beneplaciti ejus. Qui enim mentem suam, et etiam sensum sui spiritus, non erigit in e3 quae Dei sunt, quin potius contemplatur et sentit res istas, defectuosas in se et plenas malorum, quatenus tales in seipsis sunt, ille talis cito turbatur, cito frigescit, desperat de prosperis successibus, dejicitur in fugam quamdam acediosam et tristem. Is facile quoque decipitur, judicat eventus rerum in pejorem partem, suspicionibus cito repletur. O utinam malorum hominum, verorum vel imaginariorum, tepiditas, frigiditas, malitia ac defectio desinat invadere animam meam et spiritum meum, satis alioqui pauperem in seipso, tepidum, frigidum et deficientem. Utinam jam cesset haec muiabilitas mea, qua toties factum est ut antea omnia nimium prospera et prosperanda viderentur; nunc contra omnia perdita et perdenda. Haec non acciderent, si ego nescirem tam multa de causis, de occasionibus per quas generantur mala aut augentur. Sed in his quaerendis et audiendis ego fui nimius, et in pensandis illis ex me1pso. Studiose etiam meditatus sum vim peccatorum, et artes errandi et cadendi. Experientia quoque infirmitatum alienarum et defectuum in hac scientia mihi laborem addidit. Unde factum estut multa praeterierim eorum quae pertinent ad virtutes, et ad bona quae Deus seminavit in hominibus; quae bona si simplici oculo, absque praestantia alterius mali oculi, considerarentur, pax major inveniretur; et si talia reperta promoverentur, major fructus fieret. ji In festo sancti Albani martyris, quod solemne est Moguntiae, die undecimo Junii, ego celebravı missam in summo altari Ecclesiae sancti Albani, À super quo erant expositae variae reliquiae sanctorum corporum, ultra capsulam corporis ej usdem beatissimi Martyris. Inibi ego recepi multam devotionem, conside- rando tam longas peregrinationes hujus Martyris, et quod ipse venisset tempore Arianorum ut more- retur pro Moguntinis. In hoc ego animabar, et spem bonam caeoepi ad fructum faciendum in tempore istarum haeresum Lutheranarum, quae hanc Germa- niam totam prope everterunt; quae haereses nihil aliud sunt quam recessus ab Ecclesia catholica, ut - unusquisque, extra disciplinam Matris suae positus, faciat maxime, et credat, et loquatur quidquid volet, ut vere dici possit haereticos hujus temporis esse doctores discessionis et retrocessionis. Det Deus homines in contrarium sensum, qui factis et verbis doceant veram unionem, accessum ad disciplinam, progressum ad omnes virtutes christianas.
units.en: On the fourth Sunday after Pentecost, while I went to Mass, it was given me to ask the grace by which my soul and spirit might be defended from the evil spirits of the demons, and also from the evil spirits of men. Here I noted that hitherto disturbances and very great desolations have frequently come upon me from the consideration of evil human spirits — that is, from the contemplation of the evil minds of men, which presented themselves to me with various suspicions, as I imagined those men, and the evil spirit, lying in wait for my soul and my spirit, and intently considering my spiritual and human wants. I felt indeed great weakness for fighting against such imagined evil minds; so that it seemed to me far lighter if all men should bend their bodily strength to the persecution of my body, than if one single man, through his evil spirit, should strive to persecute the infirmities of my soul. Here also I understood much about the persecutions we suffer in spirit through the evil spirits of demons and of men. Here too I noted and weighed that torment of mine, which has been continual with me since I came to know Germany, over the falling away of this nation. May God avert that this should come to pass in fact, which has so often appeared in my spirit — not indeed through the good spirit, but rather through the spirit of distrust, which has hitherto vexed me in so many ways, aiming above all at this, that I should utterly despair of bearing fruit, and take flight — first in mind, and then by wishing to depart from this Rhenish lot appointed to me. I noted also here that every man must beware to the utmost of allowing himself to be penetrated by those cold winds which come from the attentive consideration of others' defects. For from these it often comes that the hope one has of a neighbour's salvation is lost, and the good opinion of him, trust in him, love and charity. These evils must be overcome in the heat of the spirit — not only as apprehended, but even, if it can be done, as they are in the neighbour — that evil may be overcome in good, and that one desist not from converse with him and care of him because of his evils. And for this it is supremely necessary, in like cases, that the thing be considered not in itself, but in God, and in the signs of his good pleasure. For he who does not lift his mind, and the very sense of his spirit, to the things that are God's, but rather contemplates and feels these things — defective in themselves and full of evils — just as they are in themselves, such a one is quickly disturbed, quickly grows cold, despairs of prosperous outcomes, and is cast down into a kind of slothful and sad flight. He is easily deceived too; he judges the issues of things for the worse; he is quickly filled with suspicions. O that the lukewarmness, coldness, malice and defection of evil men, real or imaginary, may cease to invade my soul and my spirit — poor enough in itself, lukewarm, cold and failing! May this changefulness of mine now cease, by which it has so often happened that before, everything seemed too prosperous and promising, and now, on the contrary, everything lost and to be lost. These things would not happen if I did not know so much about the causes and occasions through which evils are bred or increased. But in seeking and hearing these I have been excessive, and in weighing them out of my own head. I have also studiously meditated on the power of sins, and the arts of erring and falling; and the experience of others' infirmities and defects has added labour to me in this science. Whence it has come that I have passed over much of what belongs to the virtues, and to the goods which God has sown in men; which goods, if they were considered with a single eye, without the interference of the other, evil eye, greater peace would be found; and if, once found, they were promoted, greater fruit would be borne. On the feast of Saint Alban the martyr, which is solemn at Mainz, on the eleventh day of June, I celebrated Mass at the high altar of the church of Saint Alban, on which were exposed various relics of holy bodies, besides the casket of the body of that most blessed Martyr. There I received much devotion, considering the long pilgrimages of this Martyr, and that he came in the time of the Arians to die for the people of Mainz. In this I took courage, and began to have good hope of bearing fruit in the time of these Lutheran heresies, which have well-nigh overturned this whole Germany; which heresies are nothing else than a withdrawal from the catholic Church, so that each one, placed outside the discipline of his Mother, may do, and believe, and say whatever he pleases; so that it may truly be said that the heretics of this time are the doctors of departure and of going backward. May God give men of the contrary sense, who by deeds and words may teach true union, approach to discipline, and progress towards all the christian virtues.

units.la: In die sancti Joannis, ante missam, ego sensi magnam devotionem in qua petebàm gratiam bene ordinandi meipsum, et omnia negotia mea, et exercitia, et ea quae sunt spiritus mei. Optabam ante omnia esse gratus et acceptus Deo meo, per gratiam. Jesu Christi Domini Nostri; secundo, ut digne prae- stare possim quae eunt sacerdotis, prout est orare, sacrificare, meditari, etc.; tertio, ut ea exercitia quae mihi sunt ad prošimos possim peragere juxta praescriptum divinae voluntatis; idque sive haec sint circa familiares meos, sive circa quoscumque uena a Ban o alios; quarto, petebam specialem gratiam pro directione eorum omnium quos unquam continget - instrui per me.
units.en: On the day of Saint John, before Mass, I felt great devotion, in which I asked the grace of ordering well myself, and all my affairs, and exercises, and the things of my spirit. I wished before all things to be pleasing and acceptable to my God, through the grace of Jesus Christ Our Lord; secondly, that I might worthily perform what belongs to a priest, such as praying, sacrificing, meditating, and so forth; thirdly, that I might carry through the exercises which are mine towards my neighbours according to the prescription of the divine will — whether these concern my own household or any others whatever; fourthly, I asked a special grace for the direction of all those whom it shall ever fall to me to instruct.

units.la: Hic dum considerassem Joannem Baptistam typum fuisse paenitentiae, quique Christum digito demonstravit, ego sensi quaedam quae multum conducunt ad doctrinam exercitiorum quae sunt pro peccatis; utpote quod oporteat inibi conjectare id quod est agere paenitentiam, nec statim desiderare illam compunctionem lacrymosam, sed prius modum quaerendi, probando varios modos faciendi paenitentiam externam; licet scopus esse debeat in ipsa cordis compunctione usque ad lacrymas amaritudinis. Multi enim dolere solent quod non habeant compunctionem cordis, qui tamen nondum patientiam habent ut probent quidnam sit cordis compunctio. Hi vellent sentire tormenta animae suae, et nolunt in ullo carnem suam torquere. Deus autem ' saepe differt perfectiora dona et ipsos fines fructuum, ut interea nos discamus invenire minora dona et media ad ipsos fines. Quidam nihil magis optant quam sensa spiritualia id est ipsius animae; qui vellent experiri in carne compunctionem cordis sui; qui tamen nulla re magis egent quam patientia, aut alia quapiam virtute, cujus defectum ipsi ignorant et non sentiunt. Deus autem vult ut possideamus animam nostram; haec autem non possideri potest nisi per patientiam, juxta illud: In patientia vestra possidebitis animas vestras. Qui autem non possidet propriam animam per patientiam, quomodo justum est ut possideat Deum per sensibilem consolationem?
units.en: Here, having considered that John the Baptist was the type of penance, and the one who pointed out Christ with his finger, I felt certain things which conduce much to the teaching of the exercises which deal with sins: namely, that one must there aim at what it is to do penance, and not at once desire that tearful compunction, but first seek the way, trying various ways of doing outward penance; although the goal must be in the compunction of the heart itself, even to tears of bitterness. For many are wont to grieve that they have no compunction of heart, who nevertheless have not yet the patience to test what compunction of heart is. These would feel the torments of their soul, and are unwilling to torment their flesh in anything. But God often defers the more perfect gifts, and the very ends of the fruits, that meanwhile we may learn to find the lesser gifts and the means to those ends. Some desire nothing more than spiritual feelings, that is, of the soul itself; who would wish to experience in the flesh the compunction of their heart; yet they need nothing more than patience, or some other virtue, whose lack they do not know and do not feel. But God wills that we possess our soul; and it cannot be possessed except through patience, according to that word: In your patience you shall possess your souls. And he who does not possess his own soul through patience — how is it just that he should possess God through sensible consolation?

units.la: In die sanctorum Joannis et Pauli, mane postquam surrexissem, ego habui satis notabilem gratiam ad praeparandum cor meum ad officium dicendum, et ad hoc ut non admitterem alienas affectiones, id est, vel tristitias de aliis rebus, vel laetitias. Eram ego interim, dum vestirem me, et dum absolverem illa necessaria quae praecedunt officium meum, totus collectus ad hoc unum desiderandum, quod est bene et attente et cum devotione orare; ita ut in corde senserim ex hoc desiderio intrare bonam quamdam passionem, id est, timorem ut me non possim servare in ea dispositione. Haec bona dispositio duravit usque post missam, cum desiderio ut semper eamdem viam possem tenere.
units.en: On the day of Saints John and Paul, in the morning after I had risen, I had a quite notable grace for preparing my heart for saying the office, and for not admitting alien affections — that is, either sadnesses about other things, or gladnesses. Meanwhile, as I dressed and finished the necessary things which precede my office, I was wholly recollected towards this one desire: to pray well and attentively and with devotion; so that from this desire I felt a certain good passion enter my heart — namely, a fear that I might not be able to keep myself in that disposition. This good disposition lasted until after Mass, with the desire that I might always hold the same way.

units.la: Hic notavi quod bonum esset ut cor nostrum semper esset vel in quadam tristitia, propter privationem divinae assistentiae atque illustrationis specialis quae ex devotione actuali solet percipi, vel in consolatione, ex praesentia ejusdem. In hoc enim videtur quoddam exercitium perpetuum, ut sentiri possit quidnam sit tandem aliquando privari divina visione et fruitione, et eamdem possidere; quorum alterum est vera damnatio, alterum vero est gloria plena. Å; Missam ego hoc die dixi pro anima illius devotissimi atque docti viri Lanspergii ordinis Carthusiensium, cujus favorem ego ex bono desiderio concupivi. In ipsa etiam missa, dum facerem memoriam defunctorum, ego sensi quod ad maximam gloriam Dei et sanctorum ejus debet esse eductio unius animae de paeoena Purgatorii. Ego apprehendi etiam talem liberationem succedere in magnum subsidium viventium. In Purgatorio enim quodammodo ligata videtur anima illa, ut non possit negotiari circa salutem nostram et circa gloriam Dei; omnes autem beati, postquam in caelis sunt, procurant maxime ut in ipsis celis magis ac magis glorificetur Deus et Christus ejus, cum omnibus concivibus ejūs; simul quoque procurant ut in terra appa- reat gloria Dei, per Jesum Christum, ad pacem animarum viventium; et haec duo sunt juxta. illum hymnum angelicum: Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis.
units.en: Here I noted that it would be good that our heart should always be either in a certain sadness, on account of the privation of the divine assistance and special illumination which is wont to be perceived from actual devotion, or in consolation, from the presence of the same. For in this there appears a kind of perpetual exercise, whereby it may be felt what it is, at the last, to be deprived of the divine vision and fruition, and what to possess it; of which the one is true damnation, and the other is full glory. On this day I said Mass for the soul of that most devout and learned man Lanspergius, of the Carthusian order, whose favour I coveted with a good desire. In the Mass also, while I made the memorial of the departed, I felt that the drawing forth of one soul from the pain of Purgatory must be to the greatest glory of God and of his saints. I apprehended also that such a deliverance turns to the great support of the living. For in Purgatory the soul seems in a manner bound, so that it cannot busy itself about our salvation and the glory of God; whereas all the blessed, once they are in heaven, procure above all that in heaven itself God and his Christ be more and more glorified, with all their fellow-citizens; and at the same time they procure that on earth the glory of God may appear, through Jesus Christ, unto the peace of living souls; and these two accord with that angelic hymn: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.

units.la: Alia die infra octavas sancti Joannis, dum audirem confessionem generalem cujusdam personae, ego accepi magnam quamdam cognitionem circa id quod est facere misericordiam in proximos vivos ac mortuos; ita ut haec cogitando inciderim in lacrymas; et tamen adhuc advertebam ad confessionem mei paenitentis, Intellexi quoque, in hoc discursu, quam efficax medium esset ad inveniendam erga nos Dei misericordiam facere misericordiam, et quod facile sit Deum habere gratiae datorem, si gratis nos el nostra ipsi dederimus; scilicet si etiam circa opera misericordiae corporalia fuerimus misericordes, Deus nobis reddetur in talibus misericors et etiam in spiritualibus., Efficacius autem apud Deum meremur misericordiam spiritualem, si exéėrcemur in operibus misericordiae spiritualibus. Hinc fit ut quidam valde occupati ad orandum quandoque non inve- niant ea quae vellent pro consolatione sui spiritus, ex hoc quod non sint misericordes spiritualiter erga proximos. Quidam vero ita occupati suntcirca šalutem aliorum pure propter Deum, qui quamvis parum quaerant, inveniunt magnam Dei erga se propitiationem, non solum quantum ad remissionem peccalorum suorum, sed etiam quantum ad assecutionem variorum donorym Dei. Hinc ergo accepi magnam intentionem animi exhortandi omnes ad majorem curam operum misericordiae; et simul ad hoc ut, si quis velit Deum sibi valde propitium et non respicientem ad justitiae rigorem, ille debeat esse benignus et in omnes propitius non autem nimium justus aut austerus.
units.en: On another day within the octave of Saint John, while I heard the general confession of a certain person, I received a certain great knowledge concerning what it is to do mercy to our neighbours, living and dead; so that in thinking on this I fell into tears — and yet I still attended to the confession of my penitent. I understood also, in this round, how efficacious a means it is for finding God's mercy towards us, to do mercy; and that it is easy to have God a giver of grace, if we have freely given ourselves and ours to him: that is, if we are merciful even in the bodily works of mercy, God will be shown merciful to us in such things and in spiritual things also. But we merit spiritual mercy with God more efficaciously if we are exercised in the spiritual works of mercy. Hence it comes that some who are much occupied in praying sometimes do not find what they would wish for the consolation of their spirit, because they are not spiritually merciful towards their neighbours. But some are so occupied with the salvation of others purely for God's sake that, although they seek little, they find great propitiation of God towards themselves — not only as regards the remission of their sins, but also as regards the obtaining of various gifts of God. Hence, then, I received a great intention of mind to exhort all men to greater care for the works of mercy; and at the same time to this: that if anyone wishes God to be very propitious to him, and not to look to the rigour of justice, he ought himself to be kind, and propitious towards all, and not too just or austere.

units.la: In die apostolorum Petri et Pauli, cum dicerem missam pro quodam amico, datum est sperare el a misericordia Dei, per intercessionem Virginis et horum Apostolorum, quaedam quae mihi vide- bantur valde necessaria. Item in discursu mysteriorum vitae Christi, dum attente considerassem effusiones sanguinis ejus, et alias abundantias passionum et operationum ipsius, ego hoc modo oravi: Domine, Deus omnipotens, rogo lte, per meritum illius effusi in terram sanguinis, ut velis concedere gratiam quam postulo tali personae, ut sic non perdatur talis abundantia, quae nondum est (ut ita dicam) expensa. Imaginabar enim aliquas guttas sanguinis, item aliquos labores particulares aliquorum membrorum Christi, item aliqua verba particularia, aut facta, vel etiam signa, aut passiones, aut sudores, aut famem, aut sitim humanitatis ejus, et dicebam Deo Patri: Talia forsitan, o Deus meus, nėemo unquam sibi applicavit particulariter in medicinam vel salutem: applicentur igitur ad hanc rem quam peto, ut minus deperdita dici possint; postquam tam bonum opus operata fuerint. Multa verba ejus scilicet non fuerunt admissa ad aliquas aures mentales, neque etiam fortasse corporales; multo adhuc plura fuerunt quidem audita, sed. non intellecta; adhuc vero plura fuerunt intellecta, sed non percepta ex visceribus cordis; sed adhuc alia multa percepta sensu fuerunt cordis, quae non executa sunt per opus. Apostolorum autem officium, et discipulorum Christi; et ipsum sequentium est ut, quidquid est Christus, et quidquid est ex 1ps0, et per ipsum, et in ipso, et ipsius, et ad ipsum pertinens, et pro ipsius glọria ordinatum a Patre, haec inquam ut ipsi diligentissime quaerant, haec cogitent, sentiant, imitentur, magnificent, dilatent; ut inde fiat ne perdantur ea quae pro salute nostra facta sunt.
units.en: On the day of the apostles Peter and Paul, when I said Mass for a certain friend, it was given me to hope from the mercy of God, through the intercession of the Virgin and of these Apostles, certain things which seemed to me very necessary. Likewise, in the round of the mysteries of the life of Christ, when I had attentively considered the sheddings of his blood, and the other abundances of his sufferings and workings, I prayed in this manner: Lord, God almighty, I beg thee, by the merit of that blood poured out upon the earth, that thou wouldst grant the grace which I ask for such a person, so that such abundance be not lost, which has not yet (so to speak) been spent. For I imagined certain drops of blood, certain particular labours of certain members of Christ, certain particular words, or deeds, or even signs, or sufferings, or sweats, or the hunger, or the thirst of his humanity, and I said to God the Father: Such things, O my God, perhaps no one has ever applied to himself in particular for medicine or salvation: let them then be applied to this thing which I ask, that they may be said to be the less lost, having wrought so good a work. For many of his words were not admitted to any mental ears, nor perhaps even to bodily ones; many more indeed were heard, but not understood; more still were understood, but not perceived from the bowels of the heart; and yet many others were perceived with the feeling of the heart, which were not carried out in work. But the office of the Apostles, and of the disciples of Christ and of those who follow him, is this: that whatever Christ is, and whatever is from him, and through him, and in him, and his, and pertaining to him, and ordained by the Father for his glory — that all this they should most diligently seek, think on, feel, imitate, magnify and spread abroad; so that thereby the things which were done for our salvation may not be lost.

units.la: In die commemorationis sancti Pauli, ego inveni quemdam bonum intellectum, ad sentiendum quo päcto turpitudo animae offendit oculos sul Creatoris; foetor vero ipsius offendit olfactum; amaritudo gustum; nimia frigiditas mala ac caliditas tactum. Turpitudo porro ac faeditas potissimam ex sordibus luxuriae, et peccatorum carnalium quae sunt propter affectum carnis propriae, vel alenae, cognoscitur. Faetor vero ac odor malus deprehenditur ex malo nomine et mala fama. Homo enim cujus vita scandalosa est, non solum apud bonos homines *vivos faetere dicitur, sed etiam apud Deum; et longe prius apud Deum, quia ipse prius videt, et plura, et melius quam homines. Amaritudo autem ac tepiditas quod divino gustui displiceat, ex ira, superbia, invidia, et perversis odiis deprehenditur; tactus aulem Dei offenditur per acediam, in qua frigent homines respectu bonarum artium, et in concupiscentiis habendi, quae est avaritia. Probet igitur se homo ad proprios sensus internos, quiafacile videbit- offendi oculos mentis suae a turpitudine corporalium immunditiarum et sordium suarum, luxuriae et gulae. Sentiet quoque ipse faetorem suum, si cogitet malam de se opinionem; itaque sibi male etiam olebit. Si deprehenderit praeterea iram, vel choleram, vel invidiam ac superbiam suam, statim in se amaricabitur, id est, sentiet se amarum esse, aut insipidum propter superbiam, amarum propter alias passiones irae et invidiae. Ubi demum senserit acediam suam ac avaritiam, statim percipiet laedi tactum spiritus sui frigiditate nimia, qua nescit affici ad res bonas, aut calore quo videbit se non posse divelli a curis rerum temporalium, vel ab amore ipsarum. Sentiet alteras duas tactus qualitates, mollitiem nimiam detinentem in quiete, et duritiam nimiam qua fit ut non possit penetrari a rebus divinis. Probet igitur se homo, maxime qui vult panem caelestem edere, qui est cibus et vita totius animae et corporis, et cujuslibet sensus recreatio ac glorificatioò. Nos autem niti debemus ad hoc, ut efficiamur pabulum Christi, et cibus quem digerendo ipse possit in corpus suum mysticum convertere, ac digerere in viros perfectos, et in valida ac utilia membra ejusdem corporis. Proinde ergo cavendum est ne apud aliquem sensum Christi improbari possimus.
units.en: On the day of the commemoration of Saint Paul I found a certain good understanding, for feeling in what way the foulness of a soul offends the eyes of its Creator; its stench offends his smell; its bitterness his taste; its excessive evil cold and heat his touch. Now foulness and filthiness are known chiefly from the dirt of lust, and of the carnal sins which come from affection for one's own flesh or another's. Stench and ill odour are detected from an ill name and ill fame: for a man whose life is scandalous is said to stink, not only among good men living, but also before God — and far sooner before God, since he sees sooner, and more, and better than men. That bitterness and lukewarmness displease the divine taste is detected from anger, pride, envy and perverse hatreds; and the touch of God is offended through sloth, in which men are cold towards good arts, and in the concupiscence of possessing, which is avarice. Let a man therefore test himself by his own inward senses; for he will easily see the eyes of his mind offended by the foulness of his bodily impurities and dirt, of lust and gluttony. He will also smell his own stench, if he thinks of the ill opinion held of him — and so he will smell ill even to himself. If he further detects his anger, or choler, or envy and pride, he will at once grow bitter within — that is, he will feel himself bitter, or insipid through pride, bitter through the other passions of anger and envy. And when at last he feels his sloth and avarice, he will at once perceive the touch of his spirit hurt by an excessive coldness, whereby he knows not how to be moved towards good things, or by a heat whereby he will see that he cannot be torn away from the cares of temporal things, or from the love of them. He will feel also the two other qualities of touch: an excessive softness that detains him in ease, and an excessive hardness whereby he cannot be penetrated by divine things. Let a man therefore test himself — above all he who would eat the heavenly bread, which is the food and life of the whole soul and body, and the refreshment and glorification of every sense. And we ought to strive to become the food of Christ, a nourishment which he, digesting, can convert into his mystical body, and digest into perfect men, and into strong and useful members of that same body. Accordingly we must beware lest we be found reprobate to any sense of Christ.

units.la: Infra dies solemnitatis festi Visitationis, ego inveni, quadam vice, magnum desiderium ad eam gratiam, quae est si quis in suis operibus posset cognoscere Dei voluntatem bonam, beneplacitam et perfectam. Magnam proinde consolationem concepi, ex quo circa quoddam negotium mihi operata fuerit mens ad intelligendum modum quem deberem tenere.
units.en: Within the days of the solemnity of the feast of the Visitation I found, on one occasion, a great desire for that grace which is to be able to know, in one's works, the good, well-pleasing and perfect will of God. I conceived accordingly great consolation, because with regard to a certain affair my mind had been wrought upon to understand the way I ought to keep.

units.la: In die dedicationis summi templi Moguntini, ego inveni magnam devotionem, in qua quidquid orabam, aut sentiebam, recognoscebam hoc facere nomine et quasi in persona eorum, quos specialiter in memoria habeo. Venerabar Chris- tum, verbi gratia, in mea persona, et tanquam por uenn g e a a repraesentarem fratres meos, omnesque consanguineos. Item venerabar reliquias sanctorum in altari expositas, et nomine aliorum, et maxime eorum quos scio libenter velle posse coram eisdem reliquiis adstare. Optabam etiam ex animo ut sancti qui sunt in coelo adorarent, honorificarent, glorificarentque Deum, et ei gralias, nomine meo et omnium nostrum qui sumus in terra, agerent in Spiritu quem jam possident. Pridie octavae apostolorum Petri et Pauli, sub noctem, ego sensi multa desideria bona pro me, pro sociis meis; pro parentibus, et generaliter pro multis aliis, qui occurrebant menti meae. Sensi etiam magnum et vivum desiderium, in quo petebam a Domino ut dignaretur hujusmodi desideria acceptare, tanquam si Ipsimet pro quibus sentiebam illa sentirent et peterent.
units.en: On the day of the dedication of the cathedral of Mainz I found great devotion, in which whatever I prayed or felt, I recognized myself as doing it in the name, and as it were in the person, of those whom I specially hold in memory. I venerated Christ, for example, in my own person, and as though I represented my brethren and all my kindred. Likewise I venerated the relics of the saints exposed on the altar, in the name also of others, and above all of those whom I know would gladly wish to be able to stand before those same relics. I wished also from my heart that the saints who are in heaven might adore, honour and glorify God, and give him thanks, in my name and in the name of all of us who are on earth, in the Spirit which they now possess. On the eve of the octave of the apostles Peter and Paul, towards night, I felt many good desires for myself, for my companions, for my parents, and generally for many others who came to my mind. I felt also a great and lively desire, in which I asked the Lord to deign to accept such desires, as though the very persons for whom I felt them were feeling and asking them themselves.

units.la: Item quod in hac parte me faceret vicarium Christi, maxime in missa quam proponebam dicere.
units.en: Likewise that in this respect he would make me a vicar of Christ, above all in the Mass which I purposed to say.

units.la: In die octava, dum ecclesiam intrassem, ego habui magnam devotionem accipiendo aquam benedictam, et petivi a Deo Patre ut quidquid benedictionis et sanctificationis habet illa aqua, mihi applicaretur in lotionem animae, €t in as- persionem benedictionis, et in defensionem contra hostes meos invisibiles. Dum etiam me convertissem ad imaginem crucifixi, ad orandum Christum, ego ibidem sensi quamdam vivam intelligentiam circa utilitatem imaginum, quae ideo (ut tunc primum sensi) sunt repraesentationes personarum, quia denuo nobis praesentes ipsas faciunt. Rogavi ergo, cum magna devotione, Deum Patrem, ut dignaretur mihi applicare hanc gratiam praesentiae Christi, et ipsum praesentem faceret menti meae, juxta hane virtutem repraesentativam quam habent imagines sanctorum, apud pie credentes ac catholice fideles. Idem quoque mihi confirmabatur, dum converterer ad imaginem Virginis, per cujus imàginis aspectum, optabam ut beata Virgo perquam praesentissima fieret menti meae. A Ex loco ipso etiam in quo eram, id est, ex templo, optabam cum bona devotione ut mihi daretur major virtus orandi, juxta pactum Dei, quod est ut fideles specialiter ibì exaudiantur. In summa egohic 'sensi magnas esse harum rerum virtutes apud credentes: non sohım prop- ter pietatem et fidem, sed etiam primitus propter Dei ordinationem, et propter verba ipsius, et sanctae matris Ecclesiae sensum.
units.en: On the octave day, when I had entered the church, I had great devotion in taking holy water, and I asked of God the Father that whatever of blessing and sanctification that water has might be applied to me for the washing of my soul, for the sprinkling of blessing, and for defence against my invisible enemies. And when I had turned to the image of the crucified, to pray to Christ, I felt there a certain lively understanding concerning the usefulness of images, which are for this reason (as I then felt for the first time) representations of persons, that they make those persons present to us again. I begged therefore, with great devotion, God the Father, that he would deign to apply to me this grace of the presence of Christ, and make him present to my mind, according to that representative power which the images of the saints have among the piously believing and catholic faithful. The same was confirmed to me when I turned to the image of the Virgin, by the sight of which image I wished that the blessed Virgin might become most fully present to my mind. From the very place also in which I was — that is, from the church — I wished with good devotion that a greater power of praying might be given me, according to the covenant of God, which is that the faithful are heard there in a special way. In sum, I felt here that great are the powers of these things among believers: not only because of piety and faith, but also, in the first place, because of God's ordinance, and because of his words, and the mind of holy mother Church.

units.la: Ante Sacramentum positus et flexis genibus humiliatus, ego sensi magnam devotionem, considerando quod ibi realiter sit corpus Christi, et ex consequenti assistentia totius Trinitatis, quodam mirabili modo, quo non adsistit rebus aliis, nec in aliis locis. Alia igitur, ut imagines, ut aqua benedicta, ut templa, faciunt nobis adesse Christum, aut sanctos, aut virtutes spirituales, modo spirituali; Sacramentum vero hoc. facit adesse Christum, et omnem Dei virtutem, realiter, sub illis speciebus. Sit nomen ejus benedictum!
units.en: Placed before the Sacrament, and humbled on bended knees, I felt great devotion, considering that there the body of Christ really is, and consequently the presence of the whole Trinity, in a certain wonderful manner in which it is not present to other things, nor in other places. Other things, then — such as images, holy water, churches — make Christ, or the saints, or spiritual powers present to us in a spiritual manner; but this Sacrament makes Christ, and all the power of God, present really, under those species. Blessed be his name!

units.la: Eodem die octava Apostolorum, dum meminissem gratiarum et beneficiorum Dei, accidit mihi ut quasi querelam in anima mea sentirem, quam nunquam senseram. Videbatur enim mihi, per gratiam Dei, multis modis: fieri abundantiam et pacem in interioribus meis; me vero male respondere gratiae Dei per exteriora, id est, opera charitatis. Olim aliquando ego non sentie- ' bam defectus. meos, neque internos neque ex- ternos; et itidem de gratia Dei, quam tune nec intus nec extra experiebar, id est nec per externa mea neque per interna. Postea factum est ut daretur mihi gratia, et daretur quaerere pacem ejus; et tunc solum querebar de internis meis quae videbantur absque sensu, cum tamen corpus et mens labores sentirent. Demum ad majorem cumulum Dei misericordiae accessit, ut ego jam videar nimium quiescere in Deo meo, et in charitate proximi, deficere autem maxime in executione, et in expensione tot et tantorum talentorum. Faxit Jesus ut non nimium cito invenerim tantam pacem in meipso, quantum pertinet ad malas inclinationes et frigiditates; nimium cito, inquam, id est antequam essem omnibus modis exercitatus in victoria mei, etin pugna quae per proprium corpus fit contra daemones, etad extinguindas malas impressiones.
units.en: On the same octave day of the Apostles, while I remembered the graces and benefits of God, it befell me to feel as it were a complaint in my soul, such as I had never felt. For it seemed to me that, by the grace of God, abundance and peace were in many ways being wrought in my inward parts; but that I was answering ill to the grace of God through my outward parts, that is, the works of charity. Once upon a time I did not feel my defects, either inward or outward; and likewise of the grace of God, which at that time I experienced neither within nor without — that is, neither through my outward nor through my inward things. Afterwards it came about that grace was given me, and it was given me to seek its peace; and then I complained only of my inward parts, which seemed without feeling, while yet body and mind felt their labours. At last, to the greater heap of God's mercy, it has come to this: that I now seem to rest too much in my God and in the charity of my neighbour, but to fail most in execution, and in the spending of so many and so great talents. May Jesus grant that I have not found so much peace in myself too soon — as regards my evil inclinations and coldnesses; too soon, I say, that is, before I had been exercised in every way in the victory over myself, and in the battle which is fought through one's own body against the demons, and for the quenching of evil impressions.

units.la: Alio die infra easdem octavas Visitationis, dum sese mihi offerrent variae hominum necessitates, penuriae, angustiae, turbationes, adversitates, oppressiones, ego sensi magnum desiderium immitti mihi, in quo optabam me posse perseverare in tali consideratione miseriarum vivorum et mortuorum, et me posse semper orare pro illis, tanquam qui more Moysis sustineam manus elevatas quamdiu alii pugnant et patiuntur, aut ad aliquid boni pertendunt cum conatu, ad quod egeant auxilio aliorum. Pro hac gratia obtinenda ego obtuli Deo sanctum sacrificium; in quo officio dum pervenissem ad yerba: Orate, fratres, ego sensi vehemens desiderium ad hoc ut circumstantes orarent pro me; et ex animo adverti quod hoc ita non fit diligenter apud multos. Ideo data est mihi*bona devotio ad desiderandum quod Angeli, circumstantium hominum custodes, orarent pro me, defectum sibi commissorum hominum supplentes. Eodem die, ego satis clare sensi et agnovi quod qui volunt dilatari in Deo, et elevari, extėndi, consolari et augeri, debent spiritum bene exercere in eo quod est in seipsis, id est in carne sua et in spiritu suo restringi, refraenari, humiliari, angusliari, lugere, diminui. Ex mortificatione etenim propriae carnis et proprii spiritus abnegatione proceditur ad possessionem Dei. Intrandum est enim per angustam portam; qu ae porta angusta, si consideretur in unoquoque, ipsa est via qua itur ad cor: ad quod conversi intrant in veritatem et vitam.
units.en: On another day within the same octave of the Visitation, while there presented themselves to me the various necessities of men — their wants, distresses, disturbances, adversities, oppressions — I felt a great desire sent into me, in which I wished that I might persevere in such consideration of the miseries of the living and the dead, and might always pray for them, as one who, after the manner of Moses, holds up his hands while others fight and suffer, or strive with effort towards some good for which they need the help of others. For the obtaining of this grace I offered to God the holy sacrifice; in which office, when I had come to the words Orate, fratres, I felt a vehement desire that those standing about might pray for me; and from my heart I observed that this is not done diligently among many. Therefore a good devotion was given me to desire that the Angels, the guardians of the men standing about, might pray for me, supplying the defect of the men entrusted to them. On the same day I felt and recognized quite clearly that those who wish to be enlarged in God, and raised, extended, consoled and increased, ought to exercise the spirit well in that which lies in themselves — that is, in their flesh and in their spirit — to be restrained, bridled, humbled, straitened, to mourn, to be diminished. For from the mortification of one's own flesh, and the denial of one's own spirit, one proceeds to the possession of God. For we must enter through the narrow gate; and that narrow gate, if it be considered in each one of us, is the way that leads to the heart: and they who turn to it enter into truth and life.

units.la: Cor enim in homine est primum quod animatur ab anima nostra, et ultimum quod deseritur. Oportet igitur ut paulatim reducamur, secundum animum sensitivum et rationalem ad cor nostrum: ut tandem illic collecti et illic uniti, transeamus inde ad vitam indivisibilem ac spiritualem, quae abscondita est in Deo cum Christo. j In die Visitationis beate Mariae, ego iterum recognovi gratiam tali die mihi factam, in hoc quod professus fuerim modum vivendi qui est secundum institutionem Societatis Jesu Christi; et rogavi ut mihi detur gratia crescendi in omnibus, juxta vota hujus instituti; utper castitatis votum possim tandem inveniri mundus et ablutus corpore aqua munda; per votum paupertatis possim esse purus ab omnibus: intentionibus mundanis, et imprimis ab omni intentione habendi; per votum obedientiae possim fieri instrumentum aptum ad omne Þonum opus exequendum cum diligentia. Faxit igitur Jesus ut sim mundus et purus et fidelis, in omni dispensatione mihi credita et credenda: mundus, inquam, in corpore et in exteriori homine, purus in intimis spiritibus, et fidelis in operibus.
units.en: For the heart in man is the first thing that is animated by our soul, and the last that is deserted. We must therefore be led back little by little, according to the sensitive and rational soul, to our heart: that at last, gathered there and united there, we may pass thence to the indivisible and spiritual life which is hidden with Christ in God. On the day of the Visitation of blessed Mary I acknowledged anew the grace done me on such a day, in that I made profession of the manner of living which is according to the institute of the Society of Jesus Christ; and I begged that grace be given me to grow in all things according to the vows of this institute: that through the vow of chastity I may at last be found clean, my body washed with clean water; through the vow of poverty I may be pure from all worldly intentions, and first of all from every intention of possessing; through the vow of obedience I may become an instrument apt for carrying out every good work with diligence. May Jesus then grant that I be clean and pure and faithful in every stewardship entrusted and to be entrusted to me: clean, I say, in body and in the outward man; pure in my inmost spirits; and faithful in works.

units.la: In die sancti Anacleti papaeet martyris, dum essem celebraturus missam, et propter hoc iturus ad monasterium fratrum sancti Augustini, ego habui quamdam considerationem pro adjuvanda intentione mea, quae erat celebrare ad petitionem prioris illius conventus. Consideratio autem fuit, ut ego acciperem id quod est facere aliquid nomine illius prioris, quasi sit facere illud pro discipulo sancti Augustini. Et ex hoc venit in. mentem meam, et desideravi, ut quidquid, unquam ego possem facere pro priore alicujus conventus, esset factum tanquam pro discipulo primi institutoris ejus ordinis; puta sancti Augustini, sancti Francisci, Dominici, Benedicti, Bernardi, et ita de monialibus. Si autem hoc fieret a me pro aliquo ex reliquis fratribus, ut ipsum fieret et a Deo acceptaretur, tanquam fieret discipulo discipuli, aut confratri discipuli illius sancti. Circa Generales autem talium ordinum, ego desiderabam me habere tanquam ipsi sint (prout sunt) vicarii talium Sanctorum, et quasi ipsimet sancti essent. Circa episcopos quoque simile aliquid accidebat; unde optabam habere episcopum romanum, qui est sammus pontifex, tanquam vicarium personae Christi, successorem et locum tenentem, caeteros autem episcopos tanquam vicarios reliquorum Christi apostolorum, et quasi essent ipsimet apostoli Christi; sacerdotes vero tanquam.si essent ipsius Christi discipuli, quia et ipsi sunt vicarii discipulorum ejus; diaconos vero et reliquos Ecclesiae ministros tanquam discipulos apostolorum et discipulorum Christi; diaconi enim hujus temporis sunt tanquam successores et vicarii discipulorum et apostolorum. Itaque summus pontifex ita mihi et omnibus Christianis observandus est, quasi esset persona Christi corporati, in quantum ipse Christus est Ecclesiae caput, et sacerdos, et princeps pastorum, de cujus plenitudine omnes accepimus, et administrator gratiarum, donorum et virtutum et omnium bonorum novi testamenti. Imperator autem Christiani imperii observandus et timendus quasi minister Dei altissimi, quantum ad justitiam, et quasi brachium potentiae Christi, in quantum ipse Dominus dominantium est, et quia omnia subjecta sunt sub pedibus Christi, licet adhuc multa restent actualiter subjicienda. Et quia data est Christo omnis potestas, sive in coelo, sive in terra, hinc fit ut sint duae aucto- En Pi w = rTitates, vicarius Christi, qui est sammus pontifex, et summus rex, id est imperator romanus; et ille quidem Christum sacerdotem, et prophetam, et pontificem, et pastorem, et ministrum omnis sacrae dispensationis exhibet: hic autem Christum Regem et Dominatorem, et qui habet potestatem regendi in virga ferrea; sed quoniam talem auctoritatem sibi acquisivit (cum sua esset) per passionem et obedientiam, ideo ipsa subjecta est pontificatul ipsius. Ad haec dici quoque at necdum intelligi potest, quod pontifex summus administer est, loco Christi, misericordiae et gratiae Dei, et occullorum judiciorum quae sunt circa animas; imperator autem Dei justiciae administrator; et ille quidem quodam modo repraesentat Christum humilem, qui venit in carne et mortuus est; hic vero Christum omnipotentem, qui surrexit et regnat in caeoelis, et venturus est judicare vivos et mortuos et saeculum per ignem.
units.en: On the day of Saint Anacletus, pope and martyr, when I was to celebrate Mass, and for that purpose to go to the monastery of the friars of Saint Augustine, I had a certain consideration to help my intention, which was to celebrate at the request of the prior of that convent. The consideration was that I should take the doing of something in the name of that prior as being the doing of it for a disciple of Saint Augustine. And from this it came into my mind, and I desired, that whatever I might ever do for the prior of any convent should be done as for a disciple of the first founder of his order — say Saint Augustine, Saint Francis, Dominic, Benedict, Bernard; and so of the nuns. And if this should be done by me for any of the other friars, that it might be done, and accepted by God, as though done to a disciple of a disciple, or to a fellow-brother of a disciple, of that saint. As to the Generals of such orders, I desired to bear myself as though they were (as indeed they are) the vicars of those Saints, and as if they were the saints themselves. Concerning bishops too something similar occurred; whence I wished to regard the Roman bishop, who is the supreme pontiff, as the vicar of the person of Christ, his successor and lieutenant; and the other bishops as vicars of the rest of Christ's apostles, and as if they were themselves the apostles of Christ; and priests as if they were the disciples of Christ himself, for they too are the vicars of his disciples; and deacons and the other ministers of the Church as disciples of the apostles and of the disciples of Christ; for the deacons of this time are as the successors and vicars of the disciples and apostles. And so the supreme pontiff is to be regarded by me and by all Christians as though he were the person of Christ embodied, inasmuch as Christ is the head of the Church, and priest, and prince of pastors, of whose fulness we have all received, and the administrator of the graces, gifts and virtues and of all the goods of the new testament. And the Emperor of the Christian empire is to be regarded and feared as the minister of God most high in what concerns justice, and as the arm of the power of Christ, inasmuch as he is the Lord of lords, and because all things are subjected under the feet of Christ, though many things still remain to be actually subjected. And because all power has been given to Christ, both in heaven and on earth, hence there are two authorities: the vicar of Christ, who is the supreme pontiff, and the supreme king, that is, the Roman emperor; and the former displays Christ the priest, and prophet, and pontiff, and pastor, and minister of every sacred dispensation; the latter, Christ the King and Ruler, who has the power of ruling with a rod of iron; but since he acquired such authority for himself (though it was his own) through suffering and obedience, therefore that authority is subject to his pontificate. To this may be added — though it can hardly yet be understood — that the supreme pontiff is the administrator, in the place of Christ, of the mercy and grace of God, and of the hidden judgments that concern souls; while the emperor is the administrator of God's justice; and the former in a certain manner represents Christ humble, who came in the flesh and died; the latter, Christ almighty, who rose and reigns in heaven, and is to come to judge the living and the dead, and the world by fire.

units.la: Alia quadam die, dum sensissem me distrahi ab oratione, venit in mentem ut peterem, auxilium gratiae Dei: ad quod melius obtinendum, succur- rebat mihi quod Christus Jesus Dominus Noster, dum mortalis esset, semper vixerit distractus a gloria caelesti, quantum ad corpus, quod quidem ab instanti conceptionis fuit capax gloriae; nec ullum habuit obstaculum in se, aut maculam, aut indispositionem, propter quam debuerat primum mori; sed potuisset glorificari, et recipere dotes corporis quas postea recepit, et prout in transfiguratione apparuit. Orabam igitur remedium contra distractiones spiritus mei, et sic inveni magnam confortationem. Hic quoque mihi inciderunt multae considerationes circa distractiones beatae Virginis, quibus fuit distracta, non a gratia, qua semper plena fuit: sed a gloria corporis et animae, cum tunc nullum impedimentum haberet ex originali peccato, nec ex actuali; item fuit distracta ab aspectu illius Salutaris, quod postea concepit ipsa et peperit et nutrivit; et habuit etiam multas alias distractiones, quanquam istae non dicantur propriae distractiones, quia res non prius habentur et postea perduntur. Sed sunt remorationes quibus et Christus quantum ad corpus, et Virgo quantum ad corpus et animam, detinebantur et retardabantur a consecutione illius perfectae gloriae Dei.
units.en: On another day, when I felt myself drawn away from prayer, it came into my mind to ask the help of the grace of God; and for the better obtaining of it, this came to my aid: that Christ Jesus Our Lord, while he was mortal, always lived withheld from heavenly glory as regards his body — which indeed from the instant of his conception was capable of glory; nor had he any obstacle in himself, or stain, or indisposition, on account of which he should first have had to die; but he could have been glorified, and have received the endowments of the body which he afterwards received, even as he appeared in the transfiguration. I prayed therefore for a remedy against the distractions of my spirit, and so found great strengthening. Here also many considerations came to me concerning the withholdings of the blessed Virgin — the things from which she was withheld: not from grace, of which she was always full, but from the glory of body and soul, since she had then no impediment from original sin, nor from actual; likewise she was withheld from the sight of that Salvation which she afterwards conceived and bore and nursed; and she had many other such withholdings — although these are not properly called deprivations, because the things were not first possessed and afterwards lost. But they are delays, by which both Christ as to his body, and the Virgin as to body and soul, were detained and retarded from the attainment of that perfect glory of God.

units.la: Et ipsa Virgo, et multi aut plerique omnes alii Sancti a variis desideriis ad quae festinabant retardabantur; unde fiebat ut non satiarentur, nec possent satiari, donec apparitura esset Dei gloria.
units.en: And the Virgin herself, and many — or indeed almost all — the other Saints were retarded from various desires towards which they were hastening; whence it came that they were not satisfied, nor could be satisfied, until the glory of God should appear.

units.la: Alia autem vice, id est in die quo celebrabam officium sanctorum martyrum Processi et Martiniani, ego habui satis utilem considerationem circa quinque plagas Christi; et mihi incidit ex aspectu imaginis ipsius crucifixi. Considerabam autem eas plagas manuum et pedum, quasi me admonerent esse nobis maxime insistendum circa profectum bene operandi, et circa profectum bene desiderandi: sic ut operibus et affectibus laboremus;'item ut simus diligentes, nec timeamus pati ambulando et peregrinando pedibus nostris; sed potius ita vivamus, ut tandem in manibus etin pedibus appareant vestigia laborum, sicut Paulus dicit de toto corpore suo: Ego stigmata Domini in corpore meo porto. Circa plagam lateris, ego haec notavi, quod videlicet ipsa facta fuerit post mortem Christi, ut consummatis omnibus et jam omnibus meritis Christi accumulatis, sanguis ille tandem emanaret nobis cum aqua, qui secum portaret consummatum pretium meritorum Christi; simul autem ut docea- SOO E E a mur, quia nisi mortui fuerimus, non poterimus gustare illa interna dona quae sunt ad perfectam cordium salutem. Primum igitur nobis aperti fuerunt fontes thesaurorum manuum et pedum ante mortem, et postea thesauri dextri lateris ac viscerum.
units.en: On another occasion — that is, on the day when I celebrated the office of the holy martyrs Processus and Martinian — I had a very useful consideration concerning the five wounds of Christ; and it came to me from looking at the image of the crucified himself. I considered those wounds of the hands and feet as though they admonished me that we must above all press on in the progress of working well, and in the progress of desiring well: so that we labour with works and with affections; likewise that we be diligent, and not fear to suffer in walking and journeying with our feet; but rather so live that at last in our hands and feet the traces of labours may appear, as Paul says of his whole body: I bear the marks of the Lord in my body. Concerning the wound of the side, I noted this: that it was made after the death of Christ, so that, when all was consummated and all the merits of Christ now heaped up, that blood might at last flow out for us with water, carrying with it the consummated price of the merits of Christ; and at the same time that we might be taught that unless we have died, we shall not be able to taste those inward gifts which belong to the perfect health of hearts. First, then, were opened to us the fountains of the treasures of the hands and feet, before his death; and afterwards the treasures of the right side and of the heart.

sections.arg: In hoc Epilogo admodum pauca ab Auctore annotantur inter tot et tanta quae ab anno 1543 usque ad vitae finem anno 1546 a Deo accepit.

units.la: Circa hoc tempus ego accepi praeceptum obedientiae, qua oportuit me recedere de Colonia in Portugalliam. Ad profectionem ego me accinxi in mense. Soptembri. Veni autem Antuerpiam, et dum non possem navigare, rediens Lovanium, incidi in febrem tertianam quae me detinuit duos ferme menses.
units.en: About this time I received the command of obedience by which I had to leave Cologne for Portugal. I made myself ready for the journey in the month of September. I came to Antwerp, and when I could not sail, returning to Louvain I fell into a tertian fever which held me almost two months.

units.la: Quodam autem die, cum gravarer infirmitate, et sentirem meam ariditatem, vidererque mihi a Deo elongatus, occurrit mihi consolatio quaedam in intelligentia verborum illorum: Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Sequenti die, volens dormire (parum enim septem diebus prae infirmitate dormieram) caeoepi cogitare et mente: volvere illud: In pace in idipsum dormiam et requiescam. Sequenti die, cum dolerem et prae infirmitate nimium. gravarer, coepi cogitare caput Christi spinis obsitum, ibi usque ad multas lacrymas compunctus; et datum est mihi desiderare ut caput meum spinoso capiti Christi adhaereret et ibi pungeretur.
units.en: On a certain day, when I was weighed down by illness and felt my dryness, and seemed to myself far removed from God, a certain consolation came to me in the understanding of those words: I am with him in tribulation. The next day, wishing to sleep (for I had slept little for seven days because of the illness), I began to think and turn over in my mind that verse: In peace in the selfsame I will sleep and I will rest. The next day, when I was in pain and much weighed down by the illness, I began to think of the head of Christ beset with thorns, being pricked there even to many tears; and it was given me to desire that my head might cleave to the thorn-crowned head of Christ and there be pricked.

units.la: In die Circumcisionis Domini, quae fuit prima anni 1544, ego cum multa devotione agnovi Christum pro nobis signum circumcisionis accepisse, sicque voluisse tanquam esset unus de populo judaico reputari. Item quod nomen inter homines accipere voluerit. Ex his factum estin me magnum desiderium, quo ex Deo petebam haec duo: primo videlicet ut, in hoc die, possem aliquod signum verae circumcisionis, per gratiam Dei, in anima mea recipere, unde jam annumerari possem inter homines populi Dei; secundo petebam gratiam, qua fieret ut nunc primum nomen meum posset inscribi libro vitae.
units.en: On the day of the Circumcision of the Lord, which was the first day of the year 1544, I acknowledged with much devotion that Christ received for us the sign of circumcision, and so willed to be reckoned as one of the Jewish people; likewise that he willed to receive a name among men. From this there arose in me a great desire, in which I asked of God these two things: first, that on this day I might receive, by the grace of God, some sign of true circumcision in my soul, whereby I might now be numbered among the men of the people of God; second, I asked the grace whereby it might come about that now first my name might be written in the book of life.

units.la: Post festum Regum hujus anni, ego revocatus sum ab incaepta profectione mea, quae erat ad Portugalliam; et redii Coloniam, dimissis in Portugalliam Francisco de Strada, magistro Andrea Oviedo, domino Joanne de Aragon, et novemñ aliis quos Lovanii Domino per Jesum Christum acquisşiveramus:qui fuerunt magister Petrus Faber de Halis, magister Hermes, magister Joannes, magister Maximilianus, dominus, Leonardus, magister Jacobus, magister Daniel, Thomas parvus, Cornelius. Rediens autem Coloniam, mecum duxi magistrum Lambertum et Aemilianum; et locata Coloniae domo, inibi fui usque ad mensem Julii, ubi et latine praedicavi, in schola artium, omnibus diebus Dominicis, et reliquis festis, absque extraordinariis praedicationibus, relictis tandem ibidem dominoAlvaro, et novem aliis secum scholaribus nostrae Societatis, quos Jesus bonum fundamentum esse hic faciat suae Societatis. Inde recepi mandatum novum, praecipiens ut in Portugalliam juxta regis voluntatem proficiscerer. Decessi autem duodecima die mensis Julii, et mecum inde detuli septem capita ex sanctis corporibus XI millium Virginum, cum aliis multis sacris reliquiis Coloniae mihi datis. In die autem saneti Bartholomaei apostoli, ego appuli Ulissiponem.
units.en: After the feast of the Kings of this year I was recalled from my journey begun towards Portugal, and returned to Cologne, having sent on to Portugal Francisco de Estrada, Master Andrés de Oviedo, Don Juan de Aragón, and nine others whom at Louvain we had won for the Lord through Jesus Christ: these were Master Peter Faber of Hal, Master Hermes, Master Jean, Master Maximilian, Don Leonard, Master Jacques, Master Daniel, Thomas the little, and Cornelius. Returning to Cologne I took with me Master Lambert and Emiliano; and having rented a house at Cologne, I was there until the month of July, where I also preached in Latin, in the school of arts, on all Sundays and the other feasts, besides extraordinary sermons; leaving there at last Don Álvaro, and with him nine other scholars of our Society — may Jesus make them a good foundation here of his Society. Thence I received a new command, ordering me to set out for Portugal according to the king's will. I departed on the twelfth day of the month of July, and carried with me from there seven heads from the holy bodies of the eleven thousand Virgins, with many other sacred relics given me at Cologne. And on the day of Saint Bartholomew the apostle I landed at Lisbon.

units.la: In die trium Regum ańni 1545, haec sese mihi obtulerúnt ad praedicandum: Jesus Christus ideo inter caetera voluit latere in carne, ut homines seipsos, quales et quanti erga ipsum essent, ostendere discerent. Voluit quoque, hae de causa, abscondere sub carne omnes thesauros sapientiae et scientiae divinae, ut nobis occasionem daret expendendi thesauros quos ab ipsius majestate accepimus. Fecit itaque ut tres Magi, et reliqui omnes sérvi ejus, thesauros aperirent videntes paupertatem Domini sui. In summa, dum abscondit suam potentiam, ipse facit ut angeli descendant ad terras eamdem declaraturi; dum abscondit suam puritatem, volens baptizari a Joanne, ipse Patrem movet ut aperiat eam dicendo: Hic est Filius meus dilectus; dum item non vult manifestare charitatem suam in nuptiis, ipse aperit thesauros Matris suae dicentis: Vinum non habent; que proinde. cogit ipsum ante horam gloriam suam manifestare. Habes hic tres apparitiones quas hodie celebrat Ec- clesia.
units.en: On the day of the three Kings of the year 1545 these things offered themselves to me for preaching: Jesus Christ willed, among other reasons, to lie hidden in the flesh, that men might learn to show what and how great they were towards him. He willed also, for this cause, to hide under the flesh all the treasures of divine wisdom and knowledge, that he might give us occasion of spending the treasures which we have received from his majesty. So he brought it about that the three Magi, and all his other servants, opened their treasures on seeing the poverty of their Lord. In sum, while he hides his power, he makes the angels come down to earth to declare it; while he hides his purity, willing to be baptized by John, he moves the Father to reveal it, saying: This is my beloved Son; and again, when he will not manifest his charity at the wedding, he opens the treasures of his Mother, who says: They have no wine — and she thereby constrains him to manifest his glory before the hour. You have here the three apparitions which the Church celebrates today.

units.la: Magi obtulerunt Christo parvulo aurum, quasi qui potestatem ejus sublevare ab inopia velint, confitentes quod ab ipso habeant omne posse. Offerunt incensum in odorem suavitatis, quasi spiritum ejus confortare velint et animum, credentes nihilominus ac testantes non posse ab alio impetrari bona desideria aut bonum intellectum. Offerunt postremo myrrham, cum desi- - derio ut sanctum illud Parvuli corpus corruptionem non videat, per cujus Passionem gloria corporum atque incorruptio est acquirenda. Transeuntes magi per Hierosolymam magno discrimini sese et Christum exponere videbantur, quod stellae, non est attribuendum, quia ipsis in hoc ducatum non praebuit. Et licet ad maximum bonum haec Hierosolymorum visitatio cis et toti mundo cooperata fūerit, per aliam tamen viam -reversi in regionem suam dicuntur.
units.en: The Magi offered gold to the little child Christ, as though they would relieve his power from want, confessing that from him they have all their power. They offer incense for an odour of sweetness, as though they would strengthen his spirit and mind, believing nevertheless and bearing witness that good desires and good understanding can be obtained from no other. They offer lastly myrrh, with the desire that that holy body of the Little One might not see corruption — through whose Passion the glory and incorruption of bodies is to be acquired. The Magi, passing through Jerusalem, seemed to expose themselves and Christ to great danger; which is not to be attributed to the star, for it gave them no guidance in this. And although this visit to Jerusalem worked together for the greatest good, for them and for the whole world, yet they are said to have returned into their own country by another way.

units.la: Hic sensi quamdam in anima mea difficultatem et duritiam, qua prohibebar a gaudio et devotione tam sanctae et sublimis solemnitatis; super qua re tale habui responsum in meipso: Dies est trium Regum et adorationis veri Regis. Patere igitur hanc difficultatem et hoe gravamen, sciens quod sic melius videas num sis rex tui necne. Parum enim est regere seipsum ac vincere, cum juxta Christum per devotionem positi simus; vera autem victoria et verum regimen ac potens magis cognoscitur, cum abesse videtur Rex noster, qui bella nostra pro nobis gerere solet, donec reges nos ipsos effecerit. Dum dicitur: Omnes de Saba venient et omnes reges adorabunt eum, omnesque gentes servient ei; ex abundantia bonae spei prophetarum et Spiritus qui in ipsis loquebatur accipiendum est; qui vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et omnibus Mediatorem sufficientem atque media dedit. Potest quoque intelligi ex.eo quod si tam magni Reges sese Christo subjecerint, justum fuerit idem sperare de caeteris aequalibus, aut etiam majoribus, et multo magis de minoribus. Pridie dominicae infra octavas Epiphaniae, dum audirem confessiones, ego consideravi quemadmodum confessor non solum debeat habere curam animae ejus qui se ei submittit erudiendam, corripiendam, corrigendam et perficiendam, sed etiam curare ut provisio aliqua et favor per paenitentes perveniat, verbi gratia, ad defunctos, ad peccatores, et ad caeteros quicumque in corporali sive in spirituali necessitate esse possunt.
