Talibus namque facile per orationes, et memorias pietatis, ac eleemosynas paenitentium, succurri potest. Sit igitur confessarius procurator quidam, bonus ac fidelis dispensator, aestimans plurimum quod sibi subjiciuntur tam multae tamque divites paenitentium voluntates, et quasi thesåuri adl plurima sufficientes.
units.en: Here I felt in my soul a certain difficulty and hardness, by which I was kept from the joy and devotion of so holy and sublime a solemnity; upon which I had this answer within myself: It is the day of the three Kings, and of the adoration of the true King. Bear then this difficulty and this burden, knowing that thus you may better see whether you are king of yourself or not. For it is a small thing to rule oneself and conquer, when we are set close to Christ through devotion; but the true victory, and true and mighty rule, is better known when our King seems absent — he who is wont to wage our wars for us, until he has made us kings. When it is said: All they from Saba shall come, and all kings shall adore him, all nations shall serve him — this is to be taken from the abundance of the good hope of the prophets, and of the Spirit who spoke in them; who wills all men to be saved, and has given to all a sufficient Mediator and the means. It can also be understood from this: that if such great Kings subjected themselves to Christ, it were just to hope the same of their equals, or even of the greater, and much more of the lesser. On the eve of the Sunday within the octave of the Epiphany, while I heard confessions, I considered how the confessor ought not only to have the care of the soul of him who submits himself to him to be instructed, reproved, corrected and perfected, but also to see to it that some provision and favour reach, through the penitents, for example, the departed, sinners, and all others who may be in bodily or spiritual need. For such can easily be succoured through the prayers, the memorials of piety, and the alms of penitents. Let the confessor then be a kind of procurator, a good and faithful steward, valuing highly that there are subjected to him so many and so rich wills of penitents — treasuries, as it were, sufficient for very many things.

units.la: Dominica infra octavas Epiphaniae, Ghristi dis vina praesentia prodiit ad parentes ejus secundum carnem: ipsum requirunt anxii animo inter cognatos et notos, ubi. non invenitur" ab eis, et deinde in Hierusalem, ubi remanserat; et ipsi tertio loco ipsum inveniunt in templo, sedentem in medio Doctorum, audientem et interrogantem illos; quarto vero ipsùm inventum ad se suamque obedientiam reducunt. Christus quoque hunc ordinem servat in his quae docet nos anno duodecimo; primo videlicet quod vult se a parentibus carnis suae absentare, pro adimplenda Patris caeoelestis voluntate; secundo, quod vult requiri a parentibus suis; tertio, inveniri 1n templo. in medio Doctorum; quarto, rehaberi ad subjectionem; quinto, condescendere illis quamlibet parvis; sexto, habitare in. Nazareth, qui flos interpretatur; et septimo, subditus illis.
units.en: On the Sunday within the octave of the Epiphany, the divine presence of Christ went out from his parents according to the flesh: they seek him anxiously among their kinsfolk and acquaintance, where he is not found by them; then in Jerusalem, where he had remained; and in the third place they find him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the Doctors, hearing them and asking them questions; and fourthly, having found him, they bring him back to themselves and to obedience to them. Christ also keeps this order in the things he teaches us in his twelfth year: first, that he wills to absent himself from the parents of his flesh, to fulfil the will of the heavenly Father; second, that he wills to be sought by his parents; third, to be found in the temple in the midst of the Doctors; fourth, to be taken back into subjection; fifth, to condescend to them, little though they be; sixth, to dwell in Nazareth, which is interpreted 'flower'; and seventh, to be subject to them.

units.la: Ľarentes revertuntur secundum consuetudinem et statum, absolutis consummatisque diebus ipsius solemnitatis. Christus autem aliquando habet majora negotia in templo, quam quae possent juxta solitum absolvi. Ideo nobis opera danda est ut ne nimium resniciamus ad communem consuetudinem, in recedendo corporaliter a divinis: nam si nobis satisfactum est in divinis officiis, Deo forte satisfactum non est; unde non est recedendum, nisi prius examinaverimus utrum Christus paratus sit nobiscum. descendere vel non; et siquidem ipse diutius optet ibi nostrum obsequium, -remaneamus propter Patrem ejus et propter ipsum remanere adhuc cupientes. Equidem malım derelinqui a cognatis et notis nostris, quam Christum derelinquere.
units.en: The parents return according to custom and their state, when the days of the solemnity are finished and complete. But Christ sometimes has greater business in the temple than can be finished in the usual way. Therefore we must take care not to look too much to common custom in withdrawing bodily from divine things: for though we may have had our fill of the divine offices, God perhaps has not had his; so we must not withdraw until we have first examined whether Christ is ready to come down with us or not; and if he desires our attendance there longer, let us remain — for his Father's sake, and for the sake of him who still desires to remain. Truly, I would rather be left behind by our kinsfolk and acquaintance than leave Christ.

units.la: Quicumque docti sunt vel prudentes habeant Puerum duodecim annorumsedentem in medio doctorum, audientem et interrogantem illos; habeant ipsum, inquam, in omnibus prae oculis, ut etilli velint non sapere plusquam oportet sapere.
units.en: Let all who are learned or prudent keep the Boy of twelve years sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them and asking them questions; let them keep him, I say, before their eyes in all things, that they too may will not to be wise beyond what it behoves them to be wise.

units.la: Habeant et ipsum in tali humilitatis forma Haeretici, ut audiant et interrogent doctores Ecclesiae, in ipsorum medio sedentes ac quiete permanentes.
units.en: Let the Heretics too keep him in such a form of humility, that they may hear and question the doctors of the Church, sitting in their midst and quietly remaining there.

units.la: Christus Dominus in utero Virginis, quasi in radice arboris, habitavit novem mensibus. A nativitate autem usque ad duodecimum annum, ' quasi habitavit in trunco arboris. A duodecimo rursus usque ad trigesimum habitavit in flore; flos ipse factus. Pie credendum est quod postea habitaverit in fructu naturali, in fructu salutis nostrae.
units.en: Christ the Lord dwelt in the womb of the Virgin, as in the root of the tree, for nine months. From his birth to his twelfth year he dwelt, as it were, in the trunk of the tree. From the twelfth again to the thirtieth he dwelt in the flower — himself made the flower. And it is piously to be believed that afterwards he dwelt in the natural fruit, in the fruit of our salvation.

units.la: Si tecum duxeris Puerum Jesum in templum et in locum visionis pacis, si insuper diligenter requisieris ipse ubi te dereliquerit, aut ubi te nescio remanserit; haec, inquam, si feceris, facile fiet ut ipse descendat tecum ad te, et ut habitet in floribus spiritualis pueritiae. Spiritus tuus tandem totus tibi ad votum subjectus erit, paratus facere voluntatem tuam, quam aliquando fecisti tibi servire in tuis iniquitatibus.
units.en: If you take the Boy Jesus with you into the temple, and into the place of the vision of peace; if moreover you diligently seek where he has left you, or where, without your knowing, he has stayed behind — if you do this, I say, it will easily come about that he descends with you to you, and dwells in the flowers of spiritual childhood. Your spirit at last will be wholly subject to you at your wish, ready to do your will — that spirit which once you made serve you in your iniquities.

units.la: In octava Epiphaniae, cum accepissem pro themate sermonis: Vidit Joannes Jesum venien- tem adse; essemque proxime sacrificaturus, tactus sum magno desiderio, ut ego in missa possem videre ac sentire in corde meo Jesum ad me venturum. In sacramento agnoscebam plane ipsum ad me venisse, nimium saepe, absque hoc quod ipsum vidissem venire. Rogavi igitur Deum, Virginem et Sanctos aliquot, ut mihi et omnibus fratribus meis, omnibusque communicaturis, liceret videre ipsum venientem, proindeque revereri decenter, praepararique ipsi cum digna aliqua exspectatione. Dum etiam induerer ornamentis sacris, consideravi et hortatus sum meipsum ad compositionem illam quam debet habere qui videt Jesum ad se venientem.
units.en: On the octave of the Epiphany, having taken for the theme of my sermon: John saw Jesus coming to him, and being about to offer the sacrifice, I was touched with a great desire that at Mass I might see and feel in my heart Jesus coming to me. In the sacrament I plainly recognized that he had come to me — too often — without my having seen him come. I begged therefore God, the Virgin, and certain Saints, that it might be granted to me and to all my brethren, and to all who were to communicate, to see him coming, and accordingly to reverence him fittingly, and to prepare ourselves for him with some worthy expectation. While I put on the sacred vestments also, I considered, and exhorted myself to, that composure which he ought to have who sees Jesus coming to him.

units.la: Joannes vero animadvertit, apertisque oculis vidit Jesum ad se venientem. Sic Petrus ipsum alicubi vidit dum diceret: Exi-a me, quia peccator sum. Elisabeth quoqne similes aliqua ex parte oculos habuit, cum diceret: Et unde hoc mihi ut veniat mater Domini mei ad me? Maria autem Mater Dei tunc maxime vidit Jesum ad se venientem cum dixit: Ecce ancilla Domini.
units.en: John indeed took note, and with opened eyes saw Jesus coming to him. So Peter somewhere saw him, when he said: Depart from me, for I am a sinner. Elizabeth too had in some measure like eyes, when she said: And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? But Mary, the Mother of God, then above all saw Jesus coming to her when she said: Behold the handmaid of the Lord.

units.la: Jesum Mater detinuit in longa obedientia sub- ditum usque ad annum trigesimum. Et idem aliquo modo possunt quicumque eumdem cum multa sollicitudine et, timore observant; sicut sponsa tenet subjectum sponsum propter nimium amorern, qúo fit ut non possit pati ipsum diutius abesse a suo conspectu.
units.en: His Mother kept Jesus subject in long obedience until his thirtieth year. And the same, in some manner, can be done by all who watch him with much solicitude and fear; as a bride holds her bridegroom subject through excess of love, whereby she cannot bear him to be longer out of her sight.

units.la: Jesus a subjectione parentum recedens ad baptismum Joannis, docet oportere ut qui relinquunt unum genus officii, ipsi debeant non quaerere libertatem carnis, sicut solent mutantes strictiorem obedientiam in laxiorem; sed potius ad duriora conscendere. Christus enim sic relinquit parentum servitutem, ut ad Joannis servi sui transeat velut disciplinam. Non quaerit dominos suis parentibus honoratiores, nec absolutionem ab omni servitute; qui omnium optat fieri servus. In lucem enim prodit, ut sese omnibus qui salvari volunt offerat. Igitur quilibet mortalium excipiat eum ad se venientem. Exeat obviam ei, etrecipiat gratiam Agni Dei immaculati, dati in pretium et gratiam ejus, qui fert et aufert peccata mundi. Incipiat quoque jam oculos aperire, ut videat Jesum venientem ad se, non ut prius ad justificandum, sed ad judicandum; post nos venit nunc in multa patientia, qui, antequam essemus, quaerọns fuerat et erat ad ostium. Jamdiu stat et pulsat ignoratus a nobis Salvator. Exeamus ergo nos obviam el, ne dormientes inveniat, quia nimium diu nescivimus ipsum. Hic magno desiderio fui affectus circa illud ut, cum administratur laicis sacramentum Eucharistiae, in principio ostensionis ejus, quum scilicet sacerdos tenens hostiam se ad communicantes eonvertit, dicerentur intelligibiliter omnia verba haec: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccata mundi.
units.en: Jesus, withdrawing from subjection to his parents to the baptism of John, teaches that they who leave one kind of duty ought not to seek the liberty of the flesh, as they commonly do who exchange a stricter obedience for a laxer; but rather to climb to harder things. For Christ so leaves the service of his parents as to pass to the discipline, as it were, of John his own servant. He does not seek masters more honoured than his parents, nor release from all service — he who desires to become the servant of all. For he comes forth into the light to offer himself to all who wish to be saved. Let every mortal, then, receive him as he comes to him. Let him go out to meet him, and receive the grace of the immaculate Lamb of God, given as his price and his grace, who bears and takes away the sins of the world. Let him also now begin to open his eyes, to see Jesus coming to him — not, as before, to justify, but to judge; he now comes after us in much patience, who, before we were, had been seeking us and stood at the door. Long has the Saviour stood knocking, unrecognized by us. Let us therefore go out to meet him, lest he find us sleeping, for too long we have not known him. Here I was moved by a great desire that, when the sacrament of the Eucharist is administered to the laity, at the beginning of its showing — when, that is, the priest holding the host turns to the communicants — all these words might be said intelligibly: Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away the sins of the world.

units.la: Postridie octavae Epiphaniae, dum adhuc occurrissent quaedam circa Jesum judicem ad nos appropinquantem, venerunt in mentem illa judicii universalis praeambula, bella scilicet et seditiones, terrae motus, pestilentiae et fames, quae in variis locis quotidie experiuntur et contingunt; item et illa magis universalia quae mundo ventura sunt, pressura scilicet gentium in terris prae confusione sonitus maris et fluctuum ejus, obscuratio item solis et lunae, virtutumque coelorum commotiones, cum caeteris de coelo terroribus et apparitionibus signi terribilis:Filii hominis; quae et ipsa contingent, ita ut homines arescant prae ih a s n = Dann timore et expectatione. Horum vero signorum omnium cum considerarem violentias et tremendos effectus, non potui quin cum lacrymis optarem, et mihi et caeteris omnibus, tum christianis tum reliquis orbis habitatoribus, praesentibus et futuris, quin peroptarem, inquam, omnibus mentem vigilantem et trementem Dem judicem. Furor belli - cum invalescit in aliquam civitatem, magnopere concutit corda; et durissima fames quoque, cum grassatur usque ad alicujus totius magni populi desolationem, magnas ìn animabus quoque illorum facit commotiones; sic et terrae motus animos terrore commovere solent et pestilentiae. Longe autem amplius et fortius concuterent mortales illa quae sunt magis universalia, ut pressura illa gentium, et sonitus fluctuum maris totaliter confusi, et terrores coeaelestes, si sentirentur; quia, inquam, haec omnia terribilia sunt illis omnibus quorum corda sunt aperta nimis curis hujus vitae, aut ebrietate vel crapula gravata. Hinc fit ut valde vigilantes ac sollicitos oporteat esse homines circa ipsum ultimum diem Christi Domini Nostri, quem tam multae tribulationes praecurrunt, et sunt praepa- ratoriae ipsius. Hic venerunt in mentem verha illa quae sunt apud sanctum Lucam: Vigilate itaque, omni tempore orantes, ut digni habeamini fugere ista omnia quae futura sunt, et stare ante Filium hominis. Ad hoc visa est bona haec oratio sequens, quam optarem ab omnibus Christianis privatim et publice quotidie fieri.
units.en: On the day after the octave of the Epiphany, while certain thoughts still came to me about Jesus the judge drawing near to us, there came to mind those forerunners of the universal judgment: wars, namely, and seditions, earthquakes, pestilences and famines, which are daily experienced and come to pass in various places; likewise those more universal things which are to come upon the world — the distress, namely, of nations on the earth, by reason of the confusion of the roaring of the sea and of its waves; the darkening also of sun and moon, and the shakings of the powers of the heavens, with the other terrors from heaven, and the appearing of the terrible sign of the Son of man; which things also will come to pass, so that men wither away for fear and expectation. And when I considered the violences and tremendous effects of all these signs, I could not but wish with tears — for myself and for all others, both christians and the other inhabitants of the world, present and to come — I could not, I say, but wish for all a mind watchful and trembling before God the judge. When the fury of war grows strong against some city, it mightily shakes hearts; and the hardest famine too, when it rages even to the desolation of some whole great people, works great commotions in their souls as well; so also earthquakes and pestilences are wont to move minds with terror. But far more, and more strongly, would those more universal things shake mortals — that distress of the nations, and the roaring of the waves of the sea in total confusion, and the heavenly terrors — if they were felt; because, I say, all these things are terrible to all those whose hearts are too much open to the cares of this life, or weighed down with drunkenness and surfeiting. Hence it is that men must be very watchful and solicitous concerning that last day of Christ Our Lord, which so many tribulations run before and prepare. Here came to mind those words which are in Saint Luke: Watch ye therefore, praying at all times, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the Son of man. To this end the following prayer seemed good, which I could wish were made daily by all Christians, privately and publicly.

units.la: Domine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi, qui nos in omni tempore ad hoc vigilare et orare praecepisti, ut omnia mala tui tremendi judicii praeambula fugere possimus, et ante Filium hominis digne stare; exaudi nos, quaesumus, hoc ipsum cum timore et fiducialiter supplicantes, ut ne quemcumque nostrum dies illa opprimat imparatum; qui vivis et regnas cum eodem Patre, in unitate Spiritus Sancti, Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
units.en: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who hast commanded us to watch and pray at all times for this end, that we may be able to escape all the evils that run before thy tremendous judgment, and to stand worthily before the Son of man: hear us, we beseech thee, as with fear and yet with confidence we make this supplication, that that day may not overtake any one of us unprepared; who livest and reignest with the same Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end. Amen.

units.la: Quadam die cum missam dicerem pro fratribus meis et filiis spiritualibus, venit mihi 1n mentem hoc verbum Apostoli: Patres debent thesaurisare filiis; ubi sensi magnum desiderium ut possim aliquid spiritualis thesauri aliis reponere, quod olim in eorum consolationem: sit cessurum; et hoc ad imitationem Ejus qui factüs est reċeptaculum omnium thesauror um sapienti J aa a a et scientie Dei. Bonam spem concepi, considerando quod sancti Patres (siquidem nos veri filii eorum fuerimus) multos thesauros nobis accumularunt, non solum in colis, in donis gloriosis, sed etiam in terris, in donis gratiae. In hoc debent consolari quicumque sub disciplina aliquorum Patrum, viventes recte obedientétque ministerium quodcumque exercent. In quo quidem ministerio, etsi non habent occasionem omnimodam per se in spiritualibus sibi thesaurisandi, sciant tamen ipsi magnum repositum thesaurum apud illos Patres, quorum vices gerunt ipsi eorum superiores, sed et apud eosdem superiores, cum boni fuerint. Ipsi vero superiores, cuicumque — familie praesideant, ad hoc maxime attendere debent, ut filiis suis illis omnibus quos Christus eis subjecit thesaurisent, ante omnia ipsi facti thesauri spirituales. Generaliter etiam oportet ut qui metunt. temporalia, quae sibi aliquo modo per aliquos fuerunt accumulata ac reposita, seminent eisdem spiritualia atque reponant. Frustrarentur etenim qui personis spiritualibus thesaurisant temporalia; si nullum tandem aliquando thesaurum spiritualem per ipsos asservatum et aggregatum invenirent. Et idem dixerim de Isomnibus qui Christo serviunt in officiis minoribus ac vilioribus, in ordine ad eos qui serviunt in majoribus atque dignioribus. Sic enim oportet ut comparticipes laborum et dolorum, sint et quietis et consolationis. Ad hoc facit id quod omnibus sanctis dicturus est Christus: Intra in gaudium Domini tui; tu videlicet, qui intrasti in labores et consolationes ejusdem.
units.en: On a certain day, when I said Mass for my brethren and spiritual sons, there came to my mind this word of the Apostle: The parents ought to lay up treasure for the children; where I felt a great desire that I might lay up some spiritual treasure for others, which might one day fall to their consolation; and this in imitation of Him who was made the storehouse of all the treasures of the wisdom and knowledge of God. I conceived good hope, considering that the holy Fathers (if indeed we be their true sons) have heaped up many treasures for us, not only in heaven, in glorious gifts, but also on earth, in gifts of grace. In this all ought to take comfort who, living rightly and obediently under the discipline of any Fathers, exercise any ministry whatever. In which ministry, even if they have not full occasion of themselves to lay up spiritual treasure for themselves, let them know nevertheless that a great treasure is laid up with those Fathers whose place their superiors hold — and with those same superiors, when they are good. And the superiors themselves, over whatever family they preside, ought to attend to this above all: to lay up treasure for their sons — for all those whom Christ has subjected to them — being themselves first made spiritual treasures. Generally, too, those who reap temporal things, which have in some manner been gathered and laid up for them by others, ought to sow and lay up spiritual things for the same. For they would be defrauded who lay up temporal treasures for spiritual persons, if in the end they should find no spiritual treasure preserved and gathered by them. And the same I would say of all who serve Christ in lesser and meaner offices, in relation to those who serve in greater and worthier ones. For so it is fitting that the sharers of labours and griefs be sharers also of rest and consolation. To this belongs what Christ will say to all the saints: Enter into the joy of thy Lord — you, namely, who have entered into his labours and consolations.

units.la: In die sanctorum quinque martyrum ordinis Minorum, videlicet Berardi, Petri, Accursii, Adjuti et Othonis, cum interessem divinis officiis in ecclesia Sanctae Crucis Conimbricensis, ubi jacent corpora eorumdem, hic, inquam, ego magno sensu compassionis affectus fui erga omnes generaliter qui sunf in periculis evidentissitmis suae damnationis.
units.en: On the day of the five holy martyrs of the order of Friars Minor — namely Berard, Peter, Accursius, Adjutus and Otto — while I was present at the divine offices in the church of Santa Cruz of Coimbra, where their bodies lie, I was moved by a great sense of compassion towards all in general who stand in the most evident dangers of their damnation.

units.la: Veniebat in mentem Lutherus, rex Angliae et Turca, cum aliis aliquot. Considerabam autem pietatem illam Dei, qua fit ut tamdiu expectati sint. Intellexi autem id, quod in meum judicium et mei similium facile accipi posset: fieri etenim potest ut Deus non solum det talibus tempus paenitentiae, exspectans eorum conver- i EPILOGUS 34l sionem, quam per se possent, Christo ipso dante, adhuc operari, sed etiam ut expectet utrum ali-, quis velit amplius orare pro talibus, aut dare operam circa eorum conversionem. Ipse facile dat tempus paenitentiae; hinc solummodo ut etiam videat num aliquis ex nobis christianis alicui tandem, antequam ipse moriatur, velit. succurrere. Nobis igitur, quibus data est 'Praedicandi ac docendi potestas, valde videndum est ne multi pereant ob culpam nostram, et propter negligentiam nostram. Timendum ne Deus multos nobis conservet instruendos, ac de salute sua admonendos. Multi ubique nos exspectant; festinemus igitur crescere cunctis et eisdem bene praeparari.
units.en: There came to mind Luther, the king of England, and the Turk, with certain others. And I considered that mercy of God by which it comes about that they have been waited for so long. And I understood something which might easily be taken as a judgment upon me and upon such as I am: for it may be that God not only gives such men time for penance, awaiting their conversion, which they could still, Christ himself granting it, work out; but also that he waits to see whether anyone will pray more for such men, or take pains for their conversion. He readily gives time for penance — if only to see whether any one of us christians will at last be willing to come to the help of one of them before he dies. We, then, to whom the power of preaching and teaching has been given, must look well to it that many do not perish through our fault and our negligence. It is to be feared that God is keeping many for us to instruct and to admonish about their salvation. Many everywhere are waiting for us: let us hasten then to grow for them all, and to prepare ourselves well for them.

units.la: Sanguis multorum martyrum nos invitat ad eas gentes curandas, apud quas et pro quarum salute ipsi mortui sunt. Utinam igitur aliquando tandem aliqui ex nostra Societate occasionem et animum habeant visitandi Marochianos illos, quibus isti quinque martyres sese seminarunt in salutem. Ipsi erant verba viva ipsius Dei et Christi, et ideo non potuerunt invenire terram quae caperet verba Evangelii. Ipsimet tanquam grana optima mori voluerunt; ut inde, si non- dum collectus est fructus, aliquando tamen colligi per aliquos veros Christi operarios possit.
units.en: The blood of many martyrs invites us to care for those nations among whom, and for whose salvation, they died. Would then that some of our Society may at last have occasion and heart to visit those men of Morocco, among whom these five martyrs sowed themselves unto salvation. They were living words of God himself and of Christ, and therefore could not find ground to receive the words of the Gospel; they themselves, like the best of grains, willed to die, so that thence — if the fruit has not yet been gathered — it may yet one day be gathered by some true labourers of Christ.

units.la: In die sanctorum matyrum Fabiani et Sebastiani, quo tempore Conimbricae aderat maxima inundatio aquarum, multis modis nociva, non so- lum terrae frugibus nascentibus, sed etiam et domi- bus et rebus domesticis; hoc die, inquam, celebravi missam pro quodam monacho defuncto, quem mihi Martinus Sanctae Crucis commendarat ut virum sanctum. Sicque mihi data est magħa devotio circa liberationem animarum defuncto- rum; item quidam novus sensus ac intelligentia spiritualis circa eos qui pro minimis inibi detinerentur, quique quasi ex toto sunt felices. Imaginabar etenim animas successive et per incrementa beatam vitam intrare, fierique participes felicitatis; quod intelligendum est:de accidentali beatitudine. Essentialis enim est tota -simul et perfecta possessio vitae interminabilis, statusque bonorum omnium aggregatione perfectus. Hic etiam ego recepi magnam spem circa - temporis serenitatem, aliquot jam diebus anxie aiii te EPILOGUS i 343 desideratam et petitam. Hic sensus fuit dum rogassem Dominum ut dignaretur parcere pauperibus, quorum domus, vel alia quaecumque bona, per talem inundationem perdebantur. Petebam autem ut parceret eis, quasi omnia illa bona pertinerent ad personas tam pias et devotas quam fuerat sanctus ille monachus pro cujus anima. celebrabam, aut quomodo si omnia pertinerent ad sanctos qui sunt in caelis.
units.en: On the day of the holy martyrs Fabian and Sebastian — at which time there was at Coimbra a very great flood of waters, harmful in many ways, not only to the springing fruits of the earth but also to houses and household goods — on this day, I say, I celebrated Mass for a certain departed monk, whom Martin of Santa Cruz had commended to me as a holy man. And so great devotion was given me concerning the deliverance of the souls of the departed; likewise a certain new feeling and spiritual understanding concerning those who are detained there for the least things, and who are as it were almost wholly happy. For I imagined the souls entering the blessed life successively and by increases, and becoming partakers of happiness — which is to be understood of accidental blessedness; for the essential is the whole, simultaneous and perfect possession of interminable life, a state perfect by the aggregation of all goods. Here also I received great hope concerning fair weather, which for some days now I had anxiously desired and asked. This feeling came while I begged the Lord to deign to spare the poor, whose houses, or whatever other goods, were being lost through the flood. And I asked him to spare them, as though all those goods belonged to persons as pious and devout as that holy monk had been for whose soul I was celebrating, or as if they all belonged to the saints who are in heaven.

units.la: Hic venerunt in mentem quaedam desideria quorumdam Sanctorum, ubi ego sensi nobis magnam operam dandam esse, ut non solum Dei voluntates per nos impleantur, sed illae etiam quas constat fuisse a Deo in sanctis ejus. Sed et illud magnopere cupivi, videlicet ut nos ipsi, qui vivimus, demus operam alter alterius sanctis desideriis adimplendis circa Dei honorem; puta circa animarum salutem et circa nostrum Iīpsorum spiritualem profectum.
units.en: Here came to mind certain desires of certain Saints, whereupon I felt that we must take great pains that not only the wills of God be fulfilled through us, but those also which are known to have been from God in his saints. And this too I greatly desired: namely, that we ourselves who live should labour to fulfil one another's holy desires concerning the honour of God — for instance, concerning the salvation of souls and our own spiritual progress.

units.la: Hinc factum est ut mihi datus sit pius quidam ausus petendi ex Deo ut adimpleantur quaedam mea desideria, quae ipsius sunt, circa restitutionem Germaniae, et circa reductionem gentium aliarum ʻad fidem, et vitam puram et perfectam Christianae disciplinae. Det ipse fieri quod dat nobis pie desiderare, et perficiat. ea omnia opera quae per suas creaturas ipse concipit.
units.en: Hence it came that a certain pious boldness was given me of asking from God that certain desires of mine, which are his, may be fulfilled: concerning the restoration of Germany, and concerning the bringing back of the other nations to the faith, and to the pure and perfect life of Christian discipline. May he grant to be done what he gives us piously to desire, and bring to completion all those works which he conceives through his creatures.

units.la: In die gloriosae virginis et martyris Agnetis, ego ad hoc celebraviʻūt Deus dignaretur quodam privilegio singulari donare nostram Societatem. Privilegium est quod peccata quae commiserunt qui ingressi hanc congregationem aut ingressuri sunt, non imputata fuerint ipsi Societati. Loquor primum de peccatis commissis ante ipsum ingressum, deinde etiam de caeteris omnibus. Hoc ideo petivi, quia senseram quemdam pium timorem, ne propter peccata singulorum eorum qui sumus, vel qui futuri sunt, minus prosperatura sit ipsa Societas; maxime quod multi intrant qui Deum multis modis graviter offenderunt. Noli ergo, Domine, sanctae communitati imputare, ut cedant nobis non prospere, quaecumque honori tuo, et animarum nostrarum vel alienarum saluti, contraria unquam attentaverimus. In his autem quae bona fuerint. et aedificativa, o Deus, ne quaeso memineris nostrarum iniquitatum multarum. Quod si tibi visum fuerit ut paenas luamus vituperio- rum, tribulationum corporalium, aut paupertatis, saltem ne permittas nos puniri his flagellis quae solent esse quando peccata et errores in paenas peccatorum conceduntur miseris. peccatoribus. Absint, absint, Domine Deus, hae paenae peccati ab hac tua tenella familia! Haec occasionaliter mihi occurrerunt, eo quod decrevissem pro quibusdam ex nostris specialiter orare, quorum generales confessiones (qui multi sunt) audiveram. In festo Purificationis, ego sensi magnum et vivum desiderium non moriendi antequam in anima mea, quae Dei sunt recte compositeque se habeant. Optavi prius videre pacem mentis meae quam absolutionem ejus a corpore; et prius gustare vitam quae est Salvator quam mortem; et prius cognoscere verum Lumen quam intrare tenebras mortis, et gloriam Ecclesiae Christi, ac Societatis nostrae, priusquam moriar. Optavi etiam mihi dari graliam, qua fieret ut nullum diem praeterire sinerem absque utili fructu. Deus enim vitam dat ad salutem operandam, et omnem diem. computat in aliquod bonum opus. Excita, o Deus, igitur desideria in me, non solum quae oporteat adimpleri in fine vitae; sed illa etiam quae tu vis quotidie perfici. O quam felix esset qui noscere posset quid in singulos dies ab ipso requirat Dominus! l In festo sancti Blasii, caput unum ex sacris Virginibus, quod ego donavi magistro Simoni pro Collegio Conimbricensi, deportatum est. Conimbricam. Faxit Jesus ut inibi usque ad resurrectionem ejus et aliorum omnium humanorum corporum veneretur et devote reservetur.
units.en: On the day of the glorious virgin and martyr Agnes, I celebrated to this end: that God would deign to endow our Society with a certain singular privilege. The privilege is that the sins committed by those who have entered this congregation, or shall enter it, be not imputed to the Society itself. I speak first of the sins committed before entry, and then also of all the rest. This I asked because I had felt a certain pious fear lest, on account of the sins of the individuals who we are, or who are to come, the Society itself should prosper less; above all because many enter who have gravely offended God in many ways. Do not then, O Lord, impute to the holy community — so that things should go ill with us — whatever we may ever have attempted contrary to your honour and to the salvation of our own souls or of others'. And in those things which are good and edifying, O God, remember not, I beseech you, our many iniquities. And if it seem good to you that we pay the penalties of revilings, of bodily tribulations, or of poverty, at least do not allow us to be punished with those scourges which are wont to come when sins and errors are granted, as punishments of sins, to wretched sinners. Far, far be these penalties of sin, Lord God, from this your tender family! These things came to me by occasion, because I had resolved to pray specially for certain of ours whose general confessions (and they are many) I had heard. On the feast of the Purification I felt a great and lively desire not to die before the things of God stand rightly and well-ordered in my soul. I wished to see the peace of my mind before its release from the body; and to taste the life which is the Saviour, before death; and to know the true Light before entering the darkness of death; and the glory of the Church of Christ, and of our Society, before I die. I wished also that the grace be given me of letting no day pass without useful fruit. For God gives life for the working of salvation, and counts every day towards some good work. Stir up then in me, O God, desires — not only those which must be fulfilled at the end of life, but those also which you will to have accomplished daily. O how happy were he who could know what the Lord requires of him for each single day! On the feast of Saint Blaise, one of the heads of the holy Virgins, which I had given to Master Simón for the College of Coimbra, was carried to Coimbra. May Jesus grant that it be venerated and devoutly kept there until the resurrection of her and of all other human bodies.

units.la: Feria sexta post diem Cinerum, ego sensi magnum desiderium ut ne Societas nostra aliquid perderet ex eo quod officium nos Romanum dicamus. Timebam enim id quod fieri solet, scilicet ne Nostri, eo quod nec multa nec longa officia vocalia cogantur dicere, non nihil propter hoc amittant, Ad hoc igitur missam celebravi, videlicet cum desiderio ut, quod minus fecerimus nos vocalibus officiis, sive pro vivis, sive pro defunctis, id totum per officia operandi et meditandi ex corde suppleatur; et hoc facile erit apud diligentes Deum et proximum, qui per praedicationes, per confessiones, et pér particulares exhortationes, simul cum mentalibus exercitationibus orationum, possunt juvare et vivos et defunctos, ipsorumnecessitates multis fidelibus repraesen- ta EPILOGUS 347 tando, et eorum memoriam in seipsis continue vivificando. Hoc si omiserimus, consultius erit ut plus officiorum vocalium nobis imponatur, et ne tantum temporis reliquis piis operibus et orationibus liberum relinquatur. Nemo igitur tempore abutatur. Invenimus vivos, in omni genere necessitatis, spiritualis primum, deinde et corporalis. Invenimus et defunctos, eorutn necessitates ad vivum memoriis nostris imprimendo, et caeteros, sive paenitentes, sive auditores, sive nobiscum conversantes, ut idem faciant exhortando. Efficiamus etiam multos nobis in hac re vicarios, qui videlicet orent vocaliter, id quod nos non possumus.
units.en: On the Friday after Ash Wednesday I felt a great desire that our Society might lose nothing by the fact that we say the Roman office. For I feared what is wont to happen: namely, lest ours, because they are not bound to say many or long vocal offices, should on this account lose something. To this end therefore I celebrated Mass — with the desire, namely, that what we do less in vocal offices, whether for the living or for the departed, may be wholly supplied through the offices of working and of meditating from the heart; and this will be easy for those who love God and their neighbour, who through sermons, confessions and particular exhortations, together with the mental exercises of prayers, can help both the living and the dead: setting their necessities vividly before many of the faithful, and continually keeping their memory alive in themselves. If we omit this, it will be more advisable that more vocal offices be laid upon us, and that not so much time be left free for the other pious works and prayers. Let no one therefore misuse time. We find the living in every kind of need — spiritual first, and then bodily as well. We find the dead too, by impressing their necessities to the quick upon our memories, and by exhorting the others — penitents, hearers, or those who converse with us — to do the same. Let us also make many our vicars in this matter: who, namely, may pray vocally what we cannot.

units.la: Sabbato post diem Cinerum, cum statim a prandio me seorsum collegissem ad orandum, completa oratione, incidit in mentem afflictio cujusdam personae quae apud me cor suum aperuerat; dumque intrassem in discursum quemdam variarum adversitatum et afflictionum, quas propter temporalia magna pars hominum patitur, sensi in animo meo compunctionem quamdam cum lacrymis, cum viderem me absque ulla adversitate in hoc mundo vivere. Caeteri enim omnes qui in mundo sunt, ut mihi videbatur, varias molestias patiuntur; ego vero neminem sentio adversantem mihi. Verum est quidem eum valde liberum esse a tribulationibus carnalibus et temporalibus, qui visibilia non habeat nec aveat, sed sola aeterna; sed dolebam quod saltem pro invisibilibus non paterer plura. Sicul enim mundani homines, propter visibilia acquirenda, conservanda et augenda, multa patiuntur, et multos visibiles hostes inveniunt; ita oportet eos qui operam dant rebus spiritualibus, pro illis acquirendis, retinendis et multiplicandis, varia et gravia pati per hostes invisibiles.
units.en: On the Saturday after Ash Wednesday, when immediately after dinner I had withdrawn by myself to pray, the prayer being finished there came to my mind the affliction of a certain person who had opened her heart to me; and entering into a certain round of the various adversities and afflictions which the greater part of men suffer for the sake of temporal things, I felt in my soul a certain compunction with tears, when I saw myself living in this world without any adversity. For all others who are in the world, as it seemed to me, suffer various troubles; but I feel no one opposing me. True it is that he is very free from carnal and temporal tribulations who neither has nor covets visible things, but only eternal; but I grieved that at least for the invisible things I did not suffer more. For as worldly men, for the acquiring, keeping and increasing of visible things, suffer much and find many visible enemies, so it behoves those who give their labour to spiritual things to suffer, for the acquiring, keeping and multiplying of them, various and grave things through invisible enemies.

units.la: Eodem die, sub vesperam, exiens de palatio Regis, factum est ut inciderem in conspectum multitudinis. equorum et equitum, qui erant congregati ad recipiendum quemdam Ducem; ita ut propter hoc esset maximus quasi ad maximum et nobilissimum spectaculum concursus. Declinavi igitur a tanta turba et a tanto strepitu, in ecclesiam quae in propinquo erat; ubi dum nonnihil curiositatis ad exeundum et videndum ià quod declinaveram in me sentirem,- conjectis in ima- ginem crucifixi oculis, statim cessavit talis motus Drey aiye animae meae; ita ut gratias agerem Deo meo, qui aspectum suae imaginis concederet; et hoc sensi esse verum respicere spectaculum, memorari videlicet quomodo Deus ipse voluit carnem accipere, et eam coram-omni populo, inter duos latrones pendens, deponere.
units.en: On the same day, towards evening, going out of the King's palace, it happened that I came upon the sight of a multitude of horses and horsemen, gathered to receive a certain Duke; so that there was a very great concourse, as to a great and most noble spectacle. I turned aside, then, from so great a crowd and so great a noise, into a church which was near by; where, feeling in myself some curiosity to go out and see what I had turned away from, I cast my eyes upon the image of the crucified, and at once that motion of my soul ceased; so that I gave thanks to my God, who granted the sight of his image; and I felt this to be the true beholding of a spectacle: to remember, namely, how God himself willed to take flesh, and to lay it down before all the people, hanging between two thieves.

units.la: Huc igitur spectent quicumque ad videndum ea quae extra se sunt cupiunt; hic sanentur oculorum et aurium, et caeterorum sensuum, insatiabiles appetitus. Quod si nondum possis eo penetrare, ut in talibus requiescas, perge quaerere;. melior est hujus spectaculi nuda cupiditas et laboriosa curiositas, quam omnium temporalium et mundanorum visibilium spectaculorum ocularis aspectus atque fruitio. Etsi enim ei in monumentum sanctum intrare permissum non fuerit, non cessabit propterea foris stare plorans ad monumentum.
units.en: Hither, then, let all look who desire to see the things that are outside themselves; here let the insatiable appetites of eyes and ears and the other senses be healed. And if you cannot yet penetrate so far as to rest in such things, go on seeking; better is the bare longing for this spectacle, and its laborious seeking, than the ocular sight and enjoyment of all temporal and worldly visible spectacles. For though it be not permitted her to enter into the holy sepulchre, she will not for that cease to stand without, weeping at the sepulchre.

units.la: In die sancti Mathiae apostoli, ego obtuli regi Portugalliae et reginae duo ex capitibus undecim milium Virginum: regi scilicet caput quod habueram ex conventu carthusiensium Coloniae; regine vero caput quod mihi dederant moniales conventus sancti Maximini. Item dedi eis duo ossa magna, ex quatuor quae mihi dederant canonici sancti Hieronymi; quae sunt ex ossibus turmae sancti Gereonis. Principi autem Portugalliae dedi unum ex ossibus. undecim millium Virginum. Utinam Redemptor ac Dominus sanctorum omnium det his principibus gratiam suam, qua sciant ac velint hasce reliquias cum honore debito servare usque in diem illum in quo omnes resurgemus; item ut sciant ac velint percipere fructum caeoeaelestis auxilii sanctorum illorum; ut quorum corpora veneraturi sunt in terris, favorem spirituum corum ubique consequantur. Dixi eisdem nescire me quomodo hasce reliquias melius honorarem quam reponendo illas in manibus tantorum principum: qui jusserunt eas in pretiosa theca recondi et in reginae sacrario asservari.
units.en: On the day of Saint Matthias the apostle I presented to the king of Portugal and to the queen two of the heads of the eleven thousand Virgins: to the king, the head which I had had from the Carthusian convent of Cologne; to the queen, the head which the nuns of the convent of Saint Maximin had given me. Likewise I gave them two great bones, of the four which the canons of Saint Jerome had given me, which are from the bones of the troop of Saint Gereon. And to the Prince of Portugal I gave one of the bones of the eleven thousand Virgins. May the Redeemer and Lord of all the saints give these princes his grace, that they may know how, and be willing, to keep these relics with due honour until that day on which we shall all rise again; likewise that they may know how, and be willing, to receive the fruit of the heavenly help of those saints, so that they whose bodies they venerate on earth may obtain for them the favour of their spirits everywhere. I told them that I knew not how I might better honour these relics than by placing them in the hands of such great princes; who ordered them to be enclosed in a precious casket and kept in the queen's chapel.

units.la: Feria quarta. post dominicam /nvocavit, ego ad hoc recitavi meas solitas Litanias, ut mihi et omnibus fratribus meis prodessent in specialem quemdam et desiderabilem profectum. In me namque factum est novum quoddam desiderium, quo petebam gratias ad omnia illa opera recte- agenda, de quibus ego et caeteri reddituri sumus specialem rationem; scilicet pro quotidiana ordi- natione actionum mearum, pro recta examinatione conscientiae, pro persolvendis horis nostris canonicis; pro facienda bona et lacrymabili confessione auriculari; pro celebratione missarum, pro sumenda communione, pro administrandis sacramentis, pro recta tractatione verbi Dei, tam publice quam privatim, pro exercenda ubique sancta conversatione inter viros et mulieres. Haec enim sunt septem genera actionum, pro quibus usque ad perfectum implendis, quotidie petendae sunt ex Deo et Sanctis ejus gratiae. Propterea contraxi omnes eas gratias, quas ego in Litaniis meis petere soleo, ad idem applicans missam diei qui sequutus est dictam feriam quartam.
units.en: On the Wednesday after the Sunday Invocavit, I recited my accustomed Litanies to this end, that they might profit me and all my brethren unto a certain special and desirable progress. For there arose in me a certain new desire, in which I asked graces for the right doing of all those works of which I and the rest must render a special account: namely, for the daily ordering of my actions; for the right examination of conscience; for the discharge of our canonical hours; for the making of a good and tearful auricular confession; for the celebration of Masses; for the receiving of communion; for the administering of the sacraments; for the right handling of the word of God, both publicly and privately; for the exercise everywhere of holy conversation among men and women. For these are the seven kinds of actions, for the perfect fulfilment of which graces are daily to be asked of God and his Saints. Therefore I drew together all those graces which I am accustomed to ask in my Litanies, applying to the same purpose the Mass of the day which followed the said Wednesday.

units.la: Die quarta mensis Marti, Licentiatus Araoz et ego, obtenta tandem licentia a rege Portugalliae, recessimus ab Ebora; et in die sancti Gregorii, Salmanticam pervenimus; die autem decima octava, qua scilicet celebratur festum divi Ga- brielis, Vallisoletum. Et sic factum est, Deo dante et ducente, ut impleretur illa obedientia qua mihi praescriptum erat ut ex Colonia abi rem usque ad Portugalliam, per regem inde třansmittendus Vallisoletum. Sit benedictus Deus; qui viam tantae peregrinationis semper et ubique felicem fecit!
units.en: On the fourth day of the month of March, the Licentiate Araoz and I, having at last obtained leave from the king of Portugal, departed from Évora; and on the day of Saint Gregory we reached Salamanca; and on the eighteenth day — on which, namely, the feast of Saint Gabriel is celebrated — Valladolid. And so it came to pass, God granting and leading, that that obedience was fulfilled by which it had been prescribed to me that I should go from Cologne as far as Portugal, to be sent on thence by the king to Valladolid. Blessed be God, who made the way of so long a pilgrimage always and everywhere happy!

units.la: Pridie sancti Benedicti abbatis, sub noctem, antequam irem cubitum, mihi data est lacrymosa devotio, in qua me Deo, beatae Virgini, omnium Sanctorum ordinibus qui in hac vita dolores aut labores passi sunt, commendabam. Precabar quoque omnibus peccatoribus et peccantibus compunctionem juxta illud: Lavabo per singulas noctes lectum meum, lacrymis meis stratum meum rigabo. Hic praeterea cum audissem. quosdam nimium laetos et garrulos, qui in vicinis cubiculis dissolutionis suae verba effunderent, caeoepi dolere quod ipsi tam male se ad somnum nocturnum componerent, et dixi orationem: Visita, quaesumus, Domine, habita-- tiones istas, et reliquas omnes in quibas homines degunt, et omnes insidias inimicorum omnium invisibilium ab eis longe repelle. Angeli tui sancti habitent cum ipsis, qui nos et reliquos omnes in pace custodiant, per Christum Dominum nostrum.
units.en: On the eve of Saint Benedict the abbot, at nightfall, before I went to bed, a tearful devotion was given me, in which I commended myself to God, to the blessed Virgin, and to all the orders of the Saints who in this life suffered griefs or labours. I prayed also for all sinners, and for those now sinning, compunction, according to that word: Every night I will wash my bed; I will water my couch with my tears. Here moreover, having heard certain persons too merry and talkative, who in the neighbouring chambers were pouring out the words of their dissoluteness, I began to grieve that they composed themselves so ill for the night's sleep, and I said the prayer: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, these dwellings, and all others in which men live, and drive far from them all the snares of all the invisible enemies. Let thy holy Angels dwell with them, to keep us and all the rest in peace, through Christ our Lord.

units.la: In die sancti Benedicti,- applicavi missam specialiter in favorem Societatis nostrae, orans Patriarcham illum sanċtum Benedictum, ut dignaretur ipse eam ipsam, tanquam pius et potens in Christo, potenter protegere ac defendere: defendere inquam, contra omnes spiritus fornicationis, contra omnes spiritus mundi hujus, et contra spiritus nequitiarum atque malitiarum; protegere autem ab omni errore, abomni ignorantia mala, et ab omnibus peccatis.
units.en: On the day of Saint Benedict I applied the Mass specially in favour of our Society, praying that holy Patriarch Benedict that he, as one loving and powerful in Christ, would powerfully protect and defend it: defend it, I say, against all spirits of fornication, against all the spirits of this world, and against the spirits of wickednesses and malices; and protect it from all error, from all evil ignorance, and from all sins.

units.la: Alia vice, dum venissem ad palatium, volens audire praedicationem in capella Principis, fac- tum est ut prohiberer intrare, quippe quod essem ignotus janitori. Sic permansi aliquandiu ante fores, ubi memini quod saepe permiserim intrare in animum meum varias cogitationes malas, et varios spiritus nequam; Jesum autem et verba ejus, ac spiritum ejus, pulsare ante ostium etstare permiserim. Cogitabam etiam qualiter Christus tam male receptus sit ubique a mundo. Oravi etiam pro me et pro jani- tore illo, ut nobis concederetur ne ante fores paradisi nos diutius purgandos stare expectare- que contingat. Alia quoque multa mihi occurrerunt in eo loco, quibus valde compunctus sum: unde factum est ut magis amarem ipsum anitorem, qui hujus devotionis causa erat. Optabam etiam maxime ut nemo eorum qui nostrae Societatis futuri sunt, detrimentum unquam aliquód ex similibus repulsis, aut etiam majoribus, pati possit detrimentum nempe animae, quod solet contingere superbis et impatientibus.
units.en: On another occasion, when I had come to the palace, wishing to hear the sermon in the Prince's chapel, it happened that I was forbidden to enter, since I was unknown to the doorkeeper. So I remained some time before the doors, where I remembered that I have often allowed various evil thoughts and various wicked spirits to enter into my soul, while I have allowed Jesus and his words and his spirit to knock at the door and stand outside. I thought also how ill Christ is received everywhere by the world. I prayed too for myself and for that doorkeeper, that it might be granted us not to have to stand and wait long before the doors of paradise for our purging. Many other things also came to me in that place, by which I was much pricked; whence it came that I loved the doorkeeper the more, who was the cause of this devotion. And I wished above all that none of those who are to be of our Society may ever suffer any harm from such rebuffs, or even greater ones — harm, I mean, of soul, such as is wont to befall the proud and the impatient.

units.la: In die sanctissimae Annuntiationis Virginis Dei- parae, multa mihi occurrerunt, ut desiderarem bonas aliquas annunciationes, bona scilicet nova de mea salute. Optabam ilum diem in quo certior fieri possim de vita aeterna; reputabam ilum beatum esse, qui probabiliter novit se invenisse gratiam apud Deum, Deum esse secum, se. aliquam benedictionem inter homines invenisse, se facere opera Deo accepta. Miseri igitur sunt illi quibus prima cura est num sint in gratia hominis alicujus mortalis, et quo pacto talis: homo erga ipsos sese habeat; qui etiam maxime cupiunt scire quaenam bona sunt recepturi; qui denique nimium gaudent dum audiunt opera et officia sive servitia sua placere Dominis suis. Hic dum considerassem tali die Christum incarnatum fuisse;' -proindeque exor- dium nostrae salutis de facto et re ipsa incae- an eaS a N ta EPILOGUS 355 pisse, dum, inquam, hoc sic cogitassem, oravi Dominum ut det opere etde facto incipere quod hactenus in solis manet affectibus. Sit hic, o Deus. meus, initium conversionis desideriorum et affectuum etiam in opere et effectu. Deus ab aeterno proposuit propitiationem Jesum Christum: sed ante hunc diem Verbum non est factum caro. Conceptus Patris hodie factus est caro; ffánt ergo conceptus nostri opera ac facta benedicta, sive fructus benedictus. Det Deus in singulis verbis et actionibus, in quibus versamur et exercemur, ut novum aliquem modum proficiendi hic incipiamus. Laus Deo.
units.en: On the day of the most holy Annunciation of the Virgin Mother of God, many things came to me, so that I desired some good annunciations — good news, that is, of my salvation. I longed for that day in which I may be made more certain of eternal life; I counted him blessed who knows with probability that he has found grace with God, that God is with him, that he has found some blessing among men, that he does works acceptable to God. Wretched then are they whose first care is whether they are in the favour of some mortal man, and how such a man stands towards them; who also desire above all to know what goods they are to receive; who, in short, rejoice overmuch when they hear that their works and services please their masters. Here, having considered that on such a day Christ was made flesh, and that thereby the beginning of our salvation, in deed and in very truth, was made — having thought this, I say, I prayed the Lord to grant that there begin in work and in deed what hitherto remains in affections alone. Be this, O my God, the beginning of the conversion of my desires and affections into work and effect also. God from eternity purposed the propitiation, Jesus Christ; but before this day the Word was not made flesh. The conception of the Father today was made flesh; may our conceptions therefore become blessed works and deeds, or blessed fruit. May God grant, in every word and action in which we are engaged and exercised, that we may here begin some new manner of progress. Praise be to God.

units.la: (Anno 1540) Nolo vos in hoc errore versari ut putetis alio egere vos cibo ad augendam pietatem atque eo quo usi estis adhuc ad eamdem nutriendam. Nec sane mens est alia ac doctrina philosophi, qui cum de corporum disputat alimentis, docet ea quae sunt alendis apta corporibus, valere ctiam ad augenda. Ita cum ad alendam fovendamque pietatem usu jam vestro senseritis plurimum huc usque valuisse pia ista munera quae tractatis, prorsus statuatis oportet eadem posthac vobis necessaria fore ad augendam; praesertim caelesti gustando et frequentando Pane, quod est praecipuum animae pabulum, et quo Angeli Beatique omnes continenter aluntur, magis utique animorum vitae, quam noster hic corporum quem quotidie frangimus, necessario.
units.en: I would not have you fall into the error of thinking that you need any other food for increasing piety than that which you have used hitherto for nourishing it. Nor indeed is the mind of the matter other than the teaching of the philosopher, who, when he treats of the nourishment of bodies, teaches that the things fit for feeding bodies avail also for their growth. So, since by your own experience you have felt that these pious duties which you practise have hitherto availed very much for feeding and cherishing piety, you must fully resolve that the same will hereafter be necessary to you for increasing it; above all by tasting and frequenting the heavenly Bread, which is the chief food of the soul, on which the Angels and all the Blessed are continually fed — more necessary surely to the life of souls than is this bread of our bodies, which we break daily.

units.la: Quod ipsum de aliis pietatis studiis ac muneribus sentiendum est: quale est, quotidianae suae vitae rationem ab se repetere, peccata confessione diluere, res divinas ac salutares assidua cogitatione versare, denique misericordiae officiis constanter insistere. Quarum rerum usu atque exercitatione, si quid est a vobis, aut in animi vestri notitia, aut in Dei et hominum charitate profectum, persuasissimum vobis esse debet, oportere in iisdem vos officiis constanter insistere, quo magis in Christo crescatis.
units.en: The same is to be thought of the other pious studies and duties: such as reviewing the account of one's daily life, washing away sins by confession, turning over divine and saving things in constant thought, and finally persevering steadily in the offices of mercy. If by the use and exercise of these things any progress has been made by you, whether in the knowledge of your own soul or in the charity of God and men, you ought to be fully persuaded that you must steadily persevere in the same duties, that you may grow the more in Christ.

units.la: Ratio porro quotidianae vitae vestrae talis esse poterit. Singulis noctibus, priusquam qwieti soporique vos dedatis, nixi genibus, quatuor illa cūjusque novissima recoletis: supremum vitae diem, supremum judicium, inferorum supplicia, et paradisi gaudia; quibus in singulis contemplandis considerandisque tamdiu haerere vos volo, dum dominica ter recitetur oratio, ter angelica EOE E n a Dae E w oga a pie ra salutatio. Postea succedet observatio pectoris vestri et totius recognitio diei; in qua, post aċtas divinae liberalitati de beneficiis meritas gratias, peccata vestra cum gemitu retractabitis, et ea statuetiscerto sacerdoti destinatoque tempore confiteri.
units.en: The plan of your daily life, moreover, may be as follows. Every night, before you give yourselves to rest and sleep, on bended knees you shall call to mind those four last things of every man: the last day of life, the last judgment, the punishments of hell, and the joys of paradise; and in the contemplation and consideration of each of these I would have you dwell for as long as the Lord's prayer is recited three times, and the angelic salutation three times. Afterwards shall follow the observation of your own breast and the review of the whole day; in which, after due thanks rendered to the divine liberality for its benefits, you shall go over your sins with groaning, and resolve to confess them to a fixed priest at an appointed time.

units.la: Id autem genus est quoddam spiritualis confessionis, qua quis suis noxis animadversis, earum sese insimulat ante Deum, justo dolore et constantissima voluntate suscepta eas ad praestitutam diem sacerdotibąs enunciandi. Ad extremum rogandus est vobis Deus, ut et vobis ipsis et vivis omnibus noctem quietam atque tranquillam, mortuis vero, qui suas maculas purgant, solatii aliquid et indulgentiae largiatur; in eamque rem ter dominicam precem, ter angelicam recitabitis. Easdem genere et numero iterabitis postridie mane, et ut vos ceterosque vivos ab omni labe integros ea luce conservet, et mortuis refrigerationis aliquid tribuat ab ardoribus piacularis ignis.
units.en: And that is a kind of spiritual confession, in which one, having taken note of his faults, accuses himself of them before God, with just sorrow and with a most constant will, undertaken, of declaring them to the priests on the day appointed. Lastly, you must beg God to grant to yourselves and to all the living a quiet and tranquil night, and to the dead, who are purging their stains, some measure of solace and indulgence; and to that end you shall recite three times the Lord's prayer, three times the angelic salutation. The same, in kind and number, you shall repeat the next morning, that he may keep you and the other living free from every stain through that day, and grant to the dead some refreshment from the burnings of the purging fire.

units.la: Si fuerit otium, licebit insuper aliquid de vita Christi, vel ante signum ejus in cruce trajecti, vel mišsarum inter solemnia, tacitis mentibus retractare. Cujus ad exemplar identidem respectantes, vitam vestram moresque fingatis. Ubi sacerdos Christi corpus rite confecerit, aut excitatum ab ara sublime populo praemonstrarit, tum vos vestris malis morbisque remedia et ea quae optatis dona petetis a Deo, ut robur animi et cognitionem vestri pectoris, ut mutuam fraternamque concordiam; quodque in summis numerandum est donis, famem sitimque justitiae. Rogabitis etiam Christi corpus, ut spirituali quadan communiene sui, haud abnuat tectum animae veslrae succedere. Quo communionis genere incitabitur in vobis aviditas quaedam tanti mysterii, oblectantibus interimvos et proxime suscèpti memoria et spe denuo suscipiendi.
units.en: If there be leisure, it will be well besides to go over silently in your minds something of the life of Christ, whether before the sign of him pierced on the cross, or during the solemnities of Mass; looking ever and again to his pattern, that you may fashion your life and ways upon it. When the priest has duly consecrated the body of Christ, or raised it from the altar and shown it on high to the people, then you shall ask of God remedies for your evils and diseases, and the gifts you desire: strength of soul and knowledge of your own breast, mutual and brotherly concord, and — what is to be counted among the highest gifts — hunger and thirst after justice. You shall also beg the body of Christ that, by a kind of spiritual communion of himself, he refuse not to come under the roof of your soul. By which kind of communion there will be kindled in you a certain eagerness for so great a mystery, while you take delight both in the memory of the communion lately received, and in the hope of receiving it anew.

units.la: Haec communionis quotidianae ratio erit veluti quaedam animi praeparatio, longe efficax ad ipsum sacramentum Corporis Domini;: quemadmodum et ad sacramentum Paenitentiae spiritalis illa quam dixi confessio. Proinde venit in mentem optare ut christianus quisque multo ante percipiat animo diem illum, quo et pectus suum expiare confessione decreverit, et Christi Domini inire convivium; ita ut quotidie mane, simul ac de cubili surrexerit, ita se moneat -et alloquatur: Tali die sacerdotis ad pedes, tali. accedes ad Christi mensam; idque etiamsi -forte longius ille dies absit.
units.en: This practice of daily communion will be as it were a preparation of the soul, most efficacious towards the sacrament itself of the Lord's Body; as also, towards the sacrament of Penance, that spiritual confession of which I spoke. Hence it comes to mind to wish that every christian should perceive in his soul, long beforehand, that day on which he has resolved both to cleanse his breast by confession and to enter the banquet of Christ the Lord; so that daily in the morning, as soon as he has risen from his bed, he should thus admonish and address himself: On such a day you will be at the priest's feet; on such a day you will approach the table of Christ — and this even if perhaps that day be still far off.

units.la: Videte igitur singulis diebus ut memoriam vobis excitetis ac refricetis hujus Sacramenti, et suscipiendi pariter et suscepti: suscepti quidem, ad dimidiatum saltem spatium praestituti temporis; suscipiendi vero, toto reliquo intervallo dierum; ut hac ratione planissimum fiat vereri vos et horrere verenda illa eb sacrosancta mysteria: secus enim periculum sit ne vel aegre concoquatis quod ore percipitis, vel non satis avide suscipiatis. Nolite vobis ipsi deesse, quominus octavo saltem quoque die haec Sacramenta tractetis et renovetis.
units.en: See to it, then, that every day you stir up and refresh in yourselves the memory of this Sacrament, both as to be received and as received: as received, for at least half the space of the appointed time; as to be received, through all the remaining interval of days; that by this means it may become most natural to you to fear and stand in awe of those awful and most holy mysteries: for otherwise there is danger either that you digest ill what you receive with the mouth, or that you receive it with too little eagerness. Do not fail yourselves in this: that at least every eighth day you approach and renew these Sacraments.

units.la: Caetera vero pietatis officia, qualis est precatio, qualis piae contemplationis exercitatio, et id genus alia, videte ut fines illos, seu singulos seu universos, propositos habeant: primum Dei et ejus Sanctorum gloriam; deinde animi vestri bonum; tum caeterorum commodum animorum. Sic enim, per ea quae dixi munera quotidiana, vobis fiet virtutis accessio, ut humilitatis, ut patientiae, ut prudentiae, et aliarum hujusmodi rerum atque virtutum, quibus paratiores in dies accedatis ad recte agendum. Accedet etiam Dei notitia major, et major amor, cumulabitur in proximos charitas; et tuto denique salutis iter tenebitur, dum veluti per gradus vita spiritus sic instituetur.
units.en: As for the other offices of piety — such as prayer, the exercise of devout contemplation, and other things of that kind — see that they have set before them these ends, whether singly or all together: first, the glory of God and of his Saints; then the good of your own soul; then the benefit of other souls. For thus, by the daily duties I have spoken of, there will come to you an increase of virtue — of humility, of patience, of prudence, and of other such things and virtues, by which you may daily come better prepared to right action. There will come also a greater knowledge of God, and a greater love; charity towards your neighbours will be heaped up; and finally the way of salvation will be held in safety, while the life of the spirit is thus built up as by steps.

units.la: Quod autem ad hujus temporis et corporis vitam pertinet, oportebit ita vos vestra moderari consilia sensusque omnes, ut omnis labor corporis ac contentio Dei laudem spectet, salutem animi vestri, eorumque animorum qui in iis sunt inclusi corporibus quibus vos laborem vestrum operamque navatis. Studete igitur ut primum Deus vos ad laborem, seu etiam ad quietem impellat; deinde salus animae vestrae; tum animae proximorum; deinde vestri corporis incolumitas; postea incolumitas alieni; denique res familiaris, quaeque ad usus corporis vitaegue necessarios pertinere videantur; ne qua sit ordinis perturbatio, ne qua confùsio.
units.en: And as regards the life of this time and of the body, you must so order your counsels and all your inclinations that every labour and effort of the body may look to the praise of God, the salvation of your own soul, and of those souls which are enclosed in the bodies for which you spend your labour and pains. Study therefore that, first, it be God who impels you to labour, or likewise to rest; then the salvation of your own soul; then the souls of your neighbours; then the health of your own body; after that, the health of another's; and lastly your worldly substance, and whatever things seem to pertain to the necessary uses of the body and of life; that there be no disturbance of order, no confusion.

units.la: Nihil autem in his quae commemoravi praeposterum perturbatumque erit, si res familiaris sit famula corporis, corpus animi, animus Del; questusque vestri ad necessitatem corporum, COTporum autem incolumitas ad animorum salutem, horum verum studia ad aeternae legis regulam dirigantur. Ita, ab hoc ultimo inchoandum pri- mum, et hic ordo servandus officiorum, ut prima N a E O E at animis, caetera caeteris deinceps rebus, pro ani- morum bono commodoque debeantur.
units.en: And nothing in what I have recounted will be out of place or disordered, if your worldly substance be the handmaid of the body, the body of the soul, the soul of God; and if your gains be directed to the necessity of your bodies, the health of your bodies to the salvation of souls, and the pursuits of these to the rule of the eternal law. Thus one must begin first from this last, and this order of duties be kept: that the first be owed to souls, and the rest, in their order, to the other things, for the good and benefit of souls.

units.la: <d aan Nec imitandi enim sunt ii qui a re familiari et suo corpore inchoandum putant; ut cum haec vere constituerint, taum demum se facilius rem constituturos animorum arbitrentur. Eademque ratione, quod ad proximos spectat, eorum prius animis, quoad ejus fieri poterit, quam vestris e a a a corporibus providete; ut, si in potestate sit vestra, uno eodemque praesidio, et vos a morte corporis, et illos a morte animae vindicare, malitis utique multis partibus huic periclitanti, quam illi ruenti et jam cadenti succurrere. Si hic vobis rerum ordo servatur, facile existet ea quam quaeritis in instituto constantia. i i i i K
units.en: Nor are they to be imitated who think one must begin from worldly substance and one's own body, so that when they have set these in order, they may then, as they suppose, the more easily set in order the things of souls. And by the same reasoning, in what concerns your neighbours, provide for their souls first, so far as may be, before your own bodies; so that, if it be in your power, by one and the same aid, both to save yourselves from the death of the body and them from the death of the soul, you would by many degrees rather succour the soul that is in peril than the body that is tottering and already falling. If this order of things is kept by you, there will easily arise that constancy in your undertaking which you seek.

appendix.titel: Ad S. Ignatium et Petrum Codacium, Spira, 23. Ian. 1541

units.la: Charissimis meis in Christo fratribus, magistro Ignatio de Loyola et magistro Petro Codacio, ad Turrim Metanguli, in domo Antonii Frangipane, Romae.
units.en: To my dearest brothers in Christ, master Ignatius de Loyola and master Pietro Codacio, at the Torre del Melangolo, in the house of Antonio Frangipani, Rome.

units.la: Gratia et amor Domini Nostri Jesu Christi sit vobiscum semper.
units.en: The grace and love of Our Lord Jesus Christ be with you always.

units.la: Die 22 hujus mensis tertiam vestram accepi epistolam; tertiam, inquam, earum quae post discessum meum ex Italia ad me pervenerunt. Priorem enim 22° novembris dedistis, quo die nullam adhuc ex meis acceperatis; secundam Quod ad me attinet, suspicantibus vobis socordiam meam, non facile credar etiamsi per litteras sinceritatem satis evincam meam. Testes tamen proferam fideles qui sedulum me in scribendo vindicent. Vestrum est hujusmodi a me testimonia repetere; innuite tantum; si quid dubitatis me toties ad vos conscripsisse, quot inter lapsum trium mensium fluxerunt hebdomadae a nostro in provinciam Wormatiensem et Spirensem adventu: Vereor transitum epistolis.. nostris non satis tutum; quocirca mitter non audeo, ne forte res in pejus ingravescant. Nunc igitur ut litteris vestris recentioribus respondeam, satis sit bonam nostram valetudinem Deo opitulante profiteri. Res alias, quarum nullam hactenus mentionem feci, paucis expediam, hac ductus opinione, caeteras epistolas, ut istam, ad vos serius ocius perventuras. i Procurationes et statuta quibus de colloquiis incipiendis conventum est, tribus vix mensibus absoluta fuere. Qua de re jam plura scripsi: a decem circiter diebus colloquia incaepta: cautumque ut unus pro undecim catholicis dissereret, unusque pro totidem adversariis, Doctor Eckius catholicorum nomine, Philippus Melanchthon protestantium, coram praeside, et legatis imperatoris regisque Romanorum. Primus articulus, nempe de peccato originali exagitari caeptus. Singuli per vices locuti, atque ita ut adnotationes, et quidquid disserebatur resċribi posset. Tres dies impensi quin consentirent; ideoque praecisa hac disputandi ratione res integra ad Diaetam remissa. Itaque septem abhinc diebus DD. de Granvella et consequenter nos etiam: Wormatia profecti sumus Spiram, qua in civitate residet curia suprema Justitiae Imperialis. Nescio an sit Wormatiae qui communem discessum ita tulerit aegre,- atque etiam nunc insolabiliter feret, sicuti Decanus meus de sancto Martino qui (excepta generali exomologesi, quam, reor, postea absolvit doctori caeco, Wormatiae superstiti una cum Episcopo de Feltre et legatis sanctissimi) primam Exercitioram spiritualium hebdomadam paene absolverat. Deo gratiae referendae ob fructus quos optimus Decanus colligebat, impulsusque in cordibus vel lapideis ab eo excitatos, ita ut etiam multi in hac civitate, cognita -ex illius litteris nostra agendi: ratione, jamjam Egzercilia, peragere concupiscerent. Ipsius epistolam huc veniens attuli ad Episcopum hujus civitatis, virum principem Germaniae,: quem þene propensum inveni. Ter hunc affatus rem nostram p a a M CAER ae aiii ordinatim enucleavi; ipse multa cum aedificatione haec omnia audivit.
units.en: On the 22nd of this month I received your third letter — the third, I mean, of those which have reached me since my departure from Italy. For the first you wrote on the 22nd of November, on which day you had as yet received none of mine. As for me, though you suspect my slackness, I shall not easily be believed even if by letters I sufficiently prove my sincerity. Yet I shall bring forward faithful witnesses to vindicate my diligence in writing. It is for you to require such testimonies from me; only give the sign, if you doubt at all that I have written to you as many times as there have been weeks in the three months that have passed since our arrival in the province of Worms and Speyer. I fear the passage is not safe enough for our letters; wherefore I dare not send, lest matters perhaps grow worse. Now, then, to answer your more recent letter: let it suffice to declare that by God's help our health is good. Other matters, of which I have hitherto made no mention, I will despatch in few words, led by the opinion that my other letters, like this one, will sooner or later reach you. The arrangements and statutes agreed on for beginning the colloquies were scarcely finished in three months. On this I have already written more: the colloquies began about ten days ago; and it was provided that one should speak for eleven catholics, and one for as many of the adversaries — Doctor Eck in the name of the catholics, Philip Melanchthon for the protestants — before the president, and the legates of the emperor and of the king of the Romans. The first article, namely on original sin, began to be debated. Each spoke in turn, and in such a way that notes could be taken and everything said set down in writing. Three days were spent without their agreeing; and so, this manner of disputing being cut short, the whole matter was referred to the Diet. Accordingly, seven days ago the lords de Granvelle — and consequently we also — set out from Worms for Speyer, in which city resides the supreme court of Imperial Justice. I know not whether there is anyone at Worms who took the general departure so hard, and still bears it inconsolably, as my Dean of Saint Martin, who (apart from his general confession, which I think he afterwards completed to the blind doctor who remained at Worms together with the Bishop of Feltre and the legates of his Holiness) had almost finished the first week of the spiritual Exercises. Thanks must be rendered to God for the fruits which the excellent Dean was gathering, and the impulses stirred by him in hearts even of stone; so that many in this city also, having learned from his letters our way of proceeding, were already longing to go through the Exercises. Coming here, I brought his letter to the Bishop of this city, a prince of Germany, whom I found well disposed. Three times I spoke with him, and unfolded our affairs in order; he heard it all with much edification.

units.la: Praesul ipse egregius, die jovis mox elapso, me convivam voluit, invitatis pariter ad mensam duce Bavarensi, Palatini comitis fratre, et archiepiscopo Trevirensi; quos omnes de nostris rebus certiores reddebat. Me postea ad suum generalem vicarium misit, quem, ultimo hoc triduo, de rebus spiritualibus diuturna fabulatione allocutus sum; ex eoque ad Exercitia peragenda paratus est. Nihil tamen hic moliri ausim, imminente nostro Ratisbonam itinere, quod cras aut perindie aggrediemur. Episcopus etiam, una cum aliis Imperii principibus eo proficiscitur; ibique aliquid factūm iri confido; praesul enim est optime erga nos: affectus. Pridie nostri discessus, rem ċum principaliore quodam theologo doctore Joanne Cochleo, qui huc venerat Romani regis nomine, penitus composueram. Hic plura in rem Germaniċĉam, adversus hujus regionis haereticos, exaravit; atque hinc factom est ut, quo die spiritualia Exercitia incipere debebat, discedere coacti simus.
