Deo profecto laudes tribuendae, de extïřema. qua Exercitia aggrediebatur voluptate: Cum ipsi de discrimine sermonem habuissem inter scientiam et sensum spiritualem, coelesti subridens laetitia: Gaudeo, inquit, quod tandem magistri circa affectus inveniantur! Illum Ratisbonae revisam; unde meus inde profectus nil mihi afferet detrimenti. Decanus magnae ecclesiae Wormiensis mihi pariter promisit se eadem ibidem Exercitia facturum, cum sive nomine proprio, sive fratris Palatini comitis qui est Wormiensis episcopus, Diaetam petere cogeretur.
units.en: That excellent prelate, on the Thursday just past, would have me as his guest, there being invited to table likewise the duke of Bavaria, brother of the Count Palatine, and the archbishop of Trier; all of whom he informed about our affairs. Afterwards he sent me to his vicar general, with whom in these last three days I have spoken in long discourse of spiritual things; and by it he is ready to make the Exercises. Yet I dare set nothing on foot here, with our journey to Regensburg at hand, which we shall undertake tomorrow or the day after. The Bishop also, together with the other princes of the Empire, is going there; and there I trust something will be done, for the prelate is excellently disposed towards us. On the eve of our departure I had fully settled the matter with a certain leading theologian, Doctor Johann Cochlaeus, who had come here in the name of the king of the Romans. He has written much for the German cause against the heretics of this region; and hence it came about that on the very day he was to begin the spiritual Exercises, we were forced to depart. Praise indeed must be given to God for the extreme delight with which he was entering on the Exercises. When I had spoken with him of the difference between knowledge and spiritual feeling, smiling with heavenly gladness he said: I rejoice that at last masters are found for the affections! I shall see him again at Regensburg; so my departure hence will bring me no loss. The dean of the great church of Worms likewise promised me that he would there make the same Exercises, when, whether in his own name or in that of the brother of the Count Palatine, who is bishop of Worms, he should be obliged to attend the Diet.

units.la: Res nostras enucleate aperui Fratri Alfonso de Herrera, optime valenti, qui libenter eas excepit, vobisque se enixe commendat. Degit ibi vir religiosus, a confessionibus Imperatoris, rector quondam domus PP. Dominicanorum Salmanticensium, quum ea in urbe esset Ignatius, quique, uti accepi ex Fratre Alfonso regio concionatore, optima semper de Ignatio testatus est Biduo ante meum Wormio discessum, regis lusitani legatum invisi, obsequii et gratiarum actionis cauŝa ob., benefacta erga socios illic collata. Cui res nostras jam bene callenti necessarium visum est ut una per otium colloque- 'remur. f=iiy? APPENDIX 369 Vir est piissimus; ex eoque spero, in Domino, quidquid ad bonam aemulationem incitare poterit legatum, qui secum ducit socios nostros, Ratisbonae cum ipso conferam.
units.en: I laid open our affairs fully to Fray Alfonso de Herrera, who is in excellent health, received them gladly, and earnestly commends himself to you. There lives there a religious, confessor to the Emperor, once rector of the house of the Dominican Fathers at Salamanca when Ignatius was in that city, who, as I learned from Fray Alfonso the royal preacher, has always borne the best witness concerning Ignatius. Two days before my departure from Worms I visited the ambassador of the king of Portugal, to pay my respects and give thanks for the kindnesses conferred on the companions there. As he already knows our affairs well, it seemed needful that we should talk together at leisure. He is a most devout man; and from him I hope, in the Lord, for whatever can stir to good emulation the ambassador who has our companions with him; I shall confer with him at Regensburg.

units.la: Ducem Sabaudiae, principem regionis meae natalis, nudius tertius invisi una cum doctore Ortiz qui eum de rebus nostris erudiit; interque fabulandum, Dux interrogavit an essem"'ex iis qui orbem peragrant, opportuna mihi exhibendo si forte suas petiissem ditiones. Cui, magna adstante corona, me nullo egere temporali subsidio respondi, sed solo ipsius patrocinio ad animarum utilitatem: ad quod etiam suam qua pollet operam spopondit. Nil innuam de ipsius humanitate, nec de vultu benigno quo me excepit, ne forte dicatis laudes hoc tempore ignobiles esse, aut me nimio duci affectu erga principem meum, si quid tamen est potius meum quam vestrum in Domino. Vereor ne in itinere Ratisbonam usque, quindecim diebus hine dissitam, ad vos scribere nequeam. Me excusatum interim habetote. Et pro tempore transacto meas exhibete amicis excusationes.
units.en: The Duke of Savoy, the prince of my native region, I visited two days ago together with Doctor Ortiz, who instructed him about our affairs; and in the course of conversation the Duke asked whether I was one of those who travel the world over, offering me what I might need if I should ever visit his dominions. To whom, in the presence of a great circle, I answered that I needed no temporal help, but only his patronage for the profit of souls; to which also he pledged the service that lies in his power. I will say nothing of his kindness, nor of the gracious countenance with which he received me, lest perhaps you say that praises are cheap in these times, or that I am carried by too much affection towards my prince — if indeed anything is mine rather than yours in the Lord. I fear that on the journey to Regensburg, fifteen days distant from here, I may not be able to write to you. Hold me excused meanwhile, and for the time past make my excuses to our friends.

units.la: Epistolas quas jussistis ad vos scribi per dupli- cem tabellarium diverso itinere transmisi. Restat ut Deum Dominum nostrum enixe deprecer, qui plenitudinem suae gratiae omnibus impertiri dignetur, ut et suam noscamus voluntatem $ et noscentes impleamus.
units.en: The letters which you ordered to be written to you I have sent by a double courier by different routes. It remains that I earnestly beseech God our Lord, that he would deign to impart the fulness of his grace to all, that we may both know his will, and knowing it, fulfil it.

units.la: Spirae, 23 Jan. 1541.
units.en: Speyer, 23 January 1541.

units.la: Vester in Christo Domino Nostro frater, Petrus Faber.
units.en: Your brother in Christ Our Lord, Peter Faber.

units.la: P. S. — Doctor (Ortiz) una cumsua familia vobis se maxime commendat, aestuatque desiderio vestras praesertim litteras accipiendi.
units.en: P.S. — The Doctor (Ortiz), together with his household, commends himself to you most heartily, and burns with desire of receiving letters, above all from you.

units.la: Gratia et pax Christi Domini Nostri sit semper in cordibus nostris.
units.en: The grace and peace of Christ Our Lord be always in our hearts.

units.la: Vestram epistolam die 5*: Aprilis scriptam, 3* Maii accepi, in qua reperi materiam, unde, si aliud non possum, multas gratias agam Deo D. N., non solum pro vestro felici adventu, sed etiam pro bona valetudine, qua, ut scribitis, omnes fratres nostri fruuntur.. Largiatur Chris- tus Jesus uberem vobis gratiam, ut, quo spec- tatis, recto cursu, velut arcu mentis semper intento, studia vestra referatis, et gaudere quasi quodam triumpho possitis; quem ad extremum deportabitis, si cum scientiae spiritu sancte quoque sentiendi spiritum conjunxeritis. Quae quidem expectatio desiderii mei totiusque Societatis tum demum explebitur, Cħristo duce, cuni summus ille Magister, qui litterarum disciplinas postremus infundit, perpetuus vobis quasi quidam praefectus -affuerit magistrorum dictata reddentibus. Is est Spiritus Sanctus, quo doctore atque magistro, quidquid tenetur ac scitur, optime scitur; sine quo, quisquis aliquid scire se putat, nondum novit quemadmodum scire oporteat; ut ipsa quoque Christi Jesu praestantissimi magistri verba, ejus ore prolata, tanti Doctoris opera, quo melius recolantur et memoria repetantur, indigeant. Quid enim ille dixit discipulis suis? Spiritus, inquit, Sanctus suggeret vobis omnia quaecumque dixero vobis.
units.en: Your letter, written on the 5th of April, I received on the 3rd of May; and in it I found matter for which, if I can do nothing else, I give many thanks to God Our Lord — not only for your happy arrival, but also for the good health which, as you write, all our brothers enjoy. May Christ Jesus grant you abundant grace, that you may direct your studies in a straight course towards your mark, with the bow of the mind, as it were, ever bent; and that you may rejoice as in a kind of triumph — which you will carry off at the last, if with the spirit of knowledge you also join the spirit of holy feeling. And this expectation of my desire, and of the whole Society, will then be fulfilled, under Christ's leadership, when that supreme Master, who pours in the disciplines of letters last of all, shall be with you as a kind of perpetual prefect while you render the dictates of your masters. He is the Holy Spirit; with him for teacher and master, whatever is held and known is known excellently; without him, whoever thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know; so that even the very words of Christ Jesus, the most excellent master, uttered by his own mouth, need the work of so great a Doctor, that they may be the better pondered and recalled to memory. For what did he say to his disciples? The Holy Spirit, he said, shall suggest to you all things whatsoever I shall have said to you.

units.la: Nec modo suggeret dixit, sed prius docebit, ut magisterium Sancti Spiritus indicaret, cujus munus est hominibus, quaecumque ille dixerit, non modo suggerere, verum etiam explanatius uberiusque docere. Ergo si Christus, magister noster, via, veritas et vita nostra, suo uti Spiritu, non modo ad sensum voluntatis et cordis, verum etiam ad scientiam mentis et intelligentiae, nos voluit; quanto magis in percipiendis ab homine disciplinis necessarius ejus putandus est usus? Notum vobis Thomae Aquinatis exemplum, qui consueverat secum ipse, non modo quae a doctoribus audisset adhibita precatione recolere, verum etiam quae nondum ab his acceperat, coram hoc caelesti Doctore, prius mente ac cogitatione versare. Ergo et vos etiam atque etiam monitos velim, ut scholas a doctoribus explicandas tanto et ipsi cum Magistro prius animo percurratis; dein ab iis explicatas coram codem praefecto reddatis et memoria repetatis. Sane vobis in Domino gratulor, quod hac inm re longe nobis antecellitis, mihi, inquam, et similibus mei; quoniam priusquam ad litterarum študium vos tradatis, propositum jam habetis quo cursum studii vestri tanquam rectis lineis dirigere vos oporteat. Quare cum et principium, unde omnis sapientia manat, et cursum rectissi- ' mum teneatis, haud ignotus. vobis esse poterit m a A TW. a vestrorum exitus studiorum. Licebit igitur non modo tum, cum finis studiorum erit impositus, verum etiam in ipso studiorum cursu, ut fecistis in ingressu, animo esse quieto ac tranquillo; cujus tanti boni fons ipsa videlicet est recta mentis intentio, quoniam ad eum recta contenditis, qui vita est, et in quo tandem est vera quies. Quando autem recta ingredi via, quae Christus est, jam coepistis, necesse est ulin ea quoque tenenda acquiescatis, suscipiendis videlicet studiorum laboribus in eodem mediatore nostro Christo, qui idem et via et veritas est, quae a Patre exivit et ad Patrem rectissimis quodammodo lineis cursuque rediit. Est igitur, Fratres mei, quod et a vobis Deo grates agantur; nec minores debentur a nobis, quanquam (ut dicere institueram) defuit nobis talis ac tanta componendi ordinandique studii nostri facultas. Quippe existimabamus non in litteris situm esse ut ipsae nobis suum et principium et finem ostenderent. Gumque ignoraremus eum qui et vere principium ut bene ponerentur initia, et vere finis ut in eo velut ancora consiliorum nostrorum atque mentium jactata consisteret; fieri non poterat quin perturbato ordine, et sine pace animi progrederemur. Itaque nesciebamus uti bono litterarum, et bonum quod illae docent arripere, perturbatione finis atque viarum; dum vias pro fine, vicissimque finem pro viis adhibebamus. Aliud sat magnum incommodum (loquor saltem de me) illud erat, quod non cogitabamus crucem mereri habere locum nec in initio, nec in medio, nec in fine. Vos novistis suum praecipuum locum esse in medio, tanquam coadjutricis D. N. J. C. Non est parvae utilitatis (et in hoc etiam nosmetipsos superatis) ut bene vos habeatis cum cruce, et insuper cognoscatis ac sentiatis ordinem quo D. N; J. C. crucifixus, cui tantum debemus, procedit: cur non sinat alios ingrediin mare multarum difficultatum, et cur alios in summa gratia et misericordia eripuerit, ut non tantum possint redimere tempus, verum etiam brevi pervenire eo quo per vias obliquas nunquam pervenissent. Hic est Jesus Christus crucifixus: quem. praedicamus, quemque vobis proponimus ut illum imitemini hac in vita, non ut gloriosumet potentem in regno hujus vitae corporalis, sed eo modo quo videri potest apud gentiliter viventes stultitia, et apud Judaeos: scandalum, apud bonos autem Dei virtus et sapientia.
units.en: Nor did he say only 'shall suggest', but first 'shall teach', to indicate the mastership of the Holy Spirit, whose office it is not only to suggest to men whatever he has said, but also to teach it more plainly and more richly. If then Christ, our master, our way, truth and life, willed us to use his Spirit not only for the feeling of the will and heart, but also for the knowledge of mind and understanding, how much more must his help be thought necessary in receiving the disciplines that are learned from man? You know the example of Thomas Aquinas, who was accustomed by himself not only to go over with prayer what he had heard from the doctors, but also to turn over first in mind and thought, before this heavenly Doctor, what he had not yet received from them. Therefore I would have you admonished again and again, that you too first run through, in mind, with so great a Master, the lessons to be expounded by the doctors; and then, when they have expounded them, render them and recall them to memory before the same prefect. Truly I congratulate you in the Lord, that in this you far excel us — me, I mean, and those like me; for before giving yourselves to the study of letters, you already have the purpose by which you must direct the course of your study as by straight lines. Wherefore, since you hold both the beginning from which all wisdom flows, and the straightest course, the outcome of your studies cannot be unknown to you. You may therefore be of quiet and tranquil mind, not only when the end of your studies is reached, but also in the very course of them, as you were at the entrance; and the fountain of so great a good is the right intention of the mind, since you are making straight for him who is life, and in whom at last is true rest. And since you have now begun to enter the right way, which is Christ, you must needs also rest in keeping it — undertaking, that is, the labours of study in the same Christ our mediator, who is himself both the way and the truth, which went out from the Father and returned to the Father, as it were, by the straightest lines and course. There is reason, then, my Brothers, for you also to give thanks to God; nor do we owe less, although (as I had begun to say) we lacked such and so great a faculty of composing and ordering our study. For we supposed it did not lie in letters that they should themselves show us their beginning and their end. And since we knew not him who is truly the beginning, that our foundations might be well laid, and truly the end, that on him, as on an anchor cast, our counsels and minds might hold fast, it could not but be that we went forward in disordered fashion, and without peace of soul. And so we knew not how to use the good of letters, and to seize the good they teach, through confusion of end and ways — using the ways for the end, and again the end for the ways. Another great enough disadvantage (I speak at least of myself) was this: that we did not consider that the cross deserves a place, whether at the beginning, or in the middle, or at the end. You know that its chief place is in the middle, as the helper of Our Lord Jesus Christ. It is of no small profit (and in this too you surpass us) that you stand well with the cross, and moreover know and feel the order in which Our Lord Jesus Christ crucified, to whom we owe so much, proceeds: why he lets some enter into a sea of many difficulties, and why he has snatched out others in supreme grace and mercy, so that they can not only redeem the time, but even arrive quickly where by crooked ways they would never have arrived. This is Jesus Christ crucified: whom we preach, and whom we set before you, that you may imitate him in this life — not as glorious and mighty in the kingdom of this bodily life, but in that manner in which he can appear as folly among those who live as the gentiles do, and as a scandal among the Jews, but among the good as the power and wisdom of God.

units.la: Negotium fidei valde ambigue procedit, et eo modo ut in Deo solum immediate confidamus, cum media quibus utimur nihil sint in homi- -num judicio. Clare etiam et aperte novi quod, quanto magis desunt media ad revocandos ad fidem qui ab illa recesserunt, tanto magis crescit numerus illorum qui in fide sua redire cupiunt ad meliorem vitam, ne et ab ipsis auferatur candelabrum suum. Utinam ad hos juvandos essent multi operarii! Utinam tandem fiat ut illi qui tantum aedificare intendunt fidem catholicam, etiam incipiant verbis et vita morum structuram reaedificare, et homines aedificare! Praesertim cum nune contra haereticos adeo parum litterae solae possint. Et hoc est quia mundus jam nunc eo pervenit, ut non alia credat sibi necessaria esse argumenta quam operum et sanguinis; quae si desint, ingens et continuus fiet progressus in erroribus. Itaque vos exhortamini litteratos illos parisienses, ut spiritum vivi- ficum itterae conjunctum cum vita valde insigni in imitatione Jesu Christi, acquirere satagant, ut lapsis in errorem fidem persuadere possint. Dominus det vobis sentire de eo in charitate Dei et patientia Christi. Valete. Ratisbonae, 12 Maii t541. Vester in Christo charissimus frater, Petrus Faber.
units.en: The affair of the faith proceeds very doubtfully, and in such a way that we trust immediately in God alone, since the means we use are nothing in the judgment of men. I have also known clearly and plainly that the more the means are lacking for recalling to the faith those who have departed from it, the more grows the number of those who, within their faith, desire to return to a better life, lest their candlestick too be taken from them. Would that there were many labourers to help these! Would that at last those who aim only at building up the catholic faith might also begin, by words and by life, to build up anew the structure of morals, and to build up men! Especially since now against the heretics letters alone can do so little. And this is because the world has now come to such a pass that it believes no other arguments needful to it than those of works and of blood; and if these are lacking, there will be a vast and continual progress in errors. Therefore do you exhort those learned men of Paris to strive to acquire the life-giving spirit joined to the letter, together with a life truly distinguished in the imitation of Jesus Christ, that they may be able to persuade to the faith those who have fallen into error. May the Lord give you to feel concerning him in the charity of God and the patience of Christ. Farewell. Regensburg, 12 May 1541. Your most loving brother in Christ, Peter Faber.

appendix.titel: Ad Iacobum Laynium: de bonis a Deo acceptis

units.la: (Anno 1549) Utinam tibi, Frater charissime, explicare possem quae et quanta bona, ex quo a te Placentia digressus sum usque ad hunc diem,.et animam intra- ' verint et in ea permanserint; quae cognoverim', quae senserim, in iis quae ad Deum, quaeque ad Sacratissimam ejus Matrem pertinent, et ad Beatissimos tum Angelos, tum animas quae vel in coelo vel in purgatorio sunt! Interiora vero mea qùid referam? Elevationes et depressiones meas? Introitus in me et exitus ex me? Quomodo didicerim mundare corpus, et animam, et spiritum; purificare cor meum, etrejectis impedi- mentis praeparare ut divinarum gratiarum liquores recipiat, retineat, conservet, petendo ad omnia haec diversa dona, quaerendo, pulsando? i De iis vero quae ad proximum spectant, non minus multa possint dici, in quibus Dominus Deus modos mihi et vias dedit, veritates ostendit et vitas, ut illum cognoscam, illi de bonis congaudeam, de malis compatiar, in Christo illum amem, illum feram, illum patiar et illi compatiar, pro illo gratias et agam, et petam, et veniam ac remissionem quaeram, et excusationes inveniam, et coram Deo et sanctis ejus bona de illo et pro illo loquar. In summa, Jacobe frater charissime, nunquam ego, non dicam factis aut verbis exequi, sed neque cogitatione possim comprehendere, quae beneficia in me Deus contulit et conferre paratus est, meas contritiones alligans, sanans omnes infirmitates meas, delens meas iniquitates. Ipsi gloria, Amen! ipsi laus, ipsi honor et benedictio ab omni creatura! Ego quidem dico Amen; sed et tu etiam, obsecro, de hoc fratre tuo illum laudato, illi benedicito; quod ego. de universa Societate, et de misericordia Domini tam abundanti hactenus super illam effusa, facere quotidie non désisto.
units.en: Would that I could unfold to you, dearest Brother, what and how great goods, from the time I parted from you at Piacenza down to this day, have both entered my soul and remained in it; what I have come to know, what I have felt, in the things that pertain to God, and to his most holy Mother, and to the most blessed Angels, and to the souls which are either in heaven or in purgatory! And what shall I say of my inward states? My liftings up and my castings down? My enterings into myself and my goings out of myself? How I have learned to cleanse body, and soul, and spirit; to purify my heart, and, the hindrances cast out, to prepare it to receive, retain and preserve the liquors of the divine graces — asking for all these divers gifts, seeking, knocking? And of the things that concern my neighbour no less might be said: in which the Lord God has given me manners and ways, has shown me truths and lives, that I may know him, rejoice with him over his goods, suffer with him over his evils, love him in Christ, bear him, endure him and feel with him, give thanks for him and petition, seek pardon and remission, find excuses, and speak good things of him and for him before God and his saints. In sum, Jacob, dearest brother, never could I — I do not say carry out in deeds or words, but not even compass in thought — the benefits God has conferred on me and stands ready to confer: binding up my bruises, healing all my infirmities, blotting out my iniquities. To him be glory. Amen! To him praise, to him honour and blessing from every creature! I for my part say Amen; but do you also, I beseech you, praise him and bless him for this your brother; as I, for the whole Society, and for the mercy of the Lord so abundantly poured out upon it hitherto, do not cease to do daily.

appendix.titel: Ad Iacobum Laynium: de agendi ratione cum haereticis

units.la: Gratia et pax Redemptoris Nostri sit semper in cordibus nostris.
units.en: The grace and peace of Our Redeemer be always in our hearts.

units.la: Quod a me saepius per litteras postulasti, ut vias aliquas iis traderem, qui velint inter haereticos alienae prodesse saluti, nec suae tamen obesse, justis ego de causis necdum respondi tum quia nondum satis ad cogitandum spatii datum est; tum quia a rebus domesticis nulla quies. Accedit etiam quod ex imbecillitate praeterita, minus adhuc est firma manùs ut ea ad scribendum commode uti queam; et, quod caput est, nihil in mentem venit quod ad rem faciat. Scribam igitur ea duntaxat quae succurrunt ex tempore. Ac primum quidem iis qui prodesse velint hujus aetatis haereticis, videndum est ut magna adversus eos charitate praestent, eosque vere diligant, pulsis ex animo cogitationibus illis quae quoquo modo illorum. apuđ nos existimationem imminuant. Proximum est ut eorum nobis adjungamus animos, voluntatesque càptemus, sic ut il vicissim nos ament, et de nobis optime sentiant.
units.en: What you have often asked of me by letter — that I should hand on some ways for those who wish, among heretics, to profit the salvation of others without harming their own — I have for just causes not yet answered: both because sufficient space for thinking has not yet been given, and because from household affairs there is no rest. There is this besides, that from my late weakness my hand is still not firm enough for me to use it conveniently in writing; and — which is the chief thing — nothing comes to mind that serves the purpose. I will write, then, only what occurs to me on the spur of the moment. And first: those who would help the heretics of this age must see to it that they bear great charity towards them, and love them truly, driving out of their soul those thoughts which in any way lessen our esteem of them. Next, we must win their minds and capture their good will, so that they in turn may love us and think well of us.

units.la: E TE A ar m iaiia Ahadi e MEss PES T E E T A Id autem facile consequemur, si eos comiter alloquamur, et in familiari sermone de iis rebus dumtaxat agamus, de quibus inter utrosque conveniat, omni-altercatione sublata, ubi pars videlicet altera alteram videatur abjicere vel deprimere.
units.en: And this we shall easily obtain if we speak with them affably, and in familiar conversation treat only of those things on which both sides agree, all disputing set aside, in which one party seems to cast down or belittle the other.

units.la: Agendum quippe iis de rebus est prius que voluntates conglutinent atque conjungant, quam de iis ubi sententiarum inter se pugnantium dissimilitudo nascatur. Quoniam autem haec Lutheranorum secta, filiorum est subtractionis in perditionem, et prius in eis recte agendi pietas quam recta fides extinguitur, faciendus est gradus ab iis quae pertinent ad recte sentiendum secundum affectum, ad ea quae faciunt ad recte credendum; secusutique ac olim in Ecclesiae nascentis exordio, cum primum homines convertebantur ad fidem. Quo sane tempore, fide primum, quae est ex auditu, mentes erant imbuendae mortalium et ab erroribus revocandae; deinde sensim reducendae ad recte sentiendum de moribus, operibusque susceptae fidei consentaneis. Si quem igitur suscipiamus curandum, qui non modo pravitatis erroribus, verum etiam perditis moribus sit imbutus, omni insinualione utendum erit ut eum avocemus a vitiis, priusquam verbum ullum de pravis ejus opinionibus faciamus.
units.en: For we must deal first with the things that glue and join wills together, before those in which the unlikeness of conflicting opinions arises. And since this sect of the Lutherans is of the sons of withdrawal unto perdition, and in them the piety of right doing is extinguished sooner than right faith, a step must be made from the things that pertain to right feeling according to the affections, to those that make for right believing; quite otherwise than of old at the beginning of the infant Church, when men were first converted to the faith. At that time, indeed, the minds of mortals were first to be imbued with the faith which comes by hearing, and recalled from errors; then gradually brought back to right feeling about morals and works agreeable to the faith received. If therefore we take in hand the care of one who is imbued not only with the errors of depravity but also with corrupt morals, we must use every insinuation to draw him away from his vices, before saying a single word about his depraved opinions.

units.la: Ac mihi quidem usu venit aliquando ut ad me sacerdos accederet, rogans atque obsecrans ut suas opiniones de sacerdotum conjugio (sane falsas) si qua esset ratione convellerem. Ego vero cum familiariter in ejus me sermonem insinuassem dedissemque, ille mihi se totum aperuit. Deprehendi eum vitam agere in morte peccati, multos jam annos meretricis amoribus irretitum; perfeci tamen, disputationis pugna remota, ut vita priore damnata, ad frugem sua voluntate rediret. Is simul a peccando discessit, Deoque adjuvante, muliercula tandem caruit; continuo sūa sponte, nulla illata catholice doctrinae mentione, conciderunt errores omnes, ut qui ex inquinatae illius vitae sordibus et ortum habuerant et progressus. y Quoniam autem in caeteris Lutheranorum erroribus is est fermécommunis, ut humanas actiones ac facta suis meritis spolient, contemptisque recte factis, omnia in fide reponant, idcirco faciendum nobis est ut, in eorum con- Somir pS aa a aaa gressibus atque colloquiis, ab -operibus ac recte factis progrediamur ad fidem, iis perpetuo sermonibus inferendis, quibus eorum ad amorem ac studium excitentur. Et cum negat haereticus Ecclesiae licere, proposita capitalis peccati paeoena, quemquam alligare psalmodiae vel liturgiae, tum isti adhibenda est cohortatio peracris, qua cum ad orationis ac missae, tum ad alia hüjusmodi incitetur officia: quoniam iste ab audiendi recte sacri psallendive pietate, certis statutisque temporibus, prius excidit quam a fide.
units.en: And it once happened to me that a priest came to me, begging and beseeching that, if there were any way, I would overthrow his opinions (false ones, certainly) about the marriage of priests. But when I had worked myself in a friendly way into his conversation and given myself to him, he opened his whole self to me. I found that he was living in the death of sin, entangled now for many years in the loves of a concubine; yet I brought it about — the combat of disputation being set aside — that, condemning his former life, he returned of his own will to a sound course. As soon as he departed from sinning and, God helping, at last rid himself of the woman, straightway of their own accord — no mention of catholic doctrine being made — all his errors collapsed together; as errors which had had both their origin and their growth from the filth of that defiled life. And since among the other errors of the Lutherans this is well-nigh common — that they strip human actions and deeds of their merits, and, despising right deeds, place everything in faith — we must therefore, in our meetings and conversations with them, proceed from works and right deeds to faith, ever bringing in such discourses as may stir them to the love and pursuit of these. And when the heretic denies that the Church may, under the proposed penalty of capital sin, bind anyone to psalmody or liturgy, then a very sharp exhortation must be applied to him, by which he may be stirred both to the duties of prayer and Mass and to other offices of this kind: for such a man has fallen away from the piety of duly hearing Mass and singing psalms, at fixed and appointed times, sooner than from the faith.

units.la: Observandum est autem sane diligenter id, in quo Lutheranorum duces ministrique niti solent, cum adversus Ecclesiae praecepta sanctionesque sanctorum Patrum suos tuentur errores: id autem est, nimia imbecillitas virium ad obtemperandum, ac tolerandum aliquid propter Deum, itaut eis Ecclesiae leges atque praecepta supra vires minimeque ferenda videantur. Quocirca, ad istos erigendos et animandos, plena spiritu cohortatione opus est; ut in spem redeant, et confidere incipiant fore ut et ipsi' queant, non modo quidquid imperatur, verum etiam majora, Deo adjuvante, praestare. Atque hic ego sic existimo, si quis eflicacitate doctrinae, aut ardore spiritus, persuadere Luthero posset, ut excussis ex animo pravis suis cupidinibus, et recepto religionis ornatu, sese alacri quadam parendi voluntate, ad ca quae imperantur explenda et facienda, converteret, fore ut eo ipso, nulla adhibita concertatione, haereticus esse desineret.
units.en: And that must be observed with all diligence on which the leaders and ministers of the Lutherans are wont to lean, when they defend their errors against the precepts of the Church and the ordinances of the holy Fathers: namely, the excessive weakness of men's strength for obeying, and for enduring anything for God's sake; so that to them the laws and precepts of the Church seem beyond their strength and not at all to be borne. Wherefore, to raise up and hearten such men, there is need of an exhortation full of spirit, that they may return to hope, and begin to trust that they too will be able, with God's help, to perform not only whatever is commanded, but even greater things. And here I so judge: that if anyone, by efficacy of teaching or ardour of spirit, could persuade Luther to shake out of his soul his depraved desires, and, taking again the adornment of religion, to turn himself with a certain eager willingness to obey towards fulfilling and doing the things that are commanded, it would come to pass that by that very fact, without any contention employed, he would cease to be a heretic.

units.la: Quanquam istud quidem majorem quamdam vim spiritus copiamque desiderat; et multo igne divino opus esset, ut ad hanc ille submissionem animi ac tolerantiam, consimilesque virtutes, quas tanta hominis mutatio postulat, per veniret. Quod quoniam, sine praecipua quadam Dei ope, perditis in hominibus et jam prorsus eversis, fieri nullo pacto potest, idcirco perexigua spes est, ac pene nulla; reducendi id haereticorum genus ad sanam mentem. Quisquis autem nullis aliis sermonibus atque colloquiis, nisi de instituenda recte vita, de virtutum pūlchritudine, de orationis studio, de supremo vitae die, de aeternitate géhennae, deque aliis hujusmodi rebus quae vel ad emendandam ethnicorum vitam pertinent, cum. haereticis con- grederetur, nae ille multo magis eorum animis pamon CRITE r F T a te 'APPENDIX 383 ac saluti consuleret, quam si eos auctoritatum vi et rationum copia conaretur obruere.
units.en: Although that indeed would require a certain greater force and abundance of spirit; and there would be need of much divine fire, for him to arrive at that submission of soul and endurance, and the like virtues, which so great a change of the man demands. And since without a certain special help of God this can in no way be done in men who are lost and now utterly overthrown, therefore the hope is very slight, and almost none, of bringing that kind of heretic back to a sound mind. But whoever should meet with heretics in no other discourses and conversations than about the right ordering of life, the beauty of the virtues, the pursuit of prayer, the last day of life, the eternity of hell, and other things of this kind — such as pertain even to the amending of the life of the heathen — truly he would consult far better for their souls and their salvation, than if he strove to overwhelm them with the force of authorities and an abundance of reasons.

units.la: Denique, summatim ut dicam, id hominum genus cohortationibus et opportunis monitis eget ad componendos mores suos, et ad suscipiendum metum pariter et amorem Dei, amoremque benefactorum, ut hac veluti medicina suis illi imbecillitatibus medeantur, fastidioque rerum divinarum, et evagationibus mentis innumeris, quibus inter caetera mala morbosque laborant: quae non continuo mentis apicem intelligentiamque, sed prius pedes manusque, cum animi tum corporis, petunt. Jesus Christus, Redemptor universorum, divino suo spiritu eorum feriat leniatque praecordia, qui videt verbum suum in Chartisscriptum nequaquam esse ad permovendam hominum mentem satis.
units.en: Finally, to say it in sum: that kind of men needs exhortations and timely admonitions for the composing of their morals, and for taking up alike the fear and the love of God, and the love of good deeds; that with this medicine they may heal their weaknesses, and their distaste for divine things, and the innumerable wanderings of mind with which, among their other ills and diseases, they are afflicted: things which strike not first at the summit of the mind and the understanding, but first at the feet and hands, of soul and of body alike. May Jesus Christ, the Redeemer of all, with his divine spirit smite and soften the hearts of those men — he who sees that his word, written on papers, is by no means enough to move the mind of man.

units.la: Non dilatabo orationem meam. Tantum rogabo te animum ut spectes meum, obsequendi cupidum optimo tuae mentis studio, quo adductus hoc me rogasti. Cum plus otii nactus ero, plura forsitan in hanc sententiam. Quanquam haud scio, an huc etiam revocari possint omnia:
units.en: I will not lengthen my discourse. I will only beg you to look to my mind, desirous of complying with the excellent zeal of yours, by which you were led to ask this of me. When I have found more leisure, perhaps more to the same purpose — although I hardly know whether everything may not be brought back to this point.

units.la: Obedientia nostra debet esse caeca, id est, obedientia non debet respicere ad rationem, nec ad charitatem, vel ad spem fructus qui est in opere ei imperato. Animadvertendum autem est quod Dominus Noster volens ex una parte dilatare in nobis omne bonum, disponit voluntatem nostram et judicium ad apprehendendam aliquam rem ut bonam, ex altera vero vult aliquando nos facere contrarium, juxta voluntatem illius qui nobis executionem operis praecipere potest.
units.en: Our obedience ought to be blind: that is, obedience ought not to look to reason, nor to charity, nor to the hope of the fruit which lies in the work commanded. And it is to be observed that Our Lord, wishing on the one hand to enlarge in us every good, disposes our will and judgment to apprehend some thing as good; while on the other hand he sometimes wills that we do the contrary, according to the will of him who has power to command us the execution of a work.

units.la: Posito igitur quod accideret ut voluntas obedien- tis informata charitate vellet, ex magno zelo, quidquam facere quod esset ampli et certi fructus, et obedientia aliud opus praeciperet, in quo nullus speraretur fructus, cogitandum illi esset se non fecisse votum faciendi illum talem fructùm charitatis, sed obedientiae; et considerare deberet religiosum.,non vovisse salutem animarum juxta suam voluntatem, nec etiam juxta suum desiderium quod Dominus Noster ei infun- dere posset, sed vovisse executionem illarum ei O RRE o a C ST NT rerum quas superiores praecipere ipsi volent. Si í i y quando vero accidat, gratia Domini Nostri profluente, ex nostro modo caeco ambulandi, ut nos cognoscamus et sentiamus fructum, qui est in re nobis jussa, curandum quidem nobis est non amittere illum spiritum quo inclinamur ad talem obedientiam; sed non debemus rei ipsi quasi inhaerere, si quid aliud contrarium superior nobis praeciperet, revocando nos ab hoc quod prius jubebatur. Itaque necesse est illi qui vivit sub i obedientia nunquam seipsum quaerere in aliqua parte; nec debet sub quantumvis manifesta zeli ratione quiescere in aliqua parte, aut rebus particularibus subjectis obedientiae, ita ut gelistae dicit: Qui vult venire post me abneget - semetipsum et tollat crucem suam; id est, abnegando in nobis omnem voluntatem, poten- tiam et judicium; subjiciendo nos, in omni re, voluntati, sententiae, potentiae et judicio nostrorum Superiorum; sic assumendo nostram propriam crucem, et non cruces aliorum, quae forte leviores esse possent; et parati semper esse debemus ad ferendum, omni humilitate et patientia, quidquid e manu Domini veniet, et ad sequendum, cum cruce afflictionum, Jesum Christum, ex cujus manu exspectamus praemium ipsarum juxta illud: Sè toleramus, et conregnabimus. Neque simus conformes multis, aut majori hominum parti, qui onerati sunt crucibus sequendo mundum et ejus vanitates, qui sub finem diei, pro retributione famulatus quem ipsi mundo praestiterunt, alias cruces veras et aeternas ab illo reportabunt.
units.en: Suppose then it should happen that the will of the obedient man, informed by charity, wished out of great zeal to do something of ample and certain fruit, and obedience commanded another work in which no fruit was hoped for: he ought to reflect that he did not make a vow of producing that fruit of charity, but of obedience; and he ought to consider that a religious has not vowed the salvation of souls according to his own will — nor even according to the desire which Our Lord might pour into him — but has vowed the execution of those things which his superiors shall choose to command him. And if ever it happen, by the grace of Our Lord flowing forth from our blind way of walking, that we come to know and feel the fruit which lies in the thing commanded us, we must indeed take care not to lose that spirit by which we are inclined to such obedience; but we ought not to cling, as it were, to the thing itself, if the superior should command us something else contrary, calling us back from what was first ordered. Therefore it is necessary for him who lives under obedience never to seek himself in any respect; nor ought he, under however manifest a plea of zeal, to rest in any respect, or in the particular things subject to obedience — according as the Evangelist says: He who will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross; that is, denying in ourselves all will, power and judgment; subjecting ourselves, in everything, to the will, opinion, power and judgment of our Superiors; thus taking up our own proper cross, and not the crosses of others, which might perhaps be lighter; and we ought always to be ready to bear, with all humility and patience, whatever shall come from the hand of the Lord, and to follow, with the cross of afflictions, Jesus Christ, from whose hand we await the reward of them, according to that word: If we endure, we shall also reign with him. Nor let us be conformed to the many, or to the greater part of men, who are laden with crosses in following the world and its vanities, and who at the day's end, as the wages of the service they have rendered the world, will carry away from it other crosses, true and eternal.

units.la: Illud etiam est notatu dignum, quod res sit pernecessaria illis omnibus qui in quapiam Congregatione ac Societate vivunt, ut curent greg 1 sese conservare in bono illo spiritu cum quo Mgressi sunt, in hac vel illa Societate et congregatione, et in bona opinione et existimatione qua ab initio erga omnes afficiebantur. Et si unquam accideret ut amitterent bonum illum spiritum et bonam opinionem quam ab initio in omnes habebant, nunquam quiescendum est donec illam per orationes\et bona opera iterum acquirant; et persuadere nobis debemus, quod defectus est in nobis, et non in proximo, qui idem est ac erat initio, et forte meliore Ego in mea opinione mutatus ero, aut, ut melius dicam, omnino ab illo diversus. Denique si forte viderem aliquem defectum notatu dignum in uno ex meis sociis, non ideo amittere debeo bonam illam voluntatem quam erga illum habui semper, nec permittere ut in animam meam quaevis amaritudo ingrediatur, nec animi motus qualiscumque. Si enim hoc eveniet, magna in mea conscientia perturbatio et agitatio spiritus oriatur necesse est. Imo nec verbis, nec cogitationibus, meum fratrem judicare debeo, memor illius Christi verbi: Homo, quis me constituit Judicem inter vos? Correctio et judicium ad majores spectat: mihi sufficit judicem esse meorum defectuum; multa corrigenda in me reperiam; nulla in re parcam mihi, juxta illud Senec effatum: Aliis parce, tibi nunquam.
units.en: This too is worthy of note: that it is a most necessary thing for all who live in any Congregation and Society, that they take care to preserve themselves in that good spirit with which they entered this or that Society and congregation, and in the good opinion and esteem with which from the beginning they were disposed towards all. And if it should ever happen that they lose that good spirit, and the good opinion which at the beginning they had towards all, they must never rest until they acquire it again by prayers and good works; and we ought to persuade ourselves that the defect is in us, and not in our neighbour, who is the same as he was at the beginning, and perhaps better; it is I who shall have changed in my opinion — or, to speak more truly, become altogether different from what I was. Finally, if perhaps I should see some defect worthy of note in one of my companions, I ought not on that account to lose that good will which I have always had towards him, nor allow any bitterness to enter my soul, nor any motion of mind whatsoever. For if this happens, great disturbance of my conscience and agitation of spirit must needs arise. Nay, I ought not to judge my brother either in words or in thoughts, remembering that word of Christ: Man, who has appointed me judge between you? Correction and judgment belong to superiors: for me it is enough to be the judge of my own defects; I shall find much to correct in myself; in nothing will I spare myself — after that saying of Seneca: Spare others; yourself, never.

units.la: Amen! Amen! iterum Amen!
units.en: Amen! Amen! and again Amen!

appendix.titel: Ad amicum: de adversariis comitate devinciendis, 1543

units.la: Cum duobus meis Hispanis, usque ad decimum Octobris egi, eam mihi gentem conciliando, et habitui meo qui est secundum usum sacerdotum Hispaniensium. Quod hic ego egerim circa initia, novit per litteras meas Charitas vestra.
units.en: With my two Spaniards I stayed until the tenth of October, winning over that people to myself, and to my habit, which is after the usage of the Spanish priests. What I did here at the beginning, your Charity knows from my letters.

units.la: Benedictus Deus, qui dedit ut finis et recessus melior fuerit. Nemo enim jam Spirae erat, sive. ex saecularibus, sive ex sacerdotibus, qui nobis non esset perquam benevolus: sed et ipsi qui nobiscum maxime dissentire videbantur, quantum ad ea quae fidei sunt, videntes conversationem nostram et animos, hi, inquam, benevoli erant omnino; ita ut cum dolore recesserimus; et quantum ad spiritum semper Spirae futuri sumus.
units.en: Blessed be God, who granted that the end and the departure should be better still. For there was now no one at Speyer, whether among the laity or among the priests, who was not thoroughly well disposed towards us; nay, even those who seemed most to dissent from us in what concerns the faith — these too, seeing our manner of life and our spirit, were altogether friendly; so that we departed with sorrow; and as regards the spirit we shall always be at Speyer.

units.la: Si vis in coetu multorum vivere, cum quibus cor unum animamque unam et reliqua omnia aequum est habere communia, habeas persuasum necesse -est te ejus coetus et corporis membrum esse, quod in his, quae Dei vel Ecclesiae praeceptis non imperantur, vitam actionemque non habeas nisi ex corde animaque coetus ejusdem. Proinde hoc tanquam fundamentum pone, enitendum tibi esse ut ita componas te, ita alios, ubi opus sit, ut communis consensio semper adaugeatur. Quod perinde est ac si dicas corpore uti volenti, incolumitati corporis consulendum. Sed adversus Satanam, qui pacem ut pretiosissimam novit ita pessime odit et insectatur, his armare praesidiis. Inductio primum animi necessaria est, qua plane statuas velle semper defendere, excusare, fovere tui fratris voluntatem atque sententiam, contraque premere et infringere tuam.
units.en: If you wish to live in a company of many, with whom it is right to have one heart and one soul, and all things else in common, you must hold it as settled that you are a member of that company and body — so that, in things not commanded by the precepts of God or of the Church, you have no life or action except from the heart and soul of that same company. Accordingly, lay this down as a foundation: that you must strive so to order yourself, and others where need be, that the common agreement may ever be increased. Which is as much as to say that he who would use the body must care for the body's health. But against Satan — who, knowing peace to be most precious, hates and persecutes it most bitterly — arm yourself with these defences. First is necessary an inclination of soul by which you plainly resolve that you will always defend, excuse and cherish your brother's will and opinion, and on the contrary press down and break your own.

units.la: Deinde quantumvis rationi consentanea videantur quae tu vis aut loqueris, ubi fratris voluntas ratione dissentit, noli contendere. Sique succurrat a te stare rationem, responde fortasse a Deo non esse ut de opinione tua bene sentias, male de aliena. Item nullam esse rationem minuendae charitatis et pacis: quam haud dubie tueri magis, quam tuam debes rationem, Praeterea ubi ad te emendare non pertinet, converte oculos ad ea solum quae socii habent laudabilia; in te autem contraria inspice. Quod si non solum tibi, sed etiam externis, videatur quispiam fratrum ineptus, imprudens, molestus; vel inde suspectum habe judicium tuum, quod cum iis consentiat qui pleraque mundi oculis intueantur. Denique quidquid absurdum apparetin fratre et ab eo sejungit, cogita absurdius esse in anima tua judicium, quo absurda illa judicas; ac recordare, qui tales ineptias vel imbecillitates observat, ipsum fieri ineptum ac nihili; et contra qui erigit ad divina mentem, in iisque habitat, erectus ipse et excelsus evadit. Offensiunculas statim elide, ex illoque Apostoli monitu: Sol non occidat superiracundiam vestram! ne quieti te des, antequam fratri reconcilieris, eique ipsi simpliciter animi tui commotionem aperias. Id est colaphum cacodaemoni impingere, cui reconciliatio et demissio illa acerrimum dolorem ac probrum inurit. Jam veroad caeteram disciplinae custodiam, quemadmodum te habeas primum tecum, dein cum superioribus, et paribus, et inferioribus, et externis, breviter accipe. Primum persuasum ha- beto, in perpetua tibi pugna versandum, contra proclivitates carnis tuae et sensuum externorum; contraque prudentiam totam tuam, et memoriam et voluntatem. Propria haec voco, cum e tuo spiritu, non alieno, id est Dei et communitatis, existunt. In perpetuo igitur persevera conflictu, ad victoriam enitens tui, conculcans te abjecteque et contemptim accipiens, et includens te intra te, et transiliens te, et erigens supra te. p Cum superióribus sic ages, ut semper in tui demissione, et illorum veneratione proficias.
units.en: Then, however agreeable to reason may seem the things you wish or say, when your brother's will dissents from your reason, do not contend. And if it occur to you that reason stands on your side, answer that it is perhaps not from God that you think well of your own opinion and ill of another's; likewise that there is no reason for diminishing charity and peace — which without doubt you ought to guard more than your own reason. Moreover, where it does not fall to you to correct, turn your eyes only to what is praiseworthy in your companions; but in yourself look at the contrary. And if some one of the brethren seem, not only to you but also to outsiders, inept, imprudent, troublesome — even from this hold your judgment suspect, in that it agrees with those who look at most things with the eyes of the world. Finally, whatever appears absurd in a brother and sets you apart from him, consider that more absurd still is the judgment in your own soul by which you judge those things absurd; and remember that he who watches such follies or weaknesses becomes himself foolish and worthless; while on the contrary he who raises his mind to divine things, and dwells in them, comes forth himself upright and lofty. Petty offences crush at once, after that admonition of the Apostle: Let not the sun go down upon your anger! — do not give yourself to rest before you are reconciled to your brother, and have simply laid open to him the disturbance of your soul. That is to deal the evil spirit a blow on the cheek; for reconciliation and that self-abasement burn him with the sharpest pain and shame. Now, for the rest of the keeping of discipline — how you should bear yourself first with yourself, then with superiors, and equals, and inferiors, and those without — receive it briefly. First, hold it as certain that you must live in perpetual battle, against the inclinations of your flesh and of the outward senses, and against the whole of your own prudence, and memory, and will. I call these your own when they arise from your own spirit, not from another's — that is, from God's and the community's. Persevere then in perpetual conflict, striving for the victory over yourself, trampling on yourself, taking yourself abjectly and with contempt, and shutting yourself within yourself, and leaping over yourself, and raising yourself above yourself. With superiors you shall so act as always to make progress in the abasement of yourself and in veneration of them.

units.la: Aequalibus tuum praebe dexterum latus, et ab eorum nunquam sinistro recede: hoc et tua cum illis laeta ex aequo partire, in duris vero eorum et asperis vel potiorem partem assume. Si quibus praeponeris, memento eorum rationem tibi esse reddendam; et hoc stude, ut patientia antecedas et auctoritate, quae ex sapientia tua vera, id est ex virtute nascatur.
units.en: To your equals offer your right side, and never draw back from their left: that is, share your joys with them equally, but in their hard and rough things take even the greater part. If you are set over any, remember that account of them must be rendered by you; and study this: to excel in patience, and in an authority which is born of your true wisdom, that is, of virtue.

units.la: In juvandis proximis id specta potius ut labores quam ut tuorum videas fructum laborum: Tuum est colere, serere, rigare; caetera Christo permitte, ut fructus quos et quando velit decerpat; tum solum angare, quando labori peperceris.
units.en: In helping your neighbours, look rather to labouring than to seeing the fruit of your labours. Yours it is to till, to sow, to water; the rest leave to Christ, that he may pluck what fruits he will and when he will; then only be anxious, when you have spared yourself labour.

appendix.titel: Aureum praeceptum de castitate in hospitiis tuenda

units.la: Nostri, cunctis in hospitiis ae diversoriis, ubi nulla non pericula ex omni hominum genere sexuque struuntur pudicis ac castis, simul ac ex Christi praecepto pacem hospiti dederint, profiteantur libere pietatem, profiteantur veritatem, tum piis de Deo sermonibus inferendis, tum religionis colendis officiis: ut dum famae serviunt, caeterosque a flagitio suae probitatis opinione coercent, una eademque opera et pudori suo consulant et alieno. Nihil enim ita non continet in oflicio, ut edita jam virtutis exempla: nihil ita petulantiam hominum frangit, reprimit impudentiam, cupiditates imminuit, ut sobrii hominis et. temperantis aspectus.
units.en: Let ours, in all inns and lodgings — where every kind of danger, from every sort and sex of men, is laid for the modest and chaste — as soon as, according to Christ's precept, they have given peace to their host, freely profess piety, freely profess the truth: both by bringing in devout discourse about God, and by attending to the offices of religion; so that, while they serve their good name, and by the opinion of their uprightness restrain others from disgraceful conduct, by one and the same work they may take counsel both for their own chastity and for that of others. For nothing so holds men to their duty as examples of virtue already shown: nothing so breaks the petulance of men, represses impudence, and lessens desires, as the sight of a sober and temperate man.

units.la: Praecepta ġquaedam Cornelio Wishavaeo tradita de modo excipiendi cum fructu confessiones peccatorum. (Anno 1543) Fuerit ex usu confirmare paenitentes, ut quae maxime eorum onerant conscientiam, ea primum expromant; utque explicatum quidquam erit, opportunis interrogationibus te juvante, ad necessarias conditiones aperiendas, ad aliud item 'e gravioribus, tum ad aliud gradus fiet. Ubi autem quae succurrebant, omnia confitens aperuerit, tum dicebit praeceptorum, aut quo alio malueris ordine, ne quid praetereatur, caetera percunctari. i Providebis tamen ne, te interrogante, quisquam vitia quae ignorat ediscat. Statim ut crimen audieris, ex quo satisfaciendum cuipiam sit, ut inm re famave reponenda, antequam ultra progrediaris, ne subrepat oblivio, satisfactionis statue et injunge modum. Apprime necessarium est interrogari homines, de vitae suae studiorumque consilio ac fine: quorsam vivant; quorsum litteras, negotia, aulas sectentur; quorsum faciant rem; et similia: ne scilicet in rei totius summa erretur. Traducendus quisque est ad virtutes vitiis quibus irretitur contrarias, beneque animatus suppeditatis auxiliis dimit- - tendus.
units.en: It will be useful to encourage penitents to bring out first the things that most burden their conscience; and when anything has been laid open, you helping with timely questions towards disclosing the necessary circumstances, a step will be made to another of the graver matters, and then to another. And when the penitent has laid open all that came to mind, then he will run through the commandments — or in whatever other order you prefer, that nothing be passed over — and you will inquire after the rest. You will take care, however, that no one, through your questioning, learn vices of which he is ignorant. As soon as you hear an offence for which satisfaction must be made to someone — as in restoring goods or good name — before you go further, lest forgetfulness creep in, determine and enjoin the manner of satisfaction. It is especially necessary that men be questioned about the plan and end of their life and of their pursuits: to what end they live; to what end they follow letters, business, courts; to what end they make money; and the like — lest, that is, error be made in the sum of the whole matter. Each one is to be led across to the virtues contrary to the vices in which he is entangled, and dismissed in good heart, helps having been supplied.

units.la: Quod si id recta via effici nequeat, velut in amoribus faedis, et gravibus inimicitiis, averte inde et avoca hominis cogitationem; loquere de morte, de beneficiis Dei, mone ut gratias agat, Deumque collaudet, quod ei illa atque illa dona tribuerit. Ubi enim per haec ad timorem Dei erexeris, per se excident quae quasi magna ante tenebat. In remediis primia sunt frequens Eucharistia atque confessio apud unum eumdemque sacerdotem. Summo studio curabis, ut ad majorem virtutem, qui emersere e caeoeno lethalium criminum, per assidua incrementa ducas.
units.en: And if that cannot be effected by the straight way — as in foul loves, and grave enmities — turn the man's thought away from them and call it elsewhere; speak of death, of the benefits of God; admonish him to give thanks, and to praise God for having bestowed on him this gift and that. For when by these means you have raised him to the fear of God, the things he before held as great will fall away of themselves. Among remedies the first are frequent Eucharist, and confession to one and the same priest. With the greatest zeal you will take care to lead those who have come up out of the mire of deadly sins to greater virtue by constant increases.

units.la: Quae bona quidam faciunt, velut orationes, eleemosynas, instituendi sunt ut faciant bene. Docebis itaque orare triplici illa via, per Christi Domini Nostri mysteria, et capita christianae doctrinae, et litanias; in hisque tum gratias agere, tum veniam petere, tum necessaria dona poscere sibi, i aliisque vivis ac mortuis. Interim tamen exiguum ne putes pretium operae, quem nequeas altius attollere, intra praeceptorum divinorum cancellos cohibere. Super omnia cave ne taedium capiat te, tam sancto in opere, in quo Christum repraesentas peccatum mundi tollentem.
units.en: Those who do good works — such as prayers, alms — are to be instructed to do them well. You will teach them, then, to pray by that threefold way: through the mysteries of Christ Our Lord, the heads of christian doctrine, and the litanies; and in these now to give thanks, now to ask pardon, now to beg the necessary gifts for themselves and for others, living and dead. Yet meanwhile do not count it a small return for your labour if one whom you cannot raise higher you keep within the rails of the divine commandments. Above all, beware lest weariness seize you in so holy a work, in which you represent Christ taking away the sin of the world.

units.la: Supercilium quoque detestare pharisaicum, qui mansueti Christi.locum tenes. Erit quidem in- terdum agendum duriter, sed videndum est ut Railo exitus dulcis sit. Ac ferme, nisi forte cum obstinato qui nequaquam absolvendus sit agas, nemo ita dimittendus quin libenter -Sit redi- turus.
units.en: Detest also the pharisaic frown, you who hold the place of the meek Christ. Sometimes indeed one must deal harshly; but see to it that the ending be sweet. And as a rule — unless perhaps you are dealing with an obstinate man who is by no means to be absolved — no one is to be so dismissed that he would not gladly return.

units.la: Unum ego monuerim, ne in supremi judicii die queraris tibi non satis explicatum fuisse. Posthac, in tuo secessu usuque contemplationis, nequaquam tu pristinam pacem animi et dulcedinem experiere. Dum enim illud vitae genus sequebare quod acceptissimum Deo putabas, is tibi fideliter obsequenti coelestium contemplationum copiam large suppeditabat. Verum cum jam noveris multo perfectius vitae genus institui posse, quo in sancta paupertate atque obedientia temetipsum illi in sacrificium mactes, tuamque operam non ad exigui unius populi, sed ad omnium mortalium salutem, ex obedientiae nutu derives, plurimas hauriens aerumnas, inter ipsius vitae versans discrimina, ad gloriam ejus majorem; hinc jam tibi neutiquam consueta aderit in otio tuo tranquillitas; sed assidui pervellent animum aculei, quod declines aerumnas ét crucem, et vestigia deseras Salvatoris, esca tui commodi ac privatae quietis illectus.
units.en: One thing I would advise: that on the day of the last judgment you do not complain that it was not sufficiently explained to you. Hereafter, in your retirement and your practice of contemplation, you will by no means experience your former peace of soul and sweetness. For while you followed that kind of life which you thought most acceptable to God, he supplied to you, faithfully obeying, an abundance of heavenly contemplations. But now that you know that a far more perfect kind of life can be undertaken — in which, in holy poverty and obedience, you may slay yourself to him as a sacrifice, and derive your labour, at the nod of obedience, not to the salvation of one small people but of all mortals, drinking in very many hardships, dwelling amid the very dangers of life, to his greater glory — henceforth the accustomed tranquillity will in no wise attend your leisure; but continual stings will pluck at your soul, because you decline hardships and the cross, and desert the footsteps of the Saviour, enticed by the bait of your own comfort and private quiet.

appendix.titel: Ad Gerardum Hammontanum, priorem Carthusiae Coloniensis, Matriti 1546

units.la: Nihil est quod te oporteat timere, charissime Pater, ne vestri obliviscar. Pergite promereri in dies magis ac magis eum Spiritum, qui interpellat pro vobis in amicis vestris; ipse enim est sollicitus pro vobis, et me excitat assidue ad vestri memoriam. Excitant "quoque et illa beneficia a vobis in me et meos collata, quae et orant pro vobis: inter quae illud non minimum, quo perfecit ut nostra Societas particeps esset omnium benefactorum ordinis vestri. Hoc certe facit ut omnes fratres nostri tuae salutis et istius conventus vestri singularem memoriam agant. Magister Franciscus, ġui est apud Indos, anno šuperiore de. hac re litteras a me habuit et admonitionem, ut tui et istius conventus memo- riamfaciat semper, Ad ipsum nunc mittuntur decem ex nostris Lusitanis, qui et ipsi norunt hoc beneficium tuum, et meum amorem erga fratres tuos et totam Germaniam. Per eos recipiet magister Franciscus alteras meas litteras, in quibus legetvestri mentionem, et eorum qui nobis bene volunt Coloniae; ut sciat se esse debitorem, et me adjuvet, ne sim ingratus ego, cui tam gratis omnes bene volunt et bene faciunt.
units.en: There is no reason, dearest Father, for you to fear that I should forget you. Go on deserving, more and more each day, that Spirit who intercedes for you in your friends; for he is solicitous for you, and continually stirs me to the remembrance of you. Those benefits also stir me which you have conferred on me and mine, and which themselves pray for you: among which not the least is that by which you brought it about that our Society should be partaker of all the good works of your order. This assuredly makes all our brothers keep a singular memory of your welfare and of that convent of yours. Master Francis, who is among the Indians, had letters from me on this matter last year, with the admonition that he should always make memory of you and of that convent. To him there are now being sent ten of our Portuguese, who themselves also know this kindness of yours, and my love towards your brothers and all Germany. Through them Master Francis will receive another letter of mine, in which he will read mention of you, and of those who wish us well at Cologne; that he may know himself a debtor, and help me, lest I be ungrateful — I, whom all so freely wish well and treat well.

appendix.titel: Adhortatio ad doctum quemdam ad Societatem accedentem

units.la: Age in Christo, charissime; pergas confortari in eo quod tam feliciter caeoepisse diceris. Hactenus ipsum incipere propositum tibi ac destinatum erat: posthac in finem laborum oculus intendendus erit. Quamdiu non incaeperas, frustra quis te perseverandi labore terruisset, et vana nunc spe lactareris, si quis coronam tuis (quamvis optimis) deberi caeptis diceret; quae nisi in finem nulli unquam data est. Finis autem et perfectum in quodam significatu idem sunt.
units.en: Act on in Christ, dearest friend; go forward and be strengthened in that which you are said to have so happily begun. Hitherto the beginning itself was set and appointed for you: henceforth your eye must be bent upon the end of your labours. So long as you had not begun, in vain would anyone have frightened you with the labour of persevering; and you would now be fed with vain hope, if anyone should say that the crown is owed to your beginnings, however excellent; for it has never been given to anyone except at the end. And the end and the perfect are, in a certain sense, the same.

units.la: Profice igitur ad perfectum in omnibus. Si quid jam reliquisti, perfecte relinquilo; si cui rei oculos claudere coepisti, vel aures, aut quempiam aliorum sensuum, perfecte claudito, nunquam postea rebus ejusmodi aperturus; si qua in re te submisisti, submitte in omnibus. Patientia quoque perducatur ad opus perfectum, ut dilateris in Domino, non solum a dextris, sed a sīnistris, nec solum modis dilateris omnibus, sed pariter extendaris in omnem partem sancte acquisitionis divitiarum spiritualium. Paulus quae retro sunt obliviscens ad ea sola quae priora sunt se videtur extendere.
units.en: Go on, then, to what is perfect in all things. If you have already left anything, leave it perfectly; if you have begun to close your eyes to anything, or your ears, or any of the other senses, close them perfectly, never afterwards to open them to things of that kind; if in anything you have submitted yourself, submit in all. Let patience too be carried through to its perfect work, that you may be enlarged in the Lord, not only on the right hand but on the left; and not only enlarged in every manner, but likewise stretched out on every side of the holy acquisition of spiritual riches. Paul, forgetting the things that are behind, seems to stretch himself out only to those that are before.

units.la: Nos qui nondum quidquam perfecte incaepimus, debemus quadam ratione etiam ad ea quae retro sunt extendi, ut ex omni parte perficiatur opus nostrum. Acquirenda enim nobis illa ipsa quae dicitur compunctio atque detestatio eorum quae retro sunt. Crescendum est in peccati, inanitatisque rerum mortalium, ac demum nostri cognitione; unde suo tempore nascatur rerum spiritualium et caeoeleslium conspectus, pretium atque comþrehensio, studium virlutum et Dei amor. -Nos quidem te inter fratres infima quaerere, et ultima atque minima consectari, libentissime audimus. Nam magnitudo humanae mentis non in eo est ut magna ex suo sensu amèt atque amplectatur, magna, inquam, hujus mundi, sed ut ad minima sese extendat, Amor crucis ac vilitatis spiritum hominis fortem ostendit, non autem amor potentiae aut magnitudinis.
units.en: We who have not yet begun anything perfectly ought in a certain manner to stretch out even to the things that are behind, that our work may be perfected on every side. For we must acquire that very thing which is called compunction, and the detestation of the things that are behind. We must grow in the knowledge of sin, and of the emptiness of mortal things, and at last of ourselves; whence in its season may be born the sight of things spiritual and heavenly, their price and comprehension, the pursuit of the virtues and the love of God. That you seek the lowest place among the brethren, and follow after the last and least things, we hear most gladly. For the greatness of the human mind lies not in loving and embracing great things out of its own sense — great things, I mean, of this world — but in stretching itself out to the least; the love of the cross and of lowliness shows a man's spirit strong, not the love of power or of greatness.

units.la: Perge itaque exerceri in minimis, ut maxima aeternae vitae promerearis. Non ignoras apud arithmeticos nolam, quae cifra dicitur, nihil per se valere, verum subjunctam numeris incrementum iis tanto majus afferre, quanto post plures ponatur. Quidni ergo non omnes gaudeamus, qui novimus te, qui numero nostro accessisti, de vilibus vitae hujus tuum colligere pretium et valorem? Ama minimo nomine appellari ab omnibus, si nomem bonum velis tibi comparare. Sta in ultimo loco quamdiu poteris. Sectare vilissima et abjectissima officia: ex his enim gradum optimum in Christo crucifixo tibi acquisieris: Christus Dominus qui factus est obediens usque ad. mortem crucis, humiliatus primum usque ad carnem est, quam sibi conjunxit.
units.en: Go on, then, to be exercised in the least things, that you may merit the greatest things of eternal life. You are not ignorant that among the arithmeticians the mark which is called the cipher is worth nothing by itself, but joined to numbers brings them an increase the greater, the more of them it is placed after. Why then should not all of us rejoice, who know you — you who have joined our number — to be gathering your price and your worth from the mean things of this life? Love to be called by the least name by all, if you would win yourself a good name. Stand in the last place as long as you can. Follow the meanest and most abject offices: for from these you will have gained the best degree in Christ crucified: Christ the Lord, who became obedient even to the death of the cross, was humbled first even to the flesh, which he joined to himself.

units.la: Utinam nos quoque sic descendamus, ut vilissima quaeque hujus ministeria copulemus nobis, ad fovendam eam cui nos devovimus humilita- tem.. Utinam sımul obediamus Praesidibus nostris et per nosin caeteris regnet, qui regnatin se ipso, cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto, in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
units.en: Would that we too might so descend, as to join to ourselves all the meanest ministries of this life, to cherish that humility to which we have devoted ourselves. Would that at the same time we may obey those set over us; and that through us he may reign in the rest, who reigns in himself, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen.
